instructions.text: In a separate bowl, crack the whole egg, add the yolks, and whisk them well with a whisk or fork.
Add the grated cheese and mix well again.
Bring water to a boil, adding salt in the proportion used for all pasta, which is called 1.10.100, meaning for cooking 100 grams of pasta, you use 10 grams of salt and 1 liter of water.
Add the spaghetti and cook them until al dente (the time indicated on the package).

Cut the guanciale into thick strips, no thinner than 6-8 mm in diameter, and fry it in a pan until golden, about 3 minutes. Remove the pan from the heat. If there is too much fat, drain it from the pan.
Drain the water from the spaghetti, reserving 1 cup of liquid in case the sauce is too thick.
Add the spaghetti to the pan with guanciale, and quickly and thoroughly mix.
Add the egg and cheese sauce and mix well so that the egg and cheese mixture emulsifies with the pasta. If the sauce is not enough, add the reserved pasta cooking water.
Generously sprinkle with pepper.
Immediately serve on plates.
Top with finely grated pecorino romano.

ingredients.name: River fish
ingredients.notes: catfish, pike perch, sterlet, or perch

instructions.text: Clean and gut the fish. Small fish can be just gutted, as after straining and passing through a sieve, all the scales will remain in the sieve.

Cut off the head and tail of the carp, remove the fins, and separate the flesh from the spine. Set aside the roe and milt. Cut the meat into pieces 2 cm wide. You can also make fillets; in that case, add the skin to what will be used for making the broth.
Before we start cooking halászlé, it is necessary to salt the carp meat and put it in the refrigerator for at least an hour and a half.
In a pot, place all the small fish, head, fins, tail, and spine of the carp, and add cold water just enough to cover the fish. Make sure there is free space to the edges of the pot!!!
You can also layer the fish with the chopped onion, just as halászlé is prepared in a bogrács. How to prepare is up to you.
Finely chop the onion and fry it in fat until soft.
Bring the fish to a boil over high heat; typically, the foam is not removed, especially when made in a bogrács (cauldron) outdoors. But again, it's up to you.

Once the water boils, add the chopped tomatoes, paprika, hot paprika, and onion to the broth over the foam. Reduce the heat to minimum, and let our soup simmer almost unnoticed for at least 1 hour until the fish easily separates from the bones.
After 30 minutes of boiling, remove the carp heads from the broth, as prolonged cooking can make the entire soup bitter, which we must avoid at all costs.
After one hour, strain the broth and puree the cooked fish through a sieve or blend the meat freed from bones with a little broth in a blender. This will result in a thick base without bones.

Now, bring the base to a boil and add whole pieces of carp, roe/milt if available. Cook for another 10-15 minutes until ready. Never stir the soup with a spoon, as stirring can easily turn the fish fillet into unpresentable small pieces.
Ten minutes before the end of cooking, you can add more fresh hot paprika (red) and a whole fresh sweet paprika (green) for beauty.
Let the soup steep for a couple of hours – this will benefit it. For those who love spicy, you can separately chop hot pepper.
Serve with fresh white bread. And of course, with dry white wine!
If you want to make a different version of the soup, add the missing ingredients.
If you add a little white wine and lemon juice, it will greatly enhance the flavor. Balance it with a pinch of sugar, add a crushed clove of garlic – the taste will take on new shades!
Cascabel can be used

In a large frying pan, melt the fat. Sauté the whole pieces of meat until browned. Once a crust forms, transfer it to a large pot with cold water. The amount of water should be twice the volume of the meat.
Bring to a boil, then immediately reduce to a minimum heat so that the water is gently 'simmering'.
Add the bay leaf, coriander, and chili pepper. The roots, onion, and 1 carrot are added whole. Simmer the broth for at least 1 hour. The meat should easily separate from the bones.
When the broth is ready, remove everything except the meat, and add the previously soaked beans. If desired, the meat can be removed, bones discarded, and put back in. Do not remove from heat.
Dice the onion. Wash the carrot and cut it into thin strips. Cut the bell pepper into strips.
Heat the frying pan, melt a piece of fat, and sauté the onion over medium heat until soft. Then add the carrot and bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.
Next, add the blanched tomatoes and stir.

Peel the beet, cut it into thin strips, and sauté it in fat in the frying pan. Add sugar and sauté until a beautiful creamy color appears. Add vinegar and lemon juice, and simmer until 'al dente'. At the very end of simmering, add the tomato paste and 1 ladle of broth. Set aside.
Cut the potato into cubes. Shred the cabbage thinly.
Add the potato to the broth with meat, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to minimum.
After 5 minutes, add the cabbage, then after another 5 minutes add the sauté and beet. Season with salt to taste. Cook for another 10 minutes.
Remove from heat, add finely chopped garlic and herbs.
Serve with sour cream, pampushki, and garlic sauce.
Cut the salmon into small pieces.
Cut the avocado into small cubes.
Finely chop the shallot, green onion, and parsley.

In a bowl, combine the salmon with all the ingredients except for the avocado, drizzle with lemon juice, and add salt and pepper to taste. Mix everything well. Optionally, you can add a couple of drops of Worcestershire sauce.
In a mold placed on a plate, arrange the avocado cubes and drizzle with lemon juice to prevent browning when exposed to air. Top with the salmon mixture.
Refrigerate without removing the mold for 15 minutes.
When serving, remove the mold and garnish with microgreens.
Prepare the broth by separating the heads and shells of the shrimp, frying them in a pot, mashing with a spatula, add 1 l of water and boil for 20 minutes.
The peeled shrimp can be added to the paella during the cooking process.
First, prepare the mollusks. For this, they need to be soaked for 30 minutes in salty water to release the sand.
After that, boil the mollusks in a pot. When they open, remove them immediately. For mussels, remove one shell.
Mix lemon juice, 1 tbsp of olive oil, finely chopped parsley, and minced garlic.
This green sauce can also be used for any seafood and meat dishes.

In a large flat frying pan, sprinkle 1/2 tsp of salt over the surface, pour in olive oil, and fry the langoustines for 1 minute, sprinkle them with a pinch of salt, drizzle with green sauce, and remove from the pan. Then repeat the same procedure with the shrimp. Remove everything from the pan.
Cut the squid into rings. Fry it in the pan.

Add garlic and onion to the pan, and sauté. Add the bell pepper and chili cut into small strips. Add smoked paprika, tomato puree, and cook for 5 minutes. Add a pinch of saffron, crushing it with fingers. Add the peeled shrimp.

Add the rice and fry for 1 minute, stirring well. Add the broth and bring to a boil. Salt and evenly distribute the rice in the pan. Add the peeled shrimp cut into small pieces. Shake the pan to distribute everything evenly. After this, do not stir anymore. Cook for 9-10 minutes on high heat.
After 10 minutes, reduce the heat to medium.

Place the reserved langoustines, cardinal shrimp, fish cut into pieces, and mollusks on top of the rice and cook for an additional 8-10 minutes until the broth evaporates and you hear crackling at the bottom of the pan. Remove the pan from the heat and let the paella rest, covered with foil. Serve with lemon wedges.
Finely chop all the vegetables and sauté them in olive oil until soft. Add the wine and reduce it.
Cook the fish or shrimp broth, strain it, and add the sautéed vegetables. Add saffron, potato, and cook for 30 minutes.
Place the clean mussels in a pot with a small amount of water, cover, and boil for 2 minutes until they open. Add the water from the mussels to the broth.
Blend the broth with a blender until smooth. Reduce the heat to minimum and stir in the cream. Cook for another 2 minutes without boiling.
Place mussels in bowls and pour the soup over them. Sprinkle with parsley.
Peel the shrimp, separating the heads and shells. Place the mollusks in cold water to release all the sand.
Crush the almonds coarsely in a blender. Set aside.
Crush the saffron in a mortar with a pinch of salt, pour in just 20 ml of water to release its color.
Make a broth from the shells and heads of the shrimp, bring to a boil and add the garnish bouquet. Reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes.

In a frying pan, sauté the prosciutto over medium heat to render the fat and remove the prosciutto from the heat, leaving the fat in the pan. Lower the heat and sauté the onion, carrot, pepper, and garlic in the rendered fat until soft.

Add the wine and once the alcohol evaporates, add the tomatoes, tomato paste, and ground black pepper. Season to taste. Pour in most of the broth, add pieces of fish, ensuring there is room for the mollusks in the pan. Bring to a boil and cook for about 5 minutes.
Then add the shrimp and almond flour. Stir.
Add the mussels and clams. Cook for another 2 minutes. When the shrimp turn red and the mussels and clams open, turn off the heat and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Squeeze lemon juice into the pot.
Serve with baguette, on grated garlic, sprinkled with chopped parsley and ground paprika.

ingredients.name: Alkanet root (or a pinch of saffron
Kashmiri chili powder (or 1/4 tbsp + 3/4 tbsp paprika

instructions.text: First, grind all the spices for the marinade, cover the meat with them, rubbing the spices in well with your hands, and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare the dye. To do this, boil the crushed alkanet root in 2 cups of water, reducing the volume to 1/2 cup.

Heat ghee and mustard oil in a pot. Add the cinnamon stick, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, and black pepper. Increase the heat and add fennel seeds and the marinated meat. Mix well and sauté until browned.
Add asafoetida and ginger powder and cook for 1 minute. Season with salt to taste, stir, then add Kashmiri chili (1.5 tsp). Add bay leaves and curry leaves.
Pour in the dye. Mix well.
Add yogurt, and stir to coat the meat evenly. Add a little water in the process to ensure the sauce isn't too thick.
Cook for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and the red oil (rogan) rises to the surface.
Serve with Basmati rice or naan bread.

recipes.title: Mussels with chorizo in tomato sauce

instructions.text: Put 1 tbsp of butter in a large pot with a tight-fitting lid. Cook on low heat until soft, then increase the heat, return the chorizo, and add the wine, blanched tomatoes, tomato paste, fennel seeds, a pinch of sugar, plenty of pepper, and a little salt. Simmer for 2 minutes.
Add the chorizo and fry until crispy, then remove the chorizo from the pan to a plate and add the onion, garlic, chopped fennel, paprika, chili, and thyme sprigs to the pan.
Add the mussels, stir, cover with a lid, and steam for 3-4 minutes, shaking the pot a couple of times to help the mussels open.
Serve immediately with a baguette and a wedge of lemon.
Make a minced salmon mixture by chopping it with a knife.
Chop the cilantro, chili, and ginger and add them to the fish. Grate the zest and squeeze the lime juice into the bowl with the fish.
Add salt and pepper and mix everything well.
Form patties and refrigerate for 15-20 minutes.
Make the sauce. For this, chop the cilantro and mix all the ingredients.
Place the cut brioche on the grill and toast it. Then place the fish patty and fry for 2-3 minutes on each side, seasoning with salt.
Spread sauce on the bottom bun, place the patty, add another layer of sauce, pickled ginger, and garnish with microgreens and basil and mint leaves.

ingredients.name: Chicken egg
ingredients.group: FOR THE EGG AND TONGUE MARINADE

ingredients.name: Soy sauce
ingredients.group: FOR THE EGG AND TONGUE MARINADE

ingredients.group: FOR THE EGG AND TONGUE MARINADE

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.group: FOR THE EGG AND TONGUE MARINADE

instructions.text: Soak the bones in cold water and let them sit for 1 hour. Then drain the water and rinse the bones well under running water.
In a large pot, add enough water, place the bones in, bring to a boil, and add the tongue whole. Cook for 15 minutes. Drain the water. Rinse the bones and tongue well under running water.
Pour in more water, add the tongue and bones, bring to a boil, and cook uncovered over high heat for 15 minutes, skimming off any foam that forms on the surface.

Then reduce the heat to below medium, add the onion, the garlic heads cut in half, carrot, peeled and sliced ginger, kombu leaf, dried shiitake, and cook covered for 4-12 hours. Place a heavy object or a pot of water on top of the lid to prevent the broth from evaporating. The longer you keep the pot on the heat, the richer and tastier the broth will be.

After 2 hours, remove the tongue and place it in an ice bath for 5 minutes to easily remove the skin. The tongue is covered with a very tough skin that comes off easily after the ice bath. You can either discard it or throw it back into the simmering broth.

Place the tongue in a container, pour the marinade over it, having previously mixed all the ingredients for it. Also add the eggs, boiled for 6 minutes and peeled, and place in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight.

Remove the eggs from the marinade and set aside in a separate bowl. Sear the whole tongue in a pan with olive oil (or fat) until it has a nice roasted crust. Pour the marinade into a pot, add the tongue, and cook on low heat until the marinade reduces by 2/3.
When the broth is ready, strain it to remove any solid particles. Discard everything that was in the broth.
Add fresh shiitake mushrooms and mu'er to the broth and cook for another 10-15 minutes until the mushrooms are cooked.
Meanwhile, boil enough water for the noodles, first adding the bean sprouts for literally 1 minute, then remove them and set aside.
Then add the noodles, add the baking soda, and cook for literally 2 minutes.
Now we assemble the ramen:

Pour 1/2 cup of reduced marinade into the bottom of a deep bowl, then add 2 cups of hot broth. Place a portion of noodles, evenly distributing it in the bowl using chopsticks. On one side, place the bean sprouts and bamboo shoots, and on the opposite side, lay the sliced tongue.
Add coral mushrooms, sprinkle with green onions, garlic, and top with sliced chili peppers.
Cut the marinated eggs in half and place them in the ramen.

Separate the heads and shells of the shrimp, keeping the tails with the last joint of the shrimp. Make a cut along the "back" of the shrimp, about 2mm deep, and remove the intestinal vein. Set aside the cleaned shrimp in a separate container.

Fry the heads and shells in a pot over medium heat, breaking the heads with a wooden spatula to release the shrimp fat inside. Optionally, you can add a small amount of butter. Cook until all the shells turn red and the liquid with fat starts to "stick" to the pot slightly.
Pour 1 liter of water into the pot. Bring the broth to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 15-20 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to remove all heads and shells, leaving only the broth.
Add lemongrass, galangal, and lime leaves to it. The lemongrass stalks should be lightly smashed with a knife and then cut into thin long pieces. Slice the galangal into 2 mm thick pieces.
Tear the leaves in half by hand. Crush the chili and add it to the pot. You can adjust the spiciness to your taste by increasing or decreasing the amount of pepper. Cook for 10 minutes.
If desired, you can remove all solid parts with a slotted spoon, leaving only the broth, but in Thailand, everything is left in the pot.
Add mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes.
Add fish sauce, sugar, and Tom Yum paste and simmer for 1-2 minutes.
Pour in the milk, stir, and add the shrimp.
After a minute, turn off the heat.
Remove from heat and pour in the lime juice.
Add cilantro to the soup and ladle the soup into bowls.
You can serve rice on a separate plate.
First of all, soak the chickpeas in cold water in a 3:1 ratio for at least 3 hours.
During this time, the chickpeas will increase in size and absorb all the water.

Cut off the tops of the tomatoes and scoop out enough flesh inside to fill with the prepared stuffing. Cut a hole around the stem in the peppers and completely remove all partitions and seeds. Do not throw away the tops.
Grill the peppers in the oven at 175°C (350°F) for 10 - 15 minutes. They should become soft but hold their shape. Let them cool.
In a deep skillet, melt the fat and sauté the onion, then grated carrot until soft over medium heat.
At the same time, boil the chickpeas and rice in separate pots. Cook the chickpeas until done for 20 minutes, and the rice until half-cooked.
Add the minced meat, stir, and turn the heat to maximum, frying until the meat caramelizes. (until all moisture evaporates)
Add all the spices, garlic, tomato paste, and the flesh of the tomatoes, then add the rice, mix, season with salt and pepper, and cook for about 10 minutes. If necessary, add broth. Remove from heat.
Add the chopped parsley, cooked chickpeas, and feta. Mix well.

Stuff the peppers and tomatoes tightly with this mixture, cover with the tops, and place them tightly in a container, pouring in broth so that it covers the vegetables halfway, and place in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 40 minutes covered with foil.
Remove the foil and cook for another 20 minutes.
First, we make the patty.
For this, we grind all the ingredients in a blender, shape the patties and place them in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Mix all the ingredients for the sauce. Finely chop the capers.
Mix all the ingredients for the glaze.
Fry (seal) the halved brioche on medium heat in a dry frying pan.
Brush the patties with olive oil and fry for 3 minutes on each side. While flipping, brush with the glaze on each side. Salt to taste.
Place cheese on each patty, cover with a lid to let it melt.
Assemble the burger in the following order:
Bottom bun - sauce - ginger - patty - cheese - iceberg - chuka - sauce - top bun.
Bring water to a boil, adding salt in the ratio of 1.10.100 (for 100 g of pasta, 10 g of salt and 1 liter of water)
While the water is boiling, cut the Guanciale into cubes. On average, 50 g of Guanciale and 60 g of pasta are considered per person.
Using a fork, mash the blanched tomatoes in a bowl until they reach a paste-like consistency, add black pepper, chili flakes, and mix.
Fry the Guanciale over medium heat until it turns a nice golden color.
Add the wine and mix.
Remove the fried Guanciale from the pan, and only then add the tomato paste, frying it in the fat rendered from the guanciale. This will keep the guanciale crispy.

Add the cooked pasta, in this case Bucatini, to the sauce in the pan, mixing well so that the Bucatini is completely coated in sauce. Return the guanciale back to the pan, mix, add Pecorino, mix again, and immediately plate.
Cut the rooster into portioned pieces, set aside the back and neck for broth.
Slice the onion into half rings and the carrot into circles.
In the bottom of the container where the bird will be marinated, place the rooster, add the onion, carrot, add the bouquet garni, and pour the wine so that it completely covers the top layer.
Splash in a little cognac.
Marinate overnight.
Make broth from the rooster carcass.

For this, cover the carcass with cold water, bring to a boil, skim off the foam, reduce the heat, and add the bouquet garni from the marinade, half an onion, carrot, celery root, black peppercorns, and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Remove the pieces of bird from the marinade and dry them with paper towels.
In a heavy-bottomed pot, heat the butter. Sear the pieces of chicken until golden brown over medium heat. Sear in a single layer. Set aside.
Strain the marinade through a sieve into a separate pot and place over medium heat to reduce it by 1/3 of its volume.
Sauté the vegetables a bit in the same pan.
In the pot where the rooster will be cooked in the oven or on the stove, first layer the vegetables, then the bird, and sprinkle a little salt on top.
Pour cognac over the rooster and ignite. Be careful, as the alcohol vapors may ignite more than you expect. Wait until the flames are completely out.
Cover with a lid and place the pot with the rooster in the oven or on the stove. Cook for 1 hour at 200 degrees. Add broth as the marinade reduces (around 40 minutes in).

While the bird is cooking, cut the pancetta or bacon into 1 cm thick cubes and fry them in a dry pan over medium heat. When enough fat has rendered, add the mushrooms (originally morels were used). Cook them over low heat.
If you want to serve potatoes as a side, now is the time to start cooking them, either by baking in the oven or making mashed potatoes.
Meanwhile, roll the butter at room temperature with the flour into balls, so that they are of a fairly firm consistency. *** (see note 2)
Sauté the shallots in butter over low heat, adding sugar and a little water, until they turn golden.
When the bird is cooked, remove it from the marinade, strain the marinade, and add it to the mushrooms. Add the beurre manié sauce and reduce it to a thick consistency over 10 minutes.
Pour the reserved pieces of rooster with the finished sauce and serve with potatoes and butter-fried croutons.

recipes.title: Homemade Soup (Cult classic Moldovan soup Zama)

instructions.text: Cut the rooster into portion-sized pieces.
Place it in a pot with cold water so that the water completely covers the meat. Bring to a boil, remove the foam, and reduce the heat to a minimum so that the broth simmers gently.
Add the onion, washed and halved roots of celery, parsley, and parsnip, bay leaf, whole black pepper, and sprigs of thyme. Cook covered for 1.5 hours until the meat is ready.

Meanwhile, we will make homemade noodles. In a bowl, mix the egg and flour, add salt, and knead the dough until it is elastic. Roll out the dough into sheets and cut into noodles. Let it dry for 30 minutes.
When the rooster is ready, remove all the vegetables from the pot. Discard the onion, let the roots cool slightly, and slice them into rounds.

Slice the carrot into rounds and the bell pepper into cubes. Sauté them a little in a pan with chicken fat and add them to the pot with the broth. Cook for another 10 minutes. The vegetables should be al dente, not mushy. Season with salt to taste.
Now let's turn the broth into Zama.
Pour in the kvass and add the finely chopped parsley and lovage. Turn the heat to maximum, bring to a boil, and turn off. Zama should steep for 30 minutes.
5 minutes before serving, cook the noodles in a separate pot and add them directly to the bowls with Zama.
Serve with hot pepper and lemon.
Sour cream can also be added if desired.

First, let's make the starter. For this, pour 3-4 cups of bran with warm water to make a very thin porridge. Add pieces of white bread, cover with a clean towel, and place in a warm place for a day. The mixture should ferment.
Be careful to leave space in the bowl as the starter will rise and ferment.
Prepare the container in which you will make the kvass. A clay pot is ideal, but if unavailable, a 3-4 liter glass jar will suffice.

In a 7-8 liter pot, add the starter, bran, and cornmeal. For kvass, use 1 part starter and 2 parts bran - this way you don't have to measure grams and ml. Pour in 4-5 liters of hot water (but not boiling!) and mix well.

Add young cherry branches; some add a bit of fresh yeast and sugar. In general, everything should definitely ferment in a warm place. Then, each time you strain the kvass, set aside the first batch of starter for next time.
Cover with a lid and leave at room temperature for 1 day, stirring 2-3 times during this period.
Kvass will be ready in 15 hours.
Strain the borş through cheesecloth and pour it into bottles or jars.
It must be stored in the refrigerator until it starts to change color.
The bran mass that remains at the bottom of the pot is the real Hushte, which is used later for making kvass. You can store 1-2 jars of 800ml in the refrigerator for up to 2 months.
One jar of 800ml is enough for one batch.
Another method is to add 1 red beet sliced into the borş mass. This will give it a beautiful pink color.
Clean and wash the mushrooms well, then slice them lengthwise.
Finely chop the shallot and garlic, and sauté them for about 3-4 minutes in 4 tablespoons of oil in a skillet.*
Add the chopped rosemary.

Add the mushrooms, sauté on high heat for a couple of minutes, then add the tomatoes and 1/2 cup of wine.** Add a bit of salt and black pepper, and simmer the mixture on medium heat covered for 30 minutes.
After 20 minutes, bring water to a boil for the pasta, and when the water boils, add the pappardelle and salt based on the ratio of 1.10.100.
Drain the pasta, add it to the sauce along with the chopped parsley, and gently mix it so as not to damage the integrity of the pappardelle.
Serve, sprinkled with grated Parmesan cheese.
Heat a pan, add olive oil and a small piece of butter.
Season the meat on both sides with salt, pepper, and nutmeg shavings.
Then sprinkle with flour.
Place the 'steaks' in the pan so they do not touch each other. Sear them on each side for 2 minutes.
Sear the meat until golden brown. Remove it from the pan and pour out all the fat.
Let’s start making the sauce in which the veal will be braised.
For this, pour olive oil into the pan and add a small piece of butter.
Finely chop the onion, garlic, carrot, and celery. Add the finely chopped rosemary. Place everything in the pan and cook over low heat until softened.
Add the white wine. Stir the vegetables constantly until the wine evaporates.
Transfer everything to a heavy-bottomed pot where the dish will be braised.
Add the tomato puree to the pot, then place the 'steaks'.
Pack the pieces tightly, so they will braise in their own juice.
Pour in the chicken broth and bring to a boil.
Season with salt and pepper, add the bouquet garni and allspice. **
Cover the pot with a lid and cook for 2 hours in an oven preheated to 180°C (350°F).
While the roast is braising, prepare the 'Gremolata'.
Finely chop the garlic and parsley. Add the lemon zest. Mix everything together.
Remove the finished dish from the oven, remove the bouquet garni.
Sprinkle with gremolata.
Serve with risotto or mashed potatoes.
Mix the milk, vanilla, yogurt, and chia in a bowl, and pour half into glasses for serving the pudding.
Place in the refrigerator overnight.
Blend the raspberries and syrup until smooth.
Add the berry mousse to the glasses, topping with the remaining chia mixture.
Clean the chicken and rinse it under clean water. Then dry it with a paper towel (the drying process is very important).
Combine all the marinade ingredients in a small bowl. Add a spoonful of five spice powder.
Rub the inside of the chicken with the remaining five spice powder.

Prepare a large bag, place the chicken inside, and then add all the marinade, evenly coating the chicken. Let it marinate in the refrigerator for at least 48 hours. Turn it over 2-3 times during this period.

Take out the chicken. Shake off or rinse away any hard spice particles from the skin. Dry it with a paper towel. Then air dry until the skin is taut and dry (usually from 1 to 4 hours depending on the room's condition).
You can 'help' it dry using a hairdryer.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Brush the chicken with vegetable oil or preferably chicken fat and place it on the lower rack.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip the chicken.
Reduce the temperature to 120°C (250°F) and bake for another 30 - 45 minutes.
Let it cool for 15 minutes.
Serve it with hot sauce, soy sauce, or hoisin sauce.

recipes.title: Braised Oxtail Andalusian Style (rabo de toro a la andaluza)

instructions.text: Melt the lard or oil in a large thick-bottomed pot.
Dredge the cut pieces of oxtail (5 cm each) in flour and fry them in the fat until golden brown.
Temporarily remove the meat from the pot. Discard the fat.
Chop the vegetables. In the same fat, sauté the onion, then the carrot, celery, garlic, and peppers until soft. The hot pepper can be added whole.
Return the meat to the pot, add the chopped tomatoes, peppers, season with salt and pour in the wine. Once the alcohol evaporates, add water or broth to completely cover the meat.
Cover with a lid and simmer on medium heat for 3 hours. Add water as needed. Before serving, add the chopped parsley and stir.
When the meat is ready, temporarily remove it, and blend the liquid until smooth, return the meat and cook for another 10 minutes.
When serving, drizzle the meat on the plate with the sauce from the pot.

ingredients.name: Herb mix
ingredients.notes: from bay leaves, curry leaves, marjoram, thyme, oregano

instructions.text: Finely chop the vegetables and herbs.
In a pan, sauté the onion in olive oil until soft.
Add smoked paprika and stir.
Add carrot, garlic, and zucchini.
Stew over medium heat until soft for 5 minutes.
Add water or broth. Stew for 5 minutes.
In a mortar, crush the herb mix (can be substituted with Italian herb mix). Add the tomato, dried garlic, and spices. Mix well.
Stew for 10 minutes until the vegetables become mushy.
Then add the finely chopped parsley and basil.
Stew for another 5 minutes.
Puree everything with a blender.
Serve both hot and cold.

recipes.title: Ravioli with Rabbit and Parmesan Cream Sauce (Ravioli al coniglio con crema di parmigiano)

instructions.text: Place the flour in a large bowl and, using your fingers, form a "crater" in the center.
Pour half a tablespoon of olive oil into the center, three whole eggs, and the egg yolk.
Knead the dough with a fork until the dough particles separate well from the sides of the bowl.
After that, knead with your hands until you get a soft and shiny dough.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and let it rest in the refrigerator for an hour.
Chop and sauté the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic in olive oil. When the vegetables become soft, add the wine and let it evaporate completely. Add a sprig of rosemary to the sauté.
Add the rabbit meat and cook on low heat for 1 hour or until the meat easily separates from the bones, occasionally adding chicken broth (or water). Season with salt and pepper.
Remove the rosemary, and blend the mixture slightly in a blender. Add finely chopped sun-dried tomatoes and mix.
Roll out the dough very thinly until it reaches a thickness of about 2 mm.
Using a special mold, shape the ravioli, placing a teaspoon of filling in the center of each ravioli.
Cook the ravioli in salted water for 8 minutes.
While the ravioli are cooking, prepare the cheese cream sauce.
For this, heat the cream in a small saucepan, add the grated Parmesan cheese, and mix well.
When the sauce starts to thicken, turn off the heat. Sprinkle with grated nutmeg and a pinch of salt.
Serve the ravioli drizzled with sauce and garnished with basil leaves.
Soak the lentils in water for 20 minutes.
Finely chop all ingredients (except for the tomatoes), grind the spices in a mortar.
Then, place it in a medium-sized pot along with the dried chili, curry leaves, ground turmeric, minced ginger, and 2 cups (480 ml) of water. Bring to a boil.
Season with salt, reduce the heat, and let it simmer for about 20 minutes until the lentils are soft.
Add the coconut milk, stir, and cook for another 2 minutes.
Remove from heat. You can blend it to the desired consistency.
In a pan, heat the ghee. Add the garlic and mustard seeds. When they start to crackle, add the cumin seeds and onion. Sauté for about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes. Sauté for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the dal and all the other (optional) ingredients if using. Cook for 5 minutes over low heat.
Serve with flatbread or rice, garnished with cilantro if desired.

recipes.title: Roasted Bell Pepper Soup with Mascarpone and Basil (zuppa di peperoni al forno con mascarpone)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 225°C (425°F).
Cut the peppers in half, remove the seeds and place them on baking paper (or foil).
Bake them for about 30 minutes, until they are fully roasted.
Place the peppers in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap and let them cool for 15 minutes, so the skin comes off easily.
Once your peppers are ready, heat oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook until soft.
Add the roasted peppers, cut into cubes, then the tomatoes.
Bring to a boil, pour in the broth, and then reduce the heat to low.
Cover the pot and simmer for about 10 minutes.
Add the mascarpone and blend everything with an immersion blender until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper to taste, and serve garnished with basil leaves and grated Grana Padano.
Cut the chicken into small pieces and place them in a large bowl.
Add garlic-ginger paste, garam masala, ground chili pepper, salt, turmeric, and mix everything well. Let marinate for at least 1 hour.
In a pan, add vegetable oil, add onion and cook over medium heat until caramelized.
Put the caramelized onion, almonds, cashews, poppy seeds, grated coconut, and yogurt into a food processor and puree everything until smooth.

In a pan, melt ghee, add vegetable oil. Add cloves, star anise, black pepper, bay leaf, cinnamon, cardamom, and sauté the spices for 2 minutes. Add the chicken and sauté for 5 minutes. Add a little water if necessary.
Add the mixture from the food processor, blanched tomatoes, and mix well. Simmer for 25 minutes over medium heat with the lid on. If there is little liquid, add water.
After 25 minutes, add coconut cream or regular heavy cream to the pan and mix well, cooking for another 3-4 minutes.
Remove from heat and add roughly chopped cilantro. Mix. Serve with basmati rice and naan bread.

recipes.title: Dolma with Grape Leaves (Dolmeh Barg-E Mo)

instructions.text: Rinse the peas and rice well under running water.
Boil the peas until half-cooked in a small amount of water. Drain the water.
Sauté the chopped meat until caramelized. Sprinkle with pepper and ground cumin. Set aside.
In a pan, sauté the chopped garlic in oil, then add the onion, carrot, and diced eggplant until soft.
Add the butter, rice, and sauté while stirring. Add ground cinnamon and cloves. Pour in 1 ladle of broth, and let it evaporate almost completely. Add the tomatoes. Mix well.
Add the meat, stir until homogeneous, add the peas, turmeric, sugar, pour in a bit of broth and simmer for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Remove from heat, stir in finely chopped cilantro leaves, and add raisins. Mix well and let cool slightly.
Lay out the marinated leaves. On each leaf, place a heaping teaspoon of filling and roll it up.

Tightly arrange the dolma in layers at the bottom of a pot. Pour broth over the top so that it completely covers the dolma, add lemon juice, and press down with a plate to prevent the leaves from unrolling.
Bring to a boil and cook for 25 minutes on low heat.
Serve the dolma hot with sauce.
Garnish with green onion and chili pepper on top.
1. Pour cold water over the meat, bring to a boil, and reduce to minimum heat.
Add black pepper, ginger, 1 onion cut in half, bay leaf, thyme, garlic, and celery root.
Cook the broth for at least 2 hours.
In a frying pan, make the base of the soup by frying the fat until crispy, then sauté the onion in the rendered fat, followed by finely chopped parsnip and carrot.
If cooking without fat, substitute with olive oil.
Once the vegetables are soft, add them to the broth along with the halved young potatoes. Cook until the potatoes are ready.
Chop the herbs roughly and add them to the broth. Bring to a boil, then immediately remove from heat, otherwise the sorrel will lose its green color.
While the broth is heating, mix 2 eggs with sour cream and stir well.
Pour into the broth immediately after removing from heat and mix.
The soup should steep for at least 30 minutes to allow the sorrel to release its acidity. Alternatively, serve immediately with a splash of lemon juice.
Garnish with half a boiled egg, sprinkle with chopped green onion, and cracklings.
Cut the mushrooms into strips. Due to their uniqueness, the cap and stem of the mushroom have completely different flavors.

In a pot, heat the oil until boiling. Add the sliced mushrooms, chili, and chopped garlic. Fry for literally 1 minute until a brown hue appears. Remove the mushrooms with a slotted spoon and add them to the cooked rice.

recipes.title: Classic Ragu alla Bolognese (classico ragu alla bolognese)

instructions.text: First, we prepare the Bolognese ragu.

In a frying pan, place diced pancetta and fry it on high heat for a bit, then add finely chopped onion, followed by carrot and celery. This famous trio is called Soffritto, and it is the base for many dishes. Fry until soft.
Add the ground meat and simmer on high heat, stirring constantly, for another 10 minutes, until the water evaporates and it caramelizes.
Pour white wine into the pan with the vegetables and meat, and let it evaporate completely.

Then add the tomato paste, cook for 5 minutes, and reduce the heat to minimum so that the ragu simmers slightly. Then add the meat broth, followed by 1/3 cup of milk, stir until homogeneous and cover with a lid.
Simmer on low heat for about 2 hours. Do not stir.
After 1 hour, add salt, pepper, and the remaining milk. Add broth if necessary.
The ragu should acquire a velvety texture!
Cook for the remaining 1 hour.
After an hour, cook the tagliatelle in salted water in a ratio of 1.10.100 (for 100 grams of pasta, add 1 liter of water and 10 grams of salt). The cooking time is indicated on the pasta package.
Mix the tagliatelle with the ragu and serve immediately, generously sprinkled with parmesan on top.

recipes.title: Pho Bo with Nuoc Cham Sauce

instructions.text: Place the bones in a very large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil, and boil for 10-15 minutes to allow all unwanted particles to rise to the surface and form gray foam.
Drain the water, rinse the bones and pot well. Cover with cold water and put on heat.
Meanwhile, roast the onion and ginger over an open flame. This can be done in a pan or in the oven by placing them in for 15 minutes at 170°C (350°F).
Toast all the spices in a pan until fragrant. Do not burn them.
Add the roasted ginger and onion to the broth, cleaning off any burnt parts.

In a cheesecloth or tea infuser, add all the toasted spices, and add to the broth. Bring to a boil, skimming off any foam that forms, and reduce the heat to low. Add the beef meat (not the tenderloin), previously seared in a pan until nicely browned.
Throw all the remaining broth ingredients into the pot, namely salt, sugar, fish sauce, and simmer the broth for at least 5 hours.
After 1.5 hours, remove the cooked meat from the broth, place it in a bowl, and soak in cold water for 10 minutes, then drain completely and cover with plastic wrap.
Strain the finished broth through a sieve and keep it on the heat. Place the raw tenderloin in the freezer for 15 minutes before serving, then slice very thinly.
Soak the noodles for 30 minutes and cook according to the package instructions.
For this, first evenly place the noodles at the bottom of the bowl, top with pieces of cooked meat, slices of raw beef, and a handful of bean sprouts,
Pour hot broth over it, and generously sprinkle with chopped herbs.
Drizzle with nuoc cham sauce on top.
Cut the fillet from the fish and set aside.
Remove the heads and shells from the shrimp.

Sauté the remaining pieces of fish, tails, heads, etc. in olive oil. Add the heads and shells of the shrimp, finely chopped garlic, and ginger slices. Simmer on low heat for 20 minutes. Add the tomato and miso paste.
Add sake. Stir.
Transfer the entire mixture to the broth.
As it boils, remove the foam that forms.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium and add the kombu leaf and bonito flakes.
Cook for 25 minutes.
Strain the liquid through a sieve. Discard everything except the liquid.
Next, add the cuttlefish ink. Mix well until the color is even.
The broth is ready.
Bake the fish fillet in the oven at 175°C (350°F) on lemon slices, placing a sprig of thyme on top.
Boil water in a large pot. Add baking soda, salt, and cook spaghetti for the time indicated on the package. Add baking soda to give the spaghetti a 'chewy texture'.
Just before serving, place sliced squid, seafood, enoki, and mollusks in the hot broth.
Cook for 1 minute.
Immediately serve by first placing spaghetti on plates, then topping with seafood, enoki, wakame, fish fillet, and other ingredients.
Pour in the broth, sprinkle with green onion, and add the egg.
Garnish with a spoonful of red caviar and a sheet of nori.

Cut the avocado in half, twist the halves in opposite directions and separate them from each other. Remove the pits. Scoop out the flesh and mash it with a fork. Drizzle with lime juice. NOT LEMON! Lemon juice will make the avocado turn dark instantly and lose its appealing look.
Cut the chili peppers lengthwise. Rinse, dry, and finely chop. Peel and finely chop the onion.

Mix the avocado flesh with the pepper, onion, and cilantro. Season with salt. Wash and chop the tomato. Add to the guacamole and mix. If the sauce is prepared in advance, cover it with plastic wrap and refrigerate.
Serve with corn chips.
First, prepare the RAS EL HANOUT spice mix. To do this, mix all the spices.
Next, marinate the meat.
For this, mix the marinade ingredients in a large bowl.
Completely cover the shoulder with the marinade and marinate for at least overnight.
When the meat has marinated, sprinkle the chickpeas at the bottom of a fireproof dish.
The ideal option is a clay tagine, which is perfect for such a dish. Insert the chopped garlic cloves and cinnamon stick, and cover with coarsely chopped onion.

Top with sliced lemon and zest. Add the blanched tomatoes with all their contents from the cans. Sprinkle with the RAS EL HANOUT spice mix. Season with salt. Place the dried apricots on top. They can be added whole or chopped.
Pour in water.

Place the shoulder on top either whole or cut into 2 pieces. Drizzle everything well with olive oil. Cover with a lid and place in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F). Stew for 4-6 hours until the meat and chickpeas are fully cooked.
Before serving, add mint and cilantro, and escarole.
Let it simmer and soak together for literally 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with crushed almonds and mix the chickpeas with the prepared couscous.
In Marrakech, it is very common to serve a spicy yogurt or fermented milk drinks with the dish, and sprinkle pomegranate seeds on top.

recipes.title: Chashu Shoyu Ramen with Pork Roll

instructions.text: Thoroughly wash the bones and soak them in cold water for 1 hour. This will help remove blood clots, etc.
Cover the bones with water and bring to a boil.
Drain the first broth, rinse the bones under running water, wash the pot, and refill with clean water (2 liters).
Add the ginger root, peeled and cut lengthwise, the heads of garlic, cut in half, the leek, a whole onion, and the white parts of the green onion. Also, add the kombu leaves and dashi.
Bring to a boil, carefully skim off the foam.
Reduce the heat to medium low, cover with a lid, weigh it down, and simmer for 5-7 hours. The broth should be bubbling; otherwise, it won’t turn milky.
After that, strain the broth through cheesecloth and discard all the contents of the pot.
To prepare the roll, remove the skin from the meat.
If the layer of fat is too thick, trim it so that a small strip of fat, about 5 mm thick, remains.*
Roll the meat into a cylindrical shape, placing a lengthwise cut chili pepper inside so that it ends up in the center when rolling the roll. (You can omit the pepper)
Carefully tie the roll with cooking twine to hold the shape, wrapping the meat around every 1.5 cm.
In a pan, melt some pork fat and sear the pork roll on all sides until a uniform golden crust forms.
Meanwhile, pour soy sauce, sake, mirin, and add the lengthwise cut ginger, crushed garlic, and sugar into the pot.
Bring to a boil to dissolve the sugar.
Transfer the roll to the pot with the hot sauce, making sure the sauce covers about half of the meat's height.
Bring to a boil, cover with foil with a hole in the center, and cover with a lid.
Cook for 15 minutes.
After 15 minutes, turn the roll over, cover with foil and a lid.
Reduce the heat to minimum and cook for about 2 hours.
When the roll is ready, let it cool and place it in the refrigerator.
Remove the string from the roll, strain the sauce, and keep it until it's time to assemble the soup.
Measure the required amount of broth for serving into a separate pot and bring it to a boil. Add the mushrooms and cook for 10 minutes.
Bring the water in the pot to a boil and blanch the mung bean sprouts for 30 seconds. You can use a strainer for this.

If you are using fresh or homemade noodles, add baking soda to the water. This will make the noodles 'chewy' and elastic. ** You can just add regular soda, but the 'elasticity' effect of the noodles will be less.
Cook the noodles for 2 minutes.
Meanwhile, slice the remaining green part of the onion and the pork roll.
Pour soy sauce, leftover from cooking the pork (or eggs for ramen), into the bottom of a deep serving bowl. Approximately 1/4 cup.
Then pour in the broth (approximately 2 cups) along with the mushrooms.
Place the noodles, arranging them from one end of the plate to the other.
Add the mung bean sprouts on the side.
Place the sliced roll on the opposite side.
Add some dried wakame.
Generously sprinkle with green onions.
Add grated garlic and finely chopped chili pepper if desired.
Add the marinated egg, cut in half.***
Boil the tongue. For this, place it in a pot with cold water so that it is completely covered. Bring to a boil and drain the water. Add cold water, place the tongue, and add an onion.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cook until tender for about 1 hour.
To easily remove the skin, place the cooked tongue immediately in ice water. Cut into cubes.
Wash the potatoes and boil them in their skins. Peel and cut into cubes.
Also boil 3 eggs hard. 3 minutes before the potatoes are done, add the remaining 2 eggs for serving. Boil them so that the yolk is slightly cooked and creamy.
Cut the cucumbers, potatoes, and eggs into cubes. Slice the radish thinly into rounds. Finely chop the green onion and dill.
Mix all the ingredients and pour in the kvass. Add sour cream, salt, pepper to taste, fish sauce, and wasabi.
Stir and put in the refrigerator to chill for 1-2 hours.
Serve cold, adding half an egg for serving. Sprinkle with the reserved dill.

recipes.title: Chicken Hearts Curry with Coconut Milk

instructions.text: Heat vegetable oil in a wok. Sauté shallots and chili pepper until soft.
Add garlic-ginger paste and mix well.
Add curry paste and cardamom.
Simmer for 2 minutes until the characteristic smell of curry paste appears.
Add well-washed hearts to the pan and mix them in the curry paste.
Cook on medium heat for 5 minutes.
Add zucchini cut into half-rings, green peas, chopped green onion, and kaffir lime leaves, and mix.
Pour in fish sauce and balance the taste by adding sugar and lime juice.
Mix and cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in coconut milk and simmer on low heat for literally 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and serve immediately with rice.
Finely chop the spinach and boil it for 3-5 minutes in boiling water. Blend with chili and cilantro until creamy.
Cut the paneer into small 1 cm cubes.
Grate the ginger.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
Heat ghee in a thick-bottomed pot. Add cumin seeds, cardamom, cloves, and black mustard seeds.
Cook for a few seconds. Once the seeds start to crackle (which indicates that the seeds are releasing energy), add a pinch of asafoetida and the chili.
Add the onion and garlic and sauté until soft. Then add the spice mixture, ginger, and after a couple of minutes, the tomato paste. Simmer for another 2-3 minutes, stirring.
Then add the spinach.
Simmer for about 5 minutes. Add the cubed paneer. Simmer for a couple of minutes.
Pour in a cup of water, and add ground cumin, coriander, and garam masala. Mix well. Finally, add cream or yogurt to taste, so as not to spoil the green color of the dish.
It is best to serve the dish with plain steamed or boiled rice.
Blend everything until smooth. Serve with toasts or crackers.

recipes.title: Duck Risotto with Porcini and Cherry Tomatoes

ingredients.name: Arborio rice, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano

instructions.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Sauté the garlic clove for 2 minutes, then discard.
Increase the heat, add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Set aside.
Heat the remaining 4 tablespoons of oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the remaining garlic clove, sauté for 2 minutes, then discard.
Add the shallots and thyme and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft but not browned.
Then sauté the duck pieces for 3-5 minutes until nicely browned on all sides.
Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes until the grains are shiny.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely.
Add half of the mushrooms.
Add 2 ladles of broth, bring to a boil, and stir until the rice has fully absorbed it.
Gradually add broth as it evaporates, stirring the rice, until the rice is cooked to al dente.
This will take about 16-18 minutes.
5 minutes before it's done, add the tomatoes, parsley, and remaining mushrooms.
Remove the skillet from the heat, add the butter and grated Grana Padano cheese, and stir well for 30 seconds until creamy.
Season with salt and pepper, sprinkle with cheese on top and serve immediately.
Mix all ingredients in a bowl, taste the marinade and add spices if necessary.
Well coat the wings in the marinade, cover and refrigerate to marinate for at least 2 hours, but preferably for 24 hours.
Remove the wings from the refrigerator and let them sit to reach room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F); Line a baking sheet with foil.
Bake the wings for approximately 1 hour until tender, occasionally basting with the marinade.
Serve with a wedge of lemon, garnished with herbs and sesame.

ingredients.name: Arborio, Carnaroli, or Vialone Nano rice
Bouquet garni
ingredients.notes: a sprig of parsley, thyme, bay leaf

instructions.text: Boil the vegetable broth and keep it on low heat. It should be hot.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a deep skillet.
Caramelize the diced pears and sugar.
Set aside.
In the same skillet, melt the remaining butter and sauté the finely chopped onion until soft.
Add the rice and sauté until translucent for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in the wine and cook on high heat until all the liquid evaporates.
Pour in a ladle of broth. Cook, stirring constantly for 17 minutes, adding broth as it evaporates.
The rice should be al dente.
3 minutes before the rice is done, add the pear and stir. When the rice is ready, turn off the heat and add the gorgonzola, parmesan, cold butter, and mix well until the cheese melts.
Serve immediately.
Blend all the marinade ingredients in a blender. Squeeze in the lime juice.
Remove the skin from both sides of the wings, and trim the thin edge of the wings. Otherwise, they will look unappetizing when grilled.
Marinate the wings in the prepared marinade for at least 10 minutes.
Grease the banana leaves with oil and place the wings, cut into portions, so they can be wrapped in the leaf.
Grill the wings for 5 minutes on each side.
Serve with vegetables.
Pour water into a large pot and bring to a boil, then add the chicken and cook for 20 minutes.
Set the chicken aside, let it cool, then cut it into small pieces.
Keep the resulting broth on low heat to stay warm.
Peel the shrimp, removing the shell and head.
Remove the intestinal vein.
Sauté the shells and heads in a small amount of oil in the pot, and add water after the chitin turns red.
Put all the ingredients for the laksa paste into a food processor and blend until it forms a paste.
Add literally 1/3 cup for an even consistency of the paste.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat, add the contents from the blender and fry for 10-15 minutes.
Add water and sugar.
When done, the paste should be dark brown, and a layer of red oil should separate from the spices.
Set aside 4 teaspoons of the paste for serving.
Combine the broths in one pot.

Transfer all the contents from the wok to the chicken broth and bring to a boil. Pour in the coconut cream, season with salt, add curry leaves and sautéed tofu, fish balls, then reduce the heat and cook for about 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, soak both types of noodles in water for 15-20 minutes in separate containers,
and bring water to a boil in a pot for them.

For each serving, take a small handful of each noodle, bean sprouts, and several shrimp. Place them in a mesh strainer or sieve and soak the noodles and shrimp in hot water for 1 minute. Drain the water and shake off excess water, then transfer to serving plates. On top of the noodles, place the bean sprouts, pieces of chicken, and then pour the hot broth along with a few fried tofu and fish balls.
See here:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9WN3knltIos
In a cauldron over low heat, melt the diced smoked bacon.
Add finely chopped onion to the melted fat and sauté until golden brown.
Stir in the ground red paprika quickly. Then add the diced meat (4-5 cm) and pour in a little water.

Next, add the smoked ribs, the whole shank with the bone, and pour in enough water to cover the meat and ingredients. When the shank begins to separate from the bone, it needs to be removed, the meat taken off, cut into large cubes, and returned to the cauldron.
Simmer over low heat, stirring constantly for 2-2.5 hours. Add water as needed to keep the meat constantly in a small amount of liquid. At this stage, a little salt can be added.

While the meat is stewing, prepare the chipetke. For this, knead a stiff dough from eggs, flour, and salt. Pinch off small pieces, spread them on the table, lightly sprinkle with flour, and leave to dry.

Cut the carrot into cubes, chop the hot pepper and garlic, add to the meat, salt, and sprinkle with thyme and cumin. Peel and cut the potatoes into large pieces, add to the cauldron. Boil for another 20 minutes.
Cut the sweet pepper, tomato, and homemade sausage into cubes. Add all this to the bograc and mix. If it turns out too thick, add water.
After 15 minutes, add the chipetke and cook for just a few minutes.
Chop a lot of greens and sprinkle them over the soup.
Add wine, bring to a boil, and turn off.
Toast the sesame seeds over low heat until they turn light brown.
Finely chop the onion, ginger, and garlic, and sauté in sesame oil in a pot.
Add the ground pork and sauté, stirring to avoid raw meat.
Add the spicy bean sauce and mix, then add the miso paste.
After a minute, add the crushed sesame seeds, sugar, and pour in the sake.
Add the chicken broth, salt to taste, and white pepper. Add the wood ear mushrooms.
Cook over medium heat, while simultaneously preparing the noodles.
In a separate pot, bring water to a boil, add baking soda, and then add the noodles.
Cook for 1 minute.
Once the noodles are cooked, immediately place them at the bottom of bowls, pour the soup over, and add the toppings. The green onion and pickled ginger can be finely chopped.

recipes.title: Shrimp in Cream Sauce with Parmesan (camarones cremosos con queso parmesano)

instructions.text: Peel the shrimp and separate the heads.
To prepare the broth, fry the shells and heads in olive oil, add water, bring to a boil, and simmer for 15 minutes, reducing the heat.
Instead, you can also use either fish broth or dry white wine.
Heat the olive oil, lightly fry the shrimp over medium heat on both sides. Remove them from the pan.
Melt the butter over medium heat, and sauté the chopped garlic until fragrant.
Immediately add the shrimp (fish) broth or wine.

Pour in the cream and stir everything together. Bring to a boil and immediately reduce the heat to minimum. Add oregano, peppers, and ground garlic. Finely chop the reserved garlic and add it to the cream as well.
Simmer for about 5 minutes until the cream begins to thicken.
Add the reserved shrimp.
Evenly sprinkle in the grated Parmesan. Turn off the heat and stir until the cheese completely dissolves in just 1 minute. Add lemon juice if desired.
Add salt and parsley to taste.
Serve immediately with a French baguette.

recipes.title: Sea Razor Clams in Wine-Garlic Sauce (navajas en salsa de vino con ajo)

instructions.text: Slightly fry the minced garlic in a pan with olive oil. Add the chopped parsley and cook for another minute.
Mix a tablespoon of cornstarch with a glass of white wine.
Pour it into the garlic and let it reduce by 1/3 of the volume.
Add a pinch of salt.
Add the bay leaf and clams. Cook the razor clams for 2 minutes.
Remove them from the heat and serve immediately, sprinkled with parsley on top, and drizzled with lemon juice.
Cut the conch into small pieces.
Sprinkle with salt, ground pepper, add vinegar, orange juice and let marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour, preferably overnight.
In a deep skillet over medium heat, sauté the onion in butter until soft, add grated carrot. Cook until soft. Then add diced bell pepper, tomatoes, and tomato paste.
Add the conch, finely chopped Habanero, and mix well.
Bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for 1 hour.
After an hour, evenly sprinkle with flour, and stir. Add the cream and cook for another 10 minutes on low heat.
Serve with rice, garnished with cilantro, generously drizzled with lemon juice over the conch.
Cut the chicken into 5 cm pieces.
Mix the chicken with ginger, wine, soy sauce, cornstarch, salt, sugar, and green onions. Let marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Place the marinated chicken in a heatproof container for steaming.
Bring water to a boil and place the container with chicken inside.
Cook for 35 minutes.
Remove the lid from the steamer and let it sit for a minute.
Serve with rice, sprinkled with cilantro on top.
Pour oil into a pot and sauté the celery for 3 minutes, add the carrot, and sauté for a couple more minutes. When the root vegetables are ready, add the tomatoes, spices, and salt.

Peel the young garlic from the tough leaves and chop it along with the green tops. Cut the white part of the leek in half and slice it into half-rings. Add to the vegetables. Sauté over medium heat until the onion is translucent, stirring constantly.
Pour in the wine and partially evaporate it. Pour boiling water over the vegetables and cook until the celery is ready, about 10-15 minutes.
As soon as the soup boils, add the frozen or fresh green peas (not canned) and turn off the heat, then after 5 minutes add the peeled lobsters and let it sit covered for a couple of minutes.
When serving, sprinkle with Parmesan shavings and herbs.
Serve with slices of white bread, toasted in olive oil.

recipes.title: Chicken with Ginger in Coconut Milk

instructions.text: Heat canola oil in a skillet over medium heat and sauté the sliced ginger until it turns brown.
Remove the ginger from the skillet for a while. Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper and place them in the same skillet with the remaining oil.
Sear the chicken on all sides over medium heat until it turns brown. Return the ginger back and add the coconut milk.
Cover with a lid to allow the milk to evaporate. Bring to a boil and simmer over medium heat until the chicken is cooked through.
The meat should easily come off the bone. Add the prepared spinach and stir. Let the spinach warm up in the dish.
To prepare morels, first wash them, cut in half, and soak in water for 30 minutes. Then rinse again and boil in salted water for 30 minutes, skimming off the foam.
Next, sauté the chopped onion rings in butter and add the cut morels. Season with salt and you can add 1 - 2 bay leaves to the pan. Stew for 30 minutes.
5 minutes before the end of cooking, add 2 cloves of finely chopped garlic and 2 tablespoons of sour cream, and mix well.
Select boneless beef with no tendons. Rinse the meat and cut it into pieces.
Adjust the amount of chili peppers to taste.

Pre-cook the red beans. Alternatively, use canned beans. Drain the liquid and rinse the beans. Cut the bell peppers into large pieces. Peel and slice the red onion into rings. Prepare all the vegetables in advance.
Cut a small piece of pork fat into thin slices and render the fat in a skillet. You only need about 1 tablespoon of pork fat.
Sear the cut beef pieces over high heat in the pork fat until a golden crust forms.
The presence of a seared crust is very important; during further cooking, the meat pieces will hold their shape well and become tender.

When the meat is seared, add the chopped bell pepper, red onion, and chili pepper pods. Pour in the beef broth and simmer the meat with the vegetables covered on low heat until the meat is cooked through.
Finely chop the garlic. Add the red beans and garlic to the meat.
Add the spices: coriander, cumin, oregano, caraway, and salt – all to taste.
Add the tomato pulp and a little water.
Stir. The chili con carne should be saucy. Simmer the chili con carne without a lid over medium heat until done.
During this time, the liquid should almost evaporate, and the chili con carne should begin to thicken.
Add the chocolate. Let it simmer for another 5 minutes.
Fry finely chopped onion in lard in a cauldron (or saucepan)
Cut the meat into pieces of 2-3 cm and coat with paprika (do not salt!) Add to the onion and fry.
Fry until most of the meat juice evaporates and the meat is well cooked.
Add the flour. Mix the flour well and let it fry thoroughly while gradually adding boiling water or broth and stirring.

Add salt. Cover the saucepan with a lid and simmer. After 45 minutes, add the tomatoes, cream, lemon juice, and zest. The zest should be cut off with a knife, trying not to capture the white part. The larger the pieces of zest, the better.
Simmer the meat for another 3-5 minutes, remove the zest. Our dish is ready!
Goulash is served in Hungary with dumplings made from a firm dough with garlic and dill.
In our country, it is served with potatoes, pasta, rice, buckwheat, or vegetables.
After 45 minutes, add the tomatoes, cream, lemon juice, and zest. The zest should be cut off with a knife, trying not to capture the white part. The larger the pieces of zest, the better.
Simmer the meat for another 3-5 minutes, remove the zest. Our dish is ready!

recipes.title: Pasta with mushrooms and creamy pesto sauce

instructions.text: Sauté the mushrooms in a pan with olive oil until almost fully cooked for about 15-20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper.
Add cream and pesto sauce, stir.
Let it thicken slightly.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water (for 100 g of pasta, add 1 L of water and 10 g of salt).
Add the spaghetti to the pan, mix well.
When serving, sprinkle with Parmesan and garnish with basil leaves.

ingredients.name: Shrimp paste in Pantai soy oil

instructions.text: 1. Soak the noodles in cold water for 30-60 minutes.
In a small saucepan over medium heat, mix all the sauce ingredients. Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved.
The sauce should be balanced, both spicy, sour, and sweet at the same time.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the shrimp for just 1 minute. Set aside.
Add a bit more oil and toss in "set 1". Stir-fry until the garlic and tofu turn golden.
Add the noodles, then the sauce, and cook until the liquid is fully absorbed by the noodles.
Make some space in the wok for the eggs and crack them into the empty spot.
Stir-fry for just 30 seconds and place the noodles on top of the eggs.
After about 20 seconds, mix everything well and add "set 2".
Mix everything well for a minute and turn off the heat.
Serve on plates, add the shrimp, and sprinkle with chopped roasted peanuts.
Add a lime wedge and a pinch of chili flakes.
Sauté the octopus in a pan, add peas and tomatoes.
Add cheese and stir.
Pour in the cream.
Cook the tagliatelle al dente.
Place the tagliatelle on plates and drizzle with the prepared sauce.
Before cooking the meat, bring it to room temperature by taking it out of the fridge.
Sprinkle the meat with freshly ground pepper, rosemary leaves, and rub with a small amount of refined olive oil for frying.
Let the steak marinate for 15-20 minutes. Preheat the grill pan to maximum and the oven to 200 degrees. You will need a grilling rack and a tray underneath it for dripping fat in the oven.

Sear the steak for 2 minutes on each side. Season the steak to taste while flipping. At the end, place it on its side with tongs to seal the edges (15-20 seconds). You should have a piece of meat that is rare inside with sealed fibers and a beautiful grill pattern on the surface.
Now quickly transfer the steak to the preheated oven at 200 degrees on the grilling rack. After 8 minutes, remove the steak, place it on a plate, and let it 'rest' for 2-4 minutes.
You should have a steak cooked slightly below Medium, which is perfect for delightful juiciness! Slice into thin pieces.
Sauté the onion in vegetable oil.
Add the cream and mustard, stirring with the onion.
Reduce until thickened.
Lightly sauté the garnish ingredients on a grill pan or grill with a small amount of olive oil.
Boil the pasta.
Sauté the onion (if using) in olive oil until soft.
Pour in the cream, but do not bring to a boil, add the butter and truffle paste.
Season the sauce well with pepper and salt, then add the grated Parmesan.
Mix and add the cooked al dente pasta. When serving, top with Parmesan.
Wash the turkey fillet and dry it.
Mix pepper, salt, honey, mustard, and olive oil, and rub this mixture on the turkey.
Wash the orange, dry it, grate the zest finely (until reaching the white layer), cut the orange into slices, and squeeze out the juice (remove the seeds).

In a small frying pan, heat the olive oil, add the wine, salt, chili pepper, and honey, mix, bring to a boil, boil for 5 minutes, add the zest, lemon, and orange juice, mix, bring to a boil again and simmer, stirring, for about 5-7 minutes until the sauce thickens.
If necessary, add starch to thicken.
Place the turkey on the oranges. Bake covered or with foil for 1.5 hours.
Lay the squeezed orange slices on the bottom of a duck oven or another thick-walled pot where the turkey will be baked. The bottom should be completely covered with oranges.
Remove the cooked turkey from the oven, let it rest for 10 minutes, and remove the foil. Pour the orange sauce over it on the plate.
Prepare the vegetables: cut the round eggplants in half, slice the winter melon into pieces about 2 cm. Cut the chicken breast into slices.
In a frying pan, place the top part (cream) of the coconut milk from the can, or reduce some coconut milk to the consistency of cream. Bring to a boil, and add the green curry paste.
Fry until the coconut oil begins to separate from the milk.
For color, you can blend a little Thai (or regular) basil and pour it into the mixture.
Add the sliced chicken and ~50 ml of water. Stirring, cook for 4-5 minutes (until the chicken turns a milky opaque color).
Add the remaining coconut milk and chicken broth, bring to a boil, reduce the heat to medium, and let it simmer slowly.
Add the kaffir lime leaves, torn in half.
Add fish sauce to taste and palm sugar, and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the bamboo shoots, sliced eggplants, and sliced sweet pepper, mix and cook for another 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat, add the basil leaves, cilantro, halved cherry tomatoes, mix and serve.
Serve with rice.

recipes.title: New England Clam Chowder Recipe (new england clam chowder)

instructions.text: Fry the bacon over low heat in a large heavy-bottomed pot until crispy.
Add finely chopped garlic. Remove the bacon and garlic, and set aside.
In the rendered fat, add finely chopped onion and diced celery, then carrot. Add butter. Add wine, and let it evaporate.
Then add flour, stirring slowly to combine. Cook for about another minute.
Pour in the broth, add diced potatoes, bay leaf, thyme, caraway seeds and cook, stirring occasionally for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Add the seafood cocktail and clams. Cook for 5 minutes.
Turn the heat to low and stir in the cream and Worcestershire sauce.
If you want the soup to be thicker, add more flour. After that, cook the soup for another 2 minutes.
After adding the cream, the soup should not boil!
Turn off the heat and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Cut a circle in the top of a round loaf of bread, remove the inside, and pour the soup into the bread.
Garnish with chopped parsley and the reserved bacon with garlic.
Serve with saltine crackers.
Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pot over medium heat. Sauté the onion in the butter until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add grated carrot, and after 5 minutes, the chopped celery.
Cook until the vegetables are softened. Then pour in 1 cup of broth.
Whisk the ghee with the flour in a separate pot over medium heat; cook for 3-4 minutes until the flour dissolves, adding 1 to 2 tablespoons of milk.
Gradually pour the milk into the flour mixture, whisking constantly. Pour the chicken broth into the milk mixture. Cook without bringing to a boil until the mixture thickens.
Pour the milk mixture into the pot with vegetables, and add the chopped broccoli. Cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the grated Cheddar cheese into the vegetable mixture until the cheese melts. Add garlic, grated nutmeg, salt, and pepper to taste.
Blend the entire mixture with a blender until all ingredients are crushed.
When serving, garnish with a few reserved pieces of broccoli and croutons.
Prepare the duck very carefully*.
Gut, rinse well, and dry thoroughly.
Remove all leftover feathers.
Remove all visible fat.
Separate the skin from the meat by blowing air with a compressor between the skin and meat.

You can use a bicycle pump, or a metal tube and the strength of your own lungs. Insert the compressor hose between the skin and meat, under the duck, and also make a small hole below the duck's throat, and pump air through this hole**.
Grind half of the spices (the second half will be used for another procedure) finely, add grated ginger, garlic, salt, and hoisin sauce.
Mix well until a homogeneous mass is formed.
Thoroughly rub the marinade inside the duck.
Using a wooden skewer, sew up the belly so that nothing leaks out.
Take a large pot and fill it with water so that when the duck is immersed, it is completely covered, but does not overflow.
Bring to a boil.
Add the remaining spices without grinding them.
Add 200 g of soy sauce.
Scald the duck with this brine until its skin whitens.
After that, hang the duck in a cool place for 12 hours until the skin dries.
The next step is to prepare the syrup from a cup of sugar and a cup of soy sauce. Cook until the sauce thickens.
Brush the syrup onto the duck and leave it for 3 days. Insert a spacer between the duck's wings to dry between the wings.
It is necessary to hang the ducks in the refrigerator or a room at +5C.***
After three days, when the syrup has soaked into the skin, cut off the duck's tail to let all the inner marinade with liquid out of the suspended duck.
Prepare a "smoke" to give the duck a smoky aroma, as traditionally ducks are cooked over fruit tree wood.
You can make a pocket out of foil, ignite fruit wood chips so that the smoke envelops the duck for 30 minutes. ****
Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F), without any upper grills, and create a spacious bag around the duck from two layers of foil. Attention, the number of layers matters!
Besides the smoke, place a baking tray with water at the bottom. The duck should not touch the baking tray or any other hot metal parts of the oven.
It can be placed above the tray on several wooden skewers. Cook the duck for 30-60 minutes, depending on your oven. If you have a thermometer, the temperature inside the duck should reach 40 C.
Remove from the oven, hang, and coat the duck with the remaining syrup or honey.
Put it back in the oven at the same temperature for 30-50 minutes. The temperature inside the duck should be 55C. Take the duck out.
In a pot, heat 750 ml of good vegetable oil to 200°C (400°F).
The amount of oil is necessary to ensure temperature stability of the oil itself.

Pour oil over the entire duck with a ladle, taking small sections at a time with 3-4 ladles. The skin will immediately begin to crisp and change its color to reddish. The ideal is crispy, red skin and pink, very juicy meat!
For the sauce, mix all the specified ingredients together.
To learn how to carve the duck, it's best to watch a video about it.
Serve with mandarin pancakes, green onions, sliced cucumber, leek, and sauce.

recipes.title: Squid with Shrimp Paste and Black Pepper

instructions.text: Rinse the squid under running water, separating the head with tentacles, and then cut the squid body into rings.
Remove the eyes and beak from the squid head.
Crush the pepper in a mortar and crush the garlic cloves there as well.
Mix well.
Heat the oil in a wok, add the pepper and garlic, and mix again.
As soon as the garlic aroma appears, add the shrimp paste.
Mix well.
Add the squid, and stir them for about 3 - 4 minutes.
Add the oyster sauce and cook for another minute.
Add the cut green onion tops, about 3 cm long, mix once, and immediately turn off the heat.
Serve with rice.
Put the butter in the skillet.
Season the duck legs with salt and pepper to taste, sprinkle with thyme.
Simmer the legs until fully cooked. If necessary, you can add water.
Meanwhile, prepare the cherry sauce.
If the cherries are frozen, they need to be thawed.
It is necessary for the cherries to release their juice.
Pour the cherries along with their juice into a small pot, add wine, and bring to a boil over low heat.
Cook over medium heat until the liquid reduces by 1/3.
Pass the cherries through a sieve.
Return the cherry puree to the pot.
Add sugar, salt, cornstarch, and a teaspoon of butter.
Cook over medium heat until the mixture thickens, stirring vigorously.
Let the finished sauce cool and pour it into a sauceboat for serving.
Place the cooked duck legs on a plate, drizzle with sauce, and serve.*

recipes.title: Farfalle with Salmon in Creamy Garlic Sauce

instructions.text: Bring water to a boil. Add salt at the ratio of 10 g of salt per 1 liter of water and 100 g of pasta.
Add farfalle to the boiling water and cook for the time indicated on the package.

In a skillet, melt the butter, add garlic, parsley, and stir until fragrant. Add diced salmon and sauté for 1 minute. Salmon pieces are often sold in stores, so it’s better to find them for this dish rather than cutting up a steak or fillet.
Add the wine, and after just 30 seconds, pour in the cream. Cook, stirring over medium heat until the sauce thickens. Turn off the heat.
When the pasta is ready, add it to the salmon and mix.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Noodles with Chicken Hearts in Spicy Sauce

instructions.text: Sauté the onion in oil over high heat until golden brown.
Sauté the hearts for 5 minutes.
Add grated carrot.
Add sliced chili. Cook until the carrot is soft, stirring constantly.
Pour in the chicken broth, sprinkle with dry chili, and simmer until cooked.
Boil the noodles, generously drizzle with sauce on the plate.
Wash the ribs, make deep cuts between the ribs.
Mix water, mustard, salt, honey and marinate the ribs for 20 minutes. If the honey is hard, melt it in a water bath.
In a skillet, melt the lard, fry the ribs on high heat on all sides until a nice brown color appears. Also, fry a bit between the ribs.
Preheat the oven to 200 degrees.
Place the ribs in a heat-resistant dish, generously pour with the sauce, and put in the oven for 15 minutes.
Do not cover. Every 5 minutes, scoop the sauce from the dish with a spoon and pour it over the ribs.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Add finely chopped onion, carrot, water, and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and simmer until the vegetables are soft.
Remove from heat, add the pepper, mango, vinegar, lime juice, salt, and sugar, and blend until smooth.
Pour the sauce into sterilized jars.
The longest procedure, which takes about an hour, but it's worth it, is caramelizing the onion.
For this, cut the onion into half rings,
Sauté the onion in butter in a saucepan over medium heat. As it cooks, the onion will significantly reduce in volume.
Add salt, which will draw out moisture. When the onion is cooking, it first becomes soft and then juicy.
The onion starts to brown or caramelize, becoming sweet and tasty due to the sugar contained in it. This will take about 10 to 15 minutes.
You can help it a bit by adding a spoonful of sugar.
Stir occasionally to ensure the entire onion is cooked evenly.
Add a little water to collect all the concentrated juices from the bottom of the pan. Continue until the onion becomes soft and dark golden in color.
Optionally, add a bit of wine or liqueur for extra flavor. Madeira wine or brandy pairs well with onions.
Caramelized onion goes great with burgers and steaks, as well as in salads and soups.
Finely chop the lettuce, shallot, cornichons, and sun-dried tomatoes.
Mix all the ingredients together.
Form a patty from the ground veal and fat in a 70/30 ratio. This will make the burger juicy. Add ground pepper. We will salt it during cooking.
Place the formed patties in the refrigerator for 20 minutes so that the fat binds with the meat, preventing the patty from falling apart while frying.

Fry the pancetta (bacon) on a grill or in a pan. If frying in a pan, use this fat to toast the brioche halves until golden brown. If grilling, brush the inside of the brioche halves with butter and lightly toast.
Fry the patty on the highest heat on all sides. A burger, like a steak, can have different degrees of doneness. Salt and pepper during frying.
When the patty is almost ready, cover it with a slice of cheese and cover with a lid (or a deep plate, foil, etc., to help the cheese melt).
Grill a slice of tomato cut into rings.
Slice the brioche into 2 parts.
Spread cocktail sauce on the bottom bun.
Top with caramelized onion, then a lettuce leaf, and then the tomato.
Next is the patty with cheese, followed by bacon.
Again, add caramelized onion, spread sauce on the top bun, close it, and eat immediately!

recipes.title: Mayonnaise with Cascabel pepper (maionese con chile cascabel)

instructions.text: Blend the eggs on medium speed until creamy consistency.
With the blender running, slowly pour in the oil while gradually increasing the blender speed until the mayonnaise reaches the desired consistency (the more oil, the thicker it gets).
Continuing to blend, add the chili pepper, ground pepper, mustard powder, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, lemon juice, onion powder, honey, and salt to taste.
Chill in the refrigerator for 4 hours or preferably overnight.
Store for no more than 2 weeks.

recipes.title: Nutria Stewed in Sour Cream Louisiana Style

instructions.text: Cut the nutria meat at the joints and soak it in cold water mixed with lemon juice and rosemary for 1-1.5 hours. After that, if possible, cover the meat completely with milk and leave it for 8-12 hours.
This procedure will help eliminate the specific smell of nutria.
Afterward, remove the fat from each piece, as it does not melt during cooking. Sauté the meat in a mixture of fat and oil until golden brown in a skillet.
Pour oil into a large pot.
Sauté finely chopped onion, then carrot, and then celery until soft, add garlic, and place the meat on top.
