Add wine and let it evaporate a little. Then add tomato paste, tomatoes, spices, and broth.
Stew on low heat for 20 minutes. Then add sugar and sour cream. Continue to stew for another 40 minutes.
Before serving, sprinkle with chopped parsley leaves.
Serve with rice, lemon, and celery.
First of all, soak the meat for aspic for 5-6 hours, periodically draining and adding fresh water.
Place the soaked beef and rooster meat in a deep pot and cover with cold water.
Put the pot on the heat, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to the minimum.
Remove the foam that forms until it stops appearing.
Then cover the pot tightly and simmer the broth on low heat for 6 hours.
It should simmer and not boil at all. There should only be movement in the water.
This way it won't evaporate too much and will turn out concentrated.
It is not recommended to add water to the broth during cooking.
After 4 hours, add the parsley root and carrot, cut in half. Wash the onion with the skin well and add it whole. The skin will give the broth a golden color.

Half an hour before the end, add the bay leaf, peppercorns, and other spices to taste. Salt the broth only at the very end, otherwise, you might miscalculate the amount of salt. Moreover, you need to add a bit more salt than desired, as after cooling it may seem unsalted.
After the required time, remove all the meat and bones. Let the meat cool, separate it from the bones, and shred it. Or chop it finely.
Strain the broth through two layers of cheesecloth.
Throw away the bones and bay leaf with pepper.
Keep the carrot for decoration.

At the bottom of the mold, lay out circles of carrot, olives, cucumber, or even boiled quail eggs so that they form a pattern. Press it down with evenly placed meat to fill it with a layer of one and a half to two centimeters. Finely chop the cartilage and skin, and gradually add to each mold.
Sprinkle the arranged meat with finely chopped garlic and pour hot strained broth over it so as not to disturb the layer of meat too much.
Cool the future aspic to room temperature. At this stage, you can immerse decorations made of lingonberries, greens, and olives into the still liquid broth.
Place the dish in the cold. The setting time for aspic without gelatin is 5-6 hours.
The next day, remove the top fat with a spoon and turn the plate onto a serving dish.

ingredients.name: Lanspik
ingredients.notes: gelatin from broth made from tongue and partridges

instructions.text: Place beef shanks, beef, and chicken in a pot of at least 4 liters. Fill with cold water, bring to a boil, skim off the foam, reduce the boiling intensity to a minimum, and simmer for 4-5 (sometimes 6) hours, uncovered, adding vegetables.

2-2.5 hours before done, remove the cooked meat from the broth (leave the beef shanks in the pot and continue cooking), salt the broth with the remaining beef shanks very moderately, remembering that the broth will reduce further, and it's easy to misjudge the amount of salt.

Then remove the cooked shanks from the broth and strain the broth through a sieve lined with a cotton cloth. Cool the broth to a 'warm milk' state, add 2 whipped egg whites, bring to a boil, let the broth simmer for a minute or two (a gentle boil, stirring is necessary), and strain as described above. If necessary, add gelatin.
Pour into containers no deeper than 1 cm and place in the refrigerator to set.
Boil the beef tongue until done in salted water with half a carrot and onion for 2 hours.
At the same time, boil the potatoes in their jackets.
Boil the quail eggs for 5 minutes.
Rub the bird carcasses with olive oil, sauté in a pan until golden brown.
Put a pot of water on, add half an onion and carrot, celery, spices (salt, bay leaf, cranberries). Dip the bird into boiling water and simmer for 30 minutes over low heat. ****
Also boil the crayfish for 10 minutes.
All ingredients should be at room temperature!
Blend the eggs with a blender, then slowly pour in the refined olive oil, add vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt, lemon juice, and Worcestershire sauce.
Whip until thickened.
Refrigerate.
Allow all boiled ingredients to cool and dice the pickled and fresh cucumbers, olives, potatoes, tongue, and eggs.
Separate the meat from the bird bones and cut into cubes.
In a deep bowl, combine all ingredients, add finely chopped green onion, capers, and mix everything.
Also add the potted caviar. (See note **)
Dress with the made mayonnaise and mix.
Crayfish tails can be either chopped and added to the salad or placed on top after laying the salad on a dish.
Cut the set broth (lanspik) into cubes and place them in the center of the salad on top.

recipes.title: Marinated Veal Tongue with Sriracha Sauce and Honey (lengua de ternera en escabeche con shriracha y miel)

ingredients.name: Head of garlic, cut in half

instructions.text: In a large pot, pour enough water. Bring to a boil and put the tongue in the boiling water. The water should completely cover it. Boil for 15 minutes. Then drain the water, add new water, and bring it to a boil again. Place the tongue in it. Add the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and coarsely chopped carrot and onion.

Beef tongue is quite tough meat that needs to be simmered for about 2 hours so that the water is slightly "bubbling". Check the tongue with a fork so that it does not overcook when it becomes soft. It should not fall apart.
After cooking, place it in an ice bath for a short time before starting to remove the skin.
The entire tongue is covered with very tough skin that is easily removed after cooking. Once the skin is removed, set it aside.

Strain the cooking liquid and pour it into a container. Place the tongue in it and marinate in the refrigerator for a couple of days. It takes a long time, but it's worth it! Adjust the taste, add more sugar, vinegar, or soy sauce.
Remove the tongue from the marinade and dry it with paper towels. The base of the tongue can be removed as it does not have a presentable appearance.

Heat a skillet with a little vegetable oil and fry the tongue on all sides until it has a nice crust. Cut into small pieces and place on radish rings. Drizzle with honey on top, and add sriracha sauce.

recipes.title: Pappardelle with Zucchini, Gorgonzola, and Porcini (Pappardelle con zucchine al Gorgonzola e porcini)

instructions.text: Wash the lemon well and dry it. Grate the zest finely. Squeeze the juice.
Wash the zucchini well. Cut into thin strips down to the seeds using a vegetable peeler.
Crush the garlic cloves.
Pour oil into a frying pan, add the mixture of Italian herbs and garlic, and heat for about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat, finely chop the garlic. Add the slightly cooled oil with herbs, lemon juice, salt, and freshly ground pepper to the zucchini strips.
Add the finely chopped basil and parsley leaves.
Add the zest. Mix and let marinate for 25 minutes.
Sauté the mushrooms for 15 minutes until fully cooked.
Break the Gorgonzola into small pieces.

Combine the pasta with the zucchini. Sprinkle the plate with ground pepper, then place some zucchini, twisting the strips around a fork, then add the pasta, and again the zucchini. Add the mushrooms to the plate. Sprinkle with coarsely ground pepper, Parmesan, and pine nuts.

recipes.title: Medium Cooked Foie Gras in Terrine (terrine de foie gras mi cuit)

ingredients.name: Blackberries
ingredients.notes: or any other large berries, such as raspberries

instructions.text: First, let's deal with the liver itself. It needs to be brought to room temperature, divided by hand into 2 parts (it consists of 2 lobes) and placed in a ceramic or glass container with sides, then cleaned of the membrane and remove the venous network located inside the liver.
At the top (the thick part) is the main vein. The vein runs the entire length of the lobe.
The second main vein is located in the center of the lobe (where both lobes were attached).
To remove it, gently knead it with your fingertips, inserting your fingers into the liver, and when you feel the main vein, just pull it out of the liver.
Also remove all secondary veins.
Then, while continuing to 'massage' the liver, pierce it with your fingers and distribute it evenly across the bottom of the container.
In a bowl, prepare the seasoning; mix pepper, nutmeg, salt, and sugar.

Sprinkle the liver with the prepared seasoning, and pour the Port wine and Armagnac on top, cover with plastic wrap, and let marinate at room temperature for 4 hours. In some recipes, the liver is placed in the refrigerator to marinate for a day.

Line a rectangular baking dish with high sides with parchment paper so that the edges of the paper can later cover the liver placed in the dish. This is done so that the finished foie gras can be easily removed from the mold.
Using a spatula, transfer the liver to the dish, and spread it out evenly and tightly.
Next, you will need a deep baking tray or a large container to cook the foie gras in a water bath.
Place a square dishcloth (for washing dishes) in the center at the bottom of the tray, put the mold on it, and pour hot water into the tray so that it reaches halfway up the mold with the liver.
Place in a preheated oven at 120°C (250°F) for 50 minutes.
After this time, remove the container from the oven, and drain all the melted fat from the foie gras into a separate container. Set aside.

Place a couple of layers of paper towels on top of the wrapped parchment, and on top place a container of water or a smaller board than the mold that can be used to press down on the foie gras in the mold with a weight to compress it.
Put in the refrigerator for a day.

After a day, remove the weight, take off the paper towel, unfold the edges of the parchment, and pour the reserved fat (previously melted over low heat) over the foie gras, and leave in the refrigerator for another day.
Take the mold with the liver out of the refrigerator; you can actually leave the foie gras in the mold, but then it will be difficult to slice it nicely.

Let it sit for about 20 minutes at room temperature (otherwise it will be impossible to remove it from the mold) so that the fat softens slightly, and remove it by pulling on the edges of the parchment paper as a whole block.
Place a cutting board on top and flip it over with the block of foie gras. Remove the parchment paper.
It should be sliced with a knife moistened in hot water. Otherwise, it will stick to the blade.
Place the foie gras on a cracker, drizzle with fig jam on top, and serve with a slice of fig and berries placed on top of the block of foie gras. It can also be sprinkled with coarse sea salt on top.

recipes.title: Thai Green Curry with Shrimp and Mango

instructions.text: Heat sunflower oil in a pan.
Sauté finely chopped shallots with garlic for a bit.
Add curry paste, mix with onions, and cook for about a minute until the characteristic aroma appears.
Sauté the shrimp in the paste for 1 minute, then remove them. Set aside.
Sauté the chicken until it changes color to white.
Pour in the coconut milk.
Add eggplants, bell pepper, chopped chili, and green peas.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Cook for 4-5 minutes. The milk should evaporate a bit until the mixture thickens.
Add mango and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add finely chopped basil and green onions, fish sauce, sugar, lime juice to taste, and cook for another minute.
Remove from heat, and let it sit for 2 minutes.
Serve with Jasmine rice, placing the shrimp in the curry portion-wise.
Start by preparing the eggplants. Remove the stems and cut them lengthwise into pieces about 1 cm thick.
Salt them well on both sides and let them sit for 30 minutes. You can also soak them in salted water, as eggplants can be bitter.
Using a paper towel, press to remove excess moisture.
Fry in a large amount of oil until they are beautifully colored. Place the fried eggplants on paper to absorb the oil.
Heat a saucepan over medium-high heat and add olive oil. Fry the onion until lightly browned.
Add the garlic, minced meat, and cinnamon, breaking up the lumps with a wooden spatula.
Caramelize the meat, completely evaporating the moisture until the meat starts to brown.
Pour in the red wine and let it evaporate completely.
Add blanched tomatoes, sugar, spices, chopped parsley and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to low, and simmer covered for about 30 minutes.
In a large pot, melt the butter over low heat. Gradually add the flour, mixing it with the butter until thickened.
Pour in the warmed milk while stirring to prevent lumps. If the sauce is too thin, simmer over low heat, continuing to stir.
Remove the pot from the heat, add the egg yolks, salt, pepper, a pinch of nutmeg, grated cheese, and mix quickly.
Fry the sliced potatoes in a pan until golden brown.
Take a baking dish 20x30 cm. Grease the bottom and sides with olive oil and evenly sprinkle with breadcrumbs.
1 LAYER
Layer the potatoes at the bottom. Sprinkle with grated mozzarella.
2 LAYER
Add the eggplants, then cover with the béchamel sauce, spreading it evenly across the surface with a spatula.
3 LAYER
Top with the meat mixture, spreading it evenly across the surface.
4 LAYER - a cap of béchamel sauce. Spread the sauce very evenly and beautifully, ensuring it's well distributed across the surface using a spatula.
Drizzle with olive oil and generously sprinkle with grated Parmesan.
Cover with foil and bake the moussaka in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 40 minutes, then remove the foil and cook for another 20 minutes until the top is light golden brown.
It's necessary to wait at least 30 minutes for the moussaka to cool before serving. Otherwise, it will fall apart.

recipes.title: Herb-Crusted Lamb Rack with Pomegranate Sauce

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 225°C (425°F).
Generously season the lamb rack with salt and pepper.
Heat 2-3 tablespoons of olive oil in a skillet. Sear the meat in olive oil until nicely browned.
Place the rack on a baking sheet lined with foil, put it in the oven, and roast for 7-8 minutes.
Prepare the herb crust while the rack is cooking.
Place all ingredients in a blender, except for the mustard, drizzle with oil and blend until smooth.
Transfer the mixture to a medium-sized plate and set aside.
Remove the rack from the oven and brush with mustard. Roll the rack in the herb crust until it is fully coated.
When ready to serve, place the meat back in the oven for 3-4 minutes.
Wash the pomegranate, peel it, and separate the seeds.
Place the seeds in a bowl and put on low heat.
With a wooden pestle, crush the seeds, extracting the juice.
Then strain the juice through a sieve.
Pour the resulting juice into a saucepan and place over medium heat.
Add the wine, sugar, coriander, and ground chili.
Cook until the sauce begins to thicken.
At the end, add lemon juice.
Adjust sugar or lemon juice to taste if necessary.
Serve the rack with couscous, grilled vegetables, or ratatouille, drizzled with pomegranate sauce.
Melt the chocolate with butter in a saucepan over medium heat.
In a bowl, add sugar, cocoa, and the melted chocolate and butter mixture. Mix well.
Add the eggs and mix again.
Add the cherries and mix again.
Add the flour, mix (you may need a little more or less flour).
Grease the baking dish with butter and pour in the chocolate mixture.
Place in a preheated oven at 180 degrees and bake for 25-35 minutes.
Once the brownies are ready, take them out of the oven and sprinkle with powdered sugar on top.
Serve with a scoop of ice cream and berry jam.
Blanch the tomatoes by scoring the skin and immersing them in boiling water for 30 seconds.
Cut all the vegetables into large cubes about 2 cm by 2 cm.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and sauté the finely chopped onion and garlic.
Then add the eggplants and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the zucchini and peppers and cook for another 5 minutes. You can also drizzle the vegetables with dry white wine (a glass).
Add the tomatoes, thyme, olives, salt, and pepper to taste, and cook covered for 30 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool uncovered for at least 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
Wash the rabbit, remove the membranes and internal fat. Cut the carcass into portions,
In a deep frying pan, melt the butter and sauté the finely chopped onion until soft.
Add the sweet paprika to the onion and sauté for 1 minute, mixing the onion with the paprika until uniform in color.
Place the rabbit in the frying pan with the onion and
sauté it until lightly browned, stirring occasionally.
To ensure the rabbit in sour cream is juicy, cover the frying pan with a lid and simmer the rabbit over medium heat for about 10 minutes. The rabbit will release a lot of liquid.
Then remove the lid and let the liquid evaporate completely. This usually takes about 10 - 15 minutes.
Simmer the rabbit until semi-cooked
Add finely chopped sweet pepper
and blanched tomatoes.
Add black ground pepper and salt to taste
Mix everything well and simmer covered over low heat for 60 minutes until the rabbit meat is cooked. It is necessary for the rabbit to simmer for some time in the liquid sauce.
Add fatty sour cream to the stewed rabbit. If the sour cream is not very thick – mix it with flour.
The rabbit in sour cream should simmer on low heat under the lid for another 10 minutes.
Place the rabbit on a serving dish
Serve with a potato garnish

recipes.title: Duck roasted with apples and oranges

instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the duck of feathers. Scald it with boiling water, holding it over a pot of boiling water, and pouring from a ladle until the skin of the duck tightens.

Rub the inside of the duck very well with five spice seasoning, and stuff it with chopped apples and orange slices with the skin on, leaving enough room. Sew up the belly with either a wooden skewer or food twine.
Mix all the ingredients for the marinade, and evenly coat the entire bird with it.
Leave to marinate for at least a couple of hours, preferably overnight.
The longer the duck marinates, the juicier it will be, and the crust will be crispy.
Place the duck on a baking sheet belly side up, and surround it with the remaining apple and orange slices.
Add 1 cup of water, and cover with foil.
Put the duck in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F).
After 1 hour and 30 minutes, remove the foil, reduce the temperature to 180 degrees, and roast for another hour, basting with the pan sauce every 15 minutes.
Serve immediately. It pairs perfectly with potatoes as a side dish.

recipes.title: Kensington Club Steak with Wine Sauce

instructions.text: Prepare the marinade by mixing all the ingredients for it.
Place the meat in a food bag and completely cover it with the marinade.
Marinate the steaks for at least 24 hours, preferably 3 days.
Before cooking the steaks, prepare the sauce.
Pour olive oil into a small saucepan.
Sauté garlic and shallot over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add vinegar and completely evaporate it.
Add wine, add rosemary, and reduce the sauce to half the volume.
Add broth and reduce the sauce to 1/3 of its volume.
The sauce should be thick.
Let it cool.
Bring the steaks to room temperature beforehand.
Pat dry with paper towels.
Heat the skillet with oil.
Sear the steaks for Medium rare for 5 minutes on each side, turning them every minute.
If cooking on a grill pan, sear for 2.5 minutes on each side, then another 2.5 minutes on each side to create grill marks.
Wrap in foil and let them "rest" for 5 minutes.
Serve the club steak, cut into pieces, drizzled with sauce.
Finely chop everything. Capers, cornichons, parsley leaves (without stems).
Chop the onion.
Peel the onion, cut it in half.
First, make cuts lengthwise so that there are 4 rings for serving.
Chop the rest finely.
Cut the meat into 6x6 mm pieces.
It should remain 'meat', not minced.
Lightly drizzle with olive oil, salt, and pepper. And gently mash it with your hands.
Boil two eggs hard, separate the whites and yolks. Pass through a sieve. Arrange everything on a plate!
Make longitudinal cuts in the meat and insert strips of lard into them.
Tightly bind the meat with kitchen twine so that the meat and lard do not fall apart during cooking.
Pour olive oil into a large pot.
Heat on high. Sear the meat until browned on all sides.
Add chopped garlic, onion, celery, carrot, thyme, cloves, cinnamon stick, and rosemary.
Sauté for 10 minutes.
Add mushrooms. Sauté for literally 5 minutes.
Pour in the wine, simmer until it reduces by 1/3.
Then add the broth, add the tomatoes, and reduce the heat to below medium. Simmer for 3 hours with the lid on.
Salt and pepper should be added almost at the very end of cooking.
30 minutes before it's ready, cook potatoes in salted water.
In a blender, pour in 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 30 g of butter, add arugula, basil, 1/2 onion, and blend everything until smooth.
Set aside.
Remove the meat from the pot.
Strain the contents of the pot and puree until smooth.
Puree the potatoes in a blender, adding hot milk.
Sauté carrot rings in olive oil until browned.
Pour the gravy into the center of the serving plate, then place the carrots, puree, and meat.
Drizzle with the remaining gravy and green sauce.

recipes.title: Lasagna with Spinach, Mushrooms, and Béchamel Sauce

instructions.text: Heat the milk in a small saucepan until it comes to a boil.
In another small saucepan, melt the butter and mix it with the flour until smooth. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring constantly.
Slowly pour the milk into the flour mixture.
Stir until the sauce thickens.
Set aside.
First, thaw the spinach and drain as much water as possible.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).
In a dry skillet over high heat, sauté the spinach for just 5 minutes to evaporate any remaining moisture.
Set the spinach aside.
Add oil to the skillet and melt over medium heat. Add garlic and onion. Sauté the onion until translucent. Remove from the skillet.
In the same skillet, sauté the mushrooms in a mixture of butter and olive oil until the moisture evaporates and a golden crust begins to form.
Add half of the spinach and parsley. Stir and cook for 3 minutes. Set this mixture aside.
In a medium bowl, mix the remaining spinach, ricotta, eggs, and 2/3 cup of Parmesan.
Grease a baking dish with oil, and layer as follows:
1st layer - 1/3 of the Béchamel sauce, cover with 3 sheets of pasta to maximize coverage.
2nd layer - 1/2 of the ricotta, 1/3 of the mushroom mixture, and all the Mozzarella cheese. Then add 1/3 of the Béchamel sauce and 3 sheets of pasta.
3rd layer - all the ricotta mixture and 1/3 of the mushroom mixture. Sprinkle with Parmesan. Cover with 3 sheets of pasta.
And finally, the 4th layer - add the remaining mushroom mixture, the remaining Béchamel, and generously sprinkle Parmesan on top.
Bake, covered with foil, for 25 minutes. Remove the foil and cook for another 20 minutes until the lasagna is golden brown.
Let the lasagna cool for about 10 minutes before serving.

ingredients.name: Brine
ingredients.notes: 1 tbsp. salt per cup of hot water

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: 1500 g if making a potato base instead of dough

instructions.text: For the filling, sauté the onion and garlic in melted lard. Add the ground meat, finely chopped pepper, a couple of bay leaves, salt, pepper, and mix.
Now pour in hot water to slightly cover the meat. Add paprika, marjoram, and chili, mix, and cook for two minutes.
Add the raisins, mix, and simmer for another 30 minutes.
THERE ARE 2 OPTIONS FOR COOKING THE PIE.
1. Both the base and the top are made from potatoes. Then you need to boil not 750 g but 1.5 kg of potatoes.
2. Make the base from dough.
You need to decide at this stage.
Put the potatoes to boil in salted water. They should be cooked by the time the filling is ready (20-25 minutes).
You can also boil the eggs hard in the same pot.
If you chose the 2nd option, then after putting the potatoes to cook, prepare the dough.
Pour the flour into a mound on the surface, make a well in it, and pour in the melted lard. Knead the dough, gradually adding the brine - it should become a sticky mass.
Roll out the dough thinly. Grease the baking dish with oil, sprinkle with flour, and lay the dough in it.
Spread the filling on top, flatten it, and add sliced eggs and olives on top.
From the boiled potatoes, make a mash with milk and butter, add the yolk, salt, pepper, and nutmeg to taste.
Mix well until homogeneous. The mash should be creamy.
If not using dough, then spread the mash instead of the dough on the bottom of the dish in which you will bake.
Then follow the same steps as described in steps №10 and 11.
Spread the mash on top and create a pattern with a fork.
Using a culinary brush, carefully cover the mash with an egg-milk mixture.
Bake the pie in an oven preheated to 200 degrees for 20 minutes. Serve hot.
Place the chickpeas and 1 tsp. of baking soda (activated with vinegar) in a bowl and add cold water so that the water covers the chickpeas by 5 cm.
Leave for about 12 hours until the chickpeas double in size. Drain and rinse under running water.
Place the chickpeas and the remaining 1 tsp. of baking soda in a large pot and add cold water (3 parts water to 1 part chickpeas).
Bring to a boil, skimming off the foam.
Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer until the chickpeas are soft, about 45-60 minutes.
Drain the resulting broth into a separate container and refrigerate, and rinse the chickpeas, removing the skins by rinsing them under running water, set aside.
In a separate bowl, grate the garlic finely, add lemon juice and 1 tsp. of salt. Place in a food processor, add tahini and blend until smooth.
During the process, add ¼ cup of cold broth from the chickpeas.
Add the chickpeas and ground cumin, ground chili pepper, and smoked paprika.
Blend until the mixture is very smooth. Adjust the consistency of the hummus with the broth.
To taste, add salt, pepper, lemon juice, and cumin. Sprinkle with paprika, pine nuts, whole chickpeas, finely chopped herbs, and drizzle with olive oil.

recipes.title: Tom Yum from Pork Shank (tom yum rha mu)

instructions.text: Chop the shank into pieces and place it in a pot with water.
Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes.
Drain the water. Let the meat cool and cut it into serving pieces. The size of the pieces doesn't matter much. (Many Thai soups include meat on the bone).

Pour fresh water into the pot, add the pieces of pork, bring to a boil, and immediately reduce the heat to minimum. The water should simmer, not boil, otherwise the broth will be cloudy. Some recipes include pre-frying the pieces of meat in vegetable oil for 5 minutes (both ways are correct).

While the water is boiling, fry whole and peeled shallots, garlic cloves, and dried chilies in a dry skillet over low heat for a minute or two. As soon as the chilies start to change color, remove them from the heat or they may burn.
Remove all the foam from the surface.

Add lemongrass, cut into 2 cm pieces, smashed galangal slices, kaffir lime leaves, cut cilantro roots, tamarind sauce (or paste), a couple of tablespoons of fish sauce, and 2 teaspoons of salt to the pot. Cover with a lid and
cook for 1.5 hours or until the meat is tender enough.
Once the pork is tender, remove all the fat from the surface to keep the broth clear.
Add mushrooms, fish sauce, sugar, crushed fresh chilies, and fried dried chilies. If you don't like spiciness, just add a couple of dried chilies.
Add fish sauce, salt, or sugar to balance the flavor if necessary.
After 5 minutes, add chopped herbs, lime juice, and immediately remove from heat.
Serve with steamed jasmine rice, optionally adding a couple of cherry tomatoes to the soup.
Grate the onion (or grind it through a meat grinder) and squeeze out all the liquid with your hands.
Drain it.
Crush the saffron in a mortar.
Place the crushed saffron in a small bowl and add 2 ice cubes, set aside to allow the ice to melt.

The kebab made from minced meat is called koobideh. It is usually chopped together with the fat using cleavers on a wooden stump. If that is not possible, grind the meat with the fat once through a meat grinder. Then add the onion to the minced meat, knead the mixture well with your hands, and then grind it again with the onion. This technique will make the minced meat stickier.
Mix the minced meat in a pot with the onion, add the soaked saffron, pepper, ground cumin, finely chopped cilantro, and salt. Mix well until homogeneous.

Beat the mixture against a cutting board, slamming it down for 5-10 minutes. When the mixture is ready, cover it with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour. It’s even better to knead the minced meat with a dough mixer. This whole procedure is aimed at 'beating' the protein out of the meat, making the minced meat stickier.
When cooking, place a bowl of cold water nearby. Moisten your hands in the water. Take a small amount of minced meat and make a ball weighing 150 g.

Evenly mold this ball of minced meat around the skewer. It is best to do this with your index finger. There should be no holes or cracks in the molded meat on the skewer. Otherwise, that is where the kebab will fall apart. It should be a tight, monolithic 'sausage', tapered at the ends.
At home, use long wooden skewers.
Place the kebabs in the freezer for a short time.

Place the kebabs on a hot grill. To prevent the meat from falling off the skewers, turn the skewers literally every 30 seconds to evenly grill (seal) the meat on all sides. If you wait for one side to cook while the other remains raw, the meat will definitely fall off the skewer.
After 'sealing', grill the meat until cooked through. On a barbecue, this will take a maximum of 5 minutes on each side. Or even less.
When cooking in the oven, line the grill with foil, making grooves along the grill bars. Preheat to 250°C (475°F).
Place the kebabs on the foil. Bake for 15 minutes.
Serve the finished kebab with lavash, garnished with sumac and herbs.
Traditionally served with rice.
In Iran, this is called Chelo Kebab.
The dish is served with matsoni yogurt, grilled tomatoes, lemon wedges, and onion rings.
The most popular drink to have with Iranian kebab is Doogh (a sour milk product made with mint leaves and other herbs).

recipes.title: Classic Beefsteak with Cheese Sauce (Classic Beefsteak with Cheese Sauce)

instructions.text: Let the meat warm up to room temperature. Slightly pound it to a thickness of 1.5 - 2 cm, and shape it into a round or oval form.
Rub with olive oil, pepper, add lemon juice, vinegar, and Worcestershire sauce on top of the beefsteak. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Heat the pan, add butter, thyme, and fry the beefsteak for 1.5 minutes on each side.
Salt during cooking.
In a pan over medium heat, melt the butter, pour in the cream, and simmer for about 2-3 minutes.
When the mixture thickens slightly, add the crumbled blue cheese.
Stir until smooth,
Add salt, pepper, and chopped herbs.
When serving, pour the sauce over the beefsteak.
Peel the eggplants and cut them into large pieces.
Salt them and let sit for 10 minutes. Cut the zucchini.
Prepare the sauce:
mix soy sauce, balsamic vinegar, honey, grated ginger, garlic, and sugar.
Heat a pan with a mixture of vegetable and sesame oils.
Fry 1 clove of garlic until fragrant, remove it, and add the eggplants. Fry them for 5 minutes.
Then add the zucchini, stir, and add the tomato paste. Mix and reduce the heat to medium.
Pour in the prepared sauce, add the herbs, stir, cover with a lid, and simmer for 10 minutes. If the sauce is too thin, add starch.
Let it cool completely.
Serve on plates.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.
It pairs perfectly in taste with sweet grapes.

recipes.title: Fried Rice with Shrimp and Tobiko

instructions.text: In a small pot with sauce, sauté the green peas, bean pods, and diced carrot until cooked.
Add minced garlic and sauté the fresh shrimp.
Crack the eggs, stirring quickly to mix the eggs with the shrimp and vegetables.
Add the cooked rice and stir-fry everything together for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and mix it well with the rice so that the rice is completely colored brown by the sauce.
Drizzle with sesame oil and mix again.
Remove the rice from the heat, generously add the tobiko, and mix everything together.

recipes.title: Vegetable Stew with Turkey, Mushrooms, and Polenta

instructions.text: Cut the turkey and all vegetables into cubes.
Finely chop the onion and garlic.
First, pour 1 liter of salted water into a thick-walled pot and bring to a boil.
Gradually add the cornmeal to the pot, stirring constantly with a wooden spatula.
The temperature should stay close to boiling to prevent lumps from forming.
As soon as all the cornmeal is added, immediately reduce the heat to minimum, cover with a lid, and cook the polenta for 30 minutes, stirring every 3-4 minutes.
The finished polenta will start to separate from the bottom and sides, and a crust will form on the walls. If the polenta is too thick, you can add a few spoons of boiling water.
If the polenta is too runny, you can add a bit more cornmeal.
While the polenta is cooking, heat oil in a deep skillet and sauté the onion, garlic, and chili pepper.
Add the turkey pieces and sauté until golden brown.
Add the vegetables to the skillet and season with spices.
Simmer everything for 5 minutes.
Add the blanched tomatoes, mix, and cover with a lid.
Simmer over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Both the polenta and the stew should be ready at the same time.
Add butter to the polenta and mix in the grated Parmesan.
Let it sit for just 3-5 minutes.
Place the polenta on a plate. You can shape it if you put it in a pastry mold.
Top with the stew.
Rinse the rice several times until the water runs clear. This is a very important step in making Persian rice.
Soak the rice with a little salt for at least 20 minutes, but preferably for several hours. Rice soaked overnight yields the best results.
30 minutes before you start cooking, grind the saffron with sugar into a powder in a mortar. Transfer to a cup and add 2 ice cubes. It's better to do this in advance so that the ice melts naturally.
Boil 6 cups of water. (The rule is 3 cups of water for 1 cup of rice).
The next part of the process is very similar to cooking pasta. You salt the water (10 g per liter of water), add the pasta, and cook until al dente for 6 to 10 minutes.

Here we do the same: place the rice in boiling water and cook for 6-10 minutes. This is the first important point in cooking rice. Make sure to stir the rice a few times from the bottom up during cooking.
After 6 minutes of boiling, taste the rice. It should be al dente - soft on the outside and firmer on the inside.
Once the rice is ready, pour it into a colander and rinse with cold water to stop the cooking process.

Add a very thin layer of water to the bottom of a non-stick pot, just enough to cover the bottom. Add 2 tbsp of vegetable oil. You can also use clarified butter. Mix well to combine the oil and water. Pour in 1/3 of the saffron water. This is the first step to creating Tahdig.
Cover the bottom of the pot with rice. Sprinkle with cumin.
Often, the bottom is lined with round slices of potato.
Evenly pile the remaining rice in the middle, like a mound. Do not press the rice down.
With the handle of a spatula, make 4-5 holes, stopping 1 cm before the bottom. This is done for steaming the rice. Add pieces of butter.
Cover with a lid and cook on medium heat for 5-7 minutes until the rice starts to steam.
After that, cover the pot with a towel and place the lid on top, tucking the edges of the towel over the lid, and cook on low heat for 40 minutes to 1 hour.
METHOD 1. Place a serving dish over the pot.
Invert the pot, holding the dish firmly.
Remove the pot.

METHOD 2. Place the rice on a plate, break the tahdig into small pieces, and arrange it on the dish. Usually, when serving rice this way, the rice mixed with saffron is placed on top for decoration. Instead of adding all the saffron water to the yogurt, reserve about 1 tsp of saffron water. When the rice is ready, add a couple of spoonfuls of rice to the saffron and mix well. Place the mixture on top of the remaining rice.
Soak the chickpeas a couple of hours before cooking, or better yet, overnight.
Boil the chickpeas until ready.
Finely chop the parsley, cilantro, onion, and garlic.
Mix the herbs, boiled chickpeas, onion, and garlic, all spices in one bowl and blend in a blender.
Add salt to taste.
From the resulting puree, form patties in the shape of balls with flour. The flour will help maintain the shape and prevent them from falling apart.
Place the falafel on a baking sheet and bake in the oven until golden brown at 180 degrees.

Alternatively, you can fry it in hot vegetable oil. For this, fill the frying pan with vegetable oil to a depth of 4 centimeters. Slowly heat the oil over medium heat. The ideal temperature for frying falafel is between 180 to 190°C (375°F). If it's higher, there is a high chance that the outer layer will be overcooked while the inside will still be raw.
Fried falafel should be placed on paper towels with a slotted spoon to absorb excess fat.
Falafel can be wrapped in lavash, previously spreading tahini paste, sauce, and hummus.
Select small-sized white mushrooms. Ensure there are no worms.
Heat olive oil in a pan.
Add finely chopped shallots with a pinch of salt and sauté until the shallots are translucent.
Add sugar to balance the balsamic vinegar that will be added at the end, and stir well.
Slice the mushrooms very thinly, keeping the cap and stem intact.
Place the mushrooms on a serving plate.
Drizzle with the oil containing the sautéed shallots. Season with salt.
Garnish with ground black pepper, sliced truffle, herbs, paprika, capers, and thin slices of Parmesan.
Drizzle everything with balsamic vinegar and lemon juice.
Boil water in a pot.
Carefully place the eggs in the boiling water, having rinsed them in hot water beforehand to prevent cracking in the boiling water. Cook for exactly 6 minutes. No more, no less.
Immediately place in an ice bath or very cold water.
Mix all the ingredients and place the peeled boiled eggs in it for 4 - 12 hours.
Remove the eggs from the marinade. Store in a sealed container in the refrigerator for no more than 3 days.
Serve with ramen soup, cut in half.
First of all, wash the liver well, remove the membranes, and soak it in milk so that it is completely covered.
Leave for at least 2 hours.
Chop the shallots and garlic and sauté them on medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
Add the finely chopped mushrooms, stir, and simmer for 15 minutes on high heat to evaporate the moisture. During this process, splash in 50 ml of brandy.
Then reduce the heat to medium and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally. Essentially, this will be Duxelles - a well-known mushroom paste that serves as a base for soups, sauces, etc.

In another pan, sauté finely chopped shallots and grated carrot in butter (or goose fat) until soft, then add the liver, pour in the remaining brandy, add grated nutmeg, bay leaves, thyme, five spice seasoning, sugar, and simmer for 10-15 minutes, stirring until the liver is fully cooked.
In a blender, place 2/3 of the liver and 1/3 of the mushrooms, add 100 g of butter, and blend everything until smooth.
The texture of the pâté is a matter of personal choice.
Distribute into sterilized jars, pour melted butter or fat on top. Allow to cool and place in the refrigerator.
In this form, the pâté can last for at least 3 months.
Serve on toast with jam.
Finely chop half of the onion. Heat the olive oil in a skillet and add the onion. Sauté until soft.
Finely chop the garlic clove. Add it to the skillet with the onion and stir. Cook until the mixture becomes translucent.
Dice the bell pepper and add it to the skillet. Sauté, stirring occasionally, for another 5-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, previously sliced into rings.

Add sugar, salt, and spices. Mix everything well and let it simmer on low heat for 5 minutes to reduce the liquid in the skillet slightly. You can taste the sauce and check if the flavor is to your liking. If necessary, add more sugar, salt, or spices to taste.
Crack the eggs into the skillet with the sauce, making sure the yolks remain intact.
Cover the skillet and simmer for 10 minutes on low heat.
Remove from heat and sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Now you can serve it. Enjoy your meal!

recipes.title: Tagliatelle with Ricotta, Wild Mushrooms, and Pine Nuts

instructions.text: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat.
Sauté the crushed garlic until fragrant. Remove the garlic and sauté the finely chopped shallot onion until it changes color.
Add the mushrooms and thyme. Cook for 15 minutes until the mushrooms turn golden.
Add the peeled cherry tomatoes (optional).
Add the tagliatelle to boiling water. One minute before cooking time is up, remove from heat (check the cooking time on the package).
Drain the pasta, leaving 1/2 cup of water.
Add the pasta, water, half of the ricotta, pine nuts, salt, and pepper to the pan and mix well.
Serve on plates and garnish with the remaining ricotta, thyme, basil, and tomatoes.

recipes.title: Breakfast of Fried Asparagus, Fried Eggs, and Bacon

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Thoroughly wash the asparagus as it may be gritty, and use a vegetable peeler or knife to remove the tough skin from the bottom.
Place the slices of bacon in a roasting pan. Put it in the oven and cook for about 8 minutes or until crispy.
Remove the roasting pan from the oven and carefully transfer the bacon to a paper towel. Drain most of the bacon fat, leaving about a tablespoon in the pan.
Add the asparagus to the same roasting pan and gently toss to coat the vegetables. Arrange the asparagus in a single layer and sprinkle with lemon zest, thyme leaves, and pepper.
Roast the asparagus for about 8 minutes or until it starts to soften.
Serve the breakfast immediately. Toast is optional.
Remove the pan from the oven and carefully crack four eggs on top of the asparagus. Return the dish to the oven and bake for another 4-5 minutes or until the eggs reach the desired doneness.
Instantly plate, adding bacon, lettuce leaves, and radish.
To prepare the pumpkin puree, first preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Cut the pumpkin in half and remove the seeds.
Season the flesh with salt and pepper. Place rosemary sprigs and half a garlic bulb on each piece of pumpkin. Drizzle with a little olive oil and place on a baking tray.
Roast the pumpkin for 1 hour, until it becomes soft.
Discard the rosemary and garlic.
While the pumpkin is hot, scoop out the flesh and puree it in a blender.
For the soup, heat olive oil in a large pot, add the onions, and sauté until soft.
Add 2 cloves of garlic and a little nutmeg to the pot. Sauté for another 1-2 minutes.
Stir in the pumpkin puree and Parmesan, then pour in the broth.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and simmer for 10-12 minutes.
Add the sour cream and stir.

Blend until smooth. Add oil and blend again. For the garnish, heat olive oil in a pan and sauté the mushrooms over high heat for a few minutes until the moisture evaporates. Add oil, season the mushrooms with salt, and stir, then remove from heat.
Ladle the hot soup into bowls, spoon the sautéed mushrooms in the center. Garnish with Parmesan shavings, herbs, and ground pepper on top.

recipes.title: Beef Heart Stewed in Red Wine

instructions.text: In a pot, sauté diced shallots in butter, as soon as they are slightly browned, add pieces of beef heart for about 2 minutes to sear the meat.
Add tomato paste, and mix immediately
Add wine to the pot, bring to a boil, then add water, carrots and leek sliced into rounds, bay leaf, salt, and pepper.
Cook for 1 hour and 30 minutes until the meat is tender
When the meat is ready, add corn flour and continue to cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the sauce thickens to the desired consistency.
Serve with mashed potatoes or fried potatoes, generously drizzled with sauce.
Mix salt, sugar, and spice mix, grinding everything in a coffee grinder.
Rub the cheeks with the mixture. And leave to marinate for 5-7 days, turning and draining the marinade water every day.
Hang the cheeks in a cupboard for drying. Dry for 3 weeks at 15 degrees and 60% humidity.
Combine all ingredients together and blend until smooth.
Cook over low heat until it 'slightly bubbles' for 30 minutes.
If the sauce is too thick, add more wine.
Let cool and strain through a fine metal sieve.
Pour into sterilized containers.
Sauté the mushrooms in oil until golden brown.
In another pan, sauté the green curry paste for 30 seconds (until the characteristic smell appears).
Add the onion and ginger. Then add the chopped vegetables.
Sauté for 5 minutes over high heat. Then add a little broth.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes covered.
Reduce the heat to minimum, add coconut cream, lime juice, and sugar to taste.
Mix well and cook for another 5 minutes.

recipes.title: Mushrooms in Cream Sauce with Sweet Pepper and Black Spaghetti in Hokkaido Pumpkin

instructions.text: Cut the pumpkin in half, trim the ends so that the halves stand steadily.
Scoop out the seeds with a spoon, brush the flesh of the pumpkin with olive oil.
Place a piece of butter inside each half and bake for 45-60 minutes in the oven at 200 degrees.
Leave the pumpkin in the turned-off oven.
Sauté the mushrooms in olive oil. Add butter and sauté the mushrooms until golden.
Separately sauté the garlic until fragrant, then temporarily remove it from the pan.
In the same pan, sauté the onions until soft, add diced sweet pepper. Sauté, pour in the wine, and cook until soft.
Add the sautéed garlic and blanched tomatoes.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add ground pepper, salt, and basil. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the cream and blend everything in a blender until smooth.
Continue to simmer with the lid on for 10-15 minutes.
Before serving, add the grated parmesan and mix.
Cook the spaghetti al dente.
Place the spaghetti in the pumpkin, top with mushrooms and drizzle with sauce.
Enjoy together with the pumpkin.
Mix all ingredients, serve with ice, very refreshing in summer, served with meat and poultry.
Always served with chelo kebab.
Soak shiitake mushrooms until soft for 1 hour. Then finely chop them.
Soak glass noodles in room temperature water for 10 minutes. Drain and then cut into short pieces.
Shred the cabbage and carrot into thin strips.
Mix the minced meat with 1 tsp. of soy sauce and set aside.
In a wok or large saucepan, add a little vegetable oil. Add garlic, black pepper, and white pepper; stir until the garlic begins to turn slightly color.
Add the minced meat and cook, breaking up lumps with a spatula until fully cooked.
Add shiitake mushrooms, noodles, cabbage, carrot, cilantro stems, 1/2 tsp. of salt, 2 tsp. of soy sauce, and sugar.
Stir until the noodles are fully cooked and the cabbage is slightly wilted, adding water if the noodles start to stick.

Remove from heat, taste and add salt as needed. Place the filling in a bowl and let cool before assembling. To allow the juices to blend, place something under one edge of the bowl so that the juices flow to the opposite side of the bowl.
While the filling cools, separate the wrappers to make wrapping easier. Cover them with a damp towel to prevent them from drying out.
In each sheet, wrap 1 tbsp. of filling heaped. Wrap like an envelope, positioning the filling from the corner of the sheet.
Heat vegetable oil in a pot to 170°C (350°F). Add the filled pancakes and fry until golden brown, about 2-3 minutes.

recipes.title: Duck Leg Confit with Cherry Sauce and Mashed Potatoes

instructions.text: In a mortar, mix salt, pepper, bay leaves, and cloves. Rub the legs with this mixture, add rosemary, thyme, garlic, and marinate under plastic wrap in the refrigerator for a day.
Take out the legs. DO NOT WASH!
Carefully remove the marinade from the legs with a brush, place them in an oven-safe dish, and pour in fat so that it completely covers the legs.
Add the thyme and rosemary that were used in the marinade.
Put in a preheated oven at 150 degrees for 1.5-2.5 hours.
When the meat easily separates from the bone, take the finished legs out of the oven.
Transfer to a container where the legs will be stored in the refrigerator, and completely cover with the fat in which they were cooked.
Let cool and place in the refrigerator.
Before serving, take out the legs, fry for 4 minutes in a pan until crispy on each side.
Add duck fat to the boiled potatoes and mash into a puree. Drizzle with the fat from the pan and cherry sauce on top.
Melt the butter in a pan using half of the amount specified in the recipe, and add the sugar.
Cook the sugar for 2–3 minutes, then add the balsamic vinegar.
After a minute, add the cherries and broth. Cook for 2 minutes after the broth boils.
Use a slotted spoon to remove the berries from the broth. After that, cook the sauce until it thickens.
Return the cherries to the sauce along with the remaining pieces of butter, whisk, and remove from heat. At this stage, the sauce can be salted and peppered.

recipes.title: Sichuan Fried Spring Rolls with Chicken

instructions.text: In a large bowl, mix soy sauce, wine, pepper, and corn starch. Add the chicken and mix well. Let marinate for 10 minutes (or overnight in the refrigerator).
Cut the carrot into thin strips and shred the cabbage.
Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat. When hot, add 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil. Fry the chicken mince until crispy. Remove the fried mince from the wok and set aside.
Clean the wok and heat it over medium heat. As it heats up, add the vegetable oil.
Sauté the green onion, garlic, and ginger for 30 seconds. Do not overcook them, and immediately add the carrot and cabbage. Mix well.
Stir-fry the vegetables for 2 minutes or until the carrot is soft. Add the cooked chicken back into the wok, mixing well.
Add the oyster sauce and mix again.
Transfer the mixture to a plate and let it cool.
You can place an object under one side of the plate to allow the liquid to drain freely to the opposite side.
Mix corn starch and water in a small bowl.
Open the package of spring roll sheets and cover them with a slightly damp cloth to prevent drying.
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in each sheet, positioning one edge towards you, and roll it up.
Seal the end of the sheet with the corn starch mixture.
Keep the rolled spring rolls covered with plastic wrap to prevent drying.
When ready to fry, heat enough oil in a wok or deep, heavy skillet to 180°C (350°F).
For testing, dip a wooden spatula into the oil. If the oil is hot enough, bubbling should form around the spatula.
Carefully immerse the rolled spring rolls into the oil. Fry the rolls until they are golden brown, evenly for 3 minutes on each side.
Allow the rolls to cool before serving.
Serve with Hoisin sauce and sweet chili sauce.

recipes.title: Cannelloni with Mushrooms, Spinach, and Ricotta

instructions.text: Sauté the crushed garlic clove in olive oil until fragrant. Remove the garlic.
Chop the spinach. Sauté in garlic oil until soft. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Add the cooked spinach to a bowl with ricotta, add half a cup of grated Parmesan. Mix well.
Sauté the finely chopped mushrooms until golden brown in olive oil.
Add the cooked mushrooms to the ricotta and spinach mixture.
Add two tablespoons of marinara sauce. Mix everything evenly.
Stuff the cannelloni with the mixture. Pour the béchamel evenly into a baking dish.
Place the cannelloni in the dish. Pour the béchamel sauce on top, then the marinara sauce. Sprinkle with the remaining Parmesan on top.
Bake in the oven for 30 minutes at 170 degrees.
Finely chop the cucumber, tomatoes, garlic, and onion into a large bowl.
Add the crumbled croutons and season with salt and pepper.
Add the vinegar and a couple of tablespoons of olive oil. Mix by hand or with a masher, pressing to extract the juice.
Let marinate in the refrigerator for at least overnight.
Blend the entire mixture with the basil in a blender until it reaches a puree-like consistency. Adjust the consistency with water or tomato juice as desired.
You may need to add vinegar or olive oil individually to taste.
Keep the soup in the refrigerator until serving.
Serve the gazpacho cold with toast fried in olive oil, ice cubes, and garnish with herbs.
Before starting, bring the steak to room temperature.
20 minutes before cooking, rub the steak with olive oil and Worcestershire sauce.
Preheat the pan to the highest possible temperature. Pour in 1 tsp of oil.
Place the steak in the pan. During the process, add butter, thyme, and garlic.
Sear it on both sides until a crust forms. Then remove from heat.
Place the steak on a board, salt it, and season with the spice mix.
Place the puree on the board and send it to the oven preheated to 200-220 degrees.
After 10 minutes, the steak will be Rare.
Remove the Porterhouse steak from the oven and let it rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with rosemary and parsley.

recipes.title: Khoresh Fesenjan with Guinea Fowl (Khoresh Fesenjan)

instructions.text: Blend the walnuts in a blender until they reach a paste consistency.
Add to a dry frying pan, and caramelize for literally 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring constantly.
It's very easy to over-roast the walnuts at this stage, be careful.
Add water or broth, and mix well. Bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to low.
Cook for 20-30 minutes.
In a pot, pour in olive oil, and sauté the finely chopped onion until golden over medium heat.
Add the chicken, skin side down, and fry until golden brown.
During this process, add turmeric, and mix.
Add the walnut paste, mix, and cook for 30-40 minutes covered on low heat.
After 30 minutes, add the pomegranate sauce and freshly squeezed pomegranate juice. Mix well and cook for another 30 minutes on low heat. During this process, add sugar.
After 30 minutes, taste the dish, and depending on its flavor, add either sugar or lemon juice if the dish is too sweet.
Serve with Iranian chelow rice, sprinkled with pomegranate seeds on top.
In a food processor, grind the walnuts to a paste-like consistency. Set aside.
In a blender, combine the ground lamb and beef with onion, garlic, adding 1/2 tsp of black pepper.
Add
Transfer to a bowl, add the egg, and mix well, adding a pinch of salt.
With your hands, roll the meat mixture into balls about 2 cm in diameter, and coat each ball in flour.
Fry the meatballs in a preheated skillet with 2 tsp of olive oil until they are golden brown on all sides.
Set aside.

Slightly caramelize the ground walnuts in a dry skillet, add 3 cups of water, and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat. Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 20-30 minutes (leave the lid half open to let steam escape).
Now it's time to prepare chelo rice according to the recipe. See the recipe here: https://foodies.academy/recipe/persidskiy-parovoy-ris-chelo-chelo
Add the fried meatballs to the walnut mixture and cook on low heat for 30 minutes.
Then add pomegranate sauce with sugar (if necessary). Add if using tomato paste. Add the cinnamon stick.
Simmer on low heat, stirring occasionally, for another hour (with the lid half closed).
The sauce should thicken and darken. If it’s too thick, add water or broth.
Add saffron water and very gently stir to avoid breaking the meatballs.
Cook for another 15 minutes.
On serving plates, place the rice, top with meatballs, and drizzle with the thickened sauce.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, sauté the shallots in a small amount of oil over medium heat. Add the galangal sliced into thin rounds, the lemongrass cut into 2 cm pieces, and the kaffir lime leaves torn in half, along with the broth. Simmer for 5 minutes, allowing the broth to infuse.

Add the chicken, mushrooms, salt, and cook for 10-15 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through. Add the coconut milk, fish sauce, chili peppers slit lengthwise and seeded, and bring to a gentle boil. Cook for literally 2 minutes, then remove from heat.
Add the lime juice, adjust the taste, and generously sprinkle with chopped cilantro and/or green onions.
Serve with lime wedges and rice.
In a mortar, grind all the marinade ingredients into a paste, and rub it on the chicken.
Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes.
In a bowl, mix all the dressing ingredients.
Sauté the chicken fillet in olive oil over high heat for 3 minutes on each side, then reduce the heat to medium, and continue cooking the fillet covered for about 10 minutes.
Slice the radish and red onion into thin rings, halving the cherry tomatoes. Cut the green onion into 2 cm pieces. Slice the cucumber and chili pepper into thin strips.
In a large bowl, add all the greens and vegetables. Add the cooked and sliced chicken fillet.
Drizzle generously with the dressing on top, and gently but thoroughly mix.
Serve on plates, sprinkled with cashews on top.

recipes.title: Spicy Salad with Beef (Yum Neua Yang)

instructions.text: Prepare the marinade.
To do this, mix all the marinade ingredients in a bowl.
If you have an aged ribeye steak or tenderloin, it does not need much marinating. Bring the steak to room temperature, and brush it with the marinade 10 minutes before cooking.
If you purchased non-aged meat for the steak, it should be marinated for at least 1 hour before cooking.
Grill the steak on a grill or in a pan for 3-4 minutes on each side until medium rare.
Let the steak 'rest' for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, mix all the dressing ingredients.
Slice the radish and red onion into thin rings, halve the cherry tomatoes. Cut the green onions into 2 cm lengths. Slice the chili peppers into thin strips.
Place all the salad ingredients in a bowl, drizzle with dressing, and add the ground roasted rice. Toss to combine.
Slice the meat thinly against the grain. Add it to the bowl with the salad and mix.
Serve immediately on plates, garnished with cashews.

recipes.title: Spaghetti with Cuttlefish Ink, Squid, and Shrimp (Spaghetti al Nero di Seppia Con Calamari E Gamberi)

instructions.text: Clean the squid, remove the eyes, and rinse under running water.
Separate the tentacles, remove the skin from the body, and cut them into rings.
Bring water to a boil for the spaghetti, adding salt in the proportion of 1.10.100. Once the water is boiling, add the pasta and cook for the time indicated on the package.
Heat the olive oil in a pan, add the garlic, and sauté all the seafood for 2-3 minutes over high heat. Remove most of the seafood from the pan for presentation onto a separate plate.
Add sliced chili pepper, parsley, and cherry tomatoes. Sauté them for 2-3 minutes. Then pour in the wine and let it evaporate. Remove the tomatoes from the pan for presentation.
Add the cuttlefish ink and mix the sauce well until it is a uniform black color.
If using cream, pour it in and mix everything well.
Drain the cooked spaghetti and add it to the pan with the black sauce. If using roe, add it as well. Mix them well and immediately serve on plates, adding the reserved seafood and tomatoes.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Fry the toast or muffin cut in half in butter over medium heat.
Place them on serving plates.
Spread the toast (or muffin halves) with cream cheese. You can try using ricotta instead of cheese.
Melt the butter over low heat and remove the white foam from the surface.
Separate 2 yolks into a bowl, add lemon juice and water.
Place the bowl over a water bath (60 degrees C) and gradually whisk until the mixture has nearly doubled in volume.
Gradually add the hot melted butter while whisking (or using a mixer).
Add salt, nutmeg, chili pepper, and mustard powder if using.
Whisk until creamy.
Crack the eggs without damaging the yolk and place each egg in a separate ramekin*.
In a deep skillet (or pot), bring water to a rolling boil.
Turn off the heat and wait for the bubbles to stop rising from the bottom, and the surface of the water to be completely calm.
Very carefully add the eggs from the ramekins into the water, and after 3 minutes, remove the eggs with a slotted spoon and place them on the toast.**
Drizzle with hollandaise sauce and sprinkle with paprika. Add finely chopped green onion, caviar if desired, and eat immediately!
Cook the spaghetti according to the time indicated on the package.
Pat the scallops dry with a paper towel.
Heat olive oil in a pan over high heat.
Sear the scallops on both sides until golden brown.
Set the scallops aside.
Reduce the heat to medium, and add garlic and parsley to the pan.
After about 1 minute, pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely.
Add parsley and cream.
Simmer until thickened.
Turn off the heat and add freshly squeezed lemon juice to the sauce. Stir.
Pour the sauce onto a serving plate, top with spaghetti, and add the scallops.
Garnish with herbs.

recipes.title: Fiddlehead Fern Noodles in Sour-Spicy Sauce

instructions.text: Boil the noodles in boiling water until soft (about 8 minutes)
Cool the noodles in cold water.
Slice the peppers into rings, chop the garlic and herbs.
Mix all the ingredients in a bowl, add to the noodles and mix well.
Grind all the spices for the marinade in a mortar. Mix with yogurt and marinate the chicken in the marinade, completely covering it.
Refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Remove the chicken from the marinade and grill for 15-20 minutes or in a pan with oil, so that the marinade 'charred a little' on all sides. Set aside.
Melt the ghee, and sauté cumin, coriander seeds, and cardamom for 2 minutes, then add the onion and cook for 2 minutes, then add minced ginger, garlic, and salt.

Add paprika, cloves, chili powder, garam masala, and fenugreek seeds, mix well, and add the tomato paste. Stir, and after about 40 seconds add the blanched tomatoes, and simmer for another 2-3 minutes.
Pour in 1/2 cup of water. Stir and reduce the heat to low. Simmer for about 20 minutes. The sauce should thicken during this time.
Add the chicken pieces, sour cream, generously drizzle with lemon juice, mix, and cover. Cook for another 10 minutes.
When serving, sprinkle with cilantro. Serve with rice.

Add the dried chili peppers to a large heavy-bottomed skillet or pot and cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the peppers darken and an intense roasted aroma develops, about 2 to 5 minutes. The peppers should not smoke at all.
Remove the chilies to a small bowl and set aside.
Bring 1 liter of broth to a gentle simmer, and add the roasted peppers to it.
Simmer for 5 minutes. Then, blend the broth with the peppers until smooth.

Season the chuck roast generously with salt and allspice. Heat the oil in a Dutch oven (or pot) over high heat until it starts to smoke. Add the whole piece of meat in a single layer and cook, without moving it, until browned, about 6 minutes. Flip the meat and do the same on the other side, cooking for another 3-4 minutes. Transfer the meat to a cutting board. Once it cools slightly, cut it into pieces of 2 to 5 cm.

In the same pot, sauté the onion until translucent and softened, about 2 minutes. Add the garlic, cinnamon stick, cumin, allspice, oregano, and cook, stirring constantly until fragrant, about 1 minute.
Add all the chopped meat back to the pot along with the chili puree and the remaining liter of chicken broth. Stir well.
Bring to a boil over high heat, cover with a lid, leaving it slightly ajar, reduce the heat to low, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, stirring occasionally, until the meat is very tender.
Add fish sauce, corn flour, and vinegar if using.
Add beans and chocolate if using. Season to taste with salt.
Serve garnished with cilantro, chopped onion, green onion, shredded cheese, avocado, and tortillas if desired.
For best results, let the dish rest for at least 1 night in the refrigerator.
Reheat the next day, and serve garnished with cilantro, chopped onion, green onion, shredded cheese, avocado, and tortillas if desired.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok, add cumin, massaman curry paste and sauté over high heat.
Then add the top layer of coconut milk (cream) and stir until smooth.

Add the meat cut into 2x2 cm pieces, stir to coat the meat with the sauce. Pour in the remaining coconut milk, add sugar, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, star anise, and fish sauce. Simmer over medium heat for 1 hour.*
Add the roughly chopped potatoes, peanuts, and whole shallots, stir, bring to a boil, and reduce heat to minimum. Cook for another 20–30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Lightly Salted Salmon or Trout by Dry Method

instructions.text: Mix salt with sugar and pepper.
In the container where the fish will be salted, pour 1/3 of the mixture and place the fillet skin-side down.
Pour the remaining mixture over the fillet and distribute it evenly over the entire fillet.
Cover with a lid or plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator.
Keep the fish in the refrigerator for 1-2 days depending on its size and the desired level of saltiness; if a lightly salted fish is needed, keep it for a shorter time, if more salted, then longer.
Every 6-12 hours, the fish should be turned over so that the piece that was on top becomes the bottom. The more often it is turned, the more evenly salted the fish becomes.
The next day, take the fish out, rinse off all the salt with cold water, lightly coat with olive oil, and wrap in plastic wrap.
Store in the refrigerator for no more than a week.
Soak the dried chili peppers in water for 30 minutes.

Roast the garlic and shallots together with their skins. In Thailand, they are roasted in hot coals. Roast until the skin is charred and the flesh becomes soft. This should take about 5-10 minutes depending on your roasting method. Once the garlic and shallots have cooled, peel off the skins.
Cut or tear the chilies into large pieces.
Slice the galangal and lemongrass (green part closer to the root) into thin slices.
In a pan, roast the chilies and lemongrass until slightly brown. This should take about 2-3 minutes. Remove from the pan.
Add the remaining spices, except for the garlic and shallots, and toast them, stirring in the pan. Toast until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Remove the spices from heat.

In a mortar, first crush the salt with the chilies. When your chilies are roughly crushed, add the lemongrass. Grind, then add all the other spices except the roasted garlic and shallots. Grind until the mixture is medium-fine, then either continue grinding in the mortar, adding garlic, shallots, and shrimp paste to form a paste, or transfer to a blender and blend to a paste consistency.
Store the curry paste in the refrigerator for up to a month and in the freezer for a year.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the curry paste and cook for about 2 minutes.
Add chicken broth or water and stir until the paste is fully dissolved. Simmer quickly for 3 minutes or until the liquid reduces by half.
Add coconut milk, lime leaves, sugar, and fish sauce. Stir, then add the beef.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium. Cook on low for about 1 hour or until the sauce reduces and the beef is cooked.
Balance the taste by adding more fish sauce or sugar.
After 40 minutes, add the green beans and chopped vegetables, stir.
Remove from heat. Add a handful of Thai basil leaves.
Serve with rice, garnished with fresh slices of red chili pepper and fresh cilantro leaves.

ingredients.name: Arborio, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano rice

instructions.text: Crush the saffron threads with your fingers and place them in a coffee cup with 2 ice cubes and let steep for at least 1 hour.
In a high-sided skillet, add 30 g of butter and sauté the finely chopped onion and bone marrow.
Sauté for 1-2 minutes.
Then add the rice (do not wash it) and stir with a wooden spatula for a couple of minutes. When it absorbs all the butter and darkens slightly, pour in the wine.
After a minute, it will evaporate, and then add hot broth in portions – 2 ladles at once and another 2 when the first portion evaporates. The main principle of cooking is to constantly stir the rice.
After 10 minutes, pour the saffron-infused water into the skillet and mix thoroughly.
When the rice is ready (after 17 minutes of cooking), it should be al dente; turn off the heat, add the remaining piece of cold butter and grated cheese.
Stir and let the risotto 'rest' for 1-2 minutes.
Serve with Gremolata and fried bone marrow.

recipes.title: Mussels with Spicy Sausage and Orzo

instructions.text: Pour Pernod into a large deep skillet with a lid and bring to a boil. Toss in the mussels, cover with a lid, and cook for 5 minutes or until the mussels open. Drain the liquid into a separate container. Remove the mussels.
Heat the olive oil in the same pot, add the onion and garlic, and sauté until soft. Add the fennel seeds and chopped spicy sausage, cook for 5 minutes or until everything turns dark red.
Add the orzo and chopped tomatoes, and mix well. Pour back in 1 cup of the mussel liquid.
Cook, stirring, until all the liquid is absorbed, then add the next portion of liquid.
Once the orzo is almost cooked (2/3 of the cooking time indicated on the package), add the mussels, cover with a lid, and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
Clean the mussels. Discard any mussels that do not close during cleaning. If tapping on the shell does not cause the mussel to close, it means it is dead.
STEP 2
Heat some oil in a large pot, add the green onions and sauté for a minute, then add the torn kaffir lime leaves and red curry paste and cook for a minute.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a boil, cook for 2-3 minutes, then pour the mussels into the pot and cover with a lid.
Cook for another 3-5 minutes, shaking the pot to help the mussels open. Once they are open, add the fish sauce, lime juice, chili pepper, and basil and shake them again.
Serve in deep bowls with a small amount of steamed rice, and once you have eaten the mussels, pour the remaining sauce over the rice.

recipes.title: Mussels with Orzo, Saffron, and Tomatoes

instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a large, wide, shallow pan with a lid. Add the onion, celery, and garlic and sauté until soft.

Pour in the wine, bring to a boil and simmer for 1 minute, then add the stock and saffron. Bring everything to a boil, stirring, then add the tomatoes, orzo, and cook for another 5 minutes until the pasta is cooked about two-thirds of the way.
Add the mussels, cover with a lid, and cook for 5 minutes, shaking the pan occasionally until the mussels open.
Add the sour cream and most of the dill. No need to add salt - the mussels will bring their own saltiness.
Serve with the remaining dill.
Pour olive oil into a pan, and sauté the garlic and finely chopped capers until the characteristic garlic aroma appears.
Add the anchovies, cleaned of salt and bones, and chopped. Cook on high heat for about 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the chili flakes, and mix.
Then, add the blanched cherry tomatoes with tomato puree, and after 1-2 minutes add the chopped olives and dried oregano.
Just before turning off, sprinkle with finely chopped parsley.
Add the cooked pasta, mix and serve immediately.
Place the berries and deseeded peppers in a pot with a small amount of water and lemon juice. Cook over low heat until they become soft, which will take about 40 minutes.
Cut the apples and cook them in a separate pot with a small amount of water until they become soft.
Pass the pulp through a sieve to remove the skin pieces and set aside. Once the berries have softened, add the apple mass.
Add sugar, stir, and turn the heat to maximum. It should bubble well!
After about fifteen minutes, the mixture should thicken, add pectin or gelatin (although there is enough in the apples) and pour into sterilized jars.
Store for up to 1 year.
Add all the ingredients to a food processor and blend until smooth.
Pour the sauce into a small saucepan and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Let it cool slightly and pour into sterilized containers. If you want a milder sauce, use peppers without seeds.
Mix all ingredients except for tarragon, and simmer for 1 hour over low heat.
Then add tarragon and turn off the heat.
Once cooled, puree with a blender until smooth.
Pour into a sterilized container.

Place all ingredients in the work bowl of a food processor fitted with a steel blade. Puree until the parsley is finely chopped, about 30-60 seconds, stopping to push down any unprocessed large pieces of ingredients from the sides of the bowl as needed.
Season the sauce with salt and pepper to taste. Transfer to a small bowl and use immediately.

recipes.title: Latin American Version of Eggs Benedict (Huevos Benedictos)

instructions.text: In a medium-sized pot, add the tomatillos, garlic clove, 1/3 of the onion, and chili pepper. Add enough water to cover it and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce the heat and simmer for 6-7 minutes.

Drain the water from the tomatillos and other ingredients and place them in a food processor with raw onion, fresh cilantro, and ½ teaspoon of salt. Puree for 10 seconds, being careful not to overdo it to avoid frothy salsa.
The sauce can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to three days.
You can see how to make guacamole here by following the link: https://foodies.academy/recipe/guakamole
Add sour cream and mix.
In a deep skillet, bring water to a boil, then reduce the heat to the minimum.
Once the bubbles stop rising from the bottom of the skillet, gently pour in the eggs, which have been previously cracked while keeping the yolk whole in individual cups or coffee mugs.
The eggs will be ready in 4 minutes.
Fry the toast or muffins in butter over medium heat.
Spread a layer of guacamole, top with poached eggs, and drizzle with 'green sauce'.
Sprinkle ground chili pepper on top.

Place the cheeks in a large bowl. Add the wine, celery, carrot, onion, orange, bouquet garni, anise, and black pepper. Mix, ensuring the meat is covered with wine. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 8 hours, preferably overnight.
Remove the veal cheeks from the marinade, dry them with a paper towel, and set aside. Pour the marinade and all its contents into a small bowl, setting the bouquet garni aside.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat. Add the veal cheeks and sear for 2-3 minutes on each side. Set aside.
Immediately add the marinade contents (without the liquid) and cook until softened and caramelized.
Return the cheeks to the pot. Add the marinade liquid and bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium and simmer for 10 minutes, or until the liquid is reduced by half.
Add the bouquet garni and beef broth; add salt and pepper to taste. Bring to a boil again, then reduce heat to low and cover the pot. Simmer on low for 2 hours or until the cheeks are very tender.
Remove the veal cheeks from the pot. Pour the liquid from the pot into a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until the liquid is reduced by half, about 15 minutes.
Remove visible fat from the surface and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Add the cheeks back to the pot and warm them up. Add the butter and mix well with the sauce.
Start boiling the potatoes.
While they are cooking, separately boil the green peas in salted water for 3 minutes, then cool them in ice water to preserve their color.
Wash the mint leaves. Drain the water from the peas. Blend with the mint. Add to the purée and mix.
Serve the cheeks with the purée, drizzled with sauce on top.
Place the leftover roasted duck carcass in a large pot of water. Bring to a boil. Alternatively, use ready-made chicken broth instead of water.
Add onion, ginger, garlic, and star anise.
Turn on medium heat, cover with a lid, and simmer for at least 2 hours, preferably 4 hours. Skim off excess fat and stir occasionally.
Strain the broth to remove all solid particles. Separate the duck meat from the bones. Return the liquid to the pot and season with soy sauce. Let simmer for another 20-30 minutes.
Place the cooked noodles in serving bowls, add a leaf of bok choy, and chunks of roasted duck meat. Place a boiled chicken egg cut in half.
Evenly distribute the duck broth over each serving bowl. Garnish with green onion and drizzle a little chili oil on top. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Cocktail Sauce for Vegetable and Salad Burgers

instructions.text: Finely chop the lettuce, shallot, gherkins, and sun-dried tomatoes.
Mix all the ingredients together.
Use the sauce for burgers or shrimp.

Form a patty from the ground veal and fat in a 70/30 ratio. This will keep the burger juicy. Add ground pepper. We will salt it during cooking. Place the formed patties in the refrigerator for 20 minutes so that the fat binds with the meat and the patty doesn't fall apart while frying.

Fry the pancetta (bacon) on a grill or in a pan. If frying in a pan, use this fat to toast the brioche halves until golden brown. If on a grill, brush the inside of the brioche halves with oil and lightly toast.
Fry the patty on the highest heat on all sides for 2-3 minutes.
Salt, pepper, and brush mustard on each side of the patty while frying.
The hamburger, like a steak, can have different levels of doneness.
Grill or fry the onion rings and tomato slices until cooked.
When the patty is almost done, cover it with a slice of cheese, place the pancetta on top, and cover with a lid (or a deep plate, foil, etc., to help the cheese melt).
Chop and mix all the sauce ingredients. Salt to taste.
Spread cocktail sauce on the bottom bun.
Top with the patty and cheese, tomato, then a leaf of lettuce, followed by an onion ring.
Finally, add the cornichons, generously spread with sauce, close it up, and enjoy!
Soak the brains in cold water, add a little salt and refrigerate for 6-8 hours. If you are short on time, at least for 30 minutes.
Afterward, drain the water and remove any visible clots of blood from the brains, and peel off the visible membrane without damaging them.
Submerge the brains in boiling water in a pot. Add vinegar, and boil over medium heat until they become firm to the touch. From 5 to 15 minutes, depending on the size.
Rinse them well under cold running water. If possible, remove the remaining membrane and cut the brains into portion-sized pieces.
Place all the ingredients for breading in a blender bowl and mix well. Alternatively, you can just mix everything in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, beat the eggs until smooth, mix the flour with the starch separately, and place the breading in another container.
In a deep skillet, heat a large amount of vegetable oil to 180°C (350°F). You can easily check the oil by dipping a wooden spatula. When it is heated, bubbles should appear on the spatula.
Coat the pieces of calf brains in flour, then in egg, and finally in the cheese breading. Place in the skillet with hot oil. You can fry in batches if everything doesn't fit at once.
Fry until the brains are well browned. Place on a paper towel to remove excess oil.
Serve immediately with a wedge of lemon. Pairs well with tartar sauce.

recipes.title: Breaded Veal Rack with Sweet Paprika and Pumpkin Puree

instructions.text: Remove all fresh herbs from their stems and chop finely. Do not discard the herb stems.
Heat some olive oil in a skillet. Sear the meat on all sides, holding each side in the oil until a nice crust forms.
Place the rack on a baking sheet and roast in the oven for 30 minutes at 200 degrees.
While the meat is cooking, prepare the breading.
Chop all the ingredients for the breading, except for the mustard, paprika flakes, and chili, in a blender and blend several times until the mixture is homogeneous.
Transfer the mixture to a deep dish, add paprika and chili flakes. Drizzle literally 1/2 tsp. of olive oil, mix, and set aside.
