Remove the rack from the oven and generously coat it with mustard. Dip the meat into the breading mixture, completely covering it. Dip several times to ensure even coverage. Let the veal rest for about 5 minutes.
Put it back in the oven for 3-4 minutes when you are ready to serve.
Serve with a side of puree or vegetables.

recipes.title: Spring Rolls with Salmon and Spinach

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Sprinkle pieces of salmon with salt and pepper on both sides, then fry them in the pan until cooked, about 2–3 minutes on each side, depending on thickness. Remove from heat to let cool.
You can use either fresh salmon or lightly salted salmon. It's up to your preference.
Cut the salmon into small pieces.
Mix cream cheese with lemon juice and garlic.
Prepare the dipping sauce by mixing all the ingredients and slightly heating it to dissolve the sugar.

Prepare the ingredients for the spring rolls by cutting a slice of cucumber in half, then slicing each half into 6 cm sticks. Cut the carrot into thin strips. Cut the green onion into pieces about 13 cm long, slicing the thicker white parts in half lengthwise.
Dip the rice paper in water for 5-10 seconds, then shake off the excess water.

Roll it up, starting from the edge closest to you and using your fingers to tuck the salad in as you roll. Once you have rolled it around the filling once, fold in both side edges and continue rolling, tucking the edges as you go. The wrapper sticks to itself, holding the filling tightly.

ingredients.name: Fillet of sea fish
ingredients.notes: Sea bass, dorade, tilapia, cod, wolf fish, shark, monkfish, kingclip or salmon.

instructions.text: Cut the carrot, celery, and parsley root into small cubes. Cut part of the carrot into strips and set aside.
Cut the fish into pieces.
Melt the butter, add the flour and pour in the fish broth, stirring the soup until smooth.
Add the chopped vegetables and let it simmer for 15 minutes on low heat.
Squeeze the lemon juice and mix with curry, cayenne pepper, egg yolk, and cream, then add to the soup.
Add the fish, carrot strips and let the soup cook until the fish is done, about 5 minutes. Season with salt.
Garnish the soup with green onions (or parsley, dill) and serve with bread on the side.

In a pot, add the fish soup set, water, shallot onion, cilantro roots, garlic, tops of lemongrass, and daikon. Break a few chili peppers to release the seeds; the more you break, the spicier the soup will be, and add them to the pot. Simmer for 45 minutes, skimming off the foam that forms on the surface.
After 30-40 minutes, add the lower part of the lemongrass, galangal, torn kaffir lime leaves, and continue simmering for the remaining time.

Once the broth is ready, remove everything by straining through a sieve. These roots, leaves, and stalks are not meant to be eaten; they are used only to flavor the soup, so make sure to tell your guests not to eat them or it's better to remove them from the soup altogether. You can leave the shallot onion, garlic, and chili pepper in the soup, but it's not necessary.

At this point, you should have about 800 ml of fish broth. If you cook it longer than 45 minutes and it reduces too much, you can add water. If you have too much, don't worry, just add more seasonings.

Add fish sauce, sugar, mushrooms, tomatoes, and then the fish meat to the broth. Cook until the fish is fully cooked; 1-2 minutes depending on the size of the fish. When the fish is fully cooked, add lime juice, then taste and salt as needed.
Garnish with chopped cilantro leaves and serve!
The ideal dish is made from tenderloin, but it can also be prepared from the fillet part of beef, thin and thick edges, trimmings, or sirloin. Other parts of the carcass are not suitable.

Cut the meat into strips 0.5 cm thick and 1 cm wide across the grain, season with pepper and salt, and let marinate for some time from 30 minutes to 2 hours. If you purchased a cut other than tenderloin, slice the meat into 0.5 cm thick slices, pound them, and then cut into strips. Optionally, you can also dredge the pieces of meat in flour.
In a skillet, melt the butter, add 1 sifted tablespoon of flour, stir and lightly fry.
Then dilute with broth, add mustard, a bit of pepper, stir and cook on low heat until the sauce reduces.

Add sour cream and mix. Optionally, you can add tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce. This is where the French notes of the dish come into play. The aforementioned base sauce is nothing other than one of the French mother sauces, Velouté, and the addition of mustard, sour cream, and tomato paste comes from the derivatives of the Velouté sauces: À la Polonaise (sour cream), Ravigote (mustard), and Aurora (tomato paste).
Now sauté the onion, sliced into half-rings, in butter (you can also use vegetable oil) until golden.
Place the meat pieces in a single layer on top of the onion, and fry on high heat for just 2-3 minutes without turning. Then fry the meat on the other side.
Add the meat to the sauce, season with pepper, and salt if needed.
As soon as the sauce starts to boil, stir, and turn off the heat.
If you are cooking from the fillet part or sirloin, bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for 20-30 minutes or until the meat is tender.
Transfer to a plate and garnish with herbs or vegetables. It pairs excellently with fried potato wedges or mashed potatoes.
Pickled cucumber also goes very well with the dish.

recipes.title: Spaghetti with Cuttlefish Ink, Clams, and Cherry Tomatoes

instructions.text: Peel a large clove of garlic and cut it in half lengthwise.
Chop the chili pepper, removing the seeds.
Heat olive oil in a pan.
Add garlic and chili to the hot oil. Sauté until golden.
Add well-washed clams to the pan. The shells should be tightly closed. Discard any open shells!!!!
Sauté for a minute, shaking the pan.
Remove the garlic. Add a ladle of boiling water.
Simmer for about one and a half to two minutes on high heat until all the shells are open.
Set aside.
Add the blanched cherry tomatoes, halved (5 pieces per serving), and finely chopped parsley.
Place back on the heat. Add a little boiling water.
Let it come to a boil for half a minute.
DO NOT SALT!
Cook spaghetti al dente in salted water.
Add to the clams and gently mix.
Serve on plates....
Attention! Discard any unopened shells!!!!
Sprinkle with freshly ground black pepper just before serving.
Peel the onion, cut it in half, and slice it into 0.5 cm wide wedges.
Melt the butter over medium heat and add the onion to the pan.
Sauté the onion, stirring occasionally, until it starts to caramelize, acquiring a golden crust. The caramelization process will take 30 - 50 minutes.
Add 1 clove of finely chopped garlic and cook for another minute.
Sprinkle with flour, nutmeg and mix well
Add the wine, cognac and reduce the liquid.
Now add the broth, place the bouquet garni, tying it with kitchen twine,* bring to a boil, and cook over medium heat for about 30 minutes until the soup reduces by half.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
While the soup is cooking, preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Slice the baguette into 1 cm thick slices and toast them in the oven until golden brown, and rub the croutons with the remaining garlic.

Remove the bouquet garni, pour the ready soup into serving bowls, place the croutons on top and generously sprinkle with cheese. Put in the oven and bake until the cheese is completely melted. Serve immediately.

ingredients.name: Arborio rice, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano

instructions.text: Freeze the fresh octopus, having previously cleaned its insides.
In a large pot, pour 500 ml of water and 250 ml of dry red wine.
Bring to almost boiling. Dip the thawed octopus into this liquid for 1 minute.

Remove, let the liquid drip back into the pot, and place on a board for 1 minute. Repeat the process 2 more times. This is to prevent the octopus skin from coming off in shreds, which would look unappealing.
Then, cook the octopus for 1 hour or more over medium heat until it becomes tender and can be easily pierced with a toothpick. The water should be just 'simmering', not boiling.
Remove the octopus from the pot and let it cool.
Cut off the tentacles and slice the body into small pieces.
Heat olive oil in a pan and quickly fry the tentacles until golden.
Plate the risotto, place the tentacles on top, and apply saffron emulsion around the edges of the risotto. Serve immediately.
Step 1 – preparing the 'soffritto'. For this, melt the butter in a large skillet and sauté the finely chopped onion until soft. Increase the heat, add finely chopped garlic, and stir.
Step 2 - 'tostatura'. Add the rice, stirring it in circular motions with the oil in the skillet for about 30 seconds, then reduce the heat.
Pour in the squid ink with the rice along with the wine. Increase the heat and stir until the liquid evaporates.
Make the heat medium and pour a ladle of octopus broth into the rice, stirring constantly. When the broth evaporates, add another ladle and continue until the rice is cooked.
The time from when the rice is added until it’s ready is exactly 17 minutes. Remove the skillet from the heat and let it rest for exactly 1 minute.
The final step - 'mantecatura'.

Add cold, diced butter and grated cheese to the risotto, and quickly stir the mixture until fully homogeneous. However, in Italy, cheese is not always added, especially if the risotto is made with seafood.
Crush the saffron with sugar, and add vinegar and ice.
Let it sit for 1 hour for the saffron emulsion.
Once the ice has melted, add the saffron to a blender along with the egg yolk, mustard, and salt, slowly pouring in the oil until the mixture thickens and emulsifies.

recipes.title: Confit Salmon with Caviar and Shrimp Sauce

instructions.text: Heat the olive oil in a container in the oven to a temperature of 65 degrees C.
Place the fish in the container with olive oil, ensuring it is completely covered. Add coriander, pepper, basil, thyme, and garlic.
Put the container with the fish back in the oven at the same temperature of 65 degrees for 10 minutes.
Remove the fish and carefully remove the skin and cut into portion-sized pieces.
Mix the roe in a bowl with the cuttlefish ink.
Place the fish on top of the sauce, and evenly spread a layer of roe.
Garnish with finely chopped herbs.
In a small saucepan, melt the butter over low heat.
Add the cream, roe, and shrimp paste.
Mix everything well.
Pour vegetable oil into a frying pan and sauté the garlic over medium heat. Add the shallots and sauté everything together for 2 minutes.
Add the curry paste and sauté until the characteristic aroma appears.
Cut the squid into large pieces and place them in the pan. Sauté for 30 seconds on each side.
Pour in the water or broth, bring to a boil, and add the green bean pods.
Pour in the coconut cream, stir, bring to a boil, covering with a lid for 3 minutes.
Serve with rice or vegetables.
Slice the potatoes into 2 mm thick rounds.
Melt the duck fat over medium heat.
Sauté the garlic until fragrant. Remove it.
Sauté the shallots until soft.
Add the sliced potatoes, thyme, and cover with a lid.
Simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes without stirring.
Stir the potatoes with a wooden spatula, flipping the bottom layer to the top. Season with salt and freshly ground pepper.
Cover with a lid and simmer for the next 10 minutes.
Repeat the previous procedure once more.
The potatoes should turn golden with a crispy crust.
Serve as a side dish to any main course.

recipes.title: Paccheri Stuffed with Mushrooms and Spinach

instructions.text: Sauté garlic in olive oil until fragrant over medium heat.
Add finely chopped onion and sauté until golden.
Add finely chopped spinach and sauté until excess moisture evaporates.
Allow to cool. Mix with the mushroom duxelles paste.
Boil the paccheri in salted water for half the time indicated on the package.
Drain the water and place in a pot of cold water, adding a bit of olive oil to prevent the pasta from sticking.
Line a baking dish with foil or parchment paper, pour Béchamel sauce at the bottom.

Place the paccheri vertically and stuff each with the spinach and duxelles mixture. For convenience, use a serving knife to remove the pasta from the cold water, inserting the handle of a teaspoon inside the paccheri, and transfer to the dish. It's also convenient to stuff them with a knife and spoon without touching with hands.
Pour Béchamel on top, sprinkle with Parmesan, and place in a preheated oven at 180 degrees. Bake for 30 minutes.
Chop the shallot, garlic, and sauté over medium heat for 2-3 minutes.
Add very finely chopped mushrooms, stir, and simmer on high heat for 15 minutes to evaporate moisture. Splash in the brandy during the process.
Reduce heat to medium and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Melt butter with vegetable oil in a saucepan and mix in the flour. Gradually pour in the milk, stirring well, and bring to a boil while constantly stirring.
Add salt and simmer on low heat, stirring, for 8-10 minutes. If a thinner sauce is needed, add more milk; if not, cook longer until it reaches the desired consistency.

recipes.title: Ramp Steak Biker'S. A Manly Steak with the Most Intense Aroma and Flavor

instructions.text: Place the steak on a board and let it rest for 15 minutes to bring it to room temperature.
Mix the oil, chopped rosemary, juice, pepper, and lemon zest to create a thick paste.
Rub the steak with the mixture and let it marinate for at least 40 minutes.
Heat a skillet well with olive oil and start frying the steaks for 4-5 minutes on each side.
Do not move the steaks around in the skillet while cooking. Add the vinegar one minute before finishing.
Place the steaks on a board and let them rest.
Serve with mustard sauce.
Sauté the onion in vegetable oil.
Add cream and mustard, and mix.
Reduce until thickened for about 5 minutes.
Put 10 - 15 g of butter in a large pot and sauté the onion over medium heat until soft.
Add flour, mix and cook over low heat for 4 minutes without browning.
Add the broth, fully mixing it with the flour.
Add parsley, bay leaf, and thyme and cook for 20 minutes. Strain into a second pot.
Meanwhile, in a large skillet, melt the remaining butter over medium heat.
Add the sliced mushrooms and whole chanterelles. Sauté until softened.
Season with salt and lemon juice and cook until the mushrooms are dark golden brown, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Select and set aside beautiful chanterelles (they will be needed for serving).
Add the remaining mushrooms to the pot with the broth and cook for 5-7 minutes.
Add the cream and bring to a boil.
Blend with a blender until smooth.
Pour into bowls, top with chanterelles.
Sprinkle with parsley, grated Parmesan, and ground pepper.

recipes.title: Marinated Green Mushrooms in Garlic (Author'S Recipe)

instructions.text: Remove the skin from the mushroom caps, rinse, and soak for 1 hour in cold water to remove sand.
Boil the mushrooms for 5 minutes in boiling water. Drain the water and let cool.
Crush the garlic, finely chop the parsley and green onion.
Add salt, olive oil. Mix everything with the mushrooms, cover with plastic wrap, and place in the refrigerator for 2 days.
Serve with mashed potatoes or as a snack.

recipes.title: Pepper Ribeye Steak with Pepper Sauce

instructions.text: Bring the steak to room temperature.
Brush the steaks with olive oil.
Coat the sides of the steaks with coarsely ground pepper.
Preheat the grill or pan. Place the steaks and sear for 90 seconds on each side.
Reduce the heat to medium, add butter, thyme, and garlic.
Distribute the liquid evenly around the steaks. For medium rare, cook for 3 minutes on each side.
Salt, periodically basting with the liquid in the pan.
Wrap the steaks in foil, let them 'rest' for 5 minutes. Serve with warm pepper sauce, potatoes, or grilled vegetables.
Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the finely chopped onion until soft.
Chop the pepper and sprinkle it over the onion, mix. The amount of pepper depends on how spicy you want the seasoning to be.
Pour cognac over the onion and pepper. Ignite the alcohol and let it burn off while continuing to sauté the onion.
Be careful, as the flame can be quite strong.
Add the cream, stir.
Keep the sauce on low heat until some of the cream evaporates and it thickens enough. During this time, stir the sauce occasionally to prevent the onion from burning.
Season the sauce with salt, mix, and remove from heat after 2 minutes.
The sauce for the steak should be served chilled, so it's better to prepare it in advance. If you didn't have time to cool it – no problem, it will also be delicious hot.
Shape the central part of the tenderloin into a cylinder by wrapping it in plastic wrap, and let it rest overnight in the refrigerator.
Remove the wrap, sear the beef fillet in a hot skillet with 1 tsp of olive oil for 60 seconds on each side.
Remove from the skillet and let cool.
Spread English mustard (or Dijon) evenly in a thin layer over the meat.
Chop the mushrooms in a blender and sauté in a hot skillet with olive oil, thyme leaves, and spices.

When the mushrooms start releasing moisture, add the truffle sauce, and continue cooking over high heat for 10 minutes, until all excess moisture evaporates and a mushroom paste known as duxelle is formed.
Remove the paste from the skillet. Let it cool.
Place a large sheet of plastic wrap on a working surface and arrange 6 slices of Parma ham in the center, forming a square.
Spread the duxelle evenly over the ham. Place the fillet on top of the mushroom duxelle.
Using the plastic wrap, tightly wrap the fillet in the ham, then tie the wrap to form a uniformly thick cylinder. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Lay the pastry on the wrap, lightly dusted with flour, and roll it out into a rectangle large enough to wrap around the beef fillet.
Using a brush, evenly apply the beaten egg yolk mixed with water and a pinch of salt onto the pastry.
Remove the plastic wrap, and wrap the pastry around the ham-wrapped fillet. Tightly wrap in plastic and chill for 30 minutes.
Afterwards, remove the wrap, place the roll on a baking sheet, brush the roll completely with beaten egg yolk, and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25-30 minutes, until the roll is golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let cool for 10 minutes.
Serve the Beef Wellington sliced and drizzled with heated sauce.
Heat the oil in a large pot, sauté the beef trimmings on all sides for a few minutes until browned.
Add the shallot, pepper, bay leaf, thyme, stir and continue to cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until the shallot is golden brown.
Pour in the vinegar and let it evaporate almost completely.
Add the wine and boil until almost completely evaporated.
Add the broth and bring back to a boil. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 1 hour, skimming the surface of the sauce, until the desired consistency is reached.
According to taste preferences, sugar can be added.
Strain the liquid through a cheesecloth lined sieve.

recipes.title: Blackstone Eggs. A Variation of Benedict

instructions.text: Pour a small amount of water into a deep skillet and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to minimum. Wait until the bubbles stop rising from the bottom.
Take the freshest eggs. Crack them and pour without breaking the yolk into individual ramekins or cups.
Carefully pour the egg into hot water (the water should be 80 degrees) and cook for 4 minutes.
Cut the muffin in half and toast it in a dry skillet until golden brown.
Place a lettuce leaf on the muffin, add the ham, spread with cream cheese, and top with poached eggs. Drizzle with the prepared sauce.
Melt a large piece in a small saucepan over low heat.
Pour the yolks into a blender immersion cup, immerse the blender, and whip the yolks for about 15 seconds without lifting the blender from the bottom.

Then, gradually pour in the hot melted butter in a thin stream, gradually raising and lowering the blender. Add the lemon juice, pepper, salt, nutmeg, and water. Continue whipping for another half a minute.
Whip for 2 minutes until the sauce becomes creamy.

ingredients.name: Clarified butter
ingredients.notes: or heavy cream to increase fat content

instructions.text: Fry the flour in a pan, mix with salt and sugar, add finely chopped butter.
Add a little hot freshly brewed tea and stir until a uniform dough is obtained.
Let the tsampa sit for a few minutes to swell, then add more tea to achieve the desired consistency.
Boil water, add the tea.
Pour in the milk and cream and bring to a boil.
Add salt and cook for 10-20 minutes.
Strain through cheesecloth, whip vigorously with a mixer. In Tibet, a special device is used for this purpose.

recipes.title: Romanian Beef Tripe Soup (ciorba de burta)

instructions.text: If the tripe is already a semi-finished product, pour 4 - 4.5 liters of water over the tripe and bones, bring to a boil, skim off the foam and cook for 15 minutes.
If the tripe is raw, first boil the tripe in boiling water for 15 minutes, drain the water, and repeat the process 3 times.
Then, cook for about 2 hours with the bones on low heat.
Add the vegetables whole and a little salt, and cook for another hour until the meat is ready.
When the meat is ready, remove the contents - the vegetables will no longer be needed, remove the meat from the bones, and cut the tripe into small strips.
Strain the broth and let it cool slightly.
Beat the yolks with the flour, sour cream, and lemon juice or vinegar (2-4 tablespoons), gradually pour in the broth (3-4 ladles), stirring until a homogeneous mass forms.
While stirring, slowly pour the entire mixture into the remaining broth.
Add the meat and tripe, and cook for another 10-15 minutes.
In a small amount of oil, sauté the finely chopped garlic until fragrant, then add the grated carrot and sauté.
Pour the resulting mixture into the soup for a nice top layer.
Salt to taste. Add herbs.
Serve with mujdei (garlic + water + vinegar), sour cream, and hot pepper.
Bring the meat to room temperature. Cut the tenderloin into steaks 5 cm long.
Do not marinate, season, or salt the meat.
Heat a (non-ribbed) skillet well.
Brush the steaks with oil. Roll the sides of the steak in freshly ground pepper. (You can wrap the mignons in bacon).
Place in the skillet and "seal" them on each side for 1 minute until a brown crust forms.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add butter, crushed garlic, and thyme to the skillet. Distribute the butter all over the skillet by tilting it in different directions.
Cook on each side for 4 minutes, basting the steaks with oil from the skillet.
Before serving, let the steaks rest for a couple of minutes on warm serving plates under a lid. Season with salt, drizzle with sauce.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan.
In another saucepan, pour in the vinegar, add the bay leaf and black peppercorns, and bring to a boil.
Whisk the yolks, adding a little water.
Pour in the melted butter, then the vinegar (after removing the pepper and bay leaf).
Add a handful of capers, salt. Whisk again until smooth.

recipes.title: Black Risotto with Cuttlefish and Shrimp

ingredients.name: Arborio, Carnaroli, or Vialone Nano Rice

instructions.text: Finely chop the shallot.
Peel the shrimp, keeping the tail and the last joint. Make a cut along the entire "back" of the shrimp, about 2mm deep, and remove the intestinal vein.
Slice the cuttlefish into thin strips about 2 cm long.
In a pan, heat olive oil over high heat, add crushed garlic.

Once the garlic aroma appears, remove the garlic and immediately add the shrimp, sautéing them, turning only once for 1 minute on each side. Remove them to a separate dish and sauté the sliced cuttlefish in the same pan for 1 minute. Set aside.
Melt 30 g of butter in a pot and sauté the shallot until soft.
Add the rice and stir well in the butter until the top of the grains becomes translucent. This will take about 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely.
Add 2 ladles of hot broth. Keep it warm during cooking. Reduce the heat to medium and cook, stirring every 10 seconds. Add salt to taste.
When the broth is almost evaporated, add 1 ladle of broth at a time, stirring and letting it evaporate, adding more broth as needed.
Risotto is a very delicate dish and can easily burn if not watched closely.
Add the 4th ladle of broth and immediately mix in the ink. Add the pieces of cuttlefish, except for those you want to use for garnish.
Usually, 5-7 ladles are enough for cooking (if a ladle is 100 ml). It all depends on the rice and the cooking temperature.

When the broth is absorbed (exactly 17 minutes should pass since the rice was sautéed), remove it from the heat, add the grated Parmesan and the remaining butter. Stir the risotto until the butter is completely melted, and let it sit for 1-2 minutes before serving.
Optionally, you can add parsley.
Serve on plates, garnishing with the reserved shrimp and cuttlefish on top.
Prepare broth from poultry and 3 liters of water for at least 2 hours, so that the volume of water reduces by approximately one third.
While the broth is cooking, chop the onion, beet, carrot, and parsley root. The cabbage in Poltava borscht is cut into cubes, not julienned like in other borschts. Cut the potato into cubes.
When the broth is ready, remove the meat and free it from the bones. Strain the broth. The meat can either be set aside until serving or returned to the broth.
Take two pans. In one, stew the beets, adding vinegar, as well as a teaspoon of sugar to preserve the color.
In the second pan, sauté the onion, carrot, and parsley root.
Add the tomato paste to the beets, heat well in the pan. Simmer on low heat, adding a little broth.
Bring the broth to a boil, add the potatoes, and bring to a boil again.
After 5 minutes, add the cabbage.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the sautéed onion, carrot, parsley, stewed beets, bring to a boil, then add the dumplings, and bring to a boil again.
Dumplings can also be served separately, drizzled with sour cream or melted butter.
Season with crushed garlic with onion fat, salt, pepper, and herbs.
Cover with a lid and let it steep for about twenty minutes.
Attention: garlic is not added to Poltava borscht.
Place the meat in prepared bowls. Then pour in the borscht with the addition of dumplings.
Dissolve a third of the flour in fifty grams of boiling water and let it cool.
Beat in the eggs and add the remaining flour. Knead until the consistency of a liquid dough.
Take the dough with a teaspoon, drop it into boiling salted water, and cook until the dumplings float (5-7 minutes).
Drain the dumplings in a colander.

Take a large, thick-walled pot, place it over medium heat, and melt the butter. Then sauté the finely chopped garlic, onion, and leek in it (you can add the celery stalk), stirring the vegetables occasionally so they don't burn.
When the vegetables soften, pour in the wine and bring it to a boil (if you are cooking with defrosted mussels, add the liquid that was released during thawing along with the wine).
When the contents of the pot come to a boil, add the mussels, cover the pot with a lid, and increase the heat.

After a minute, shake the pot, and after another minute, add the cream, stir the sauce, cook the mussels in the cream sauce for another 1-2 minutes, and remove the pot from the heat. Do not let the sauce boil after adding the cream, otherwise, it may curdle into unappetizing flakes.
Finally, add the finely chopped parsley, shake the pot again to mix the mussels with the cream sauce, and then serve them immediately.
Serve them with fresh baguette for dipping into the sauce.

ingredients.name: Pork
ingredients.notes: any meat or even fish can be used

ingredients.name: Millet
ingredients.notes: you can use rice, buckwheat, pearl barley, etc.

instructions.text: Cut the meat into pieces and boil until done for 1.5 hours.
Grate the celery and carrot, finely chop 2 onions. Sauté in a pan with butter until soft.
Drain the sauerkraut from the juice, finely chop and sauté for 15-20 minutes until done, adding broth from the pot with meat.
Finely chop the fat, mix with the remaining finely chopped onion, washed millet, and parsley. Mix and grind in a mortar.
When the meat is ready, add potatoes cut into small cubes and cook for about 15 minutes.
Add the sautéed cabbage, the fat mixture with millet and herbs, bay leaf, sautéed celery root with carrot, salt, and pepper. Cook for another 15-20 minutes until done.
Serve hot, adding sour cream to taste.

recipes.title: Classic Mignonette Sauce for Oysters (Mignonette sauce)

instructions.text: Mix the finely chopped shallot and pepper. Add powdered sugar if desired.
Pour in the vinegar and stir.
Serve with fresh oysters.
Cut the bones, rinse them and boil for an hour, strain the broth.
Wash the beets well, boil them in their skins (with added vinegar) until cooked. Then peel, cut into strips and sauté for a few minutes with tomato paste, adding a little broth if necessary.

Add diced potatoes to the boiling broth and bring to a boil. Add the prepared beets, sautéed and cut into strips carrots, parsley, and onions. Season with salt and pepper, add bay leaf, sugar, and cook for 15-20 minutes until ready.
In the nearly finished borscht, add lightly fried sausages cut into small pieces.
When serving, put sour cream in the bowl with borscht and sprinkle with finely chopped parsley.
Cut the lard into pieces or strips of the necessary size. No more than 4-5 cm in width and about 8-10 cm in length.
Make incisions and place half a clove of garlic into each.
Mix all the spices into a homogeneous mass with salt in a ratio of 3 cups of salt to 1 cup of spices and dried herbs.
For brining, use a glass container. Place a layer of 2-3 mm of the spice mixture with herbs on the bottom.
Thoroughly rub the lard with the salt and spice mixture on all sides. Ensure that the lard is completely covered with salt.
Place it in the prepared glass container on a layer of salt and spices, very tightly - skin to skin.
Pour the remaining salt and spices on top. Close the container and place it in a cold dark place or refrigerator for 3-4 days to allow it to salt well.
After the necessary time, take it out and scrape off the excess salt with a knife and paper.
It is categorically not recommended to store lard in salt, as it loses its taste qualities and ages quickly.
Rinse the meat and dry it with a towel.
Cut the meat and fat into small cubes.
Add salt, black and red pepper, marjoram, nutmeg, and cognac to the minced meat. Mix well. If the mixture is too dry, add 1/4 cup of water.
Cover the minced meat with plastic wrap and place it in the refrigerator for 5-6 hours to mature. It can also be left overnight.
Stuff the intestines with the minced meat, not too tightly. Tie them into small rings.
Pierce the sausage with a thin needle every 5-7 cm to allow air to escape during cooking.
Boil the sausage in salted water for 10-15 minutes. You can add a bay leaf.
Remove the sausage, let the water drain. Grease with oil and place on a baking sheet.
Place a tray of water at the bottom of the oven to prevent the sausage from drying out during baking.
Bake at 200 degrees for 25 minutes on one side.
Turn over, grease with the fat that has formed during cooking, and bake for another 25 minutes on the other side.
Allow to cool.
Store in the refrigerator in an enameled (glass, ceramic) container, covering it with melted lard.
Serve the sausage sliced into rings.
To clean the intestines, turn them inside out and soak them in water for 30 minutes, adding 1/2 tbsp of salt and 1/2 tbsp of soda.
Then, clean them well with the blunt side of a knife on a wooden board.
Rinse and soak in a weak solution of potassium permanganate for 5 minutes to remove the pink color from the intestines. Then rinse again and slightly salt.
Clean and rinse the intestines, soak them in lemon puree.
Remove the skin from the cheek, separate the fat from the meat.
Cut the fat and meat into cubes about 1 cm.
Render the fat over low heat for about 20 minutes. Add the meat 5 minutes before the end and fry until golden brown.
Cool the meat and separate a little fat for the sausage.
Pour boiling water over the buckwheat, add salt, and place in a preheated oven at 220 degrees under a lid for 20 minutes. Immediately turn off the oven.
Strain the blood through a sieve and pass any clots through a meat grinder.
Add milk to the blood. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the meat, cracklings with fat, and crushed garlic. Gradually add the buckwheat and mix well with your hands.
Stuff the intestines, filling them to 2/3 of their capacity.
Tie the ends of the intestines in a knot. Then tie with strong thread. Coil the sausage into a ring and connect it with thread.
Boil the blood sausage for 5 minutes in boiling water and place it on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, and pierce with a needle.
Bake for 30 minutes. Initial temperature 160°C (325°F). Increase the temperature by 10 C every 10 minutes.
After the first 10 minutes of baking, brush the blood sausage with melted fat.
Soak the legs in cold water for 4 hours.
Drain the water. Pour in new water and put it on the fire, bring to a boil, remove from heat and scrape the legs with a knife.
Cut the legs in half.
Soak the meat in cold water, cut into pieces, and rinse with warm water.
Roast the turkey wing and chicken thighs over the fire and clean them with a knife.
Place the meat in a five-liter pot, pour in water to cover it by 2 cm.
Add unpeeled onion, pepper, salt, 3 cloves of garlic, bay leaf. Put on the fire, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat to minimum so that it barely bubbles.
Remove the first foam with a slotted spoon. The cooking process will take about 4 hours. Salt to taste half an hour before finishing.
Remove the meat and squeeze 3 cloves of garlic. Let it cool and strain through one layer of cheesecloth.
Skim the fat from the surface of the broth with a ladle. It will be useful later for making sauces and soups.
Shred the meat into small pieces. Remove skins, tendons, and bones.
Evenly distribute the meat in deep plates. Pour over the broth and place in a cool place.
You can also sprinkle with pepper to taste on top. The plates must be covered to prevent the aspic from absorbing foreign odors.
Horseradish sauce is usually served with aspic.
Soak the beans in a large amount of clean cold water for 8-12 hours. After soaking, drain the water, add clean water to the beans, and boil until cooked. Usually, beans take about 1 hour to cook.
Drain the water from the cooked beans and let them cool.
Thoroughly wash the beets and boil them in their skins until cooked.
When the beets cool, peel them and cut into cubes of 1×1 centimeter.
Rinse the prunes, soak in clean cold water for 15 minutes. After 15 minutes, drain the water. Cut the prunes into small pieces.
Mix the cooled beans, beets, prunes, add sauerkraut, salt, and pepper. Dress with vegetable oil.
Rinse the pork meat in water and lightly dry it with a paper towel.
Cut the meat into thin slices and pound each one with a meat mallet on both sides.
Cut the cheese into long sticks the size of the pounded meat slices. Place a stick of cheese on a slice of meat.
Roll it up and wrap it with kitchen twine.
Stuff all the meat slices in the same way and roll them up.
Pour vegetable oil into a frying pan or saucepan and fry the rolls until golden brown on both sides for about 15 minutes.
While they are frying, grate the hard cheese on a fine grater.
Chop the washed herbs and mix them with the cheese.
Remove the twine from each roll, place them back in the dish, and sprinkle with cheese so that they are completely covered with it.
Place the saucepan in the oven and bake for about 15-25 minutes until a golden cheese crust forms.
Serve the dish hot, equipped with any side dish of your choice.
Rinse the pork fillet and dry it with a paper towel.
Peel the garlic, wash it, and roughly chop it. Stuff the meat with garlic. For this, make a cut in the meat with the tip of a knife and insert a slice of garlic.
Rub the piece of meat on all sides with vegetable oil, then with the prepared spice mix.
Tightly wrap in food foil or tie with kitchen twine and bake in a preheated oven for 1 hour at 180º.
Do not rush to cut the meat into pieces immediately after taking the baking tray out of the oven. Let it 'rest' a bit so that all the juices distribute evenly and soak the entire piece.
Peel the potatoes and onion and grate them on the finest grater by hand. Or use a food processor or meat grinder.
Drain the liquid. Add the egg, salt, pepper, and flour. Mix well.
Heat enough oil in a frying pan. Fry over medium heat. If the heat is too low, the deruny will absorb a lot of oil, and if too high, they will become too tough and overcooked.
Spoon the batter onto the frying pan, forming a round shape. Not too thick, maximum 5-8 mm.
When one side is fried to a golden color, flip it to the other side and fry until it reaches the same golden color.
Serve hot with sour cream or mushroom sauce.
Thoroughly wash the white mushrooms and leave them in salted water for 30 minutes.
Remove from water, cut into pieces, and immerse in boiling water for 10-15 minutes.
Peel the onion, finely chop it, and lightly fry it in vegetable oil.
Add the mushrooms to the onion and fry them together until cooked. Add salt and pepper.
Optionally, you can add garlic that has been pressed.
To the nearly cooked mushrooms, add sour cream or cream, reduce the heat to low, and let the mushrooms simmer a bit.
Wash the parsley and finely chop it.
Remove the mushrooms from heat, add the parsley, and serve hot.
Slice the mushrooms. If using dried mushrooms, soak them in freshly boiled water for 20-30 minutes.
Peel and cube the potatoes and boil them in salted water for about 10 minutes. The potatoes should be "al dente", slightly undercooked. Drain the water and set aside.
Wash the meat under running water and dry it with a paper towel, then cut it into 1.5-2 cm cubes.
Preheat the oven to 220 ˚C.
Place meat and a piece of butter at the bottom of each pot, season with salt and pepper.
Chop the peeled onion, grate the carrot on a coarse grater. Distribute the onion and carrot among all the pots.
Then distribute the mushrooms among the pots.
Add chopped garlic (not too finely) and water (about halfway up the pot) to each pot. Season with salt and mix everything.
Layer the potatoes on top in each pot.
Cover the pots with lids and place them in the oven for 1 hour - 1 hour 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and sprinkle cheese on top, bake for another 10 minutes until golden brown.
For cooking banosh, it is better to take a cast iron pot, put the sour cream in it, dilute it with cream, and mix until a homogeneous consistency.
Turn the heat to maximum and gradually pour the cornmeal into the pot while constantly stirring.
Bring to a boil, and immediately reduce the heat to minimum. Add salt on the tip of a knife.

Intensively stir with a wooden spatula in one direction without stopping, until the banosh thickens and drops of fat appear on the surface. This will take about 15-20 minutes. The finished banosh should easily come off the walls of the pot.
Cover the pot with a lid and place it to 'rest' in a preheated oven at 80°C for 10 minutes.
This step can be skipped if you prepare the fat with onion and mushrooms simultaneously or before making the banosh.
Meanwhile, let's prepare everything else.
Peel, wash, and slice the onion into half rings.
Break the bryndza cheese into small pieces by hand.
Cut the fat into small pieces, about 4 by 2 cm.
Fry the fat in a pan until golden brown.
Add the onion and pepper, mix the ingredients with a wooden spatula and sauté until golden.
On a large flat plate, pour the porridge, top with cracklings and onion, sprinkle with bryndza, and drizzle with the remaining pork fat.
Serve hot with buttermilk or milk whey, and lightly salted cucumbers.

ingredients.name: Kefir
ingredients.notes: or sour milk, at room temperature

instructions.text: Sift the flour, add kefir, salt, baking soda (do not extinguish), and knead the dough.
Cover the dough with a towel and let it rest for 30-40 minutes.
Place the dough on a floured surface and cut it into several pieces, each of which is shaped into a sausage. Cut into small pieces.
Poltava dumplings are best steamed for no more than 7 minutes. They double in size during cooking.

If boiling in water, drop the dumplings into already boiling water, stir with a slotted spoon, and let the water come to a boil. Boil for 3-4 minutes. Remove and brush with butter. The finished dumpling is porous and soft like a ball.
Place in a serving dish and generously pour over the gravy.
Serve with herbs, green onions, and squeeze garlic on top.
Dumplings can also be added to borscht, served with cracklings or with sour cream and mushroom sauce.
Fry the grated carrot and onion in butter in a pan until soft.
Cut the chicken meat into pieces and add to the pan, fry and simmer everything together until cooked, approximately 25 minutes.
At the end, add bay leaf, pepper, sour cream, or low-fat cream. If necessary, add a little water.
Dip the head of cabbage into boiling water for 5 minutes.
Take it out of the water and remove several outer leaves. Cut off the thick part near the base from the remaining leaves.
In a frying pan, first fry the onion in vegetable oil, then add grated carrots.
Boil the rice until half-cooked.
Combine the rice and ground meat. Mix well.
Add the fried carrots and onion to the meat mixture. Season with salt and pepper and mix again.
Wrap the meat mixture in cabbage leaves.
Tightly arrange the prepared cabbage rolls in a pot seam side down.
Pour in water so that it does not reach the upper edge of the cabbage rolls.
When the water boils, add the tomato paste and sour cream.
Simmer on low heat for about 1 hour.
Cabbage rolls can be served immediately and definitely with sour cream.
Separate 400 g of pitted cherries and mix with sugar. Leave for 10 minutes, then drain the juice into a separate container.
Take kefir, add flour and 3 tablespoons of sugar. Then add baking soda - this will make the dough fluffier. Knead the dough and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough (thickness 2-3 mm), cut out circles (you can use a glass), place two berries on each circle, and pinch the edges to make dumplings.
Steam for 5-7 minutes. If you don't have a steamer, place a colander over a pot of boiling water, arrange the dumplings, and cover with a lid.
Drizzle the finished dumplings with cherry sauce.
Blend the remaining cherries and juice with a blender and set over low heat.
In a separate bowl, dissolve the starch in 2 tablespoons of cold water. Gradually pour the starch into the boiling sauce while stirring slowly.
Add 1 tablespoon of sugar and continue to stir. Keep on heat until the desired consistency is reached.
In a large bowl or on a work surface, sift the flour. Form a mound with a well on top.
Take the eggs, separate the whites from the yolks, and add only the yolks to the flour.
Pour in the melted butter and water.
Gradually knead the dough starting from the center. A firm mass should form.
Wrap the dough in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Take it out and roll it out to a thickness of 1-2 mm. Cut into circles of even diameter.
Place filling in the center of each circle. Approximately 1 teaspoon.
Pinch the edges in the usual way or in a "braid".
Boil the dumplings in boiling salted water. The dough is ready 4 minutes after boiling.
Serve hot with sour cream and cracklings.
Peel and boil the potatoes. Rinse and chop the mushrooms. Peel and finely chop the onion.
Heat vegetable oil in a pan and sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the mushrooms and simmer until the moisture evaporates.
When the potatoes are cooked, drain the water and mash them into a puree.
Mix the potatoes with the mushrooms and onion, add parsley, salt, and pepper.
Take the butter out of the fridge and let it warm up a bit.
Finely chop the herbs. Add the finely chopped garlic and softened butter. Mix well and beat a little with a fork.
Divide the prepared butter into parts and shape into sticks.
Send to the freezer for 30 minutes.

If you bought a whole chicken, you need to butcher it to get two fillets with the wing bone. Remove the skin. Place the fillet skin side down, cut from the middle along both sides, place the halves so that the filling fits, and gently pound. Trim the white tendons so that the cutlets do not shrink.
Prepare a special batter - a liaison. For this, mix the eggs with milk and a pinch of salt in a plate.
Sprinkle breadcrumbs, take the 'green butter' out of the freezer.
Place the pounded fillet on a board, salt and pepper it.
In the center of each piece of fillet, place a stick of butter and a piece of hard cheese.
Wrap the butter and cheese in the meat, carefully rolling it into a roll. The main thing is that there are no holes through which the butter can leak.
Coat the prepared cutlets in flour and send them to the freezer for 10-15 minutes. This helps the cutlets retain their shape better.
Before frying the cutlets, they need to be coated in breadcrumbs twice. For this, first dip the cutlet in the liaison and then in the breadcrumbs, and repeat.
Place lard in a deep frying pan and heat it. The melted lard or oil should cover the cutlets, so don't skimp on it.
Place the cutlets in hot oil. Fry on both sides until golden brown for about 5-7 minutes.
Transfer the cutlets to a baking sheet using a slotted spoon.
Finish cooking in an oven preheated to 200°C (400°F). Baking will take 10-15 minutes.
To remove excess fat from the cutlets, you can dab them with a paper towel.
Serve with fresh vegetables or salad. You can also use any other more filling side dish.
Knead the dough with flour, sugar, cream, yeast and put it in a warm place to rise.
Then add melted butter, knead again and put in a warm place.
When the dough rises, roll it out into a thin flatbread, place it on a greased sheet, brush with yolk, and sprinkle with almonds.
Bake in the oven at moderate heat for about 25 minutes.
Cut the potatoes into slices 0.5 cm thick and fry them in vegetable oil until golden brown.
Season the fish fillet with salt and pepper, coat in flour, and fry in oil as well.
In a pan, heat the butter, add the shrimp, fry for 1 minute, pour in the wine, and bring to a boil.
When the alcohol smell dissipates, pour in the cream and bring to a boil.
Grease a baking dish with oil, layer the potato slices, place the fish on top, and add halved eggs on the fish.
Pour the shrimp sauce over the eggs and sprinkle with grated cheese.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) until a golden crust forms.
Serve with lemon slices, sprinkled with chopped herbs.
Dissolve the yeast in 2 tbsp. of warm milk with 1 tbsp. of sugar and let it ferment.
Pour into a bowl with flour, add sour cream or kefir, yolks rubbed with sugar, clarified butter, salt, zest and knead until bubbles appear. Cover and place in a warm place to let the dough rise.
Place on a floured board, knead, divide into four parts and roll out so that two of them - the bottom and top are thicker.

Place the first layer on a baking tray lined with parchment paper, and prick it with a fork. Spread the jam and cover with the second layer, prick it and put the poppy filling on top, cover with the third layer, prick and spread the nut filling. Cover everything with the fourth layer, which should also be pricked with a fork.
Cover the perekhladanytsia and let the dough rise.

Then brush it with egg white and bake in a hot oven at about 200°C (400°F) for 45-50 minutes. (It may take a little longer, depending on the oven). If the perekhladanytsia is burning too much, cover it with damp paper on top.
Let it cool and carefully remove from the tray.
You can flip it over and cover the top with meringue.

ingredients.name: Brandy
ingredients.notes: or you can use alcohol or rum

instructions.text: In a deep bowl or mixer bowl, beat the egg yolks with sugar, salt, brandy, and sour cream until smooth.
Add flour and knead an elastic dough. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Take the dough out of the refrigerator and place it on a floured work surface. Roll the dough well with a rolling pin.
When it flattens, fold it in half and roll it out again firmly, repeating this for about 10 minutes. Then let the dough rest for another 10 minutes.
Divide the dough into 3 parts. Roll each part of the dough and cut strips about 10 cm long and 3 cm wide. Make a longitudinal cut in the middle of each strip.
Turn one half of the strip through the formed hole.
In a cauldron or wok, heat a large amount of vegetable oil or lard. The oil should reach a temperature of 162°C (325°F).
Reduce the heat to medium and drop the verguny into the heated oil. Fry until cooked on both sides until a rich bronze color.
Place the verguny on a plate lined with a paper towel and immediately sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Mix the batter from flour, eggs, milk, and sugar, and bake the pancakes.
Chop the nuts, add milk, sugar, and rum - the mixture should have a puree consistency.
Add raisins and grated orange zest.
Place the filling on the pancakes, roll them up, and fry in butter until golden brown.
Serve drizzled with chocolate sauce.
Beat the egg yolks with sugar and flour.
Add milk, cream, and heat the sauce over fire without boiling.
In the hot mixture, add chocolate, cocoa powder, and rum. Heat again and remove from fire.
First, crack the egg yolks into a deep bowl and rub them with sugar until homogeneous using a tablespoon.
Then add previously softened cream margarine. It won't be completely mixed, the margarine will remain in pieces, but that’s how it should be.

Sift the flour directly into the bowl with all the ingredients, add the bitter cocoa powder, sour cream, and baking powder. Knead the dough in the bowl with your hands until it reaches a thick consistency.
Then transfer it to a floured table and knead the dough more firmly. The dough should be dense but soft.
Divide the ready dough into 3 equal parts, wrap each separately in cling film, and place in the freezer for 30 minutes along with the grater that will be used to grate it.
Prepare similarly to the chocolate dough. Rub the chicken egg with sugar in a deep bowl until homogeneous using a tablespoon.
Add pieces of softened cream margarine, sour cream, baking powder, vanilla sugar, sifted flour, and knead the dough directly in the bowl.
Then place the dough on a floured table and incorporate the remaining flour that was left in the bowl.
Divide the dough into 3 equal parts, wrap in cling film, and place in the freezer for 30 minutes. This dough will be softer.
While the dough is resting in the freezer, preheat the oven to 200 degrees.
After 30 minutes, take out 1 part of the white dough and place it on a floured table. Take a large rectangular sheet and line it with parchment paper so that the edges extend beyond the sides.

Roll out the dough into a circle to fit the rectangular sheet, flatten it and carefully place it onto the baking tray. If the layer is slightly uneven, carefully trim it with clean fingers along the edges of the tray. The thickness of the layer should be from 1 to 1.5 centimeters.
Then, using a tablespoon, spread the thick plum jam over the layer and sprinkle walnuts on top.
Take 1 part of the chocolate dough and grate it evenly over the jam using a large grater.
Bake the layer for 10 - 12 minutes until fully cooked.
Bake 2 more layers in the same way and let them cool. Do not remove the last baked layer from the tray; let it cool in it.

Take the sour cream frosting out of the refrigerator and divide it into 3 equal parts. Place 1 part of the frosting on the last layer that cooled in the tray and spread it over the entire surface with a kitchen spatula.

Place the second layer on top and spread the second part of the frosting over it again. Do the same with the third layer as with the previous two. The thickness of the frosting on the layers should be approximately 5-7 mm.
Take a large grater and grate 1 bar of milk chocolate over the top layer coated with frosting so that its entire surface is covered with chocolate crumbs.
Cover with cling film and place in the refrigerator for 8-9 hours to allow the layers to soak up the frosting.
Cut into portioned pieces with a knife.

A day before making the pie, place sour cream in sterile cheesecloth folded in 3-4 layers. Tie it tightly at the end with string and hang it up. Place a plate underneath to catch the whey. Keep the sour cream like this for 2-3 hours at room temperature. During this time, a lot of whey will drain, but not all of it. After this, place the drained sour cream in the refrigerator for a day.
Take the sour cream out of the refrigerator. Place it in a deep bowl.
Add powdered sugar and vanilla sugar.
Beat all the ingredients with a mixer for 15 - 20 minutes. During this time, the sour cream will thicken and become airy and fluffy.
Place the ready frosting in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Wash the meat and cut it into cubes of about 2 cm.
Chop the onion, pepper, and tomatoes into small pieces.
Sauté the finely chopped onion until translucent, add garlic, cumin, and paprika.
Mix everything, put on high heat, and add the cubed meat.
Stew until it boils in its own juice.
Sprinkle with red pepper, add diced sweet pepper and mashed peeled tomato, and simmer with a little water for 4-5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Cover with a lid, reduce the heat, and cook for another 1-1.5 hours on low heat. Remember to stir. Add more spices if necessary.
Serve with mashed potatoes, egg noodles, or Hungarian dumplings 'nokedli'.
Cut the well-chilled lean pork and bacon into pieces of 6-8 mm. You can pass them through the large holes of a meat grinder.
Chop the beef 2-3 times.
Separate the garlic into cloves.
Thoroughly mix the meat, bacon, and spices with the added water.
If not smoking, you can add liquid smoke; in this case, you need more pepper.
Stuff the pork intestines with the resulting minced meat and twist them into sausages about 20 cm long. Leave them in a cool place for 1 day.
Smoke the sausages with warm smoke for 1 hour.
Debrecen sausages are rarely consumed as a standalone dish. They are more often added to goulash.

ingredients.name: Flour
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

ingredients.name: Egg
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

ingredients.name: Sweet paprika
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

ingredients.name: Sour cream
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.group: FOR THE DRESSING AND CHIPETKE (HUNGARIAN DUMPLINGS)

instructions.text: Rinse the beans well, cover with water, and leave overnight. In the morning, rinse and transfer to a bowl.
Place the pork knuckle in water and boil until completely soft. This will take about 1 hour.
Add the soaked beans and boil for 30 minutes.
Add the bay leaf, pepper, and tomatoes.
Meanwhile, sauté the onion in vegetable oil for 5 minutes, add the paprika and sauté for another 5 minutes.
Add the chopped carrots, parsley, and celery root, and sauté everything together for 10 minutes.
Add the vegetables to the soup and cook for another 20 minutes.

Remove the knuckle from the soup. Mix the flour dressing well with a small amount of water and pour it into the soup, then boil the soup, stirring several times, for 2 minutes, add chipetke, salt, and spices to taste.
When serving, remove the bones from the knuckle, cut it into cubes, and place it back into the soup along with the sautéed sausage slices or serve in bowls separately.
Pour the hot soup into bowls, drizzle with sour cream, but it's also good to offer sour cream separately. Garnish with parsley greens.
If desired, each person can season the soup with tarragon vinegar right in the bowl.
Fry the sliced sausage and remove it from the pan.
In the fat rendered from the sausage, brown the flour until dark golden for 1-2 minutes.
Then remove the pan from the heat, mix in the paprika and crushed garlic and let it cool.
Dissolve the flour with the egg and a pinch of salt (without water), knead, and roll out on a floured surface to a thickness of 1-2 mm, then pinch off tiny shapeless pieces with floured fingers.
Cook in boiling soup. When the dough is ready (after 3-4 minutes), it will float to the surface.

recipes.title: Hungarian Vegetable Lentil Soup Főzelék (Vöröslencse Főzelék)

instructions.text: Rinse the lentils, cover with water about a finger above the contents of the pot, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the bay leaf and parsley root. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and cook (for about 20-30 minutes) until the lentils are tender.
Heat the lard in a frying pan and add the chopped onion. Fry until translucent.
Add the mint and sauté a little more. Add the tomato paste and paprika, mix quickly, and remove the pan from the heat to prevent the paprika from burning, which would make it bitter.

Prepare the habarash: mix the milk and sour cream, add the flour, and stir until smooth; then add 3 tablespoons of water from the pot with lentils to prevent lumps from temperature differences. Mix well and pour back in.
Cook the főzelék on low heat until thickened, stirring constantly.
Remove the parsley root and bay leaf, season with salt, caraway seeds, and white pepper.
Serve as a standalone dish, it can be served cold with a spoonful of sour cream. Add a boiled egg, meatballs, fried sausage, or croutons to the finished dish.
Pour boiling water over the tomatoes, then rinse with cold water and peel off the skin, chop the flesh into cubes.
Chop the bell pepper and peeled onion into cubes as well. Cut the chicken fillet into small pieces.
Fry the onion in vegetable oil until soft. Then add the ground paprika and a little water. Cook for a few minutes.
Add the chicken fillet and fry for 10 minutes.
Add the chopped bell pepper and tomatoes. Salt, add chili pepper, cover with a lid and cook for 30 minutes.
Mix the sour cream with the flour to avoid lumps. Add to the pan and cook for another 10-15 minutes.
Serve the paprikash with dumplings or mashed potatoes.
Immerse the tomatoes in boiling water for a few seconds, peel them, and cut each into four parts.
Remove the seeds from the bell pepper, cut each into 5-6 parts lengthwise.
Cut the bacon into small cubes, fry it a little in a small amount of oil, and add the chopped onion.
Once the onion turns golden, sprinkle it with red paprika, add the bell pepper and tomatoes, and simmer covered on low heat for about 30-40 minutes.
Serve with potatoes or rice.
Boil the potatoes in salted water until soft (but not as for mashed potatoes). Cool, peel, and slice into rounds.
Boil the eggs hard. Cool and slice into rounds.
Peel the sausage and slice it into thin rounds.
Preheat the oven to 200 degrees. Grease a baking dish with vegetable oil.
Layer the potatoes, then alternately layer the eggs and sausage.
Sprinkle with half of the paprika and spread half of the sour cream on top.
Repeat the layers once more (the last layer should be potatoes), add salt and pepper, and add the second half of the paprika and sour cream.
Bake for 30-40 minutes until a golden crust forms. The finished dish can be garnished with herbs.

recipes.title: Hungarian Noodles with Township Cottage Cheese

instructions.text: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and tablespoon of water, knead in the flour to make a stiff dough, like for dumplings (you may need more flour).
Cover the dough and let it rest for 20 minutes. Then roll it out into a thin layer, cut into small pieces or tear by hand.
Boil in salted boiling water with a small amount of vegetable oil added (to prevent sticking).
In fat over medium heat, fry the diced bacon, remove it, and dry it.
Remove the cooked noodles, rinse with cold water, and place in a pot with the cracklings. Drizzle with half of the sour cream, add half of the cottage cheese, and mix.
Serve the dish on a plate, add the remaining sour cream and cottage cheese, and salt to taste.

Mix the flour, yeast, salt, sugar, and warm milk in a bowl. Knead the dough. Add the necessary amount of water for the desired consistency. Cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm place for about 30 minutes.
Peel the garlic, crush it in a mortar or press it with a garlic press. Add cold boiled water, add a pinch of salt, stir.
Gently knead the dough. Pinch off a piece from the total mass for one flatbread; the size will depend on the diameter of the frying pan.
Roll the dough into a ball. Roll it out into a small not-thin flatbread, then carefully stretch it. The flatbread should be thinner in the center than at the edges.
Heat vegetable oil in a pot or deep skillet; the oil should be boiling. Carefully lower the langos into it. It should float in the oil, not touching the bottom.
Fry the langos in boiling oil until golden brown on both sides.
Place the finished langos on a plate lined with a paper towel.
Brush with garlic sauce, sour cream, sprinkle with grated cheese, and serve immediately.

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs (green onion, parsley or dill), finely chopped

instructions.text: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper in a bowl.
Cut the bread into pieces 1.5-2 cm thick, and then into small cubes.
Squeeze the garlic into the milk, mix, and soak the bread pieces in it. Let them sit to absorb the milk.
Then dip the bread pieces in the egg, making sure they are coated on all sides. Quickly place them in a preheated pan with oil.
Fry, turning regularly, until golden brown.
Place the finished toasts on a paper towel.
Generously sprinkle with sweet paprika and herbs.
You can also serve a sweet version, preparing it in the same way but without garlic and sprinkling with powdered sugar and cinnamon before serving.
Mash the curd and whip until smooth with the sour cream. Add salt to taste.
Add finely chopped onion, paprika, and caraway. Mix thoroughly and refrigerate for a few hours.
The resulting mixture can be used to stuff boiled eggs, lettuce leaves, bell peppers, tomatoes, and can also be wrapped in thinly sliced ham. Körözött is also served with toast and fresh bread.
Wash the legs and offal, clean them, remove excess hair, and place them in a pot to boil. The water should just cover everything.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes. Then turn off the heat and drain all the water.
Thoroughly rinse all parts individually under running water. Also, wash the pot clean.
Then place everything back into the pot, rinse the meat and smoked meat, cut them into smaller pieces, and place them in the pot as well.
Wash the onion with the skin, but do not peel it, as it will give a nice color. Peel the parsley root and cut it into pieces. Separate the garlic into cloves. Slice the carrot into rounds.
Put all the ingredients in the pot along with paprika, salt, and pepper. Fill with water to cover everything by 3-4 fingers.
Cook for about 4 hours, skimming off the foam from the surface of the broth, until the meat easily separates from the bones.
Strain. Let the broth cool slightly and then remove the top layer of fat.
Discard the vegetables: onion, parsley, and garlic. Strain again. Let the broth cool slightly and then remove the top layer of fat.
Separate the meat (skin, cartilage, and tendons) from the bones and cut it into pieces, then distribute it onto plates along with the carrot and halved eggs.
Pour the broth over the meat. Cover and place in a cool place to set.
Sprinkle with paprika, a few drops of vinegar or lemon juice.
Serve with pickles, horseradish, red onion, and fresh, crispy homemade bread.
Add eggs, vegetable oil, and salt to warm milk and mix.
Gradually add flour in small portions. Whip everything well with a blender or whisk to avoid lumps.
Pour in 1 cup of water (or whey), cover with film and let it sit for 30 minutes.
Cook pancakes on a heated pan with vegetable oil.
Place 1-2 tbsp of filling without liquid (it will be needed for the sauce) on the edge of the pancake, roll it up like cabbage rolls or fold it. Do this with all the filling and pancakes.
Arrange the pancakes in a baking dish and pour sauce over the top. Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for about 15 minutes.
Serve with sour cream.
Finely chop the onion. Heat sunflower oil in a pan and sauté the onion until lightly golden. Sprinkle with paprika and mix well.
Then add beef cut into pieces about 2-3 cm. Add salt, mix, and simmer on low heat for about 20 minutes.
Add chopped tomato and pepper. Cook until done. Remove from heat and let cool. The filling can be left as is or passed through a meat grinder.
Mix sour cream, paprika, and flour.
Add the remaining liquid from the filling, if necessary dilute with water to the desired consistency, blend until smooth.
Heat on the lowest heat without boiling, remove from heat while keeping warm.
Mix the lightly beaten egg, vinegar, oil, and flour.
Gradually add warm water, knead the dough to a medium consistency.
Knead until it stops sticking to your hands.
Divide the prepared dough into 2 parts, roll into balls, dust with flour, cover with a bowl, and let sit for about 15 minutes in a warm place.
Roll out the dough thinly with a rolling pin, then stretch the dough by hand until it becomes thin almost like paper.
You can do this directly on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Let the dough rest a bit, then grease it with oil, sprinkle with breadcrumbs, and evenly distribute honey, grated apples, and cinnamon with vanilla sugar on one third of the sheet.
Roll up the dough, transfer it to a greased baking tray, brush with oil, and bake until golden brown at 180 degrees for 25-30 minutes.
Repeat with the remaining dough.
Remove the finished roll from the oven, let it cool for 5-7 minutes, then cut into portioned pieces.
RETES can be served hot or cold.
Whip the egg whites with half of the powdered sugar until stiff peaks form, and beat the yolks with the remaining powdered sugar and butter until creamy.
Mix the flour with cocoa. Alternately add the flour and egg whites to the yolk and butter mixture and gently fold.
Pour the resulting mixture into a baking pan lined with parchment paper.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180 degrees for 35-40 minutes.
Let it cool, cut into two rectangles. Spread jam on one side of one rectangle and glaze on the other. Cut the cake into squares.
Spread cream on the second half of the cake. Place the squares closely together on the cream layer and refrigerate.
After a while, take out the cakes and cut into portioned squares with a warm, dry knife.
Melt the chocolate in a water bath. Whip the cream with sugar until foamy.
Carefully mix the cooled chocolate with the cream. Place the resulting cream in the refrigerator.
In a small saucepan, bring the milk and sugar to a boil.
Remove from heat, add finely chopped chocolate and butter, and stir until smooth.
Soak the raisins and finely grated zest in rum overnight.

The next day, bring the cream to a boil, add the coarsely ground nuts, sugar, a little cinnamon, raisins, and zest removed from the rum, and cook for 1-2 minutes (if needed, adding a little milk) until a puree-like mass is obtained. Once the puree cools slightly, mix in half of the specified amount of rum.
Using a whisk, blend the eggs with cold milk and, while continuing to whisk, gradually add the sifted flour. Thin the well-mixed dough with sparkling water to the consistency of liquid sour cream.
Fry 12 thin pancakes in a pan. Sprinkle each finished pancake with a pinch of sugar.
Place filling on each pancake, roll it up or fold it into a triangle.
Before serving, lightly fry the pancakes in butter and drizzle with chocolate sauce.
Bring the cream to a boil, add the coarsely ground nuts, sugar, and a pinch of cinnamon.
Remove the raisins and zest from the rum and add them to the filling as well. A puree-like mass will result.
Cook for a couple of minutes until the sugar melts. Remove from heat, add half of the remaining rum (in which the raisins and zest were soaked), and mix well.
Whip the cream in a large bowl until fluffy (so the sauce is not too thick and lumpy).
Melt the chocolate over low heat.
Rub the yolks with 30 g of sugar. Add cocoa and mix. Add the melted hot chocolate, a couple of tablespoons of milk, and whisk into a homogeneous mass.
Bring the milk together with 70 g of sugar and vanilla sugar to a boil.
Remove from heat and pour the hot milk in a thin stream into the chocolate mixture, constantly stirring.
Gradually fold the finished chocolate mass into the whipped cream. Finally, add the remaining half of the rum. The result should be a very delicate, airy chocolate sauce.
Separate the yolks from the whites. Whisk the yolks with half of the sugar.
In a separate clean bowl, whisk the whites with the remaining sugar until foamy. Add the vanilla sugar and combine with the yolks. Gradually, while stirring, add the sifted flour.

Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Pour 1/5 of the batter into a greased pan and bake for 10 minutes until golden. The layer bakes fairly quickly as the batter is thin; doneness can be checked with a wooden stick.
Remove from the oven and immediately take off the parchment from the baking sheet. While the batter is still hot, cut out a biscuit of the desired diameter (about 27 cm).
Wait a couple of minutes until the biscuit cools and can be easily separated from the parchment. Bake 6 layers this way.
Stack the baked layers on top of each other, spreading cream on each layer. Apply the remaining cream on the top and sides of the cake.
Decorate with caramel shards.
Break the chocolate into pieces and melt it, stirring, in a water bath. Let it cool slightly.
Beat the slightly softened butter with sugar, combine with chocolate, vanilla sugar, and egg.
Pour sugar into a large saucepan with a thick bottom, add 2–3 tbsp of water, and slowly melt over low heat.
Add butter, stir, and cook until a homogeneous mass of golden-brown color is obtained.
Quickly pour the caramel onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, allowing it to fully set. Then separate the caramel from the paper and break it into pieces.
Cut the hare into portion-sized pieces and remove the membranes.
Place in a large container and cover with the mixture of sparkling water and kefir.
Add the thyme on top and let it marinate for at least 4 hours (for hare, at least 24 hours) in a cool place.
Remove the pieces of rabbit (hare) from the marinade and pat them dry with a towel.
Sprinkle with salt and white pepper, and let marinate for 30 minutes.
Sauté the chopped shallots in butter in a skillet. This will take 3-4 minutes.
Pour in the white wine, bring to a boil, and let it evaporate.
Add the mustard, thyme, and water and bring to a boil.
Taste the sauce for salt and add if necessary.
Heat the butter over medium heat in a large skillet or pot with a lid. Sear the pieces of meat until brown on all sides.
Pour in the sauce to completely cover the meat. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.
Cover with a lid and simmer the rabbit on low heat for 1 hour (for hare, 2 hours). Wild hare requires a long time for the meat to literally fall off the bone.
When the meat is ready, carefully remove it to a plate.
Reduce the sauce by increasing the heat to half its volume.
Turn off the heat and add the sour cream. Stir the sauce until smooth, then add the parsley and stir again.
If you want to thicken the sauce, add sifted flour while constantly stirring.
Return the pieces of rabbit to the skillet.
Serve this dish with a crispy baguette and white wine, such as white Bordeaux or Cotes du Rhone.
Pairs perfectly with mashed potatoes or fondant potatoes.
Rinse the meat, pat dry with a paper towel, cut into pieces, and quickly fry until browned in a hot skillet with a small amount of oil.
Transfer the chicken to a plate and set aside.
Reduce heat. Add the remaining oil in the skillet, add onion, garlic, and ginger, and sauté, stirring until the onion is translucent. This will take about 8 minutes.
Stir in curry powder, cumin, turmeric, coriander, cayenne pepper, and 1 tablespoon of water, and add to the onion mixture. Cook for about 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add tomatoes, yogurt, cilantro, salt, water, and return the chicken to the skillet.
Pour in coconut milk, bring to a boil. Sprinkle with garam masala.
Cover and simmer on low heat until cooked, about 20 minutes.
Before serving, drizzle with lemon juice.
Serve with rice or Indian flatbreads.

ingredients.name: Yellow lentils (or pigeon peas (Toor dal), split pigeon peas
Sesame oil
ingredients.notes: or ginger oil, coconut oil, or regular ghee

instructions.text: Bring water with salt to a boil. Sort, rinse, and add the lentils to the boiling water.
Cook uncovered for 10 minutes.
Skim off the foam, then cover and cook on medium heat for 15-25 minutes, stirring occasionally. The lentils should be soft but not mushy.
Add two cups of water and cook on low heat for another 15 minutes.
Lightly peel and rinse the moringa, cutting it into pieces about 5 cm long. Peel and dice the onion, tomato, and pumpkin.
Cook the vegetables on low heat until soft. (Alternatively, you can sauté the vegetables in oil for about 3-5 minutes).
While the vegetables are cooking, take 1/4 cup of hot water from the pot and soak the tamarind in it.
When the vegetables are ready, add the sambar powder, turmeric, and salt. Cook for another 3-5 minutes.
Add the tamarind (squeeze the pulp and pour the liquid into the soup).
Add the cooked lentils to the vegetables in the broth and mix well.
Bring to a boil, check for salt, add coriander, and mix well.

Meanwhile, heat the sesame oil in a pan. Add mustard seeds, cumin, and fenugreek. After a couple of minutes, add the curry leaves and finely break the dried chili. When the leaves start to crackle, reduce the heat. You can add another 1/4 teaspoon of sambar powder.
Quickly pour this into the vegetables with the lentils and stir thoroughly. Cook on low heat for 2-3 minutes until the soup becomes aromatic.
Cover and let it sit for 4-5 minutes.
Mix thoroughly again, cool, and refrigerate. (To preserve the flavor of sambar, it should be stored for 2 hours in the refrigerator after cooking).
Serve sambar hot with rice or idli flatbreads.
Grind the dried red chili into a coarse paste, adding 1 teaspoon of water.
Mix the red chili paste and tamarind juice with coriander, turmeric, and salt. Then add the grated coconut and half of the coconut milk. Mix well.
Place the pieces of fish in a large shallow dish and pour this mixture over to completely cover the fish. Marinate for 3 hours.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Add curry leaves, fenugreek seeds, and green chili. Fry for about 2 minutes or until the oil stops splattering.
Now add half of the onion paste. Fry until the onion turns very brown. Add the chopped tomato.
Fry until the spices start to release oil and the tomato darkens. Stir frequently.
Now add the fish marinade and mix.
Bring to a boil over medium heat. Add garlic paste, pepper, cumin, the remaining onion paste, and the rest of the coconut milk.
Simmer until oil starts to appear over the sauce.
Add the pieces of fish and simmer until cooked. Stir very gently to avoid breaking the pieces of fish.
Serve with boiled rice.
In a large bowl, combine the ground beef, chopped onion, garlic paste, ginger paste, garam masala, tomato paste, coriander leaves, and salt, and mix well.
Form the mixture into balls of equal size. Carefully add to the pan with the sauce and let it sit for 5 minutes. Then gently stir to avoid breaking the balls.
Simmer over medium heat until cooked, about 10 minutes. You can add water to bring the curry to the desired consistency.
Serve with rice or cucumber salad.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the chopped onion. Fry until light brown. Add the ginger paste and garlic paste. Fry for another minute.
Add the spices (coriander, cumin, red chili powder, garam masala, and turmeric) and fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and mix well. Fry until the oil begins to separate from the onions and tomatoes.
Add warm water and season with salt to taste.
Heat a pan over medium heat. Add the spices (cumin, poppy seeds, fennel seeds, bay leaf, cinnamon, cloves, pepper). Fry until the spices become slightly darker and more fragrant.
Remove from heat and let cool for about 10 minutes. Grind to a fine powder in a coffee grinder.

Place the coconut flesh cut into thin long strips about 2 cm wide in a container, add garlic and ginger paste, cumin, ground chili, and the spices from the grinder. Add 3-4 tablespoons of water and mash until smooth.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Add the onions and fry until golden brown.

Add the aforementioned masala (spice paste) and slightly reduce the heat (just below medium). Fry, stirring often, until the oil begins to separate from the paste. You may need to add a little water to prevent the masala from burning and sticking to the pan.
Add the meat and fry until it turns brown.
Add the chopped tomatoes, coconut milk, and 1 cup of warm water. Season with salt to taste and mix well.
Simmer until the meat becomes tender. At this stage, there should be enough thick gravy. If necessary, add warm water to ensure there is enough sauce.
Serve hot with rice and Indian flatbreads.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a deep pot, add the onion. Fry until lightly golden. Remove from heat.
Place the onion in a food processor. Grind the onion, tomatoes, and green chili pepper into a puree. Do not add water.
Heat the remaining oil and add the freshly made paste. Fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes, all the dry spices (coriander, cumin, garam masala, turmeric, and red chili), then mix and fry until oil begins to separate on the surface.
Add 2 cups of warm water and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Cook the potatoes until half done.

Cut the boiled eggs vertically in half and carefully add them to the curry. Cook on low heat for 10 minutes or until the sauce thickens or reduces to about 3/4 of its original amount (before the water was added).
Add the potatoes, simmer for another 3-5 minutes.
Turn off the heat and garnish with chopped coriander leaves and sliced green chili pepper. Serve hot with boiled basmati rice and a vegetable side.
Chop 2 onions, tomatoes, ginger, and garlic paste in a food processor until it becomes a paste.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot with a thick bottom over medium heat.
Add bay leaf, cloves, cardamom, and peppercorns and sauté until slightly dark and fragrant.
Add the remaining sliced onion and fry until light golden.
Add the tomato-onion paste prepared earlier and sauté until the oil starts to separate from the paste.
Add the dry spices - cumin, coriander, red chili, turmeric, and garam masala. Sauté, stirring frequently, for another 5 minutes.
Drain the water from the can of chickpeas and rinse thoroughly under running water.
Now add the chickpeas to the masala prepared earlier. Mix very well.
Add salt to taste and enough hot water - about 1 1/2 cups.
Simmer covered for 10 minutes.
Then mash and mix well.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh ginger and finely chopped fresh coriander leaves. Squeeze some lemon juice and a handful of very finely chopped onions for garnish.

recipes.title: Rajma Curry with Red Beans (Rajma Dal Curry)

instructions.text: In a deep pot, heat the oil and add the cumin seeds. When they stop crackling, add the onion and sauté until soft.
Add ginger and garlic and sauté for 2 minutes.
