Add green chili pepper, tomatoes, coriander, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala and sauté until the oil separates from the masala.
Add the red beans, warm water, and asafoetida, along with salt to taste. Cook until the beans are soft, about 10 minutes.
Mash the beans slightly to thicken the curry. Garnish with coriander and serve hot with rice, Kachumber salad, and pickles.
Wash the chickpeas well. Add the fenugreek seeds and pour enough water into a bowl to cover by 5 cm. Soak overnight.
The next morning, drain all the water. Place in a food processor with the rice flour and grind into a smooth but slightly grainy paste. If necessary, add a little water -
Add salt to taste and place in a warm dark place covered for 6-8 hours. Then stir the batter well.
Fold a paper towel into a ball and lightly dip it into a bowl of vegetable oil. Squeeze out the excess, then grease the surface of the pan. Turn on medium heat.
Fill a ladle with 3/4 batter. Carefully pour this batter into the center of the pan - just like for pancakes - until the ladle is empty.
Spread the liquid batter in circular motions to form a pancake.
Sprinkle vegetable oil over the entire surface of the dosa, as well as the edges. Shake the pan so that the oil spreads evenly across the surface.
When the top of the dosa dries out, flip it over. By this time, ideally, the surface on the other side should be light golden in color. Cook for 1 minute after flipping.
Fold in half and let sit for 30 seconds.

Before starting to make the next dosa, fold another paper towel into a ball and dip it in cold water. Squeeze it out and wipe the entire surface of the pan to cool it and prevent the next dosa from drying out due to the very hot pan. Now repeat everything.
Sprinkle the dosas with lemon juice (optional). Serve with chutney and a salad of fresh vegetables.
In a non-metallic bowl, soak the mustard seeds in malt vinegar overnight.
Blanch the tomatoes. Cut into 2-3 cm cubes.
Place the mustard seeds, the vinegar they were in, ginger and garlic in a food processor and grind into a smooth paste.
Heat the mustard oil in a pot over low heat. Add turmeric, cumin, and ground chili. Cook on low heat for 5 minutes, stirring frequently.
Add the peeled and chopped tomatoes, green chili, the mustard mixture, vinegar, ginger, and garlic, sugar, and salt.
Continue to cook on low heat until the tomatoes become soft and pulpy. When this happens, oil will start rising to the surface.
Remove from heat and let cool. Blend until smooth.
Place a pan over medium heat, warm it up, add cumin seeds and roast, stirring frequently, until they darken and become aromatic. Remove from heat and grind into a coarse powder.
Place the diced mango, salt, and turmeric in a plastic bowl. Mix well and let sit for 30 minutes.
Then put everything into a cheesecloth, tie it up, and hang it so all the liquid drains out. It will not be needed anymore.
Put it back in the bowl and add sugar. Stir with a wooden spoon until all the sugar dissolves.
Place the mango-sugar mixture into a large heavy-bottomed pot and cook over medium heat. Stir frequently until the sugar becomes syrupy.
Add red chili and cumin, mix well, and remove from heat immediately. Before the sugar crystallizes.
Allow to cool, transfer to a sterilized jar. Store for no more than one month.
Chunda is served with rice and various Indian flatbreads.
Mix 2.5 tablespoons of tandoori masala with yogurt, 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil, and salt to taste to make a paste.
Place the paneer cubes in a bowl and pour the tandoori paste over them. Gently mix to coat the paneer. Cover and marinate in the refrigerator for two hours.
Mix the remaining 0.5 tablespoon of tandoori masala with the onion.
Thread the marinated paneer, onion, and 4 cm diced bell pepper pieces onto bamboo skewers.
Place the skewers on a hot grill and brush with a little vegetable oil. Grill until the paneer is light golden and the onion is soft.
Sprinkle the finished dish with chaat masala and squeeze lemon juice over it. Serve hot with lemon wedges.

ingredients.name: Mustard oil
ingredients.notes: can be replaced with vegetable oil

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a large pan. Fry the mustard seeds and cumin for a few minutes until they start to crackle.
Add the onion, ginger, and jalapeño pepper and fry for another 3-4 minutes.
Add turmeric, coriander, garam masala, and warm for another minute, then add the cauliflower, green peas, tomatoes, and bell pepper.
Reduce the heat to medium and simmer for 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are cooked.
Add the spinach and cook until it wilts. Season with salt to taste.
Serve with Basmati rice.
Make small diagonal cuts on the pieces of chicken.
Mix tandoori masala with yogurt, 2 tbsp of vegetable oil, garlic paste, and salt to taste.
Make a puree-like paste.
Coat the pieces of chicken with this paste, paying special attention to the cuts.
Place all the pieces and marinade in a deep bowl and cover. Leave to marinate in a cool place for 12-18 hours.
Preheat the grill to medium heat. Place the chicken on it and quickly sear (sealing in the juices) on both sides until browned. Brush with oil as needed.
Reduce the heat and cover the grill. Cook until the chicken is tender. The key is not to overcook it, otherwise, the chicken will become dry.
Can be baked in the oven at 180°C (350°F).
While the oven is heating, cover a baking sheet with foil and brush with vegetable oil. Place the pieces of chicken and lightly drizzle with vegetable oil.
Bake for 15 minutes, then turn the pieces and bake for another 10 minutes.
Transfer the chicken to a plate or dish and sprinkle with chaat masala, squeeze lime juice, and garnish with lime wedges and onion rings. Serve hot.
Place the chicken pieces in a colander and let them drain to remove most of the liquid. Pat dry with a paper towel and place in a large bowl.

Add ginger and garlic pastes, garam masala, turmeric, salt, and mix well. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for marination for 1-2 hours. The longer it marinates, the tastier the pakora will be.
Sift the flour, add corn flour, red chili, onion, green chili, curry leaves, and chopped coriander. Mix thoroughly.
Meanwhile, heat oil for deep frying in a pot.
Add a few pieces of chicken coated in marinade at a time. Fry until golden brown on all sides. Carefully turn them occasionally.
Place on paper towels and blot to remove excess oil.
Serve hot with raita and a cup of masala tea.
Carefully roast and then crush the coriander seeds.
Heat the oil in a pan and add the mustard seeds, curry leaves, and green chili pepper. Fry for about 2-3 minutes.
Add the ginger and peanuts. Fry the mixture for another minute.
Add the turmeric powder and turn off the heat.
Add the lemon juice and mix well.
Add the cooked rice, roasted coriander powder, salt to taste, and mix thoroughly.
Serve as a standalone dish or with raita, yogurt, chutney, or kosambari.
Clean the shrimp by removing the heads and shells, setting them aside, and leaving the tails intact.
Remove the intestinal vein.
Sprinkle the shrimp with salt, ground black pepper, and turmeric, mix well, and set aside to marinate while you prepare the curry base.

Heat a pan over medium heat and add coconut oil. Add the shrimp heads and sauté them for 5-10 minutes until they become crispy and slightly caramelized. Add the onion, ginger, garlic, a generous pinch of salt, reduce the heat to medium, and cook until they become soft - a few minutes.

Add the curry powder, fennel powder, paprika, cayenne pepper, black pepper, curry leaves, and sauté, stirring frequently for about 5 minutes until the spices become fragrant and form a paste with the onion, garlic, and ginger.

Add the coconut milk, ⅓ cup of water, fresh red chili pepper, sugar, and lemon or lime juice, and mix. Bring the mixture to a boil. Cover and simmer for about 10 - 15 minutes until the mixture thickens and turns dark red.
Add the cleaned shrimp to the sauce base and gently stir to combine and fully coat the shrimp with the sauce. Add ¼ cup of water if the sauce is too thick, or if you want more sauce.
Gently stirring, bring the mixture to a boil. Cook for another 10 minutes, or until the shrimp is cooked and turns nice and pink. Taste and season with salt if necessary.
Turn off the heat and cover the pan with a lid, letting it rest for a few minutes.
Garnish with chopped cilantro (optional) and serve with rice or roti.

recipes.title: Aloo Matar Gobi Potato with Cauliflower (Aloo Matar Gobi)

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: washed, peeled, and diced into cubes about 2-3 cm

instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the cauliflower. Place fresh cauliflower in a large bowl and cover with hot water. Add a teaspoon of salt and mix well. Let it sit for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan over medium heat. Add cumin seeds and cook until they stop crackling.
Add the onion and sauté until it becomes soft, stirring frequently. Add ginger and garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute.
Add all the spices and sauté everything together for another minute. Now add the chopped tomatoes and green chili. Mix well and sauté for about 2-3 minutes.
Now add the cauliflower, potatoes, and peas. Mix everything well. Add salt to taste. Cover the pan and cook for 3-5 minutes. Turn off the heat.
Garnish the dish with chopped fresh coriander and serve hot with chapati, paratha, or naan.

ingredients.name: Poppy seeds
ingredients.notes: lightly roasted and ground to powder

ingredients.name: Nuts
ingredients.notes: cashews and almonds, ground to a thick paste

instructions.text: Wash, peel, and dice the potatoes. Boil in a pot until cooked, drain the water, and set aside. Do the same with the vegetables.
In a large bowl, mix the boiled potatoes, vegetables, paneer, and cream.
Add the kofta spices - cumin, coriander, and red chili, and mix well. Season with salt.
In a small bowl, mix the chopped nuts and raisins.
Divide the potato and vegetable mixture into portions and place 1/2 teaspoon of the nut and raisin mixture in the center of each. Roll into perfect balls.
In a large pot, heat the oil and fry the kofta over medium heat until lightly golden. Place on paper towels.
Carefully add the kofta to the lightly bubbling sauce and cook together for 2-3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and sprinkle with garam masala. Cover and let sit for 5 minutes.
Serve with hot Indian bread or rice.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a deep pot and sauté the onion until light brown.
Blend into a paste - sautéed onion, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, coriander, cumin, and red chili.
Return this paste to the pan and sauté until the oil begins to separate.
Add the poppy seed powder and nut paste and sauté for another 2-3 minutes.
Add 1 cup of warm water (the sauce for this dish should be thick). Mix well. Season with salt.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then reduce the heat so that the sauce simmers gently and add the kofta.

ingredients.name: Goat legs
ingredients.notes: or lamb on the bone, cut into 5-7 cm pieces

instructions.text: Place all the ingredients (including the garam masala powder) for the marinade in a large non-metallic bowl and mix until a homogeneous consistency is achieved.
Add the pieces of meat and stir. Leave to marinate in the refrigerator for 1 hour.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot and add the onion. Fry until the onion turns pale golden.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes and fry for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add couscous, coconut, cashew, and fry for another 1-2 minutes, stirring continuously.
Add tomato puree and fry for 1 minute.
Now add the marinated meat and marinade, and mix well.
Cover with a lid and simmer until the meat is almost cooked.
Thoroughly rinse the rice under running water until the water runs clear. Place in a deep pot and add enough water, about 2-3 cm above the rice. Cook over medium heat until done. Drain the water.
Soak the saffron threads in warm milk.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F).

Grease a deep baking dish and add a layer of cooked rice at the bottom. Now add half of the meat (and its sauce) on top of the rice. Add another layer of rice, another layer of meat, and then the final layer of rice (rice-meat-rice-meat-rice).
Drizzle with ghee and the saffron-milk mixture. Cover tightly with foil or a lid. Bake for 20 minutes.
Turn off the oven and let the dish stay in the oven. Remove before serving.
Grate the cucumbers, chop the mint leaves. To remove excess moisture from the cucumbers, pat them dry with a towel.
Mix all the ingredients in a large bowl, removing large lumps.
Serve the raita chilled. A versatile accompaniment to all main dishes, rice, and traditional Indian flatbreads.

The eggplants for Baingan Bharta need to be roasted. This can be done in several different ways. Roast on a gas stove, in a broiler, on a grill, or in the oven. Until the entire skin of the eggplant is charred and the flesh becomes really soft.
After the eggplants are roasted, let them cool completely, and then peel off and discard the charred skin. Roughly mash and set aside temporarily.
Place a pot on medium heat and add vegetable oil. Fry the cumin seeds until they stop 'crackling'.
Add the onion and sauté until soft and translucent. Add the garlic paste and ginger and sauté for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, chili pepper, and all the spices, including garam masala. Mix well and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently to prevent the spice mixture from sticking to the pan. Add a little water if necessary.
Then add the eggplants and mix well.
Add the chopped cilantro and mix. Cook for another 1 minute and turn off the heat.
Serve hot with Indian flatbreads or rice and your favorite dal dish.
Place the rice in a dry pan. Heat over medium heat until the rice turns light brown.
Add the remaining spices and sauté in the pan for another 3 - 5 minutes until the spices are brown, roasted, and fragrant.
There are 2 types of curry powder, spicy and non-spicy. If making non-spicy curry, do not add chili.
Continue stirring to prevent the spices from burning.
Remove from heat and let the spices cool.
Once the spices have cooled, use a spice grinder (or mortar and pestle) to grind the spice mixture into a powder and mix well. Store in an airtight container.
Thoroughly wash the spinach and chop it. Place it in a pot, add half a glass of water, season with salt to taste, and cook until done.
Blend the spinach into a paste in a food processor.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat and fry the chicken pieces until browned. Remove and set aside.
Heat the same oil again, and add the whole black pepper, cloves, and cardamom.
When the spices darken slightly, add finely chopped onion, ginger paste, and garlic paste, and fry until the onion turns pale golden.
Add all the other spices: coriander seeds, cumin, and garam masala. Fry for 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and fry until the oil starts separating from the masala.
Add the chicken, mix well, and add half a glass of water. Simmer until the chicken is cooked.
Add the spinach and mix well. Cook until most of the water evaporates. Remove from heat and garnish with a spoonful of fresh oil.
Serve hot with Indian flatbreads.
Mix the flour, baking powder, yogurt, and food coloring into the dough and let it sit for 24 hours.
Pour the dough into a bottle.
Heat the oil in a deep pan or wok. Reduce the heat to medium.
Squeeze the dough into the hot oil in spiral shapes. You can fry several pieces at a time.
Fry until golden brown, then remove and place directly into the sugar syrup for 2-3 minutes, then remove and transfer.
Serve jalebi warm, possibly in warm milk.

Melt the sugar with rose water in a small saucepan and boil until you reach the desired consistency. To check - carefully dip the tip of your index finger into the syrup, connect it with your thumb and pull apart; if a single thread forms between them, the syrup is ready.
Turn off the heat, add the saffron strands, cardamom, and mix well.
Grill the eggplants over an open medium flame until the skin is completely charred and the eggplants become soft.
Remove the burnt skin and discard the stem. Mash the flesh into a puree.
Add mustard oil, onion, tomato, finely chopped green chili pepper, minced garlic, cilantro leaves, and salt to taste. Mix well.
Add the juice of lime and mix well.
Add freshly squeezed lime juice and mix well.
Heat a pan over medium heat and add cumin seeds. Roast, stirring frequently, until the seeds become slightly darker and more aromatic. Remove from heat and grind in a coffee grinder.
Add the yogurt to the prepared eggplant puree and mix. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes.
Before serving, sprinkle with roasted ground cumin.
Goes well with Indian flatbreads and rice.
Heat the vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the finely chopped spinach, ginger, and green chili, and sauté until the spinach becomes soft. Remove from heat and let it cool.
Place the spinach mixture in a bowl. Add yogurt and salt to taste. Mix very well.
Heat the remaining vegetable oil in a small saucepan, when hot, add cumin seeds, crushed garlic, and pieces of red chili. Fry until the cumin darkens and stops 'crackling'.
Remove from heat and pour into the yogurt with spinach. Mix thoroughly.
Serve the raita chilled with Indian flatbreads and rice.

recipes.title: Deep-Fried Kheema Pan Rolls (Kheema Pan Rolls)

instructions.text: Combine all the dough ingredients in a deep bowl and whisk until smooth.
Place a pan over medium heat. Lightly grease with oil.
Pour a small amount of liquid dough in the center. Spread the dough by tilting the pan to form a thin crepe, then cover with a lid. Cook until the crepe is golden brown. No need to flip.

Transfer to a plate (do not cook a new one at this time). Immediately add 2-3 tablespoons of filling in the center of the crepe. Roll up while the crepe is warm, folding in from both sides. Place seam side down on a baking sheet or tray lined with parchment paper.
Prepare one at a time, placing on the baking sheet. Leave some liquid dough.
When all are ready, dip each in the remaining liquid dough to coat the roll well on all sides, then roll in breadcrumbs.
In a large pot, heat about 1 liter of oil to 200°C (400°F).
Fry one or two rolls at a time until golden brown. Place on paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Serve warm with chutney.
Heat oil in a wok or deep frying pan over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds and fry for 1 minute. Add onion and fry until pale golden.
Add ginger-garlic paste and fry for 1 minute.
Add ground beef and coriander, cumin, garam masala, and salt. Cook until the meat is evenly browned, stirring frequently for 5-7 minutes.
Add tomatoes and cook until soft, stirring frequently.
Remove the pot from heat; add lime juice and chopped cilantro leaves and mix. Allow to cool.
Cut off any thick stems of mint and coriander and discard.
Peel the garlic, ginger, and chili pepper. Rinse thoroughly.
Blend all ingredients into a smooth paste.
Chill and serve with rolls, biryani, samosas, or any other main dishes.

recipes.title: Flatbread with Minced Meat Kheema Paratha (Spicy Minced Meat Kheema Paratha)

instructions.text: Knead the flour into a smooth, soft dough, gradually adding water.
Place the dough in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rest for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into balls of equal size, about the size of a golf ball.

Roll each ball into a circle about 7 cm in diameter. Place about 1-2 tablespoons of kheema masala in the center of the dough and fold the edges upwards, pinching with your fingers to completely conceal the filling. (Note: like dumplings)
Roll out the stuffed paratha to about 15-20 cm in diameter. Stack the finished flatbreads between layers of plastic wrap to keep them ready for further cooking.
Heat a pan with oil and place one paratha. When tiny bubbles rise to the surface, flip it and immediately drizzle ghee evenly on top, using about 3/4 teaspoon.
Fry for 30 seconds and flip again. Drizzle ghee on this side as well. Flip once more to brown the other side. Continue cooking until both sides are crispy and golden brown.
Serve the finished parathas hot, garnished with fresh coriander leaves. With chilled raita, pickles, or chutney.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or pan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and fry for 1 minute.
Add the onion and fry until it becomes pale golden - about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger pastes and fry for 1 minute.
Add coriander, cumin, garam masala, salt to taste, and simmer, stirring constantly, until the oil starts to separate from the masala.
Add the meat to the masala and fry until browned, stirring frequently to avoid overcooking - about 5-7 minutes.
Add the chopped tomatoes, mix, and cook until they become soft.
Turn off the heat, add lime or lemon juice, and mix well. Let it cool.

ingredients.name: Rose water
ingredients.notes: or a few strands of saffron

instructions.text: Bring the milk to a boil over medium heat, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
Once the milk boils, add the lime juice and stir well.
When the cottage cheese starts to separate from the milk, turn off the heat and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Strain the cottage cheese and rinse it well under running water to remove the lime juice.
Place the cottage cheese in cheesecloth and hang it for 1 hour over a bowl to completely drain all the liquid.
Put the dried cottage cheese in a bowl and start kneading until all lumps are removed and the cheese is absolutely smooth.
Sprinkle with flour and mix thoroughly.
Combine the sugar and water in a pressure cooker and bring the mixture to a boil (without closing the pressure cooker).
While the sugar syrup is boiling, divide the dough into small balls and roll them between your palms until uniform.
Carefully add the balls to the sugar syrup. Cover the pressure cooker and wait for the first whistle. Wait another 8-10 minutes, then turn off.
Release the steam from the pressure cooker and let the rasgullas cool completely.
Once cooled, drizzle the rasgulla with rose water or saffron syrup (made by soaking saffron strands in a small amount of warm water).
Chill for several hours before serving.
Mix semolina with water and let the mixture sit for 30 minutes.
Finely chop the onion, tomato, and chili.
Add lemon juice, baking soda, and a pinch of salt to the semolina and water mixture, and mix everything well.
Heat a pan (preferably a griddle), grease it with oil. Pour 2-3 tablespoons of the batter and spread it evenly into a thick pancake.
After a minute, place the chopped vegetables on the surface of the pancake and distribute them evenly, drizzle oil on top. Cook on medium heat until the utthapam is cooked on one side.
Flip and fry on the other side until the utthapam turns golden brown.
Serve with any chutney and raita. Optionally, you can sprinkle cheese on top.
Mix sifted flour and salt to taste, add water to make a stiff dough.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté the onion until translucent. Add garlic and fry until golden.
Add the meat and fry until browned. Add soy and chili sauce and mix well.
Add freshly ground pepper, salt to taste, and simmer until the meat is cooked.
Divide the dough into equal-sized balls and roll out into very thin circles about 8-10 cm in diameter.

Slightly moisten the edges of the dough. Place a tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle. Fold the edges over the meat and pinch and twist to seal the momo. You can fold it in half (into a semicircular shape) and tightly pinch the edges.
Place all momos in a steamer dish and cook for 10-15 minutes.
Serve hot with spicy tomato chutney.

recipes.title: Cheese in Spicy Butter Masala Sauce (Paneer Butter Masala)

instructions.text: Peel the onion, chop it into cubes, and place it in a pan with heated vegetable oil. Fry for 2-3 minutes.
Add cashews. Continue frying for another 2-3 minutes.
Add the chopped (blanched) tomatoes, green chili, bay leaf, and a little salt. Leave it on medium heat, stirring occasionally. Cook for 15 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Transfer to a blender. Gradually add water (about 1 cup), and blend until smooth.
In the same pan, add the butter and melt it. Add mustard seeds, Kashmiri chili powder (or regular chili powder, but half the amount). Optionally, add a couple of whole green chilies.
Add the ginger and garlic pastes, stir and simmer for a couple of minutes. Add the prepared puree to the pan. Simmer on very low heat for 4 minutes.
Add paneer and simmer for 5 minutes.
Then add the ground fenugreek seeds, garam masala, coriander seeds, sugar, and turmeric.
Pour in the cream. Mix well and remove from heat.
Serve with rice and Indian flatbreads.
Heat a shallow frying pan over medium heat and gently roast the whole spices until fragrant. Stir frequently to avoid burning. Remove from heat and let cool.
Grind the spices into powder and mix with the other spices.
Place yogurt in a large bowl and add the spice mixture. Mix all ingredients into a smooth paste with a whisk.
Add chicken to this marinade and mix to coat on all sides. Cover and marinate for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat. Add onion and fry until pale golden. Then add tomatoes and fry until they become soft.
Add chicken and marinade and fry for 10 minutes until the chicken is browned on all sides.
Add water, stir, and cover. Reduce heat and cook for about 10 minutes.
Remove the lid, add ginger (reserve some for garnish), stir, and increase heat to medium. Cook (checking and stirring every 2-3 minutes) until most of the sauce has evaporated.
Turn off the heat, garnish with the remaining ginger and chopped coriander, and serve with chapati or paratha and green salad.
Boil the lentils in a pot with warm water until they become soft. Whip and completely mash.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a deep skillet with a thick bottom and add the chopped onion. Fry until soft. Add the ginger-garlic paste and fry for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken, coriander, cumin, red chili pepper, garam masala, and fry for another 5 minutes.
Add the lentil paste, coconut milk, salt to taste, and cook the mixture until the chicken becomes tender.
Cook the noodles according to the package instructions. Drain and rinse under running water. Pour 1 tablespoon of oil over the noodles to prevent sticking and mix.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a small saucepan. Turn off the heat and add 1 tablespoon of red chili powder, stir. Let it cool.

Serve in a deep bowl (each portion) as follows: noodles, topped with chicken and gravy, then add the chopped garlic, green onions, leeks, and boiled egg. Drizzle with chili oil and sprinkle with shrimp powder to taste. Garnish with potato chips and chopped fresh cilantro. Add a little lemon juice.
Heat a frying pan or flat pot over medium heat.
Beat one egg at a time, adding salt and pepper to taste.
Pour oil into the pan. Pour half of the beaten egg into the pan and scramble it like an omelet.
Place the chapati on top of the egg and flip it over after 30 seconds.
Pour the remaining beaten egg on the chapati and spread it to cover the entire surface. Drizzle with oil and flip again. Cook until both sides are done.
Roll it up and serve with mint coriander chutney. You can fill it with grated Cheddar cheese, or Paneer, Keema Masala filling, or any other filling of your choice.
Add flour and salt to a large bowl. Add ghee and mix well.
Pour in warm water and mix until a dough forms. Knead the dough for 10 minutes, shape it into a ball, and wrap it in plastic. Set aside for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 6 equal-sized balls. Using a rolling pin, roll each ball on a floured surface to a diameter of about 15 cm.
Heat a dry skillet and cook each chapati one at a time until they brown and puff up, about 1 minute on each side. Lightly press the edges with a spatula.
Serve warm with any Indian dishes and sauces.
In a blender, mix all the marinade ingredients and grind to a smooth paste.
In a large non-metal bowl, place the cleaned prawns (remember to remove the intestinal vein), pour the marinade over them and mix well.
Cover the bowl and refrigerate for about 30 minutes.
Heat a pan over medium heat. Add the prawns and marinade and fry until the prawns turn opaque.
Add the prepared masala and 1/4 cup of boiling water and mix well. Cook for 1-2 minutes and turn off the heat.
Garnish with chopped coriander and serve with chapati or plain rice and salad.
In a heavy-bottomed pan, heat 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil over medium heat.
When the vegetable oil is hot, add the chopped onion, frying until the onion becomes pale golden brown.
Add the garlic and ginger pastes and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, all the spices, and salt to taste. Mix well.
Cook the masala (the mixture of onion, tomatoes, and spices) until the oil starts to separate from it. This may take up to 10 minutes. Turn off the heat. Let it cool slightly.
Place the prepared masala in a food processor and blend into a smooth paste (without adding water). Transfer to a separate container.
Mix flour and salt in a bowl, adding enough water to make a batter with the consistency of pancake batter. Whisk until smooth.
Coat each piece of potato on all sides. Fry in oil until golden brown on all sides.
In a separate pan, heat the chopped green chili and garlic, soy sauce, chili sauce or hot sauce, and tomato paste in a small amount of oil, stirring well.
Add sugar, salt, pepper, and potatoes, and mix well to coat the potatoes evenly with the spices.
Remove from heat and garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and sliced green onion. You can also add diced avocado.
Goes well with many Indian dishes. Serve with curry, tofu, or sabzi and Indian flatbreads.
Cut the pork into thin strips. Add the marinade ingredients, with cornstarch last, and mix well. Let it sit for 30 minutes.
Mix dark soy sauce, rice wine, and sugar for the sauce, adding cornstarch last.
Place the dried wood ear mushrooms and lily buds in separate bowls with water and let soak for about 30 minutes.
Squeeze out excess moisture from the wood ear mushrooms and lily buds, slice the mushrooms into strips, and trim the tough ends off the lily buds.

Rinse the bamboo shoots under warm running water. Drain and cut into thin strips. Separate the green parts from the white parts of the green onions, cutting the green parts into 3-4 cm pieces and the white parts into rings. Slice the ginger into thin strips. Lightly beat the eggs with salt.

Heat a wok over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of oil, distributing it evenly across the bottom of the wok. When the oil is hot, add the beaten eggs and stir until they are cooked. Remove the eggs from the wok. Clean the wok.
Add 2 tablespoons of oil. When the oil is hot, add the ginger and stir-fry for about 30 seconds. Add the pork until it changes color and is nearly cooked. Remove from the wok.

Add 2 tablespoons of oil. When the oil is hot, add the wood ear mushrooms, lily buds, and wood ear mushrooms. Stir-fry for about 1 minute. Move to the side. Add the sauce in the center of the wok and quickly stir to thicken it.
Add the pork and eggs, green onions. Mix everything together. Taste and season as needed. Remove from heat and add sesame oil.
Serve with Mandarin pancakes and Hoisin sauce. Place the pancakes on a plate and spread them with sauce. Add the Moo Shu pork and roll up the pancake.
In a large bowl, add boiling water to the flour and immediately start kneading. Knead until a smooth dough forms. Cover and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Transfer the dough to a floured surface. Cut it in half. Use a lightly floured rolling pin to roll out each half to about 0.5 cm thick. Cut out dough circles about 7 cm.

Use a pastry brush to coat 2 circles of dough with sesame oil. Stack them on top of each other, making sure the oiled sides are touching. Roll out to a circle about 12 cm. Repeat with the remaining dough. Cover with a damp cloth to prevent drying out.
Heat a skillet over low heat. Place 2 pancakes in the skillet and cook until browned on both sides (about 3 minutes total; the second side will cook faster than the first).
Remove the pancakes from the skillet and stack them separately. Continue cooking the remaining pancakes. Serve hot with all main dishes and sauces.
Cut the meat into thin strips. Mix with the marinade (all ingredients except for green onion, sesame oil, and garlic). Marinate for 25 minutes, then drain the marinade.
Heat a wok over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil. When the oil is hot, add the garlic. Fry until ready, about 30 seconds.
Add the meat. Stir-fry very quickly until the lamb changes color, 1-2 minutes. Pour in the previously drained marinade and bring to a boil.
Stir-fry with the onion, stirring. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from heat, add sesame oil, and serve.
Mix salt and flour. Slowly add cold water, stirring until a smooth dough forms. Knead it into a ball. Cover and let it rest for at least 30 minutes.
Knead the dough and divide it into 60 pieces. Roll each piece into a circle about 7 cm in diameter.
Place about 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of each circle. Slightly moisten the edges with water. Fold the dough into a half-moon shape and pinch the edges to seal.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add half of the dumplings, stirring gently to prevent them from sticking together. Bring back to a boil and add 1/2 cup of cold water. Cover and repeat. When the dumplings boil for the third time, they are ready. Remove and drain excess water. They can also be pan-fried afterwards.
Serve hot with a salad of finely chopped cucumber and green onion, drizzled with lemon juice.
Add soy sauce, salt, rice wine, and white pepper to the meat mixture and mix well.
Add the remaining ingredients and mix well again.

recipes.title: Hua Juan Buns (Flower Roll Hua Juan)

instructions.text: Place the yeast in a bowl and pour warm water over it. Add sugar and dissolve. Let it sit for 15 minutes.

Sift the flour into a bowl. Add the yeast and water mixture and immediately start mixing until the dough no longer sticks to the sides of the bowl and reaches the desired consistency. This is best adjusted by the amount of water, adding more or less as needed.

Place the dough on a lightly floured surface and knead until it becomes smooth and elastic (about 10 minutes). Add more flour or water if necessary. Cover with a lid and let it sit for 1.5 hours. Knead again and let it sit for another 1-1.5 hours, until it doubles in size.
Dissolve the baking powder in 2 teaspoons of water and add it to the dough. Knead vigorously for a few minutes until it becomes elastic again.
Roll out the dough into a large rectangle, brush with sesame oil. Evenly sprinkle with salt and finely chopped green onion.

Roll the dough into a roll. Cut into pieces about 5 cm in size, take each piece and, with the cut sides facing outward, use chopsticks to press down along the middle. Press down hard enough for the layers on each side to stretch outward, but not so much that the dough is cut through. The layers will push outward, forming two connected hemispheres.
Take the dough by the rounded ends and stretch until they meet underneath the roll and pinch them together underneath. This will create a more rounded shape.
Let the rolls sit for 10 minutes, then steam for 20 minutes.
Mix the flour and water and stir thoroughly. Knead the dough on a lightly floured surface for a few minutes. Place in a bowl, cover with a lid, and let sit for 30 minutes.
Roll out the dough to a thickness of 0.3 cm. Brush the top with oil, sprinkle with salt, and then press a layer of green onions into the dough.

Roll the dough into a cigar shape. Then roll it out again on a floured surface to a thickness of about 0.3 cm, pressing the green onions into the dough if they pop back out. This is very important for making pancakes with the right texture.
Make two or three large pancakes, but it's better to make as few as possible. The finished pancakes are cut into pieces.

Fry in 0.5 cm of vegetable oil in a pan over medium heat. Cook each pancake with onions for about 3 minutes on one side, then flip and cook for another 2 minutes, transferring to a plate lined with paper towels.
Season with salt to taste and serve immediately with soy sauce.

recipes.title: Noodle Soup Tang Mien (Noodle Soup Tang Mien)

instructions.text: Thinly slice the meat. Soak the mushrooms, squeeze well, and remove any tough elements. Finely chop the mushrooms, bamboo shoots, onion, and green onion.
Cook the noodles in boiling salted water according to the package instructions, then drain and rinse under cold water. Place in a serving bowl.
Bring the broth to a boil and pour over the noodles; warm through.
Heat the oil in a preheated wok, add about half of the green onion and all the meat, stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Now add the vegetables (mushrooms and greens), stir-fry for another minute. Add all the seasonings and mix well.
Pour the 'dressing' over the noodles, garnish with the remaining green onion, and serve.

ingredients.name: Green chili pepper
ingredients.notes: small size with seeds and finely chopped

instructions.text: Mix the minced chicken with a pinch of salt, egg white, and about 1 teaspoon of cornstarch paste.
Blanch in warm oil and stir. Transfer, removing as much oil as possible.
Drain excess oil, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the wok.
Add ginger, green onion, bean pods, and green pepper and stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Mix salt and sugar and stir well. Put the chicken back along with soy sauce and rice wine and fry for another minute. Add broth and monosodium glutamate.
Thicken the sauce with the remaining cornstarch paste. Drizzle with sesame oil and serve hot.
Pour 500 ml of vegetable oil into a preheated wok or pot over high heat.
Add small pieces of ginger root. After a few minutes, the ginger pieces should rise to the surface.
Watch the color of the ginger, when it turns dark brown, turn off the heat and let the oil cool slightly before removing the ginger pieces.
Store the seasoned oil in a container.
Wash and finely chop the green onion. Whisk the eggs lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat a wok or frying pan and add 2 tablespoons of oil. When the oil is hot, add the eggs. Cook, stirring. Transfer the eggs out and clean the pan.
Add 2 tablespoons of oil. Add the rice. Fry for a few minutes. Optionally add additional (optional ingredients) and add soy or oyster sauce.
When the rice is heated, add the scrambled eggs back into the pan. Mix thoroughly. Add the green onion.
Serve hot. With a vegetable salad or as a main dish - with fried pork, chicken, or shrimp.

recipes.title: Cantonese Pork in Sweet and Sour Sauce with Pineapple (Sweet and Sour Pork With Pineapple)

instructions.text: Cut the pork into 1-2 cm cubes 'for one bite'
Marinate the pork with soy sauce, rice wine, five spice powder, ground white pepper, and minced garlic for 15 minutes
Add the egg, corn flour, and regular flour and mix evenly to ensure the pork pieces are fully coated. Keep in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Put all the sauce ingredients in a pot and mix evenly before starting to cook.
Stir the sauce constantly in case it clumps up.
Bring the sauce to a boil, then reduce the heat to the lowest temperature and simmer until the texture of the sauce becomes thick and sticky. Then it is ready.
Heat 3 cups of oil in a wok or deep pot to 170°C (350°F).
Fry the marinated pork pieces until golden brown.
Place a couple of kitchen paper sheets on a plate and place the cooked pork on it.
In the same wok, stir-fry the minced garlic and ginger in the oil until fragrant.
Add the diced sweet peppers, white onion, and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Then add the pineapple pieces.

Add the pork to the wok, as well as the sweet and sour sauce, and mix evenly, cooking covered for 3-4 minutes. Then uncover and cook for another 2 minutes. Adjust the amount of sweet and sour sauce to your liking.
Garnish with sesame seeds, green onions, and serve.
Heat a dry and clean frying pan (or wok) over medium heat.
Add sesame seeds and stir with a wooden spoon.
Once the sesame seeds turn light golden brown, immediately remove from heat. Let cool. Store in a dry, clean, and airtight container at room temperature.
Cut the chicken into cubes about 3 cm in size. Thoroughly mix with marinade ingredients and marinate for 20 minutes.
Add a few pieces of marinated chicken at a time and deep fry until golden. Place on paper towels.
Just before finishing frying the chicken, bring the sauce to a boil.
Place the chicken on a large platter and pour hot sauce over it. Sprinkle with sesame. Serve with rice.
Mix all the sauce ingredients. In a small saucepan, bring to a boil, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to low and keep warm while frying the chicken.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Cut the ends off the eggplant, then cut the eggplant in half crosswise. Cut each half lengthwise into quarters.
Align the eggplant slices from left to right and cut diagonally into pieces about 2 cm thick.
Place the eggplant in the water and boil for 1 minute (start timing when the water comes back to a boil). Lay out on paper towels.
In a separate small bowl, mix black pepper and cornstarch into the pork with your fingers.
Heat a wok over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon of oil. When the oil is hot, add garlic, ginger, and green onion. Stir-fry for 10 seconds, then add the pork and garlic sauce.
Stir-fry until the pork turns white and is nearly cooked (about 1 minute), breaking the pork into small pieces with a spatula.
Add the eggplant and stir for a minute. Add the sauce and mix well. Lower the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for about 10 minutes or until the eggplant is tender.
In a small bowl, mix cornstarch and water. Add it to the middle of the pan, stirring quickly to thicken. Once thickened, the dish is ready.
Serve the dish hot.
Rinse the chicken breast and pat dry, trim the fat. Cut into thin strips. Add soy sauce, salt, pepper, and cornstarch. Marinate for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix 1 tablespoon of water with 1 teaspoon of cornstarch. Mix the remaining 2 tablespoons of water with oyster sauce, soy sauce, and sugar.
Heat a wok and add 2 tablespoons of oil. Add the chicken and fry until it changes color and is 80 percent cooked. Remove from the wok.
Clean the wok and add 2 tablespoons of oil. Add minced garlic and stir-fry for 15 seconds. Add the julienned celery and chopped onion. Fry until the onion turns brown.
Add diced sweet pepper, sliced mushrooms, and bean sprouts. Add some salt and sugar, as well as the green onions.

Add the chicken back into the wok. Push everything to the sides and pour the oyster sauce and water mixture into the center. Add the cornstarch and water mixture quickly stirring to thicken. Remove from heat and cool.
Heat oil for frying to 170 degrees. Whisk the eggs.

Place a rice wrapper in front of you. Put 3-4 tablespoons of filling in the center, avoiding the edges of the wrapper. Dip a finger in the mixture of 2 tablespoons of cornstarch and 1 tablespoon of water. Moisten 3 edges of the wrapper, excluding the bottom edge closest to you. Lift the bottom of the wrapper over the filling and fold it in. Fold the sides in, pressing to seal, and roll the egg roll until the end. Press the top edge to seal.
Dip the roll in the beaten egg and coat with cornstarch. Carefully add to hot oil, one or two at a time, and fry until golden brown.
Place on paper towels. Serve with sweet and sour sauce or hot mustard.
Fill a large bowl halfway with hot water (but not too hot, as you'll need to dip your fingers in it).
Set the bowl and rice wrappers on a clean work surface, such as a cutting board.
Take one of the rice wrappers and place it in the bowl of hot water. The rice paper will soften in about 30 seconds.
When the wrapper is soft enough, remove it from the water and place it on a clean work surface.
First, marinate the chicken.
In a bowl, mix the pieces of chicken well with the ground chili powder, turmeric, and salt.
Set aside for an hour.
Add 2 tablespoons of coconut oil to a deep skillet and heat over medium heat. Add the sliced onion and curry leaves.
Add a pinch of salt.
This will take about 5-7 minutes.
Once the onion turns brown, add the garlic-ginger paste.
Stir until the garlic smell disappears.
Add the blanched tomatoes.
Then add the spices - ground red chili, coriander powder, fennel, turmeric powder, garam masala, salt and mix the ingredients well.
Once the oil starts to separate, add the marinated chicken pieces along with the marinade and gently mix until the chicken is well coated with the sauce.
Cover and cook on low heat for about 10-12 minutes.
Usually, the moisture in the chicken is enough, and there is no need to add water.
After, pour in the thick coconut milk, adjust the salt, and bring to a boil over medium heat.
Adjust the consistency to your preference and turn off the heat.
Fry the shallots in oil until golden and add them to the curry.
Add chopped coriander leaves.
Let the dish sit for 10 minutes with the lid on.
Serve with flatbreads or rice.

ingredients.name: Tofu
ingredients.notes: medium firm or soft, cut into 1.5 cm squares

ingredients.name: Chinese black beans
ingredients.notes: dou-chi and fermented soybeans, roughly chopped

instructions.text: Mix ground pork, wine, soy sauce, and ginger in a bowl. Let sit for 20 minutes.
Mix cornstarch with 1 tablespoon of water in a small bowl. Stir well and set aside.
Cut tofu and blanch (put in boiling water for 2-3 minutes). Remove from boiling water and drain.
Heat a wok and add oil and Sichuan pepper. When the Sichuan pepper turns dark brown and crispy, remove and transfer to a bowl with a paper towel. Save to use as a garnish for the dish.
Add the marinated pork and beans to the wok. Stir-fry until the pork darkens. Add salt and mix.
Add green onions and stir-fry for another minute.

Evenly distribute the tofu over the minced pork. Add chili oil, five spice powder, and sugar. Pour in water or broth and simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes until the tofu is soft and the sauce reduces to half of its original amount. Gently stir with a spatula.
Grind the Sichuan pepper in a grinder.
Mix water with starch until fully dissolved and add to the tofu. Gently stir a few times with a spatula until the sauce thickens. Turn off the heat.
Garnish with green onions and ground Sichuan pepper. Serve warm over steamed rice.
Peel the apples and cut them into cubes.
Pour the eggs into the flour, add sugar, cinnamon, and vanilla.
Dissolve the soda with vinegar, add it to the flour, and mix everything well.
Add the apples, cherries, and forest berries to the dough and mix again.
Now it's time to prepare the meringue.
Whip the chilled egg whites until stiff peaks form. At high speed for about 2-3 minutes.
Then add sugar, citric acid, and whip for another 2-3 minutes.*
Grease the baking dish with butter, place the apple mixture in it, and put it in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F)
to bake for 30-40 minutes.**
Check with a toothpick for readiness. It should come out dry when inserted into the pie.

After 30-40 minutes, remove the almost ready pie, cover the apples with the whipped egg whites, spreading it evenly over the surface of the pie with a knife, and return it to the oven for another 15-20 minutes. The egg whites should turn into a crispy meringue.
Melt the required amount of butter in a small saucepan. Let it cool slightly. In a bowl, combine the sifted buckwheat flour and wheat flour.
Add salt, add the eggs to the flour and mix well, you can use a mixer.
While continuing to beat the flour with the eggs, add the melted warm butter, then the regular water.
Cover the container with the mixed batter with plastic wrap and keep it in the refrigerator for 3-4 hours.
Take the batter out and stir. Put a pan on the heat, and while it heats up — grate the cheese on a medium grater.
Take a cup and pour the first egg for the filling into it.
The pan is already hot, grease it with butter and pour a little batter with a ladle.

In Brittany, the batter is not flipped! Cook over high heat, and as soon as the top stops being liquid, the filling is added, first the egg is carefully poured in the middle to avoid breaking the yolk. The egg white is spread over the surface of the crepe, and then the edges are closed at the last moment.
Then, grated cheese is sprinkled on top of the egg white, and bacon is added. Season with salt and pepper.
The egg white should cook, and the cheese should melt.
Now, using a spatula, fold the browned edges of the crepe inside, carefully transfer it to a plate, sprinkle with finely chopped green onions, and serve immediately. Bake the remaining portions.
Mix a quarter cup of boiling water with green onions, ginger, Sichuan pepper, and salt in a small bowl. Let it steep for 20 minutes. Strain and discard all solid ingredients.
Combine all sauce ingredients in a medium-sized bowl.
Add minced pork to the bowl, along with the fragrant water, egg, cornstarch, and white pepper. Mix until a smooth and sticky paste forms.

Place about half a teaspoon of filling (or 1 teaspoon for larger wontons) on the lower third of the wrapper. Fold the bottom side over the filling, then fold it over to the other side of the wrapper. Brush a thin layer of egg white on one end of the wrapper, seal both ends and press them together to secure the filling inside. Arrange on a large plate, making sure they don’t touch. Cover with a damp paper towel.
They can be stored in the refrigerator for a day or frozen for up to a month. To do this, seal the tray with plastic wrap and place it in the freezer.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Add no more than 20 wontons at a time. Stir gently to prevent them from sticking to the bottom. Cook until they float, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Place 7 to 8 pieces in each bowl. Pour 2 tablespoons of sauce and 2 tablespoons of the hot broth they were cooked in. Mix well and serve.
Whisk the sesame paste and light soy sauce until fully dissolved. Add Chinkiang vinegar. Keep stirring.
Mix garlic, green onion, and honey. Add homemade chili oil, 1/3 cup at a time, and mix.
Add toasted and ground Sichuan pepper, 1/2 teaspoon at a time. The more chili oil you add, the more Sichuan pepper you need.
Heat oil in a pan or wok over medium heat until hot. Add pork and sauté, stirring until the meat turns white.

Switch to medium-low heat. Add ginger, green onion, fermented black beans, Sui Mi Ya Cai, wine, and sugar. Cook and stir until all the liquid evaporates and the pork turns dark brown. Transfer to a bowl.
Cook the noodles according to the instructions. Bring the chicken broth to a boil.
Quickly blanch the greens, then drain.

For each bowl of noodles, pour in 1/4 cup of hot chicken broth. Add 1/4 cup of noodle sauce and mix with the broth. Add noodles, top with a few spoonfuls of pork and some spinach. Garnish with crushed peanuts and chopped green onion. Sprinkle with a pinch of ground Sichuan pepper.
Cut the pork into strips. Mix the marinade ingredients and marinate the pork for 20 minutes.

Cut the tofu into small squares, bamboo shoots into thin strips, and then into small slices. Soak the dried mushrooms in warm water for 20 minutes. Rinse and slice thinly. Rinse and slice the fresh mushrooms.
Soak the lily buds in hot water for 20 minutes or until soft. Trim the tough ends.
Bring water to a boil. Once boiling, add the bamboo shoots, mushrooms, and lily buds. Stir. Add the tofu. Bring to a boil again and add the marinated pork.
Add salt, sugar, soy sauce, vinegar, and sesame oil.
Mix the cornstarch with water. Slowly pour the cornstarch mixture into the soup while stirring. Let the broth come to a boil again. Once boiling, remove from heat.
Carefully add the beaten egg while stirring. Add green onion and white pepper to taste. Optionally drizzle with chili oil. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Shrimp in Black Bean Sauce (Stir-Fry Shrimp in Black Bean Sauce)

instructions.text: Cut the bell pepper into strips.
Rinse the shrimp and dry them. Transfer to a bowl and add the marinade ingredients. Marinate for 15 minutes.
In a small bowl, mix the sauce ingredients and set aside. In another small bowl, dissolve 1 tablespoon of cornstarch in 2 tablespoons of water and set aside.
Heat a wok and add oil for frying. When the oil is hot, add the black bean sauce and fresh ginger, stir for a few seconds.
Add the shrimp. Stir quickly and add the red bell pepper. Stir-fry for about a minute, add a bit of water, broth, and rice wine.
Push the shrimp and vegetables to the sides of the pan. Stir the sauce and quickly pour it into the center. Bring to a boil.
Dissolve the cornstarch, stir quickly, and add it to the shrimp, stirring quickly to thicken.
Add green onions. Serve hot with rice.

recipes.title: French crepe with apples and orange syrup

ingredients.name: Wheat flour
ingredients.group: OPTIONAL INGREDIENTS (IF BUCKWHEAT FLOUR IS CORRECT)

ingredients.name: Butter 82.5%;
ingredients.group: OPTIONAL INGREDIENTS (IF BUCKWHEAT FLOUR IS CORRECT)

instructions.text: Melt the required amount of butter in a small saucepan. Let it cool slightly. In a bowl, combine sifted buckwheat flour and wheat flour.
Add salt, add eggs to the flour and mix well, you can use a mixer. While continuing to beat the flour with the eggs, add the melted warm butter, then the regular water.
Cover the container with the diluted dough with plastic wrap and keep it in the refrigerator for 3-4 hours.
Peel the apples and cut them into cubes.
Grate the zest from the oranges, then cut them in half and squeeze the juice into a separate container.
Heat the saucepan, add a little olive oil, and add the minced ginger and zest. Sauté slightly and pour in the cognac. Let it evaporate.
Pour in the orange juice, add sugar, and reduce it by 1/3.
Add the apples, bring to a boil, and add water in portions. Optionally add ground chili.
Let them cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool. If the consistency is liquid, add starch and stir.
Take out the dough and mix it. Place a pan on the heat and heat it.
Once the pan is heated, grease it with butter and pour a little dough with a ladle. Fry one side until a crispy crust appears on the edges, then flip with a spatula and fry for another minute.****
Place the crepe on a plate and fry the remaining crepes.
Arrange the crepe on a serving plate.
Place the filling in the middle, and wrap the crepe. In a tube shape, as a pocket, it's all individual.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar, drizzle with hot chocolate, and serve immediately.
Clean the shrimp, remove the intestinal vein.
Mix the wine and soy sauce in a medium-sized bowl. Add the corn starch and stir well again. Add the cleaned shrimp, mix and marinate for 10 minutes.
Heat a wok over medium heat. Add the oil and swirl the wok to coat the bottom. Add the minced ginger and stir a few times until fragrant.
Add the shrimp, quickly spread them across the wok. Do not stir for 20-30 seconds. Then stir and flip the shrimp. Continue cooking until the surface turns golden, which will take about 1 minute.
Add the garlic-pepper sauce and sugar. Stir for about 1 minute. Switch to the lowest heat. Mix well and remove from heat.
Serve warm with rice or noodles.
Cut the bananas into pieces about 3-4 cm wide (about 5 pieces per banana). Whisk the egg lightly, add water, mix, and then add flour to the batter. Heat the oil for frying to 170°C (350°F).
Using a fork, dip each piece of banana into the batter.
Carefully add a few pieces of banana to the hot oil. Fry until they are golden brown and the batter is crispy (about 3 minutes). Place on paper towels.
Fill 2 bowls with ice water and a few ice cubes and place in the refrigerator.

Heat 1 tablespoon of oil over medium heat, then add 3/4 cup of sugar, stirring constantly until it turns golden brown (about 5 minutes). Be careful not to burn the sugar. Remove the wok from the heat and stir in the sesame seeds.
Using a fork, place a piece of banana into the syrup mixture. Immediately transfer it to the ice water for a few seconds until the syrup hardens. Transfer to a wax paper-lined sheet.
If the syrup starts to cool and harden, reheat it over low heat, stirring constantly until it becomes liquid.
Cut the chicken breast into strips, the carrot into julienne, and the broccoli or cauliflower into pieces about 3 cm.
Mix the marinade ingredients. Marinate the chicken for at least 20 minutes.
Mix the sauce ingredients. Cook the noodles. Use chopsticks to separate the noodles while the water is boiling. Drain the water.

Heat a wok, add 1 tablespoon of oil. Add garlic, chicken, and stir-fry. When the chicken is almost cooked, push the chicken to the sides of the wok and add the shrimp to the center. Fry in hot oil. When the shrimp is ready, mix the chicken with the shrimp and transfer them from the wok to a plate.

Reheat the wok and add 1 tablespoon of oil. Add onion, bok choy, carrot, green bean pods, and broccoli and fry until cooked and crispy. Sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon of salt and mix. Transfer the vegetables to a plate.

Wipe the wok with a paper towel. Heat again and add 3 tablespoons of oil. Place the noodles in the wok, using chopsticks to separate them. Add 2 tablespoons of hot soy sauce and 1 tablespoon of light soy sauce. Stir-fry until the noodles are well heated. Add chicken, shrimp, and all the vegetables.
Add the sauce and wait until it boils. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Broccoli Gai Lan with Oyster Sauce (Broccoli Gai Lan)

instructions.text: Wash the broccoli, trim the ends, and cut into pieces about 5 cm in size.
In a large pot, add enough water to cover the broccoli. Add salt, baking soda, and ginger and bring to a boil.
Mix the chicken broth or water, oyster sauce, rice wine, and sugar. Bring to a boil in a small saucepan, then reduce heat while blanching the broccoli.
Add the broccoli to the boiling water. Cook until the stems are tender but crisp - about 3-4 minutes.
Rinse under cold running water and drain. Pour the sauce over the broccoli and toss well. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chicken with Mushrooms Moo Goo Gai Pan (Moo Goo Gai Pan)

instructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice wine, sesame oil, and 1 tablespoon of cornstarch until smooth.
Add the chicken cut into strips, making sure all sides are coated, and marinate for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them thinly.
Drain and rinse the bamboo shoots and chestnuts. Chop and mince the ginger. Peel and mince the garlic clove.
In a small bowl, whisk together chicken broth, oyster sauce, sugar, and 1 tablespoon of cornstarch until smooth.
Heat a wok and add 2 tablespoons of oil. Add the chicken and fry until it changes color and is nearly cooked.
Add 1 tablespoon of oil. Add the ginger and garlic.
Add the mushrooms and stir-fry for a few seconds.
Then add the bamboo shoots, water chestnuts, and stir quickly.
Stir the sauce and add it to the center of the wok. Cook, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Return the chicken to the wok. Mix and cook for another minute.

recipes.title: Smashed Cucumber Salad Pai Huang Gua (Smashed Cucumber salad Pai Huang Gua)

instructions.text: Peel the cucumbers from the hard parts. Then smash the cucumbers with the flat side of a knife. Cut lengthwise into pieces 3-4 cm long.
Transfer to a large bowl. Sprinkle with salt, mix well and set aside for 10 minutes. Then drain the excess liquid.
Add cilantro and bell pepper along with all the seasonings and ingredients. Mix well and serve immediately.
Cut the tofu into cubes about 2-3 cm in size.
Soak the mushrooms in hot water for 20-30 minutes. Squeeze out excess water and slice.
Rinse the bamboo shoots under warm running water.
Mix the chicken broth, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar.
Heat a wok and add 2 tablespoons of oil, spreading it across the bottom. When the oil is hot, add the tofu cubes. Fry until golden brown. Remove from the wok.
Add 2 tablespoons of oil to the wok. When the oil is hot, add the garlic and fry until fragrant. Add the dried mushrooms and bamboo shoots. Stir-fry for 1 minute.

Push the vegetables to the sides. Re-stir the sauce and add it to the center of the wok. Dissolve the cornstarch in 1 tablespoon of water and add it to the sauce, stirring quickly to thicken. Add the tofu. Cook for another 1 minute.
Remove from heat and add a few drops of sesame oil. Serve hot.

recipes.title: Steamed Fish with Ginger and Soy Sauce (Ginger-Soy Steamed Fish)

instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine ginger, garlic, three tablespoons of oil, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, sugar, cornstarch, and white pepper.
Place the fish fillet on a heatproof dish suitable for steaming and large enough to lay the fillet in a single layer. Spoon some of the sauce over the fish fillet.
Steam the fish over high heat for 7-10 minutes. Carefully transfer the fillet to a warmed serving dish and drizzle with the remaining sauce.
Heat two tablespoons of oil in a small saucepan almost to boiling.
Garnish with green onion and cilantro and gently drizzle the hot oil over the fish. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Da Pan Ji Chicken Potato Stew with Noodles

ingredients.name: Noodles
ingredients.notes: preferably flat noodles of thicker type

instructions.text: Pat the dry chicken with a paper towel and sprinkle salt on both sides.

Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat until hot. Add the chicken skin side down. Fry until golden brown for 4 to 5 minutes. Flip to the other side and fry until golden again. Transfer the chicken to a large plate.
Remove some fat from the skillet using several layers of paper towels held with tongs. Turn the heat to medium-low.
Add Sichuan pepper. Cook until it darkens, then remove. Add ginger, garlic, dried chili pepper, and star anise. Stir a few times until fragrant.
Add the bean paste, cumin powder, and tomato paste. Mix and simmer until the oil rises, about 1 minute.
Pour in the beer. Add the chicken, chicken broth, soy sauce, and sugar. Cook over medium heat until boiling. Switch to medium-low heat. Cook covered for 20 minutes.
Add the potatoes and onion. Cook for 15 minutes.
Add the bell pepper. Simmer until the pepper is soft, about 5 minutes.
Mix corn starch with 1/3 cup of water and stir until fully dissolved. Add half to the skillet and stir. Continue adding the rest and stirring until the broth thickens enough.
When the chicken is almost done, bring a large pot of water to a boil. Cook the noodles according to the instructions.
Serve by placing noodles on a plate and topping with chicken and potatoes.

recipes.title: Pork Belly Bun Rou Jia Mo

instructions.text: Place the pork in a heavy-bottomed pot and add cold water so that it is 2 cm above the meat. Bring to a boil over medium heat. Boil for 10 minutes. Skim off the foam.
Add chili pepper, clove, nutmeg, star anise, cinnamon, ginger, green onions, and wine. Bring to a boil over medium heat, switch to low heat and simmer for another 30 minutes.
Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and salt to the pot and mix. Continue to simmer for another hour.
Remove the lid and continue to simmer for another hour or so, until the broth reduces to about a quarter and thickens slightly.
Cut the meat into pieces. Fill the bun with a mixture of pork, cilantro, and pepper. Spoon some broth over the top and add chili oil or chili sauce. Serve immediately.
In a medium bowl, mix wheat starch, tapioca starch, and salt. Slowly add boiling water while stirring.

Add oil and knead the dough with your hands. Add 2 tablespoons of boiling water if the dough is too dry. Knead for another 2 minutes until the dough is smooth and shiny. Cover and let sit for 20 minutes.
Place shrimp in a medium bowl and add bamboo shoots, green onion, rice wine, sesame oil, salt, pepper, egg white, and cornstarch. Mix well. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.

Grease a paper towel with vegetable oil and grease a cutting board or work surface, as well as the flat side of a knife for cutting. Keep the dough covered to prevent it from drying out while making the dumplings.

Take 1 teaspoon of dough and roll it into a ball. Flatten it by pressing it with your palm. Place the dough on the greased work surface and press it with the greased side of the knife to form a circle 7-8 cm wide.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the center of the wrapper, spreading it evenly but not touching the edges.

Carefully lift the top edge of the wrapper and fold it over the filling towards yourself (it should be a semicircle). Use your thumb and index finger to create pleats in the dough and pinch the edges.
Place the finished dumplings on a plate and cover them with a damp cloth to prevent them from drying out while making the remaining dumplings.

Prepare a steamer and a greased plate that fits inside the steamer. Place a few dumplings on the greased plate and steam in batches until the dough becomes translucent and the shrimp turn slightly orange, about 13 to 15 minutes.
Serve har gow with chili oil or soy sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok or pot and sauté the green onion until fragrant. Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken broth to the wok and bring to a boil. Let it steep for 1-2 minutes before adding the eggs.
After adding the eggs to the soup, bring it back to a boil and season with sugar and salt.
Garnish the soup with green onion and add sesame oil.
Soak the beans in water for 2-3 hours. Drain the water and place the beans in a pot. Add 750 ml of water and cook.
Once it boils, reduce the heat and cook for about 1 hour until the red beans are soft enough. Stir occasionally to prevent the beans from burning.
Add more water to the pot if necessary.
Mix sugar and salt with the red beans while they are still hot and let sit for a few hours to cool.
Mix 400 g of sugar and salt with the red beans while they are still hot and let sit for a few hours to cool.
Boil 420 ml of water in another pot and add brown sugar. Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved and let it cool.
Add the sticky rice flour, ensuring no lumps form. Mix with the sweet red beans.
Grease a container with oil and pour the mixture in. Steam it. Allow to cool completely before removing from the mold (otherwise it will stick).
Cut into 3 cm rectangular cubes and wrap them in wonton wrappers. Fry until the pastries turn golden brown. The oil temperature should be about 180°C (350°F).

Nian Gao can be stored in the refrigerator for 5 days after cooling or kept in the freezer for up to 1 month. Use cling film to wrap them individually before placing in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent surface drying.
Mix the sauce ingredients in a small bowl and stir well.

Thoroughly dry the green beans. Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat. Add the green beans and stir. Cook, stirring constantly, until the surface is brown and dried, about 10 to 15 minutes. Transfer the beans to a plate.
Add 1 tablespoon of oil and Sichuan pepper to the skillet. Cook over medium heat until the pepper darkens. Remove from the pan.
Add the pork and 1/4 teaspoon of salt. When the surface of the pork turns golden, add the dried chili peppers, garlic, and ginger. Stir for a few seconds to release the aroma.
Add the green beans back and pour in the sauce. Cook and stir until the sauce is absorbed, about 1-2 minutes.
Transfer everything to a plate. Serve hot over rice with sauce as a main dish or side.

recipes.title: Tang Yuan Sweet Rice Balls with Peanut Butter Filling

ingredients.name: Butter 82.5%
ingredients.notes: melted, coconut oil can be used

instructions.text: Spread the peanuts in a pan and heat over medium heat. Shake the pan occasionally. Roast until the peanuts are golden, but not dark brown. You can also roast them in the oven at 170°C (350°F) for 8-15 minutes or until the surface is golden.

Chop the peanuts, but not into powder. Transfer to a bowl. Add peanut butter, sugar, and coconut oil, and mix well. Refrigerate for 30 minutes or longer. But not too long, otherwise it will be difficult to shape.
Take about 1 teaspoon or 1/2 teaspoon of filling. Shape into a ball and place on a small tray or in a container. Transfer the finished balls to the freezer while preparing the dough.

Pour the flour into a large bowl. Slowly add warm water and stir with a pair of chopsticks (or a spatula). When the water is fully absorbed. If the dough is too sticky, add more flour, 1 tablespoon at a time, and continue kneading the dough.
Transfer the dough to a large bowl and cover with plastic wrap or a clean damp towel to prevent it from drying out.
Divide the dough into 4 equal parts. Shape each piece into a round ball. Work with one ball of dough at a time. Roll the dough into a long flat strip. Cut into 8 pieces. Roll into small balls.

Flatten the dough into a round disc with a dent in the center. Place the filling in the center of the dough. Carefully seal the filling, wrap it up, and spread the dough. When the filling is no longer visible, roll the dough into a round ball with both hands. It is very important to wrap and seal the dough tightly so that the balls do not fall apart during cooking.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the number of rice balls you plan to serve. Cook and stir occasionally until the rice balls float to the top and the dough becomes transparent.
Immediately transfer the rice balls to small serving bowls with enough boiling water to cover them. You can add a few drops of honey or osmanthus syrup to the hot water to sweeten.

ingredients.name: Corn kernels
ingredients.notes: cans of 700 g, rinsed and dried

ingredients.name: Arbol chili
ingredients.notes: bird's eye variety, you can use an even spicier variety

instructions.text: Drain the liquid from the canned corn and rinse.
Place in a large pot and cover with water so it rises 5 cm above. Simmer while the pork and chilies are cooking.

Put the pork, garlic, bay leaves, and onion into a large pot and cover with water (about 6 cups). Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and cook for 45 minutes. If the pork is not tender enough, cook for another 15 minutes. Remove it, let it cool, and shred into long pieces about 2-3 cm long. Strain the broth into a separate container.

Remove the stems and seeds from the chilies and discard. Place the chilies, garlic clove, and 1/2 of the white onion in the pot and cover with water (about 3 cups). Bring to a boil and then turn off the heat. Let the chilies sit for 15 minutes to soak.
Add the chilies, onion, garlic, oregano, and liquid into a blender. Blend for 1 minute until smooth.
Heat 3 tablespoons of oil over medium heat and pour in the chili mixture. Reduce the heat when it comes to a boil. Cook for 30 minutes until thickened and darkened.
Pour the chili mixture into the corn. Then add the pork broth and shredded pork, along with 2 teaspoons of sea salt.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Shred the cabbage, chop the onion, radishes, and lime. Finely chop the arbol chili. Place each ingredient in a separate bowl. Ladle the pozole into separate bowls and serve.

recipes.title: Stuffed Chili Peppers Rellenos (Chiles Rellenos de Puerco)

instructions.text: Char the chili peppers over an open flame until completely blackened. You can also place the chilis on a dry baking sheet, leaving space between them, to char evenly for 1-2 minutes on each side.

Place the charred chilis in a plastic bag to 'sweat', which will make peeling easier. Remove them once cooled and use a knife blade to scrape off the charred skin. Remove seeds and veins but leave the stem.

Cut the pork into 2-3 cm cubes, place in a large pot, add 1/4 of the white onion and enough water to cover the pork. Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 35 minutes. Once the pork is cooked, remove it from the water. Continue to boil the pork broth until it reduces to 250-300 ml of liquid, about another 10 minutes.
Add roughly chopped tomatoes, 1/2 of the white onion, 2 cloves of garlic, 1/2 teaspoon of salt, and 1/4 cup of water into a blender. Blend for 1 minute until smooth.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan. Slowly pour in the mixture and cook on low heat for about 10 minutes until thickened and cooked through.
In the pot with 1 batch of salsa, add the chopped pork, 1/2 of the finely chopped onion, parsley, walnuts, raisins,
cinnamon, cloves, apple cider vinegar, and 1 cup of pork broth.
Stir and cook on low heat, stirring, for about 20 minutes until moisture evaporates.
Separate the egg whites and yolks, placing the egg whites in a large bowl, and beat with a mixer until fluffy. Add 1 yolk and beat until combined. Then add the remaining 2 yolks one at a time.
Dust the chilis with flour on all sides. Carefully dip each stuffed chili into the eggs using a spatula.
Heat 4 cups of oil over medium heat in a pan. Gently lower the chilis in and fry until golden brown, then flip. Place the cooked peppers on a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Serve by placing some salsa on the plate, with the chili in the center, and drizzle more salsa on top.
Place the shrimp in a large bowl and then squeeze the juice of 4 limes and 4 oranges into it. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Remove the flesh and seeds from the tomato, cut into pieces about 1 cm, quarter the onion, and finely chop the cilantro.
Take the shrimp out of the refrigerator, and add all the remaining ingredients except for the avocado. Gently mix all the ingredients so that the tomato retains its shape.
Just before serving, add the avocado and gently mix. Serve with salted crackers on the side.
Place one chicken breast in a small pot and cover with water. Turn the heat to medium and cook for 15 minutes or until fully cooked.
Remove the chicken breast from the water and let it cool. Shred the chicken into pieces about 3 cm long.
In a large wide pot, bring the salsa to a boil, then immediately reduce the heat to low.
Add the chips and stir. Add the shredded chicken and mix.
Divide the chilaquiles into four portions. Garnish each serving with 2 tablespoons of Mexican cream or sour cream, crumbled cheese, and 3 thinly sliced onion rings. Serve immediately.
In a medium-sized pot, heat the oil and add the chopped onion. Cook until the onion becomes translucent.
Add the chopped garlic and cook for another minute.
Add the cooked beans with a small amount of water, salt, and pepper. Cook for 2 minutes.
Mash the beans. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
Turn off the heat and let it sit for 3 minutes before serving.
Serve with burritos as a standalone dish, as a side dish, or as a snack with tortilla chips.
Chop the tomatoes, onion, garlic, and serrano chili roughly and place them in a blender. Add thyme and 2 tablespoons of water. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.

Heat 1 tablespoon of vegetable oil in a pan and warm it up. Carefully pour in the contents of the blender. Cook on low heat for about 10 minutes, until the salsa turns dark red and slightly thickens. Season with salt to taste.
Pour 1/2 cup of vegetable oil into a medium-sized pan. Heat the oil to medium temperature.
Place the tortillas in the oil and fry on both sides for about 20 seconds. Fry them one at a time, making sure not to overcook them so they don't become hard. Drain excess oil from the tortillas.
Use the same vegetable oil in which the tortillas were fried. Maintain the oil temperature on medium heat.
Add two eggs and slightly tilt the pan to one side so that the eggs fit closely together. Cook until the whites are just set, while the yolks remain runny.

Place 2 tortillas on a plate and add a spoonful of stewed beans. Carefully place the eggs on the tortillas. Top with warm spicy tomato salsa over the eggs. Garnish the beans with 3 chips. Serve immediately.
Heat the oil in a pot until it starts to smoke. Fry the chilies in hot oil for no more than a few seconds, do not overcook.
Remove the chilies from the oil, then add garlic and raisins. Sauté the garlic and raisins while constantly stirring for 1-2 minutes, then remove the pot from the heat and set aside.

Place the chilies in a pot with water. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat. Simmer the chilies for another 20 minutes. Drain the water and remove the stems and seeds. Place the chilies in batches in a blender with enough water to cover them by about 4 cm.
Add the raisins and garlic to the blender and puree on low speed for 30 seconds, then blend on high speed until smooth.
Strain the puree through a fine sieve, using a flexible spatula to scrape the inside of the sieve to push the sauce through.

Preheat the oven to 170°C (350°F). Place the pistachios, pumpkin seeds, and sesame seeds on a baking tray and roast for 8 to 10 minutes. It is important not to burn the seeds, otherwise the sauce will be bitter. Remove from the oven and let cool. Grind in a coffee grinder.

In a blender, combine the ground seed mixture with 1 cup of water, 1 cup of chili puree, the tortilla, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, and masa. Blend on low, then high speed until smooth. Slowly add the remaining chili puree and continue blending until homogeneous.
Heat a pot with oil, add the chili mixture, brown sugar, Mexican chocolate, and cocoa powder. Bring to a boil, whisking well.
Continue to simmer on low heat for 20 minutes. Add salt to taste.
Serve with meat main dishes and appetizers.
Place the chicken breasts in a pot and cover with water. Cook on low heat until the chicken is cooked through, about 20 minutes. Allow to cool, then shred by hand.
Heat the vegetable oil. Fry the tortillas individually in hot oil for about 10 seconds on each side. Place the fried tortillas on a plate lined with paper towels.
Add 1 tablespoon of shredded chicken to the tortilla.
Roll the tortilla tightly into a tube.
Place 2-4 enchiladas on each plate. Drizzle with salsa, add 1 tablespoon of Mexican cream, and sprinkle with crumbled cheese. Garnish with 3 thin rings of red onion.

recipes.title: Fajitas with Chicken in Adobo Sauce

instructions.text: Toast the chilies in a dry, not very hot skillet for about 30 seconds on each side until they become fragrant and pliable.
When the chilies cool, remove the seeds and stems. Place them in a pot and barely cover with water. Bring to a boil, turn off the heat. Let sit in the water for 15 minutes.
Chop the tomatoes and onion roughly. In a heated skillet with 3 tablespoons of vegetable oil, sauté the tomatoes, onion, and garlic.
Add the chili, tomato, onion, garlic, and 1/4 cup of water to a blender. Blend until smooth, about 1 minute.
Heat a skillet with 4 tablespoons of oil, then pour in the vegetable mixture. Add vinegar and sugar. Stir.
Cook until most of the liquid evaporates. Let sit for about 2 hours while the chicken marinates.
Slice the chicken so that it is of even thickness - 1 cm.
Season both sides of the chicken breasts with salt. Brush both sides of the chicken breasts with adobo sauce. Let marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Remove the chicken from the refrigerator and let it warm to room temperature before cooking.
Heat 4 tablespoons of vegetable oil to medium heat in a wide skillet. Cook the chicken until a good crust forms on both sides.
Once the chicken is cooked, remove from the skillet and let sit for 5 minutes. Slice into strips about 0.7 cm wide.
Slice the onion and bell peppers into strips about 0.7 cm wide.
Heat a wide skillet to medium heat with 3 tablespoons of oil. Add all the sliced vegetables.
Cook until the vegetables start to darken and are fully cooked. Cook them 'Al Dente'. Add a pinch of salt.
