Place the vegetables and chicken fajitas on a large dish. Serve with hot tortillas.

recipes.title: Peppers in Walnut Sauce (Chiles en Nogada)

instructions.text: Place the meat in a pot and cover with water. Bring to a boil and cook the meat until it is done (about 20 minutes). When the meat is cooked, remove it from the pot and let it cool. Keep the broth.
Cut the meat into cubes, then mince it. Dice the onion, carrot, zucchini, potato, and candied fruits into pieces about 0.7 cm. Chop the almonds.
Cut the tomatoes in half and add them to a blender with 1/2 cup of meat broth. Blend until smooth.

Sauté the onion in 3 tablespoons of oil for 2 minutes. Add the potato, stir, and cook for 5 minutes. Add the chopped meat and mix. Add the blended tomatoes, carrot, zucchini, and raisins, and cook for 5 minutes until the tomato puree starts to reduce.
Add the peas, candied fruits, and almonds, stirring well.
Cook for 15 minutes until all the vegetables are fully cooked and soft, and the liquid has reduced.
To prevent drying out, add a few tablespoons of meat broth at a time as needed.
Place the chiles over an open flame on the stove burner. Wait until they are charred on all sides. Place them in a plastic bag. When cool, peel the skin off the chiles with a knife blade.
Using a small knife, carefully split the chiles in half without cutting all the way through. Remove the seeds without tearing the chiles.
Place the cream, walnuts, and cinnamon in a blender.
Blend until the sauce is smooth.
Cut the pomegranates in half. Remove the seeds.
Finely chop the parsley, saving a few leaves for garnish.
Fill each chile with enough filling so that it closes. Use toothpicks to secure if necessary.
Place 1 stuffed chile on each plate.
Add one tablespoon of nogada sauce on each chile, sprinkle with pomegranate seeds and chopped parsley.

recipes.title: Filling for pancakes with tuna and processed cheese

instructions.text: Mix tuna with cheese until smooth.
Add roe and finely chopped parsley.
Mix everything well.
Place 50 g of filling in each pancake, and if desired, drizzle with garlic oil when serving.
In a large bowl, beat the eggs and sugar.
Part of the milk can be heated, salted, and thoroughly mixed with the beaten eggs and sugar.
Gradually add the sifted flour to the mixture, constantly stirring to avoid lumps.
Add the oil and mix.
Add the remaining milk and whisk. The batter should be moderately liquid.
Heat a frying pan and grease it with a napkin soaked in olive oil.
Pour the pancakes with a ladle, measuring the portion of the liquid batter so that when pouring it into the pan, it spreads evenly in a thin layer with one circular motion.
Fry the pancakes on both sides until golden.
You can periodically grease the edges of the pan with a napkin with oil. After every 4th pancake.

recipes.title: Filling for pancakes with lightly salted salmon and Mascarpone cheese

instructions.text: Cut the salmon into long thin slices if you have good fillet.
If not, just cut it into pieces.
Mix with mascarpone, drizzle with lemon juice, add parsley and mix everything.
If you want to make it like rolls, then do not mix the fish and cheese.
Just spread the pancake with cheese and place a thin layer of salmon on top.
Wrap the pancake tightly and cut into several pieces.

recipes.title: Corn Tostadas with Chicken (Tostadas de Pollo)

ingredients.name: Beans
ingredients.notes: cooked, you can use canned refried beans, then one 500 g can is enough

ingredients.name: Queso Fresco Ranchero cheese
ingredients.notes: white crumbly Mexican cheese, queso panela, queso fresco or grated mozzarella.

instructions.text: Add chicken to cold water, then bring the water to a boil. Cook for about 20 minutes until fully cooked. Remove from water and let cool slightly. Shred by hand: Cut each chicken breast into three pieces, then tear thin strips with your fingers.
Heat the refried beans. Spread about 1 tablespoon of beans on each tortilla, add the still warm shredded chicken, lettuce, sliced onion, 1 tsp of cream, 15 g of grated cheese and salsa.
Add cilantro, onion, garlic, and 1/2 cup of water to a blender. Blend until smooth for about 1 minute.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat. Pour the raw rice into the hot oil, stir to coat the rice with oil, and cook for about 30 seconds until the rice is brown and fragrant.
Add the cilantro mixture puree, 4 cups of water, and 1 teaspoon of salt. Stir once.

Reduce heat to low (do not cover). Cook the rice for another 20 minutes. The rice should fully absorb the liquid. If the rice is not fully cooked at this stage, add 1/4 cup of water until the rice is completely cooked and the water is absorbed again.
Turn off the heat. Fluff the rice with a fork and let it sit for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with a sprig of cilantro.
Serve with meat and fish dishes.
Chop the garlic and add it to a bowl. Squeeze the juice from 8 limes into it. Add salt and mix with a fork.
Trim all the sinews from the meat. Pour half of the marinade over it,
flip it over and pour the other half of the marinade.
Place it in the refrigerator for 2 hours.
Bring the meat to room temperature before grilling.
Grill the meat for about 7 or 8 minutes on each side.
Let it rest before serving. Lightly grill the green onions.
Serve each portion of carne asada with 4 tortillas, green onions, smoked tomato salsa or salsa verde, and half a lime. It can be served as tacos. Or with a side of cucumber salad.

recipes.title: Black Bean Soup (Sopa de Frijol Negro)

instructions.text: Sauté the tomatoes, onion, and garlic until they darken. Blend the sautéed vegetables, cumin, and oregano until smooth. You can add a little water.
Then mix the black beans with the vegetables until smooth.
Place in a pot. Cook for one hour. (Add water if necessary). Season with salt to taste.
Garnish each bowl of soup with strips of tortilla, 1 tablespoon of Mexican cream, 30 g of diced cheese, and avocado.

ingredients.name: Pork shoulder
ingredients.notes: roasted, boneless and trimmed of excess fat

instructions.text: Rub the meat with salt and pepper. Sear the pork in a large skillet.
In a blender, combine chicken broth, chipotle, pineapple, red onion, chili powder, cumin, lime juice, white vinegar, and garlic until completely smooth.
Cut the meat into quarters, place it in an oven-safe dish, pour the marinade on top, and cover. Let marinate for about 2 hours or more.
Preheat the oven to 100°C (200°F). Cook the meat for one to one and a half hours.
Remove the pork from the marinade and slice it. Return to the marinade and sauté in the skillet for 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Serve with warm corn tortillas, pineapple, cilantro, cheese, red onion, and hot sauce.
Pour the vinegar, water, sugar, garlic cloves, soy sauce, and cayenne pepper (if using) into a pan. If you are using dried chili instead of sambal paste, add it to the pot at the same time.
Heat over medium heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Increase the heat to medium and bring to a boil. Allow it to boil for about 2 minutes.
Add sambal oelek and stir. Cook for a few minutes until the sauce reduces slightly (2 - 5 minutes)
Mix cornstarch and water into a smooth slurry and add this to the sauce.
If it is too thick, add a little water to thin it out. If you are using Clear Jel, the sauce will thicken mainly as it cools.
Cook the sauce for another 2–5 minutes, stirring, or until it reaches the desired consistency. Remember, the sauce will become thicker as it cools.
Pour into glass jars with airtight lids (or sterilize jars for longer storage).
Cool to room temperature and store in the refrigerator.
Mix water with flour and salt. Knead until a smooth dough forms. Divide into 12 portions and make 12 balls.
Place a piece of plastic wrap on a flat surface. Put a ball in the center and cover it with another piece of plastic wrap. Flatten the ball until it is about 15 cm in diameter.
Fill with cheese and jalapeño. You can also add other ingredients: ham, chicken, diced tomatoes. Fold the tortilla in half (like a crescent) and press the edges to seal it.
Place them in the oven until the tortillas are golden brown on the outside and the cheese melts.
You can fry in a pan on low heat for about 3-6 minutes on each side until golden, and when the cheese melts, flip once.
Serve the quesadilla with guacamole, pico de gallo, and refried beans.

recipes.title: Corn Cake Pan de Elot (Pan De Elote)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 165°C (325°F) and grease the baking pan.

Beat the butter, adding the eggs one by one. Mix the corn kernels with the condensed milk. Add this mixture to the bowl with the butter and eggs. Add the flour and the remaining ingredients, as well as a pinch of baking soda.
Pour the batter into the baking pan and bake for 40-60 minutes.
Remove and let cool. Sprinkle with cinnamon and powdered sugar.
Rinse the beans well and drain the liquid. Dice the bell pepper and onion into small cubes.
For the sauce, chop the ingredients and mix them together.
Combine all the ingredients. Serve chilled or at room temperature.
First, blend the red chili pepper, ginger, lemongrass, and garlic in a food processor. Gradually add the vinegar while blending to achieve a smooth paste.

Once the paste is ready, transfer it to a saucepan. Place the saucepan over medium heat and bring the mixture to a boil, stirring occasionally. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat and add the sugar. Simmer this mixture until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Add lime zest and salt to this mixture. Turn off the heat and let it cool. Transfer to a sterilized jar with a lid.
Use as a base for pepper pastes, sweet chili sauce, etc.
Soak rice, cinnamon, and almonds in a bowl of water overnight or at least for 5 hours.
Drain the water. Blend cinnamon, rice, and almonds with condensed milk until a smoother mixture forms and the rice grains are completely crushed.
Strain the resulting liquid into a pitcher and add sugar, vanilla, and milk. Mix well. Add a liter of water and serve with ice.

recipes.title: Corn Tortilla Tacos with Barbecue Beef (Tacos De Barbacoa)

instructions.text: Pour water over the meat, add onion, garlic, bay leaf, and salt to taste, cover with a lid, and bring to a boil.
Once the meat is ready, strain the broth and reserve 2 cups for the sauce.
In a pot, heat some water, when it starts to boil, add the chilis and boil for 5 minutes, remove from heat and let sit in hot water for another 5 minutes.
Place the chilis in a blender along with the broth, cinnamon, vinegar, garlic, black pepper, oregano, thyme, cumin, ginger, clove, and pepper. Blend until you get a thick and well-mixed paste.
Put the pot over medium heat and add the sauce along with the meat, cook for 30 minutes.
Heat a skillet over medium heat. Fill the tortillas with meat, fry until golden brown, flipping several times.
Serve with cilantro, onion, salsa verde, and lime.

recipes.title: Flatbreads with Meat and Beans Burritos (Burritos)

instructions.text: Heat olive oil over medium heat, then sauté the onion until it becomes translucent.
After that, add the meat to the pan and fry everything together for about 5 minutes, stirring regularly to prevent burning.
Add the beans and salt as soon as the meat is ready. Simmer for another 1 minute.
Place the filling in the center of each flatbread, along with tomato, cilantro, cheese, and roll it up.
Can be reheated before serving.

recipes.title: Pico de Gallo Sauce (Salsa Pico de Gallo)

instructions.text: Place the already chopped tomato, onion, and chili in a bowl. Mix well and add lemon juice and cilantro. Mix again thoroughly to maintain the texture of the ingredients. Season with salt to taste.
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and chill for at least 20 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Poblano Chili Peppers in Cream Sauce (Rajas de Poblano)

instructions.text: Roast the peppers over an open flame until the skin starts to blister on all sides, about 10-15 minutes.
Then place them to 'sweat' in a plastic bag for another 15 minutes.
Afterwards, peel them, remove the seeds and stems, and cut the flesh into strips about 1 cm wide.
Heat a large skillet (preferably cast-iron) over medium heat, add the oil.
When the oil is hot, add the onion. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the onion becomes translucent and starts to brown, about 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low. Add the peppers to the onion. Add the cream, salt, and pepper and cook everything on low heat for 3-5 minutes.
Add canned or boiled corn
Serve with rice and tacos.

recipes.title: Tortillas Tacos with Shrimp and Garlic Sauce (Tacos de Camarones al Mojo de Ajo)

instructions.text: Cut the tomatoes into quarters. Peel the garlic cloves.
Heat a large dry skillet over medium heat. Add the tomatoes, garlic, and chili.
Roast the chili for 30 seconds on each side, then remove from the pot.
Roast the garlic for another 2 minutes, then remove from the skillet.
Continue roasting the tomatoes until they darken.
Add all ingredients except for the oil to a blender and blend for 1 minute.
In the same skillet where the tomatoes, garlic, and chili were roasted, heat 2 tablespoons of oil. Pour the blended salsa into the hot oil. Reduce the heat and cook for 10 minutes.
Pour 2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar into a bowl with the chopped cabbage.
Add 1 teaspoon of salt. Mix thoroughly to ensure all the cabbage is coated with vinegar and salt.
Cut the peeled shrimp by making a slit along the length and carefully remove the black vein with the tip of a knife. Finely chop the garlic.
Heat a large skillet over medium heat. Add the chopped garlic and sauté for 1 minute, stirring to prevent the garlic from burning. Add the shrimp and stir.
Cook the shrimp for about 6 minutes. Stir and flip every minute. Check for doneness.
Heat the tortillas in a skillet. On each corn tortilla, place a layer of cabbage, 3 shrimp, and then a spoonful of salsa on each shrimp.
Serve 3 tacos per person.
Prepare the chicken fillet: immediately cut it lengthwise into 2 parts, then wrap them in plastic wrap and pound them well with a mallet on both sides.
Beat the chicken eggs in a small bowl until you get a homogeneous mass. If desired, you can add your favorite spices or pepper directly to the egg mixture.

Grate the hard cheese into a shallow plate. There are also various options here: for example, add finely chopped fresh herbs to the cheese to make the dish more beautiful and aromatic. Also, add the breadcrumbs and mix the mass.
Place a frying pan on the stove, pour in the vegetable oil, and heat the pan. Dip the pounded chicken fillet first in the egg mixture, then coat it in the cheese shavings.
Fry the schnitzels on both sides: first on one side until a dense golden brown crust forms, then do the same on the other side.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Sichuan Hot Pot or Chinese Samovar

ingredients.name: Oyster mushrooms
ingredients.notes: or shimeji, champignon, enoki, king oyster, etc.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

ingredients.name: Sesame paste
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

ingredients.name: Light soy sauce
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

ingredients.name: Black rice vinegar
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

ingredients.name: Chili oil
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

ingredients.name: Sesame oil
ingredients.group: FOR SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE (per person)

instructions.text: Bring a pot of water to a boil.
Remove the paste from the package and fry it in a pan for 5 minutes.
Add the paste to the boiling water and stir well.
Roll the green onions into rings and add them to the broth.

Rinse the chicken carcasses. Place them in a suitable pot, cover with water, and add ginger. Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, add Shaoxing wine, and simmer on low heat under a lid for 30 minutes; season with salt shortly before finishing, then remove from heat.
Heat oil in a pan until it is hot.
Pour ground chili pepper into a bowl and pour the hot oil over it.
Add finely chopped garlic, onion, and cilantro, and mix.

instructions.group: PREPARING SESAME PASTE AND CHILI OIL SAUCE
instructions.text: Peel the garlic and press it through a garlic press. Mix all ingredients in a bowl. If the paste is too thick, it can be diluted with broth or water.
Place the hot pot (divided into 2 halves) on the stove. Pour 2 liters of each broth into separate compartments of the pot, bring to a boil, and reduce the heat so that they 'simmer.'
Keep in mind that the broths will gradually evaporate from the pot, so when preparing meat broth and soup base, be sure to cook extra broth and soup base to add as needed.
Slice the meat as thinly as possible. To do this, it is usually frozen and sliced thinly with a slicer. In Chinese stores, meat is already sold thinly sliced in the refrigerators.

Drop a handful of thinly sliced meat into the boiling broth. Wait a couple of minutes and fish out the pieces of cooked meat from the boiling broth, dip them into various dipping sauces, and enjoy your meal. In addition to the ingredients listed above, you can add whatever you want to the pot – wontons, dumplings, meatballs, vegetables, tofu, etc.
It is advisable to have a small slotted spoon for hygiene reasons, to serve guests ingredients as they are ready, so they do not fish out ingredients with their individual chopsticks.
Heat the oil to 160 degrees while preparing the dough.
Put water with vanilla, salt, and butter on medium heat.
Once it boils, add the sifted flour (at least 2 times). Quickly stir the dough with a wooden spoon or spatula.

Remove the pot from the heat, wait about 1 minute, then add the beaten egg. Continue mixing (you can use a blender) until you get a soft and smooth dough that separates from the bottom. About 5 minutes.
Place the dough in a piping bag with a star tip. Make sure there are no air bubbles in the dough.
Form strips of dough about 15 cm and place them on a prepared tray. You can also place the dough strips directly into the hot oil, cutting them with kitchen scissors.
Fry the churros for about 2-2.5 minutes until they are golden brown, then turn the churros to achieve an even golden color on the other side.
Once they are golden, place them on paper towels, sprinkle with powdered sugar and cinnamon.

recipes.title: Fried Bananas in Condensed Milk (Plátanos Fritos Con Lechera)

instructions.text: Peel the bananas. Cut them in half, then cut each piece in half lengthwise.
Sprinkle the bananas with ground cinnamon and sugar (if desired).
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Place the bananas in the skillet with the cinnamon side up.
Cook for 2-3 minutes on each side until the bananas are golden brown.
Place 4 slices of banana on a dessert plate, then drizzle with condensed milk. Serve warm.
Wash the tomatoes and cut them into four pieces. Peel the garlic, onion, and potatoes, and dice the potatoes (medium size), peel and chop the carrots into small cubes.
Add half a glass of water to the blender, tomatoes, onion, half a teaspoon of cumin powder, a clove of garlic, a little black pepper, mix, and blend until smooth.
Chop the second half of the onion. Heat a pan with oil and sauté over medium heat. When the onion becomes transparent, add the diced carrots. Cook for 5 minutes.
Add the potatoes, cook for another 5 minutes. Then add the ground beef. Mix and season with salt and pepper. And simmer until cooked for about 5 minutes.
Add the peas, sauce, and bay leaf. Mix and cook for a full 10 minutes covered.
Serve with rice or freshly made corn tortillas to make taquitos.
In a mixing bowl, combine butter, sugar, anise, salt, and 1/2 cup of flour.
In a separate small bowl, beat the eggs, water, and orange zest. Add to the mixing bowl along with another 1/2 cup of flour. Mix well.
Add the yeast and another 1/2 cup of flour, mixing.
Add the remaining flour 1 cup at a time, mixing well.
Place the dough on a floured surface for about 1 minute. Cover with a clean damp cloth and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour and 30 minutes.
Separate about 1/4 of the dough and use it to shape bones to decorate the loaf.
Shape the remaining dough into a hemisphere with a flat bottom. Place the bone shapes on top of the loaf and press lightly to adhere. Let the dough rise for another hour.
Bake the loaf in the oven at 170°C (350°F) for about 40 minutes. Cool, glaze, and sprinkle generously with white or colored sugar before serving.
Serve with Mexican hot chocolate or champurrado.

ingredients.name: Goat meat
ingredients.notes: or lamb, you can also use beef and pork

instructions.text: Season the meat with salt and pepper and place it in a large baking dish.
Clean and remove the seeds from the peppers, lightly roast them over medium heat, being careful not to burn them (burnt chili makes the dish bitter). Soak the chili in hot water for 20 minutes.
Sauté the onion and garlic and place them in a blender. Add cloves, cumin seeds, black pepper, roasted tomatoes, herbs, 1/2 onion, cinnamon, and vinegar.
Once the peppers are soft, drain the water, add them to the blender, and blend with all the ingredients until you have a smooth sauce. Add a few tablespoons of water, season with salt.
Pour the sauce over the meat, cover the baking dish with aluminum foil, and refrigerate overnight or for at least 4 hours.
Preheat the oven to 170 º F. Bake the meat for about 4 hours or until cooked through.
Serve the hot meat with sauce, garnished with chopped onion and cilantro, with hot tortillas and spicy sauce.

recipes.title: Baked Dorada Basque Style (doradas al horno con patatas)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place the sliced potatoes in a baking dish, drizzle with oil, lightly salt, sprinkle with fennel seeds, and cover with foil, then bake in the oven for 15 minutes.
Remove the potatoes from the oven.*
Season the inside of the fish with sea salt and place the fish on top of the sliced potatoes. Make three diagonal cuts on one side of each fish and insert a lemon wedge into each cut.
Squeeze juice from the remaining lemon.
Drizzle the fish with 2 tablespoons of olive oil and season the outside of the fish with sea salt.
Cover the baking dish with foil and bake for 20-25 minutes, occasionally spooning the liquid from the dish over the fish.
Remove the foil and bake for another 10-15 minutes to achieve a crispy crust on the fish and potatoes.

While the fish and potatoes brown, prepare the garlic-pepper oil. For this, heat the remaining 6 tablespoons of olive oil in a pan. Once the oil is hot, add the garlic pieces and sauté over low heat until slightly golden, then add the chili flakes and chopped parsley.
Remove the fish from the oven, drizzle it completely with the reserved lemon juice and garlic-pepper oil.

ingredients.name: Cooked chicken mince
ingredients.notes: can use beef mince or grated cheese. The filling should be cold

instructions.text: Mix flour, salt, and warm water, kneading the dough until smooth. Divide the dough into 12 balls, flatten them, and cover with plastic wrap.
Place a ball of dough between two pieces of plastic wrap and press with a plate or skillet (anything handy will work).

Remove the top piece of plastic wrap and spoon the filling onto the dough circle. Leave enough space around the edges. Using the bottom piece of plastic wrap, fold the dough to form a crescent shape. Pinch the edges to prevent the filling from spilling out during frying. Remove the dumpling from the wrap, place it on a large plate or tray, and cover with plastic wrap. Repeat the same with the remaining dough.
Heat the oil in a pot or deep skillet over high heat. Fry the empanadas one or two at a time until golden brown. About 2 minutes on each side. Place them on paper towels.
Serve hot with sauce, topping with salad and avocado.
Place the Achiote paste, citrus juices, oregano, and cumin in a blender. Blend until smooth.
Put the chicken in a large glass bowl and pour the Achiote sauce over it. Marinate for at least 30 minutes in the refrigerator.
Cut the banana leaves or aluminum foil into squares. Prepare a steamer or a large pot with a lid.

Place a piece of chicken in the center of the banana leaf, add some marinade sauce, a piece of tomato, a few rings of onion, 1 epazote, and 1 roasted garlic. Season with salt and pepper. Wrap the chicken in rectangles, just like tamales.

If cooking the chicken in a steamer, simply add hot water as needed. If using a pot or large pan, line the bottom with banana leaves or aluminum foil, add 1 cup of hot water, and place the wrapped chicken evenly. Cover with banana leaves or aluminum foil and cover the pot.
Cook for about 12 minutes on medium heat, bring to a boil, then reduce heat and cook for another 30 minutes.
Unwrap the chicken, remove the banana leaves or aluminum foil, and serve with pickled red onions, habanero sauce, and hot tortillas. It can also be served with rice and salad.
Chop all the vegetables and sauté them over low heat with the meat. Add the taco seasoning.

Layer in the following order: sauce, 6 tortillas, meat with vegetables, beans and corn, sauce, cheese, another 6 tortillas, beans, meat with vegetables, sauce, cheese, remaining tortillas, sauce, jalapeños, and more cheese.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Bake on a large baking sheet for 30 minutes.
Let it cool slightly before cutting and serving.
Mix all the ingredients except for the frying oil. Gently knead until a firm, elastic dough forms.

Roll out the dough until it is about 1 centimeter thick. Fold the dough in half, roll it out again, then fold again, roll out again and repeat this process a total of 10 to 12 times. Let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
Shape the dough into thin rectangles about half a centimeter in size. Place a pan with oil on the heat.
When the oil is hot, dip the dough into it. While the sopaipillas are cooking, they will puff up and darken. Fry on one side for at least 1-1.5 minutes and flip. Be careful not to burn them.
Place on a plate lined with paper towels to remove excess oil.
Sprinkle powdered sugar on top and serve with honey or chocolate sauce. You can also sprinkle with cinnamon.
Preheat the oven to 260°C (500°F). Place the garlic in for 10 minutes.
In a large pot, add the chicken breasts and pour in 3 liters of water. Add the roasted garlic, white onion, oregano, clove, bay leaf, salt, and pepper and simmer for 40 minutes.
Remove the chicken breasts. Let them cool, then shred into thin pieces. Strain the broth into a large bowl and add the shredded chicken.
Chop the onion, bell pepper, and tomatoes.
In a large pot, heat the oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion, pepper, tomatoes, and salt. Cook for 10 minutes, until the vegetables are tender.
Pour the chicken broth with the shredded chicken into the pot, simmer for about 10 minutes.
Cut the corn tortillas into strips 5 cm long and 1 cm wide.
Heat oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Fry the tortilla strips for no more than 20 seconds or until golden brown. Place them on paper towels. Season with salt.
Pour the soup into separate bowls and add the chopped lime. Top with tortilla strips and garnish with a lime wedge and cilantro leaves.
Peel and dice the cheese, tomatoes, and avocado.
Boil the chicken thigh with the bone in 1.5 liters of water for 30 minutes after boiling. During the process, season with epazote, celery, half of the cilantro, bay leaf, and oregano.
Remove the cooked chicken, chop it up. Save the broth.
Cut the tortillas into thin strips.
In a pan, heat the oil and very quickly fry the strips of tortillas in very hot oil. Stir well, trying not to burn them. Remove them from the oil and place on paper towels to remove excess oil.
In the same oil, fry the chili over medium heat and set aside.
Heat the olive oil and sauté the garlic and onion until they become translucent. Add the tomatoes and chili, cut into strips. Mix well. Cook over low heat for 10 minutes.

Mix with a small amount of broth and stir for 3 minutes (the mixture should be liquid). Pass the mixture through a fine sieve and pour directly into the chicken broth. Cook over low heat until thickened.
At the bottom of a bowl, add strips of tortillas, chopped chicken, and pour in the broth. Add some chicken breast, cheese cubes, avocado, and fried chili pepper.
Serve garnished with cream, cilantro, and season with freshly squeezed lime.

recipes.title: Cabbage and Radish Salad (Ensalada De Rábanos y Col)

instructions.text: Mix cabbage, radishes, olive oil, salt, and lime juice, let sit for 15 minutes.
Before serving, mix with cilantro and sprinkle with chopped jalapeño pepper.

ingredients.name: White fish
ingredients.notes: e.g., catfish, cod, halibut, or tilapia

instructions.text: In a small bowl, mix mayonnaise, sour cream, milk, garlic, and half of the lime juice. Cut the remaining limes into quarters.
Cut the fish into strips of 8 x 2 cm.
Heat the oil to 180°C (350°F) in a pot over medium heat.
In a bowl, mix flour, beer, and salt. When the oil is hot, dip the pieces of fish into the batter and fry until golden brown, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Place on paper towels and season with salt.
Place a piece of fish in each tortilla. Top with a handful of shredded cabbage, sauce, a piece of avocado, and cilantro leaves.
Serve immediately with lime wedges and cold beer.
Boil the potatoes and make a puree while still hot. Add chili pepper, lime juice, salt, and pepper, mix well and knead to achieve a very creamy texture. Divide into three parts.
Cook the chicken breast, shred it, and mix with finely chopped onion and mayonnaise. Add salt.
Slice the avocado into 0.5 centimeter pieces.
Place one third of the potato mixture at the bottom and place the avocado on top. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Cover with a second layer of potato.
On the potato, place the mixture of chicken, mayonnaise, and onion, pressing lightly with a fork. Finish with the last layer of potato.
Serve with a salad of leafy greens. Optionally, you can add huanqaina sauce or olive oil.

recipes.title: Chicken in Ají de Gallina Sauce (Ají de Gallina)

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.notes: you can use a whole chicken

ingredients.name: Chili pepper (aji amarillo) or any medium-hot pepper

instructions.text: Boil the whole chicken breast in a pot of water, without salt or anything else. Let the meat cool and reserve the broth.
Remove the seeds and veins from the peppers and blend with a small amount of broth until creamy.
Crush the nuts in a mortar or by other means. Crumble the crackers or bread by hand.
Heat a deep skillet and sauté the chopped garlic and onion. When the onion becomes translucent, add the chili paste, mix well, and add salt and pepper.
In another bowl, add the crackers (or bread) with a small amount of chicken broth until a thick mixture is formed.
Add this mixture to the skillet with the peppers and onion. Mix well and add the chicken breast.
Add 1 cup of broth and reduce the heat, cook for 5 minutes.
Add the parmesan cheese. Cook for another 5 minutes.
If it thickens too much, you can add more broth; if it becomes too watery, add more cheese.
Remove from heat, add condensed milk and mix well. The milk can be replaced with 10% cream.
Serve with white rice, sliced potatoes, half a boiled egg, and black olives.

ingredients.name: White fish fillet
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Freshly squeezed lime juice
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Ginger root
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Fresh cilantro
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Red onion
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Chili pepper
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Fish stock
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Celery
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Crushed ice
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.group: FOR THE TIGER'S MILK (LECHE DE TIGRE)

instructions.text: Cut the fish into 2 cm pieces. In a clay or glass dish, mix the fish, chopped garlic, chili pepper, coriander, and lime juice. Season with salt.
Cover with plastic wrap and leave in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes.
Place the sliced red onion in a bowl of cold salty water.
Boil the potatoes in a large pot of cold salty water until soft, about 25 minutes. Peel and slice into 3 cm pieces.
Add the corn to boiling water and cook for about 8-10 minutes. Cut into 5 cm sections.
Place the lettuce on a plate. Add the corn and sweet potato on the sides.
Drain the liquid from the fish and mix with the onion. Place the fish mixture on the lettuce leaves. Add salt to taste.
Serve immediately with any side dish, white wine, or tequila.

recipes.title: Grilled Chicken Pollo a la Brasa

instructions.text: Place the chicken in a large bowl and make a couple of holes (especially in the breast) from the inside using a thin knife.

In a separate bowl, mix all the other ingredients and apply them to the chicken inside and out. The main thing is that the marinade does not leak out. Cover and let marinate in the refrigerator overnight.
Place on a baking sheet and bake in the oven at 170°C (350°F) for 1.5-2 hours.
Serve with French fries, fresh salad, and sauces such as mayonnaise, mustard, ketchup, chili pepper, or crema criolla.
Cut into pieces about 3 cm x 1 cm and season with garlic, cumin, oregano, salt, pepper, and vinegar. Let sit for about 10 minutes.
Heat a skillet over high heat with a little oil. Add the meat and fry for 10 minutes, the time will depend on how hot the skillet is. Then leave it in a bowl and cover to keep warm.

Now in the same skillet add the sliced onion, tomato, yellow pepper, and a little oil. Sauté everything for a few minutes and add some beef broth, soy sauce (sillao), and vinegar. Add the meat, gently mix everything, and after about 30 seconds or so add a little chopped coriander.
Lomo Saltado should be juicy, so add a bit more broth if necessary.
Serve immediately with rice, fries, and sauces to taste.
Thoroughly wash the peppers, cut off the top of each, leaving the stems. Remove the seeds and inner membranes. Be very careful not to break them.
Fill a pot with water, add 2 tablespoons of sugar and place the peppers in it. Once the water boils, drain it and repeat the process 3 times, adding 2 tablespoons of sugar each time.
Remove the peppers and leave them in a bowl of cold water to preserve their texture.
Pour 1/4 cup of vegetable oil into a pot, and once heated, add the onion, garlic, and cumin, sauté until the onion becomes translucent (about 5 minutes).

Add the ground pepper, meat, oregano, peanuts, and salt to taste, mixing everything very well so that the flavors infuse and the color is uniform. Cook over medium heat until the meat is cooked and the liquid has evaporated.
Meanwhile, drain the soaked raisins and chop them, do the same with the olives and boiled eggs. Add all of this to the meat and mix well.
Use a medium spoon to fill each pepper with the filling to the top, add a piece of cheese on top, and cover with a "lid."
Slice the potatoes and place them at the bottom of a baking dish.
Beat 4 eggs with milk and season with salt and pepper. Pour over the peppers before placing them in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 200 degrees and bake for 15 minutes, until the cheese melts and turns golden brown.
Serve warm, with each pepper having its own potato base.

recipes.title: Potato Papa a la Huancaina (Papa a la Huancaina)

instructions.text: Boil the potatoes, peel them, and when they cool, slice them.
Slightly fry the chopped pepper, garlic cloves, and onion, then let cool.
Put the chili, garlic, and onion, cheese, crackers, and milk into a blender and blend.
Place the lettuce leaves, potato slices, sauce, and garnish with eggs, olives, and parsley.
Put sugar in a pot and heat. Continue stirring until the sugar dissolves and takes on a caramel color.
Add a glass of warm water gradually to the sugar. Stir constantly until the caramel dissolves and stops boiling. Turn off the heat and add anise, cinnamon, and chancaca. Mix well.
Peel the pumpkin and sweet potato and cut into medium pieces. Place in a pot and add water. After 5 minutes of boiling, add cinnamon and anise. Cook until ready.

After boiling, remove the cinnamon sticks, drain the water from the pumpkin and sweet potato. Mash into a puree, let cool slightly, and add yeast, flour with a pinch of salt, knead well. Cover with plastic wrap and let sit in a warm place for about 2 hours.

Heat oil in a pan or pot. Fill a cup with warm water and dip your hands in it before handling the dough (to prevent sticking), take a portion of dough, form a ring with your fingers, and place it in the hot oil.
Fry each picarón for 10-15 seconds on each side, then place on paper towels.
When all the picarones are ready, drizzle them with syrup and serve immediately.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: mashed, variety Bintje, Charlotte or Manon

instructions.text: Cook the potatoes with the skin in a large pot of boiling salted water for 30-40 minutes. Peel while still hot, and immediately mash. Add flour and mix well by hand.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium heat. Sauté the onions for 1 minute, then add the garlic. Sauté over low heat for another minute.
Add cumin, pepper and cook over medium heat for 3 minutes, stirring regularly. Add the ground beef and cook for another 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the eggs, raisins, and olives and cook over medium heat, covered, for 10 minutes, stirring regularly.
Dust your palms with flour. Take 1 to 2 tablespoons of mashed potatoes and shape them into a ball, forming it into a circle.
Place a teaspoon of filling in the center. Close and shape it into a pie.
Heat a large skillet with vegetable oil.
Carefully coat each potato in flour, then in beaten eggs. Fry for a few minutes on all sides until golden brown.
Serve hot, warm, or cold.

recipes.title: Mussels a la Chalaca (Choros a la Chalaca)

instructions.text: Thoroughly clean the mussels with a brush. Place them in a pot and bring to a boil. Remove them when they open to avoid overcooking. Allow the opened ones to cool and place half in a dish.
In a bowl, mix the onion, pepper, tomato, parsley, corn, lime juice, yellow pepper, oil, salt, and pepper. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes.
Place about 1 tablespoon of the mixed ingredients in each mussel shell.

recipes.title: Peruvian Fish Soup Chilcano (Chilcano de Pescado Peruano)

instructions.text: Wash the fish head and backbone very well. Cut into several pieces.
Boil the potatoes and cut into cubes.
In a medium heat, sauté the chopped carrot, garlic, onion, celery, leek, chili pepper, and cilantro.
Add the head or backbone along with 10 cups of water and salt to taste. Cook over low heat for 1 hour. Strain the broth, removing the head and backbone.
Add the cubed potatoes and corn to the broth and cook for 20 minutes.
Add a spoonful of oil and sauté the fillet over medium heat for 2-3 minutes on each side.
Serve in portions along with the broth, lime, and enjoy.
Pour beer over the duck legs, cover, and refrigerate for at least 8 hours. Remove before cooking and pat the pieces dry with paper towels.
In a pot, heat the oil over medium heat, and fry the duck until golden brown. Cover and keep warm.
Add the chopped onion and garlic, cook for 10 minutes over medium heat. Add the yellow pepper paste, turmeric, and cumin, mix and cook for another 10 minutes.

Blend the coriander and spinach leaves with ½ cup of water in a blender. Add to the pan along with the broth, the second can of beer, and the roasted duck. Season with salt and pepper, cover, reduce heat, and cook for 1.5 hours or until the duck starts to pull away from the bone. Serve with a little sauce.
Add rice to the pot with broth, bell pepper, and peas. Cover, reduce heat, and cook for 20 minutes. Turn off the heat and after 5 minutes, fluff the rice with a fork.
Serve the rice with a piece of duck on top and Creole sauce.

ingredients.name: Beef
ingredients.notes: preferably a part of the sirloin

instructions.text: Cut the meat into thin strips, then each strip into smaller pieces, about 1 centimeter each.
Place a pot on the stove, add oil and sauté the onion until it becomes transparent, then add garlic and yellow pepper, sauté for a couple more minutes.
Add the meat and oregano and stir, cook until it becomes slightly golden brown, then add the tomato paste and a bit of salt, cook for another minute.
Add the meat broth, season with salt and pepper to taste, cook for 5-10 minutes.
Add the noodles and milk, stir. Cook until the noodles are ready.
Fry the eggs, seasoning with a small amount of salt.
Serve the soup, placing a fried egg and some croutons in each bowl.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: dried, lightly roasted and soaked for a couple of hours

instructions.text: Sauté the meat with a small amount of vegetable oil. Transfer to a closed container to keep warm.
Heat some oil and add the red onion, diced, add garlic, red pepper and cook for a few minutes.
Add the meat, mix well, add a little cumin, pepper and let it brown a bit.
Add the dried previously soaked potatoes and mix everything. Then add a cup of beef broth and wine, mix everything and cook for 10 minutes over medium heat.
Add peanuts, mix and cook for another 5 minutes.
Serve with white rice or yuca, Creole sauce, and garnish with a little parsley.
Mix all the marinade ingredients. Cut the heart into cubes and place them in the marinade. Mix well. Marinate for 6 hours, stirring occasionally.
Prepare the heart skewers and grill them, or cook over coals, spraying with a mixture of sunflower oil and chopped chili and/or red pepper. 5 minutes on each side.
Serve with pieces of potatoes, corn, and hot pepper sauce.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Mix the flour with the butter, powdered sugar, and lemon zest. Knead until smooth and homogeneous dough.
Add and mix until the dough becomes uniform and smooth (add another tablespoon or two of brandy if the dough is too crumbly).
Form a ball and place the remaining dough in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Roll out the dough and cut into circles about 5 cm in diameter.
Bake the cookies for 10 to 15 minutes until they are just golden brown. Allow to cool completely.
Spread cooked condensed milk on the flat side of one circle, cover with another cookie, pressing lightly. Coat the sides of the resulting 'sandwich' with condensed milk and roll in coconut flakes.
Store in an airtight container.

recipes.title: Pork Tacacho with Cecina (Tacacho con Cecina)

instructions.text: Fry the bacon until golden brown, place on paper towels and let cool.
Peel the bananas and cut each in half. Place in the same skillet where the bacon was fried. Fry over low heat, turning occasionally, until golden-brown and soft, about 25 minutes.
Transfer the hot bananas to a bowl with the butter and mash with a pestle or potato masher. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Chop the bacon. Divide the banana mixture into 8 portions and shape each into a ball. Fill with chopped bacon.
In the same skillet, fry the chorizo, adding water up to 1 cm, turning often until the water evaporates.
Add the meat to the skillet and fry on both sides, remove and keep warm.
Add the banana balls and a little vegetable oil if needed, and fry quickly on both sides.
Serve with 1 slice of ham and chorizo. Garnish with lettuce leaves and onion, as well as with Creole sauce or Cocona sauce.
Boil water, add oil, and garlic. Bring to a boil, add rice and cook until done. Let cool.
Boil the eggs with a little salt.
Melt the pork fat and add garlic, onion, saffron, chicken broth, oregano, bay leaf, and salt. Sauté slightly.
Add the chicken. Pour in water and simmer for half an hour over medium heat.
Divide the rice into eight portions and add a piece of chicken, an olive, and an egg to each. Wrap each portion in two banana leaves and tie with string.
Place in a pot with boiling water and a broth cube, cook for about 50 minutes.
Then remove and let cool.
Fry the wontons in plenty of oil until golden brown, then set aside.
Season the chicken with salt, pepper, soy sauce, and a pinch of cornstarch. Clean the shrimp and marinate with salt and a pinch of cornstarch.
Fry the chicken and shrimp. Add sesame oil and onion. Sauté for 2 minutes and add the pork, tamarind, peas, diced pineapple, pepper, and peach. Season with soy sauce, salt, and pepper to taste.
In a separate bowl, dissolve the remaining cornstarch in cold chicken broth.
Add the dissolved cornstarch to the meat and bring to a boil, stirring until the sauce thickens.
Pour the hot sauté over the fried wontons and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Mushrooms and quail eggs can be added. Serve with rice.
Peel the avocados and cut them in half lengthwise to get 2 equal halves. Then remove the pit. Drizzle with lime juice and season with salt. Set aside.
Preheat the oven to 200℃.
Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Then bake for about 20 minutes. After cooking, chop the chicken into small pieces. Mix with the red pepper and half of the mayonnaise.
Fill each half of the avocado, garnishing with a strip of fresh red pepper and halved olives.
Serve on a plate lined with chopped lettuce leaves.
Pour 4 liters of water into a pot along with all the ingredients except for the sugar. Boil the water over medium heat.
Remove from heat, strain. Serve hot or warm, seasoning with lemon juice and sugar to taste.
Cut the trout in half lengthwise, remove the bones and season.
Heat some oil in a pan. Place the trout skin-side down and add the garlic pieces. Fry on both sides.
Before serving, sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve with French fries and/or rice, criollo sauce, and half a lemon.
Clean the shrimp but keep the head and shell. Heat some vegetable oil and sauté the onion, garlic, ground pepper, salt, and pepper.
Once the seasoning is ready, that is, when the onion becomes translucent, add the shrimp and cook for 5 minutes.
Bring 2 liters of water to a boil. Once boiling, add the corn slices, peas, and rice.
After a few minutes, add the potato and cook for 5 minutes. A few minutes before the potato is done, add the shrimp.
After 2 minutes, add diced fresh cheese, beaten eggs, oregano, and mix everything.
After 1 minute, when the cheese melts and the egg is cooked, add the milk and season to taste, mixing everything well.
Serve hot or warm. Garnish with cilantro leaves or yellow chili pepper, cut into strips.
Thoroughly clean the fish.
Mix onion, garlic, oil, pepper, cumin, green pepper, chopped cilantro, and salt to taste.
Stuff the fish with this mixture, then wrap it in a banana leaf and place it on the grill. Bake for 15 minutes.
Serve with boiled cassava or fried bananas.
Boil water in a pot.
Add rice and cook until fully done.
Add mozzarella and stir while pouring in the milk.
Sprinkle with green onions on top. In Peru, rice is served with fried bananas and egg.
Rinse the fish well, cut into three pieces.
Bring 2 liters of water to a boil, add the fish and let it boil for about
5 minutes. Season with salt.
Finely chop the onion, garlic, chili pepper, and bell pepper, and sauté in a pan with vegetable oil for about 5 minutes.
Add the sautéed vegetables to the fish, and cook all together on low heat for another 20 minutes. Add diced potatoes (optional)
If desired, add the peeled shrimp and mollusks 5 minutes before the end of cooking.
Add cilantro.
There are also recipes where a beaten chicken egg is poured into the soup just before serving.
Serve in a deep plate, with yuca, fried banana, and onion sauce.
Boil the chicken broth in a pot with two cloves of garlic.
Cut the yuca into cubes and add to the pot.
In a blender cup, place a cup of water, peanuts, corn flour, hot peppers, and a bunch of fresh coriander. Blend well.
Add this mixture to the chicken broth and let it simmer until the yuca becomes soft. Stir occasionally.
Boil the quail eggs in boiling water for about 10 minutes. Peel them.
Season the thighs with salt and pepper to taste. Heat a small amount of olive oil in a pan and fry the thighs with the chili pepper.
Remove and place on a plate with paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Serve in a deep dish with quail thighs, boiled eggs, and coriander leaves.

recipes.title: Shrimp in Coconut Sauce Kamba Wa Nazi

ingredients.name: Bell pepper
ingredients.notes: diced red, yellow, green or a combination

ingredients.name: Fresh herbs
ingredients.notes: for garnish, cilantro, basil or parsley

instructions.text: Clean the shrimp and remove the shell, leaving the tail on. Marinate with salt and black pepper.
Heat oil in a large skillet, add onion and sauté over medium heat until translucent or light brown.
Add garlic and ginger, continue cooking for another minute.
Add black pepper and turmeric, stirring occasionally for 15 minutes on low heat; add tomato paste and stir for 1 minute.
Combine with bell pepper and cook for about 1 minute, add tomatoes and salt. Cover the skillet and continue cooking until the tomatoes and pepper are soft, about another 10 minutes.

Remove the lid from the skillet and pour in the coconut milk, bring to a boil and add the shrimp in a single layer, if the skillet size allows, cook for 3 minutes; flip the shrimp and continue simmering for another 2 minutes.
Garnish with herbs and serve with Ugali, Tanzanian rice or favorite vegetables.

ingredients.name: Moroccan spice mix ras el hanout
ingredients.notes: a complex spice blend widely used in Arab and North African cuisines

instructions.text: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes, or until soft and translucent.
Add garlic and carrot and cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Add the crushed tomatoes and ras el hanout and cook for 5-6 minutes.
Add the vegetable broth, simmer uncovered for 10 minutes.
Add tahini and mix well, then add chickpeas and red wine vinegar. Cook for another 10 minutes. You can slightly mash the chickpeas right in the skillet.
Serve hot drizzled with a little olive oil or with quinoa.

ingredients.name: Lentils
ingredients.notes: ideally French green, sorted and washed

ingredients.name: Tomato paste
ingredients.notes: mix evenly in 1 or 2 cups of water

instructions.text: Place the meat, soup bones, and oil in a large pressure cooker and cook over medium heat for a few minutes, stirring to brown on all sides.
Add cilantro, parsley, celery, onion, chickpeas, rice (if desired), spices, and tomatoes. Stir with 3 cups of water.
Cover tightly and bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce heat to medium and cook for 20-30 minutes.
Add lentils, tomato paste mixture, and 2 liters of water. Cover the pot and bring to a boil again over high heat. Reduce heat to medium and continue cooking for 30 minutes.
Reduce heat and add rice (or vermicelli). Cover and cook for another 15 minutes.
You can use 2 or 3 beaten eggs to thicken the harira. (Beat the eggs with 1/4 cup of fresh lemon juice.) Add the eggs in a thin stream to the boiling soup, stirring constantly.
Serve hot with fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: Lamb
ingredients.notes: or young lamb, cut into pieces of 5-7 cm

instructions.text: Mix the meat with the onion, garlic, and half of the spices. Cover and leave in the refrigerator overnight.
Chop the onion and place the onion rings at the bottom of the tajine. Layer the meat on top. Add water, cover with a lid, and place the tajine on a diffuser over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to the minimum necessary to maintain a simmer.
Cook for 3 hours or longer until the meat is very tender.
While the meat is cooking, place the prunes and dried apricots in a small pot and cover with water. Simmer over medium heat, partially covered, until the prunes become soft, about 15 to 30 minutes.
Drain the water from the prunes and apricots, then add 1/2 cup of reserved meat liquid. Add honey, saffron, and cinnamon, and cook for another 5-10 minutes.
Transfer the meat to a large plate and top with the prunes and apricots and syrup. You can add dates and raisins.
Garnish with sesame and roasted almonds, cilantro. Serve with Moroccan bread.
Peel the eggplants and cut them into pieces about 1 cm thick. Drizzle a large baking sheet lined with parchment paper generously with a tablespoon of olive oil and evenly distribute the slices.

Sprinkle with a pinch of salt and roast in the oven at 200°C (400°F) until the slices are cooked and browned, about 35 minutes. Once they are golden brown, remove them from the oven and let cool for a few minutes.
Mix all the other ingredients in a large deep skillet or pot. Cover and bring to a boil for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.

Cut the eggplant slices into smaller pieces. Add them to the sauce and mix well. Reduce the heat and cook for another 5 minutes. Slightly mash the tomatoes and eggplants with a spoon or potato masher.
Continue cooking on low heat for 10 minutes or until the liquid reduces.
Garnish with cilantro, add olive oil and freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Serve warm or cold with meat dishes and crusty bread.
Preheat the grill or skillet to high heat. Place the green pepper on the grill and turn occasionally every 3-4 minutes until each side is lightly charred and soft. Then remove and cool.
Peel and roughly chop the tomatoes into 1.5 cm pieces. Peel the green pepper and cut into 1.5 cm pieces.

In a deep skillet, heat the olive oil over medium heat and add the chopped tomatoes, garlic, spices, herbs, salt, and sugar. Cover with a lid for 10 minutes until the tomatoes soften. Stir occasionally.
Add the chopped green pepper and mix all the ingredients together. Leave on low heat for 10 minutes until the liquid evaporates.
Serve warm or cold, as a side dish or with bread.

ingredients.name: Chicken
ingredients.notes: legs and thighs can be used. Traditionally, pigeon is used

instructions.text: In a large skillet, heat the olive oil and add the chicken, onion, turmeric, ginger, saffron, salt, and pepper. Leave on medium heat for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add parsley and cilantro along with 1 cup of water. Bring to a boil, reduce heat to medium and cover. Cook on low heat until chicken is cooked through, about 50 minutes.
Place the blanched almonds on a baking sheet and drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil. Bake in the oven until golden, about 18 minutes. Allow to cool.
Place the almonds in a food processor, add 1 ½ teaspoons of cinnamon, 3 tablespoons of powdered sugar, and grind to a coarse texture.

When the chicken is cooked, remove it from the skillet (leaving the cooked herbs and onions). Add honey, 2 tablespoons of powdered sugar, and 1 teaspoon of ground cinnamon. Cook on medium or low heat uncovered until all the liquid evaporates and the onion turns golden brown, about 30-40 minutes. Stir occasionally to prevent the onion from sticking to the pan.
After the chicken cools to room temperature, remove the skin and bones. Cut the chicken into smaller pieces (about 1 cm). Place in the refrigerator.

• In a small skillet, melt 20 g of butter, beat the eggs and scramble them. Set aside until ready to assemble. Ensure that the scrambled eggs are not overcooked and not runny, as the liquid can affect the dough during assembly.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Unroll the sheets of dough, keeping them under a damp cloth to prevent drying out, and cut the sheets of dough according to the size of the dish.

Melt the remaining butter. Place a sheet of filo on the working surface, brush it with melted butter, and cover it with another sheet of filo, which is also brushed with butter. Carefully place the two layers of filo dough in a shallow dish.

Layer in the following order: a layer of chicken pieces (about 1 cm), a layer of caramelized onion (less than 0.5 cm), a layer of scrambled eggs (about 1 cm), and finally, a layer of almonds (less than 0.5 cm).
Fold the dough to cover the pie. Lightly brush with melted butter. Carefully flip the bastilla out of the dish and place it in a greased baking tray.
Brush the pies with beaten egg and bake in the oven until golden, about 25 min. Serve hot and sprinkle with powdered sugar and cinnamon.
In a large bowl, mix all the ingredients for the kefta by hand or with a large spoon. Add salt to taste.
Melt the butter in a large skillet and add the minced meat. Cook over medium heat, stirring to break the meat into small pieces, until the meat is browned and fully cooked, about 7 minutes.
Add three eggs and cook over medium heat until the liquid evaporates. Transfer the cooked kefta to a large bowl.
Unroll the filo pastry and cut it into strips 10 cm wide and 30 cm long. Cover the rectangles with a damp towel to prevent drying out.

Place a rectangle of dough on the work surface and brush it with melted butter. Place 3 tablespoons of the kefta and egg mixture in the top corner of the rectangle and fold to form a triangle, folding right and left until a triangle is formed.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Transfer the triangles to a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Brush with egg yolk and bake in the oven for 20-25 minutes until golden.
Serve the briouate warm with mint leaves, sprinkled with powdered sugar and ground cinnamon.

recipes.title: Sweet Pancakes with Almond Filling Briouate (Briouate)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Place the blanched almonds on a baking tray and drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Bake in the oven until lightly golden, about 20 minutes.
Once the almonds have cooled, chop them in a food processor with powdered sugar, 2 tablespoons of orange blossom water, cinnamon, and salt.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Transfer the almond mixture to a bowl and add 20 g of solid coconut oil. Mix until all ingredients are combined and knead into a firm mass.
Unroll the dough and cut it into strips 6 cm wide and 30 cm long. Cover with a damp towel to prevent drying out.
Place a rectangle of filo on the work surface and brush it with coconut oil. Place a spoonful of the almond paste at one corner of the rectangle and fold to form a triangle, right and left.
Brush with melted coconut oil and place in the oven for 10 to 12 minutes until golden.
Heat the honey with 1 tablespoon of orange blossom water.
Immediately transfer the finished briouates to the boiling honey for 2–3 minutes (turning them if necessary).
Transfer the briouates to a flat dish and let cool before serving. Garnish with crushed nuts and/or chopped dried fruits.

ingredients.name: Red olives
ingredients.notes: such as Kalamata, pitted and chopped

instructions.text: Wash the spinach thoroughly several times in a large bowl. Drain the water completely.
Cook on low heat for 15-20 minutes until the leaves darken and become soft. Drain and squeeze out the water.
Heat the olive oil, add the spinach and the remaining ingredients (except olives), stir and cook over medium heat for 5-10 minutes.
Stir occasionally. Remove the lid and simmer for another 5 minutes until all the liquid evaporates.
Serve warm or at room temperature, garnished with olives and lemon zest.
In a clean pot, place the gunpowder tea and half a glass of boiling water. Let it steep for 1 minute and pour the water into a separate cup.
Repeat the same process, pouring half a glass of boiled water into the same teapot, but this time shake the teapot several times to rinse the tea leaves. Pour out the water.

Now add fresh mint, sugar, and the first cup of water. Fill the teapot with the remaining boiling water and let it stand over medium heat until it boils. It's important for the tea to slowly come to a boil.
When it comes to a boil, carefully open the teapot and stir the tea with a large spoon to ensure that the sugar dissolves well.
Serve hot. Place some fresh mint in each cup.
You can add any other aromatic herbs such as verbena, sage, and geranium.
In a large pot over medium heat, heat the olive oil and add the onion. Cover and let the onion cook until soft and translucent, about 10 minutes.
Add the diced pepper, herbs, spices, and salt, and cover. Let it cook until the pepper is done and soft, about 5 - 7 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Once the pepper is soft, increase the heat and add the ground meat. Stir to break up the meat, cooking for about 5 minutes. Allow to cool or even place in the refrigerator.
In a large bowl, mix all the ingredients to form a dough. If the mixture is too dry, gradually add a couple of tablespoons of water.
Lightly dust the work surface with flour and knead for 10 minutes until the dough is light and soft.

Divide the dough into 12 small balls (7 cm in diameter), roll into flatbreads about 15 cm, place on a baking sheet, lightly drizzle with olive oil, cover with plastic wrap, and let rest for 30 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Lightly grease the surface with olive oil, place a ball of dough on it, roll out to 15 cm in diameter, and pour about one teaspoon of olive oil. Add the filling.
• Using your hands, roll the dough very thinly to form a circle or square.
• Place a small amount of filling on the rolled-out dough, ensuring the filling does not go beyond the edges (place about 2-3 tablespoons of filling for 7 cm diameter dough balls).
Fold each side of the dough vertically, and then horizontally towards the center to form a square, making sure the filling remains enclosed, and place the msemmen on a greased baking sheet.
Place in the preheated oven for 18–20 minutes and bake until lightly golden.
Serve hot with tea for breakfast or as an evening snack.
Drain the water from the peas and rinse them again. Transfer to a large pot, add 1 liter of water (completely cover with water). Add the garlic cloves (unpeeled) and baking soda.
Bring to a boil, cover with a lid, and reduce the heat to low. Let simmer for 20 minutes.
Remove the garlic cloves, crush and mash them. Transfer the garlic puree, olive oil, paprika, cumin, and salt to the pot.
Cover with a lid and let it simmer on low heat for another 20 minutes. Stir occasionally.
Once the peas are fully cooked and soft, mash or blend until smooth.
Serve hot with bread or flatbreads, drizzled with olive oil, paprika, and cumin, and topped with freshly chopped onions.
Soak the fenugreek seeds in water overnight, then drain the water. Soak the lentils for a few hours.
Place the chicken with all these spices and oil in a pot, mix well. And leave to marinate for several hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
Put the chicken on the stove over medium heat and cook covered, stirring occasionally, for 15-20 minutes.
Add the lentils, fenugreek seeds, saffron, parsley, cilantro, and 3-4 cups of water. Cover and simmer over medium heat for one hour or until the lentils are soft and the chicken is well cooked.
Mix the dry ingredients for the dough in a large bowl. Then add a little warm water until the dough is soft and sticky. Knead the dough for a few minutes.
Form into balls, and let sit for 10 minutes. Then roll out into thin cakes on a work surface.
Heat a shallow pan. Place the dough and fry on each side until golden brown. Place in a towel to keep warm for longer.
Cut the cakes into small pieces and place them on a plate. Top with the cooked chicken and lentils along with the broth, allowing the dough to soak up the flavors.

recipes.title: Couscous with Seven Vegetables (Seven Vegetables Couscous)

ingredients.name: Chickpeas
ingredients.notes: canned, or 125 g dried chickpeas soaked in cold water overnight

ingredients.name: Fresh tomato
ingredients.notes: cut into large pieces about 2 cm

ingredients.name: Sweet potato
ingredients.notes: peeled and cut into large pieces

instructions.text: Mix the meat, onion, tomatoes, oil, and spices in the bottom of a pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for about 10-15 minutes or until the meat is browned.
Add 1.5 liters of water and chickpeas. Bring to a boil, reduce the heat, and place the coriander bouquet in the pot. Cover and let simmer on low heat for 45-50 minutes.

Grease the steaming container with oil. Place dry couscous in a very large bowl and thoroughly knead with vegetable oil using your hands, tossing and rubbing it between your palms. Transfer to the steamer container. Steam for about 15 minutes.

When the couscous has cooled (it can be handled without burning), mix it by hand and return it to the steamer, leaving it on the heat for 10 minutes and repeating the process (the couscous should be steamed 3-4 times).
Removing the couscous from the heat for the last time, immediately add a teaspoon of salt and 2 tablespoons each of olive oil and butter or ghee. Mix everything well.
Add cabbage, turnip, and carrot to the meat, cover, and let it stew for 35 minutes. Add sweet potato and cook for another 20 minutes.
Set aside some broth (about 6 tablespoons) in a separate pot or large deep skillet over medium heat and add zucchini. Cover and cook for 20 minutes until fully cooked.
Carefully remove the meat with tongs and cut into individual pieces.
Place the couscous on a plate and add the meat, vegetables, and a few tablespoons of broth to moisten it. You can add raisins (optional).
Boil the potatoes with the skin for at least 30 minutes or until cooked. Peel the potatoes and mash them.
Add breadcrumbs, garlic, onion, cumin, turmeric, parsley, beaten eggs, salt, and pepper.
Form fritters about 5-7 cm in diameter.
Heat enough oil for frying. Dredge the maakouda in flour on both sides. Fry on one side, then on the other.
Place on paper towels. Serve hot with freshly squeezed lemon and tomato sauce or harissa, as well as with bread as a sandwich.

recipes.title: Meatballs with Egg Kefta Mkaouara (Kefta Mkaouara)

instructions.text: Mix the ground meat, onion, garlic, paprika, cumin, cinnamon, hot paprika, salt, pepper, parsley, and cilantro by hand to shape the mixture into round meatballs about 1 cm in size.
Drizzle olive oil or clarified butter in the bottom of a tagine or deep skillet with a tight-fitting lid over medium heat. A diffuser is necessary for clay tagines.
Add the chopped onion and cook until soft. Sprinkle with minced garlic and place the meatballs mainly in a single layer over the onion. Cook, stirring gently, until browned.
Layer enough tomatoes to mainly cover the meatballs.
Add cumin, paprika, cinnamon, hot paprika and gently mix. Cover with a lid, reduce the heat to low, and let simmer for 30 minutes.
Remove the lid, break the eggs into separate areas between the meatballs and sprinkle with parsley, cilantro, salt, and pepper. Cover again and cook for 7-10 minutes.
Serve immediately from the tagine with crusty bread.
Serve with rice and fresh herbs.

recipes.title: Layered Nut Pastry Baklava Moroccan Style (Baklava)

instructions.text: In a small saucepan, combine water, sugar, and orange blossom water. Place over medium heat, stirring constantly to dissolve the sugar, and bring to a boil.
Reduce the heat and let the syrup simmer for 12-15 minutes until it thickens. Remove from heat.
You can use honey instead of syrup. Heat honey in a saucepan until it becomes hot, adding a little orange blossom water to taste.

You can use ready-made phyllo dough (500 g) or mix semolina, white flour, and salt in a large bowl. Add the eggs, vegetable oil, orange blossom water, and enough warm water to make a pliable but not sticky dough.
Knead until smooth, cover with plastic wrap or a towel, and let it rest for 30 to 40 minutes.
If desired, lightly toast the almonds in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 5-7 minutes.
Grind the almonds to a coarse powder texture, then mix with sugar, cinnamon (if desired), and a small amount of syrup or honey. Set aside.
Combine melted butter with vegetable oil in a small bowl. Grease the inside of the baking dish well.

Divide the dough into 24 smooth balls. Keep the balls covered. Sprinkle the work surface with corn starch and roll one of the balls into a rectangle the thickness of paper, slightly larger than the baking dish. Place it in the baking dish and grease it well with butter; trim the excess edges.
Repeat until half of the dough is used, totaling 12 layers.
Spread the almond filling over the layered dough, pressing down slightly. Drizzle the almonds with a little melted butter.
Roll out the remaining dough balls, layering them over the almond filling and generously brushing each layer with the melted butter mixture, including the top layer.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). If necessary, warm the syrup and keep it warm.

Using a long sharp knife, carefully cut the unbaked baklava into small diamond or square pieces, trying to cut through all layers of dough and filling. Decorate each piece with a whole blanched almond (gently push it into the dough).
Bake the baklava in the preheated oven for about 25 minutes or until golden brown. Remove from the oven.
Carefully pour the warm syrup over the baklava. Leave the baklava overnight to cool and fully absorb the syrup before serving.

ingredients.name: Lemon (amount as desired, preferably Meyer lemon with thin skin

instructions.text: Carefully cut off the very tips of the lemons, exposing the white core. Place the lemon on one side. On the other side, make two large cuts as if slicing into quarters, stopping about 2 cm from the bottom.
Put one teaspoon of salt into the cavity of each lemon.
Place one teaspoon of salt at the bottom of the jar. Place the lemon in the jar cut side down, pressing firmly to release the lemon juice.
Add a teaspoon of salt on top of the lemon. Firmly press the second lemon on top of the first lemon. Repeat with the third lemon, pressing down firmly. Add a teaspoon of salt on top of the lemon.

The jar should be half filled with lemon juice. If necessary, squeeze some extra lemon juice into the jar to bring it to the middle, slice this into wedges and place it in the jar. Pour boiled/cooled water into the jar to fill it to the top.
Tightly close the jar and keep it in a cool dark place for 4 weeks, shaking it and turning the jar upside down several times a day to evenly distribute the salt and juice.
After 3 days, transfer the jar to the refrigerator and leave for at least 3 weeks before using. Can be stored in the refrigerator for up to a year.
Use for garnishing and decorating dishes. In whatever dish the lemons are used - dispose of the pulp (the peel is used) and thoroughly rinse the peel to remove excess salt.
Prepare fresh orange juice. Peel the carrot and grate it on a fine or medium grater.
In a large bowl, place the grated carrot, add the orange juice, freshly squeezed lemon juice, orange water, a pinch of salt, and sugar. Mix well.
Chill the salad for 30 minutes before serving. Sprinkle with cinnamon. You can decorate with raisins and nuts or fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: Beef fillet
ingredients.notes: or venison, rabbit, game, horse meat, anything except pork

instructions.text: Cut the meat into strips 5 cm wide. Add salt, coriander seeds, brown sugar, and black pepper.
Spread part of the mixture on the bottom of a deep rectangular dish. Place the strips of meat, sprinkle with the remaining mixture.
Alternate layers of meat strips with the spice and salt mixture.
Pour vinegar over, leave for a few hours (the longer you leave it, the saltier it will be).
Mix 100 ml of vinegar with water and rinse the meat. Hang the meat in a well-ventilated area for 3 to 6 days.
Slice into pieces and serve with cold beer.
Dice the bell pepper and chili, grate the carrot, and shred the cabbage.
Heat oil over medium heat, add onion and cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add all the spices: garlic, ginger, smoked paprika, curry, cayenne pepper, thyme and continue stirring for 1 minute.
Add tomatoes, sweet pepper, carrot, and cabbage. Simmer on low heat for about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the baked beans and the bouillon cube. Continue cooking for about 2-3 minutes.
Chakalaka should not be of a liquid consistency. Serve hot or cold.
Sear the meat, season with salt and pepper, and cook over medium heat until done. Remove the meat.
Add the onions and sauté until soft, about 8 minutes. Return the meat and add beef broth. Reduce the heat to low and simmer for an hour.
Add the carrots and potatoes and continue to stew for another 30 minutes.
Mix sugar, curry powder, and turmeric with milk and add to the meat. Bring to a boil and cook for another 30 minutes.
Serve with rice or mieliepap (corn porridge).
Pour the milk into a separate bowl and soak the bread.
In vegetable oil, sauté the onion and garlic, then add the minced meat. Sauté lightly for a few minutes until the meat is soft and crumbly. Break up large chunks with a spatula.
Add all the spices, grated carrot, lemon juice, soaked white bread, almonds, and mix.
Then add the parsley, raisins, and halved dried apricots. Sauté for a few minutes and turn off the heat.

Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Lightly beat the milk and eggs. Transfer the mixture to a baking dish, pour the milk and egg mixture over it, garnish with bay leaves, and bake covered in the oven for 40 minutes.
Serve hot with basmati rice, chutney, coconut flakes, tomato sambals, or bananas with condensed milk.
Soak the raisins in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Bring the water to a boil over medium heat. Add all ingredients, including the raisins, and bring to a boil again.
Reduce heat to low, cover tightly, and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Remove from heat, let sit for another 15 minutes. Remove the cinnamon stick, fluff with a fork, and you can add 1-2 tablespoons of oil.
Serve hot with bobotie.

ingredients.name: Lamb meat
ingredients.notes: neck or chop on the bone

instructions.text: Heat a cast iron or heavy pot on the stove and add oil. Once the oil is hot, brown the meat in batches until it is golden brown.
Remove the meat and sauté the onion, garlic, and spices in the same pan until the onion is soft.
Add the meat and broth to the pot and simmer on low heat until the meat is tender.
Place the meat in the oven. After about 1 hour, add the waterblommetjies and potatoes and, if it needs more broth, but not too much. Cook for another hour or so.
Season with salt and pepper before serving, add a bit of lemon juice, and garnish with parsley.
Serve on fluffy white rice with a sweet and sour cucumber salad.
Peel the cucumber, thinly slice it in half and then into wedges.
Remove seeds from the pepper and finely chop.
Mix soy sauce, sugar, shallot, chili, ginger, lime juice, and mint and stir well.
Add the cucumber and mix well. Cover and let sit at room temperature for 1 hour.
Mix the corn and beans together and soak overnight. Drain the water after soaking and place the mixture in a large pot.
Add 5-6 cups of water and let it simmer slowly, allowing most of the water to evaporate. Cook until the corn and beans are soft. Season with salt to taste.
Sauté the onion in a small amount of oil until translucent. Add garlic and curry powder. Cook for 1-2 minutes.
Add the tomato, broth, ½ cup of water, and potato. Cook until the potato is slightly soft.
Add the corn and bean mixture. Cook slowly until the potato, corn, and beans are soft.
Stir in the butter, season with salt and pepper. Serve hot with meat dishes.
Sauté onion, carrot, leek, greens, garlic, chili pepper, and celery in oil.
Add tomato paste and brown sugar, curry, turmeric. Cook for a few minutes, then add broth and wine. Bring to a boil.
Sear the lamb in another pan until golden brown.

Preheat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Place the lamb in a deep roasting pan. Pour the sauce over, cover with foil, and place in the oven for 3 hours. Until the meat becomes tender and starts to pull away from the bones.
Remove from the oven and transfer to a dish. Strain the sauce.
Serve with roasted vegetables, roasted potatoes, and spicy grape-tomato sauce, along with steamed white rice and sambals of choice.
Place the diced tomatoes, apples, onions, sugar, vinegar, raisins, and salt in a large pot. Cover and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the halved grapes, pitted and the remaining ingredients, cover, and cook for another 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Reduce the heat to a gentle simmer until the sauce thickens.
Remove from heat and store in sterilized jars.
Cut all the meat and bacon (speck) into cubes, mix everything and roughly grind the meat.
Place the coriander in a dry skillet and continue to stir until it browns, then grind the seeds.
Put all the meat and dry spices in a bowl, add vinegar and brandy, mix lightly and leave the marinade in the refrigerator for a few hours.
Then soak the sausage casings in water, fill them with meat (firmly, but not too tightly).
Grill and serve hot with spicy sauce.
Beat the butter with sugar for 2 minutes. Then add the eggs one at a time and continue to beat well.
Add the apricot jam and mix well.
Add the milk, baking soda, and vinegar. Gradually add the sifted flour and continue to mix.
Preheat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Pour the liquid batter into a greased baking dish. Bake for 45 minutes.
Combine all sauce ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, then remove from heat.
Take the pudding out of the oven, then pour the sauce on top.
Let it sit for 15 minutes before serving to allow the cake to absorb the sauce.
Serve with custard, vanilla ice cream, or whipped cream.
Bring water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.

Slowly add the cornmeal. Reduce the heat to medium and continue to stir regularly, breaking up lumps with a spoon, until the porridge pulls away from the sides of the pot and becomes very thick, about 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly.
Place the ugali in a large serving bowl. Wet your hands with water and form it into a ball.
Serve with milk and sugar or maple syrup for breakfast, or with brown sauce and barbecue meat, stewed meat, greens.
Heat a large pot with oil and add onion, garlic, cinnamon stick, curry leaves, cardamom pods, and curry powder, stirring occasionally for 2-3 minutes until the onion becomes translucent.
Add tomatoes and chicken, mix and cook for another 2-3 minutes. Add chicken broth/water if necessary.
Add chickpeas, potatoes, and chicken broth as needed. Bring to a boil and let it simmer until the sauce thickens, which may take about 25 minutes or more.
Serve in broken bread with salad, garnished with herbs.

Add cream of tartar, salt, sugar, ginger, lemon juice and cinnamon stick, water to a pot. Bring to a boil and let it steep for about 10 minutes, stirring the syrup occasionally. Allow it to cool and chill.
In a large bowl, mix all the dry ingredients - corn flour, flour, sugar, baking powder.
Then add all the liquid ingredients - milk and egg, followed by the butter. Knead a few times. Let it rest for 30 minutes.
Place the dough on a board and roll it out to a thickness of about 2 cm. Cut into thin strips, and then into shorter strips.

Divide the dough into three parts and gently stretch until the strips are of even thickness. Pinch the ends together, take the left strand and cross it over the middle strand. Cross the right strand over the middle strand. Press tightly to seal the end.
In a large pot, pour vegetable oil at least 7 cm deep. Check that the oil is hot enough. If using a deep fryer, fry at a temperature of 200 degrees.
