Carefully place the koeksuster in the oil and fry for a few minutes until the bottom side is golden brown.
Flip over and fry for a few more minutes until the other side is golden brown.
Remove from the oil and place in the syrup. Let sit in the syrup for a while. It is important that the syrup is cooled.
Cool completely before serving.
Whisk together milk, butter, and sugar until smooth. Add the egg.
Add the dry ingredients for the dough and mix well.
Spread into a greased baking dish.
Bake at 190°C (375°F) for about 20 minutes or until golden brown.
Boil milk, sugar, and oil. Whisk eggs with dry ingredients for the filling.
Pour the hot mixture over the cold and mix well. Add vanilla essence. Thicken over low heat.
Pour the filling into the pie crust. Allow to cool, then sprinkle with cinnamon.
Place the chicken in a large pot with water, salt, allspice, pepper, and bay leaves, along with vegetables cut into large pieces, and sprigs of parsley tied together.
Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes or until the vegetables are soft but still slightly crisp.
Remove the vegetables and chicken from the pot and set aside. Strain the broth into a bowl.
Finely chop the vegetables. Cut the meat.
Boil 3 eggs hard, and beat 1 egg with 1 tablespoon of water.
In a baking dish, add the chicken, vegetables, ham, and hard-boiled eggs.
In a saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter and add 2 cups of strained chicken broth, sherry, lemon juice, and nutmeg to the flour. Cook until the sauce thickens.
Slowly add the egg yolk to the sauce and stir for another minute. Pour the sauce over the chicken-vegetable mixture.
Cover the pie with a layer of shortcrust pastry. Fold the edges of the pastry.
Brush the pastry with beaten egg and bake in a preheated oven at 250°C (475°F) for 25 minutes.
Serve with mashed potatoes or roasted potatoes and peas.
Sauté the lamb leg and cut the meat into 2-3 cm cubes. Cut
the lamb fat and onion.
Heat the oil and sauté the onion rings until translucent. Remove the onion and place it on a paper towel.
Place all ingredients except the lamb, dried apricots, and onion into a glass or ceramic bowl and mix well.
Add the meat and onion to the marinade. Cover with a lid and leave in a cool place for 24-48 hours to marinate. Turn the meat 3 or 4 times during the marinating process.
Soak the apricots in warm water.
Remove the meat and onion from the marinade. Thread onto skewers alternating pieces of lamb, dried apricots, and onion.
Grill over hot coals, turning several times until cooked. Alternatively, they can be grilled in the oven or even pan-fried.
Meanwhile, pour the marinade into a pot and heat it almost to boiling.
Serve immediately hot. When serving, pour the sosaties with hot marinade and serve with breadcrumbs, or mashed potatoes, or crispy French bread with butter.
Alternatively, you can use the marinade for lamb chops and cook as described above.

Preheat the oven to 250°C (475°F) and place the rack in the upper third. Place the chilies on a baking sheet and roast until they blacken and soften, about 10-15 minutes. (Alternatively, you can dry roast them in a cast iron skillet over medium heat). Let cool, trim the stems, cut in half lengthwise, and remove the veins and seeds.
Blend the chili pepper, garlic, paprika, lime juice, and vinegar in a blender until smooth, about 1 minute. Add the olive oil and blend until the marinade thickens slightly.
Mix the marinade with the shrimp. Let marinate for 20 minutes to 24 hours in the refrigerator.
Heat a large cast iron skillet over medium heat. Add the shrimp and cook until they turn pink.
Season well with salt, garnish with cilantro, and serve with lime wedges and rice.
Soak the whole dried peaches and apricots in vinegar overnight. Then chop in a food processor.
Dice the onion or chop it in a food processor.
Place all ingredients in a pot and gently heat for 20 minutes to fully dissolve the sugar.
Simmer for about 1 hour, uncovered and stirring occasionally.
Let it cool for 10-15 minutes before pouring into hot sterilized jars. Store in a cool dark place.
Boil the potatoes with caraway seeds until soft and strain through a colander.
Add the soup spices to the potato broth and the egg, and simmer on low heat.
Fry the onion in fat or oil, add the potatoes, salt, and pepper, and slightly crush.
Prepare a paste from garlic, pepper, a teaspoon of fat, all to taste.
Add the garlic paste, chopped potatoes, onion, and pour in the boiling broth.
Serve hot with cubed cheese if desired, garnish with parsley (optional), and add fried bread cubes.
Place the mushrooms in a pot and cover with water, bring to a boil. Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and cut them into cubes, peel the carrot, celery, and parsley, and chop them finely.
Slice the leek into half-moon pieces. Peel and finely chop the onion. When the mushrooms start bubbling, drain the water, add new water, and bring to a boil again.
Sauté the finely chopped onion, add caraway seeds and flour. Pour in hot water and mix thoroughly.
Add the chopped vegetables except for the potatoes, salt, crushed garlic, previously soaked mushrooms, and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the potatoes and cook for another 20 minutes. Add some pepper, marjoram, and season with salt.
Garnish with chopped parsley when serving. Traditionally served in bread.

recipes.title: Beef in Cream Sauce (Svíčková na smetaně)

instructions.text: Stuff the meat, cleaned of membranes and fat, with bacon cut into strips.
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Tie the meat with twine into a neat, even roll. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and dice the parsley, carrot, celery, and onion.
Melt the butter with the fat and fry the meat until golden brown. Once the meat is browned, transfer it to a baking dish.
Add the onion and continue stirring until golden brown, then add all the root vegetables and all the spices.

Add sugar and let it caramelize for half a minute. Pour in the vinegar and wait for it to boil, then add the mustard and pour in the broth or water. Heat to boiling and pour everything into the baking pan.
Cover the baking dish with aluminum foil or a lid and place it in the oven. Bake for at least 2 hours until the meat is tender, turning the meat every 30 minutes.
Remove the meat from the sauce and place it on a plate in the oven. The optimal temperature in the oven is between 80-100 degrees.
Remove all spices from the sauce, strain, and pour to separate the liquid from the vegetables.
Add the flour. Stir on low heat for 20 minutes.
Season the sauce with caramel, lemon juice, vinegar, mustard, thicken with cream, and simmer on low heat. Then strain or blend the sauce.
Remove the twine from the meat and slice it.
Serve in cream sauce with dumplings, garnished with a spoonful of whipped cream, cranberry, and a slice of lemon.
Wash the pork knuckle. In 1 liter of water, mix vinegar, 1 teaspoon of salt and add spices. Place it in a pot with brine and boil for about 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Mix beer, honey, garlic, ground pepper, and a pinch of salt.
Make several cuts on the knuckle and place it in a baking tray. Pour the marinade over it and sprinkle with chopped vegetables.
Bake in the oven for 2.5 hours, including 1.75 hours covered, then turn it over and bake for 45 minutes uncovered, regularly turning and basting with sauce.
Serve with bread, mustard or horseradish, beer. With a side of boiled potatoes and sauerkraut.
Cut the cheese into slices 0.7-1 cm thick.
Beat the eggs with a fork and add a little salt.
Soak the cheese pieces in cold water.
Coat the cheese in flour, beaten eggs, and breadcrumbs, then coat again in egg, and then again in breadcrumbs.
Fry in heated oil until golden brown.
Serve with boiled potatoes, vegetable salad, and tartar sauce.
Soak the intestines in a large bowl of warm water for 2 hours, rinsing several times.
Clean the meat and bacon from tendons and cartilage, roughly chop and place in a blender.
Add cold milk with salt, pepper, and the remaining ingredients to the blender.
Wash the parsley and chop it very finely. Mix the meat with salt and knead for 10 minutes, adding lemon zest, pepper, nutmeg, and mustard seeds.
Stuff the meat mixture into the intestines. Heat water in a large pot and boil the sausages for 25 minutes at 75 °C.
You can briefly fry them in fat.
Serve with mustard sauce, sauerkraut, and potatoes, along with beer.
Mix the flour with the starch, add a couple of pinches of salt.

Then gradually add the hot water and immediately knead the dough. Mix the dough first with a whisk and then with your hands. The kneading process will take at least 5 minutes. After that, wrap the dough in plastic wrap and chill.
Sprinkle the work surface with flour. Roll out the dough thinly into a long 'stick.'
Cut it into portion-sized pieces and roll them out as thinly as possible.
If using shiitake mushrooms, soak them in warm water beforehand, then slice them into thin strips.
Wash and dry the green onion and napa cabbage, then finely chop them. Don't forget to cut off the thick part of the cabbage leaves.
Using a garlic press or a fine grater, mince the garlic and a small piece of ginger (about 1 cm).
Add the chopped onion and cabbage, garlic, ginger, lemon juice, soy sauce, fish sauce, rice vinegar (the Japanese also add a bit of sake) to the ground pork.
Season with pepper and mix well. Add salt to taste if necessary.
Place 1 tsp of filling on each round of dough and shape the dumplings into crescent shapes with pinches on one side.
Before folding the dough, brush a little water on the inner edges to help it stick better.
Fry the gyoza in a pan with a small amount of oil (I used vegetable oil with sesame oil added) until golden brown.
Then add a little boiling water (the water should cover the gyoza by 1/4 - 1/3, no more), cover with a lid, and continue cooking until all the moisture evaporates.
Serve the gyoza with dipping sauce and chopped green onion.
Fry the bacon cubes in butter. Add the onion and sauté until golden brown.
Add the broth, bay leaf, and juniper berries. Add the rinsed sauerkraut.
Season with spices and simmer for about 35 minutes with the lid on.
Grate the peeled potato directly into the sauerkraut and cook for 10 minutes over low heat.
Before serving, season the cabbage again with salt and serve as a side dish with roasted pork, sausages, and dumplings.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for about 40 minutes, drain, peel while still warm, and slice.
Peel and dice the onion. Heat the oil and sauté the onion for about 15 minutes.
Add mustard and broth and bring to a boil.
Add vinegar and diced ham, season with salt and pepper.
Chop the green onion and add it to the salad. Season with salt, pepper, and sugar.
Serve the potato salad warm or cold.
Wash the shanks, pat them dry and rub with salt and pepper. Place in the oven, cover with a lid and bake at 200°C (400°F) for about 45-60 minutes.
Sauté the onion. Peel and prepare the potatoes.
Crush the juniper berries slightly, add the bay leaf and the other spices and warm them with the beer.
Pour the spice and beer mixture over the shanks and bake for another 60-90 minutes in the oven.
30 minutes before the cooking time is up, remove the lid. Mix the mustard and honey. About 15 minutes before the end of cooking, brush the shanks and roast them until done.
Serve the knuckle with potatoes and onions, sauerkraut, and wheat beer.
Mix the flour, 1 tablespoon of cocoa powder, 1 teaspoon of baking powder, 50 g of sugar, 1 packet of vanilla sugar, and butter. Roll out and place in a baking dish.
Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for 15 minutes. Then increase the temperature to 175°C (350°F).
Whip the egg whites until stiff and set aside. Then mix 8 egg yolks, 180 g of sugar, and 1 packet of vanilla sugar until creamy and fluffy.
Add 2 tablespoons of cinnamon and 6 drops of bitter almond oil. Now carefully fold in the egg whites.
Add 220 g of flour, 20 g of cocoa powder, and 3 teaspoons of baking powder to the butter (do not mix). Place this batter in a greased baking dish.
Bake in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F) for about 30 minutes. Then allow to cool.
Boil the cherry juice and mix with 5-6 tablespoons of flour, starch, and 3 tablespoons of sugar. Set aside 12 cherries for decoration.
Whip 4 cups of cream with 4-5 tablespoons of powdered sugar.
On the bottom layer of the cake, spread a layer of cherries, then apply a layer of cream. The cream should not turn red from the cherries, but should remain separate.

Then place the first sponge cake and repeat the same two more times. Decorate the cake with the remaining cream. Spread the cream around, both on top and around the edges. Decorate with cherries and sprinkle with grated chocolate.
Before serving, refrigerate for 2 hours.

ingredients.name: Orange liqueur
ingredients.notes: or orange juice, or Cointreau, or rose water

instructions.text: Mix ground almonds, sugar, liqueur, powdered sugar, and vanilla sugar.
In a small bowl, mix cocoa powder and cinnamon. Form balls and roll them in cocoa and cinnamon.
Place on parchment paper to dry. After completely drying, store in a closed container.

ingredients.name: Celery
ingredients.notes: diced, celery root can be used

instructions.text: Clean and chop all the vegetables. Cut the bacon into thin strips.
Fry the bacon and set aside. Sauté the onion in the bacon fat, then add the garlic, leek, celery, and carrots. Sauté for a few minutes.
Add water or broth, bay leaf, and rinse the pearl barley. Add the cleaned parsley sprigs.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 1-1.5 hours.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Remove the parsley sprigs and bay leaf.
Serve with crusty bread.
Put the flour, eggs, salt, and a pinch of nutmeg in a bowl and vigorously beat with a wooden spoon until the dough starts to bubble.
Let the dough rest for 10 minutes, then beat again. Add water or flour to adjust the consistency of the dough.
Use a colander, grater, or other device to shape the pasta.
Immediately drop the pasta into boiling salted water. Cook for 2-3 minutes after they rise to the surface. Then remove and rinse in hot water, then drain well and set the pasta aside.
Slice the onion into thin rings and sauté it in butter until golden yellow.
Mix the spätzle with the grated cheese. Bake in a preheated oven at 160°C (325°F) for about 10 minutes or until the cheese melts.
Season with salt, pepper, and grated nutmeg. Serve with green onions.
Wash the meat, pat it dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Dip the meat in the beaten egg yolk and flour. You can also use breadcrumbs and fry in a pan on both sides in oil until golden brown. Remove from the pan and keep warm.
Fry the sliced mushrooms, stirring in the pan for about 2 minutes. Then remove from the pan.
Pour more oil into the pan and sauté the chopped onion and finely chopped bacon. When the onion is slightly browned, add the mushrooms and pour in the cream.
Season with salt, pepper, and add dried thyme. Slowly cook the sauce, stirring occasionally, until the liquid evaporates. This can take up to 15 minutes, depending on the temperature.
The sauce should not be too liquid and have a creamy consistency. Place the chopped parsley into the sauce and season with salt and pepper if necessary.
Place the schnitzel on a plate and pour the sauce over it. Garnish with parsley.
Serve with French fries or potato croquettes, spaetzle.
Chop the onion and gherkins into cubes and sauté in a small amount of oil with a pinch of sugar.

Lay out the beef rolls, season with salt and pepper, mustard, bacon, gherkins, and onion, and roll them up. Secure the ends with toothpicks or tie the rolls with string. Sear briefly in oil, remove, and set aside.
(more on kochbar.de)
Peel and dice the carrot and onion. Dice the tomato, pepper, and garlic. Clean the celery and cut into medium cubes.
Fry the bacon in a small amount of oil, add the onion, celery, pepper, and carrot, and sauté well.
Add the garlic and a pinch of sugar along with the tomato paste. After a while, deglaze with red wine.
Season with salt and pepper, bay leaf, add the beef roll and remaining spices, and cook covered on low heat for 1.5 hours until the rolls are tender.
Remove the rolls, bay leaf, bacon, and carrot from the pot. Blend the entire sauce in a blender. If necessary, with some cornstarch previously dissolved in water.
Plate the rolls, pour sauce over them, and serve immediately with dumplings, fresh salad, or potatoes.

ingredients.name: Breadcrumbs
ingredients.notes: or a couple of slices of bread

instructions.text: Mix all the ingredients for the dough, form a ball and wrap it in cling film, chill for about 30 minutes.
Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 2 minutes and cool. Peel the onion and finely chop.
Knead the spinach with the minced meat, sausage, egg, and onion, breadcrumbs, season with nutmeg, marjoram, salt, and pepper.
Roll out the dough on a floured surface to about 0.5 cm, cut into rectangles.
Place the filling on the rectangles one tablespoon at a time. Brush the edges with water, place the second rectangle on top and press the edges with a fork.
Boil the beef broth and cook the Maultaschen on low heat for 7-12 minutes.
Garnish with parsley before serving. Serve with fried onions and a fresh salad.

ingredients.name: Dried Meat (beef and pork belly) or salt pork)

instructions.text: Place the dried or fresh meat in a large pot and add water to completely cover it. Add spices and bring to a boil. Reduce heat and cook the meat for about 60-90 minutes.

Boil the unpeeled beets in a large amount of water for an hour. In a separate pot, boil the potatoes with the skin for about 20-25 minutes. Allow the potatoes and beets to cool slightly, then peel them.
Mash the potatoes in a large pot until slightly chunky. Finely chop the beets and cornichons and add them to the potatoes.
Grind the cooked meat through a large meat grinder and add the remaining ingredients.
Peel the onion, finely chop it, and sauté in lard or oil. If cooking with salt pork, sauté it together with the onion.
Depending on the desired consistency, add vegetable broth. Season with salt and pepper. Then mix well and simmer for about 20 minutes on low heat.
Serve on a plate with a fried egg, add herring and cucumbers, and you can also add a few slices of beet.

recipes.title: Meatballs with Caper Sauce - Koenigsberger Klopse

instructions.text: Peel and boil the potatoes in salted water.
Peel the onion and dice it finely. Then melt 40 g of butter in a pan and lightly sauté the onion until it becomes translucent.
Cut the white bread and anchovy fillets into small cubes and soak them in 5 tablespoons of cream.

In a large bowl, combine the minced meat, onion, egg, white bread, anchovies, parsley, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, black pepper, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Mix well. Let it sit for about 10 minutes.
Season to taste, then shape into round balls of equal size. Each meatball should weigh about 100 grams.

Pour 1 liter of water and white wine vinegar into a pot and bring to a boil with the bay leaf, clove, allspice, and vegetable broth. Then reduce the heat and let the meatballs simmer for about 15 minutes. Remove them.
Strain the broth, then cook with 350 g of cream. Continue simmering until the liquid reduces and thickens.

Whisk 2 egg yolks and 50 g of cream in a cup and pour into the sauce that is no longer boiling. Gradually add the capers, juice, and grated half of the lemon, the remaining parsley, and 60 g of butter. Season with salt, black pepper, and Worcestershire sauce.
Place the meatballs in the sauce and warm them slightly. Traditionally served with beets and potatoes.
Boil the eggs for about 10 minutes. Peel, cut in half lengthwise. Soak the bread in water. Chop the onion and garlic and sauté.
Mix the minced meat, onion, egg, soaked bread (breadcrumbs), and chopped parsley in a large bowl.
Season the minced meat with plenty of salt, pepper, and a little mustard.
Form the minced meat into a relatively flat patty with a depression in the middle. Place the two hard-boiled eggs in and fold over. Carefully shape into a round roll.
Place on a baking sheet and put in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Bake for about 50-60 minutes. Turn off the oven and let it sit for another 10 minutes.
It can be served hot or cold with mashed potatoes with sautéed onions and any vegetables, green peas, and carrots.

recipes.title: Beetroot and Herring Salad (Rote Bete Salat mit Hering)

instructions.text: Boil the eggs, let them cool, peel and cut into cubes. Boil the beetroot, peel and cut. Dice the onion, apples, cornichons, and herring.
Put all the ingredients in a bowl and mix. Add sour cream, mayonnaise, and natural yogurt and stir. If the salad is too thick, add a little milk and mix. Season with sugar to taste.
Serve with boiled potatoes in their skins or simply on bread, like a sandwich, garnished with herbs.
All meat should be well chilled before processing.
Cut the pork and beef into pieces and mince them very finely in a meat grinder.
Add the meat to a blender and mix with salt, pepper, and water (in ice form).
Coarsely mince the bacon in a meat grinder and mix it with the meat.
Peel the onion, grate it, and mix it with marjoram, nutmeg, and the meat. Chill.
Grease a baking dish with butter and place the meat mixture in it. Smooth the surface.
Bake at 180°C (350°F) (circulating air about 160°C (325°F)) in a preheated oven on the middle rack for about 1 hour.
Slice the warm or cold Leberkäse and serve on a bun.

ingredients.name: White bread
ingredients.notes: finely chopped, soaked in 200 ml of milk

instructions.text: Mix the egg yolks with butter, combine with white bread and add the egg whites. Season with salt.
Pour 500 ml of water over the asparagus and boil for 12 minutes (season with salt and a small amount of sugar), then remove from the broth. Boil the cauliflower and carrot for 9 minutes, then remove.
Boil the peas for 3 minutes, then remove. Cover everything and keep warm at 80 °C.
Take 250 ml of vegetable broth. Form balls from the bread and egg mixture and boil in salted water for 8 minutes.
Rinse the morels in cold water. Strain. Boil in vegetable broth with cream.

Mix 80 g of butter with flour to a smooth consistency. Bring the butter and flour mixture to a boil while stirring for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper and add 2-4 tablespoons of white wine. Remove the dumplings from the water.
Stir the morels and crayfish tails in a little butter and season with salt. Place everything together on a plate.
Serve hot with dill and lemon, alongside veal or schnitzel with fried eggs and parsley.
Place the stomach in water, preferably overnight, so that it becomes elastic again.
Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water for 10 minutes, so they remain firm. Drain the water. Prepare meat or vegetable broth.

Put the filling into a chilled bowl. Cut the pork and pre-cooked potatoes into medium cubes. Pass one kilogram of meat through a meat grinder directly into the pre-chilled bowl with the filling. Add the remaining meat cubes to the meat and mix the mixture thoroughly again.
Season with the spice mix (all spices except marjoram) and about 50 g of salt. Mix again, add the potato cubes and mix everything again. Finally, add the marjoram. Knead everything again.

Thoroughly rinse, pat dry, and turn it inside out so that the wall of the stomach is on the outside. Tie the two openings of the stomach with kitchen string. Fill the stomach not too tightly so that it doesn’t burst during cooking.
Tie the last opening well, place the saumagen in the broth, and simmer for four hours at around 80 °C - it is important that it does not boil.

Remove from the broth, drain the water, and let cool slightly. Before serving, cut into slices and can be fried in hot oil or baked in the oven at 200°C (400°F) for about 10 minutes until golden brown.
Serve with fried potatoes and sauerkraut.

recipes.title: Cottage Cheese Pie with Prunes (Käsekuchen mit Pflaumen)

instructions.text: Mix flour with sugar, 1 packet of vanilla, 1 pinch of salt, 1 egg, and butter. Knead the dough using a hand mixer.
Place half into a greased baking dish, spread and press down, chill.
Wash, halve the prunes. Mix cottage cheese, mascarpone, lemon juice, 100 g of sugar, and 1 packet of vanilla until smooth. Add 3 eggs and the custard powder.
Spread a thin layer of plum jam on the dough. Add the cheese mixture and level it.
Place the halved prunes into the cheese mixture. Distribute the remaining on top.
Bake in a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F) (with air circulation at 150°C (300°F)) for 50-60 minutes. Let cool on a rack.
Dust with powdered sugar before serving.
Heat the butter in a pot. Add the onion and garlic and sauté with the flour. Add the broth, bring it to a slight boil, then add the beer (do not let it boil).
Add salt, pepper, and nutmeg and cook for 10 minutes. Add the cheese and cream, stirring constantly.
Simmer until the cheese is completely dissolved.
Slightly fry the bacon in a small skillet without fat.
Pour the soup into deep bowls and place some fried bacon in each bowl. Garnish with green onions.
Serve with rye bread or rye bread croutons.
Freeze the octopus if you bought it fresh or buy it already frozen.

Put a pot of water on the fire without adding salt. When the water boils, you need to 'scare the octopus'. To do this, take it by the head and dip it in boiling water for a minute, pull it out and dip it again for the same time. Repeat this 3-4 times; this will make the meat tender, the skin will remain whole, and the tentacles will curl at the ends as if in fear.

Then cook the octopus for 30-40 minutes with the bay leaf and peeled onion, timing it from when the water starts to boil again. The meat will be ready when a fork or wooden skewer can easily go into the tentacle.
Remove the pot from the heat and let it sit for 10-15 minutes. Cut the octopus with kitchen scissors, the legs into pieces 1 cm thick, and the head into small pieces.
Peel, wash, and cut the potatoes in half. In the same water, throw in the potatoes and cook for 15 minutes.
Place the potato base and top with slices of octopus. Sprinkle with sweet or hot paprika and generously drizzle with olive oil.
Traditionally served on a wooden plate.

ingredients.name: Beans
ingredients.notes: large white Asturian, can be replaced with regular ones

ingredients.name: Asturian blood sausage
ingredients.notes: smoked blood sausages, can be replaced with regular ones

instructions.text: Soak the beans for 8-12 hours. Then drain the water.
Cover with water to about 2-3 fingers above, bring to a strong boil. Drain the water completely, add new water and bring to a boil again. Regularly skim off the foam.
When it boils again, add the blood sausage, bacon, and chorizo. Continue to skim off the foam, also remove some fat from the sausages along with the foam.
Add the whole peeled onion and reduce the heat to almost minimum, but keep the soup at a gentle simmer.
After an hour, pour in half a cup of cold water. Repeat the same in the second hour. Add a little salt.
After 3 hours of cooking, the fabada should be ready. Remove from heat and let it rest for 1 hour. It can be left until the next day, then the flavor will be even better.
Cut the sausage and bacon into pieces, place them in bowls, pour over the fabada, and serve with bread.
Cut all the vegetables into cubes. Chop the garlic very finely. Blend the tomatoes.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan, add the onion, and sauté until translucent.
Add the pepper and garlic and continue to sauté over low heat until the pepper changes color and becomes soft.
Add the zucchini and continue cooking slowly until it becomes soft, stirring occasionally, for about 5 minutes.
Add the blended tomato and white wine, season with salt, and cook for some time until the liquid reduces. About 25 minutes.
Serve with crispy white bread or as a tapas appetizer with a slice of ham and manchego cheese or a fried egg.
Boil the eggs hard for about 10 minutes. Peel and cut into pieces.

Wash the peppers, place them on a baking tray, drizzle with oil and season. Season the tomatoes and wrap in foil. Place the tray in the oven and roast the vegetables at 190°C (375°F) for 35-40 minutes.
Remove the peppers, peel and cut into strips. Place in a bowl.
Remove the aluminum foil from the tomato. Peel and put in a blender with garlic and puree.
Drizzle the peppers with tomato puree. Add oil and a little vinegar. Add a clove of minced garlic and onion. Season and mix well.
Top with the chopped eggs and serve, sprinkled with finely chopped parsley.
Remove the crust from the bread with a knife, place it in a bowl, and pour in some water.
If the almonds are unpeeled, dip them in a pot of boiling water in a colander 2 or 3 times. Let cool, and peel.
Place in a blender cup: almonds, breadcrumbs (bread), peeled garlic, oil, vinegar, and a pinch of salt. Pour in some water. Blend for about 2 minutes.
Add the remaining water, salt to taste. Leave in the refrigerator for at least an hour.
Serve with seedless grapes or apples and ham or cured meat, as well as olive oil.
A few days in advance, the cod needs to be desalinated. Soak it and change the water every 8 hours. Drain the water and dry it, then crumble the cod by hand.
Peel and chop the onion, wash and dice the tomatoes, red and green peppers, and onion.
Add the olives, dress with good olive oil and, if desired, a little vinegar. Mix well. Add salt cautiously.
Serve Esqueixada cold with a glass of white wine.

recipes.title: Cordoban Tomato Soup Puree Salmorejo (Salmorejo Cordobés)

instructions.text: Peel the tomatoes and place them in a blender cup along with the garlic, blend until smooth.
Add the bread, oil, and salt and blend again until you have a homogeneous and smooth mixture. Place in the refrigerator.
Serve in bowls and garnish with Serrano ham, chopped boiled egg, and a small amount of olive oil.
Beat the eggs with the brandy and butter, and sugar. Add a pinch of salt and vinegar, anise.
Gradually add the flour, mixing well until a soft texture is achieved, cover with a cloth and let it rest at room temperature for 1 hour.
Roll the dough thinly. Cut into even pieces and fry in a pot with hot oil until golden.
Place on paper towels, let cool, and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Soak the chickpeas overnight with a tablespoon of coarse salt and a small amount of baking soda.

In a large pot, add 60 ml of olive oil. When it heats up, add the meat, sausage, rinsed bones, and ham. Pour in four liters of water and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam, reduce the heat, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and bring to a boil again, skimming off the foam. Cover and reduce the heat. Simmer on low for at least 3 hours, constantly removing any foam that may form on the surface.
After a couple of hours, add the peeled potatoes whole, peel and cut the carrots into medium pieces, and add the turnip. Cover and cook for 30 minutes.
In a separate pot, boil the chopped cabbage (30 minutes). Drain the water and sauté with garlic and olive oil.
In another pot, boil the chorizo and blood sausage.
Boil the noodles for about 15 minutes. Let them steep. Strain the broth from the first pot. Add the noodles and cook until done.
Serve everything in portions on each plate and ladle the broth over it. Serve with tomato paste, garnished with chopped parsley.

The traditional stew is served in three stages. First, the soup with noodles is served. Then the chickpeas and vegetables (cabbage, carrots, and turnip). Finally, in the third stage, the cooked and sliced meat dish is served.
Wash and dry the eggplants, peppers, and tomatoes. Peel the onion and garlic. Puncture the eggplant with a sharp knife to prevent it from bursting while heating in the oven.
Place all the vegetables in a baking tray, except for the tomatoes, and drizzle with a small amount of olive oil. Cook in a preheated oven at 170°C (350°F) for 1 hour.
Turn the vegetables, add the tomatoes, and cook for another 30 minutes.

Depending on the size of the vegetables, especially the onion, the time may vary, so the indicated value is only approximate. Make sure the vegetables are tender before removing the tray from the oven, let them cool to remove the skin.
Place all the ingredients in a dish, to which add a pinch of coarse sea salt and juice from the tray. You can add a few drops of vinegar.
Serve both cold and hot, with anchovies or cod and bread. Or as a side dish to meat.

ingredients.name: White bread
ingredients.notes: Spanish, should be hard, not fresh

instructions.text: Cut the bread into very small pieces, crumbling it, and place it in a large bowl.
Mix water with olive oil and sweet paprika.
Spread the mixture over the crumbled bread, making sure all the bread gets moist but not soaked. Cover the bowl with 'wet' bread with a clean cloth and leave for 4 hours.
In a large pot, add oil and heat well. Fry the garlic without peeling. Fry the bacon cut into strips. Slice the chorizo into medium-thick slices and fry in the same oil as the bacon.

Fry the eggs in the oil with the bacon and chorizo. Remove the eggs, add the bread to the pan, and fry in the same oil, stirring constantly, until the crumbs become loose and crispy. About 8-10 minutes.
When the bread is well toasted, add the chopped bacon and chorizo and mix well.
Add the fried eggs and mix again. Season with salt to taste, garnish with grapes and finely chopped parsley.
Serve with a good bottle of red wine made from Garnacha grapes from Ávila.

recipes.title: Spanish Omelette or Potato Tortilla (Tortilla De Patatas)

instructions.text: Peel the potatoes and cut them in half. Then cut them in half again and slice thinly.
Heat a large amount of oil. When hot, fry the potatoes over medium heat until soft. About 15 minutes.
Remove the potatoes and place them in a bowl with paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Beat the eggs with salt to taste and add them to the potatoes, mixing well.
Heat a non-stick pan with a small amount of oil (about two tablespoons).
When the oil is hot, add the potato and egg mixture to the pan and spread it out. Cook over medium heat.
When browned, flip it over and cook on the other side.
The Spanish omelette can be served hot or cold with bread and salad. You can also make a version with onions and peppers, or with Serrano ham or chorizo.

ingredients.name: Cod fillet
ingredients.notes: or 2 cans of light tuna in olive oil

instructions.text: The first step is to desalinate the cod for 24-48 hours, changing the water every 6-8 hours. After this time, remove it from the water, dry it as much as possible, and crumble it.
Boil the potatoes with their skins, peel them, and cut them into pieces.
Peel the orange 'a la vivo', meaning to remove any white parts and chop it. Add the juice as well.
Clean the green onion and cut it into thin strips, and peel the eggs and cut them into 'wedges'.
Combine all the ingredients, generously drizzle with olive oil, salt, and vinegar, and mix well. Garnish with parsley.
Pour the milk, orange zest, lemon zest, and cinnamon into a medium saucepan. Heat over medium heat. When it boils, remove from heat, cover with a cloth, and let steep for about 45 minutes.
Mix the egg yolks and sugar in another bowl. Add the starch and stir.
Strain the infused milk into the previous mixture and mix.
Pour the contents into a saucepan and heat over medium heat until it thickens (do not boil), and immediately remove from heat. Stir for another minute.
Distribute the cream into 4 containers and let cool for two hours. Then cover with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator for at least 4 hours.
Before serving, sprinkle with sugar and caramelize until crispy.
Preheat the oven to 175°C (350°F). Mix sugar, ground almonds, cinnamon, and lemon zest.

Add the eggs and mix everything well. Grease the baking dish with butter. Then pour the mixture into the dish and place it in the oven at 170°C (350°F) for 50 minutes, until the surface is golden brown.
Remove from the oven and let cool. Unmold and sprinkle with powdered sugar.
Finely chop the onion, carrot, and leek. Sauté with garlic, mushrooms, bay leaf, and pepper for 15 minutes.
Pour in the wine and increase the heat, cook for about 3 minutes. Reduce the heat again and add vinegar and water or chicken broth. Cook for 5 minutes over medium heat. Adjust salt.
Separately, fry the chicken over high heat until they are raw inside and golden outside.
Add the breasts to the pan with the marinade and cook for 5 minutes over low heat. Remove the meat to a plate and cook the marinade for another 5 minutes.
Pour the marinade over the meat, let it cool, and if possible, store in the refrigerator in a glass container.
Serve with a salad of fresh vegetables and toasted homemade bread.

ingredients.name: Pumpkin
ingredients.notes: flesh diced and pumpkin for serving

ingredients.name: Beef fat (lamb or pork) or corn oil

instructions.text: Sauté the onion in fat and add the meat. After mixing, add the tomatoes, spices, and sugar, and sauté for 5 minutes.
Add the pumpkin, potatoes, sweet potatoes, corn, peaches, and carrot. Mix and add the broth. Cook for about 15 minutes.
Add the rice and more broth, simmer until the rice is cooked. Turn off the heat and let it sit covered for a few minutes.
Traditionally served in baked pumpkin or in bread.
Wash the pumpkin. Cut off the top. Remove the seeds and fibers. Grease with oil, wrap in foil, and place in a preheated oven at 200 degrees for 30-35 minutes.

ingredients.name: Chopped parsley
ingredients.notes: fresh, finely chopped. Dried can be used

ingredients.name: Oregano
ingredients.notes: fresh, finely chopped. Dried can be used

ingredients.name: Hot chili pepper (finely chopped
ingredients.notes: can be replaced with 1-2 teaspoons of chili flakes or dried hot pepper

ingredients.name: Red wine vinegar
ingredients.notes: amount can be adjusted to taste

instructions.text: Mix all the ingredients and stir well.
Store in the refrigerator, and it is best to consume within 24-48 hours after preparation.
If using dried ingredients, let it steep overnight in the refrigerator instead.
Used to accompany meat and chicken dishes - especially for roasting or grilling, with bread, or pies and vegetables (prepared on the grill, steamed, etc.)
Cut the tomatoes into quarters, remove the seeds and discard. Finely chop the flesh and place it in a large bowl.
Add the pepper, onion, oil, and vinegar to the bowl with the tomatoes, and season well and mix.
Meanwhile, heat a pan or grill over medium heat. Cook the chorizo, turning often, for 10 minutes or until browned.
Transfer the chorizo to a cutting board and cut in half. Cover with foil.
Slice the buns lengthwise, open them and grill, cut side down, for 2 minutes. Divide the chorizo among the buns, top with chimichurri and the tomato mixture.
Place 500 grams of chickpea flour in a bowl, add salt, pepper, and gradually add 1 liter of warm water, constantly whisking to avoid lumps.
Add the egg and whisk again until a thick homogeneous mixture is formed and let it rest for 30 minutes.
Put 2 or 3 tablespoons of olive oil in a large pizza pan and place it in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F).
First, place it on the lower rack for about 10 minutes, then move it to the upper shelf until a golden crust forms. The total cooking time is between 20 to 25 minutes.
Cut into portions and serve hot alongside onion pizza or mozzarella pizza, with a filling of onion, ham, cheese, rosemary, or thyme.

recipes.title: Fish with Potatoes (Abadejo Guisado Con Patatas)

instructions.text: Heat the oil and sauté the finely chopped onion and green pepper with a pinch of salt.
Add the wine and increase the heat.
Peel the potatoes. Add them and slightly reduce the heat.
Pour in hot water. Season with a small amount of pepper, ground cumin, paprika, and thyme to taste. Increase the heat again and cover. Cook for about 20 minutes.
Cut the fish into pieces and place it on top of the potatoes. Cover and cook for another 20 minutes.
Remove from heat and let sit for a couple of minutes.
Serve in a deep dish with broth and garnish with fresh herbs.
Boil milk with salt, the cinnamon stick, and the zest of 1 lemon (and orange) for 10 minutes.
Add rice, cook for 1 hour on medium heat (until cooked), add sugar and cook for 5 minutes while stirring occasionally.
Pour into separate molds or one large one. Mix cinnamon with sugar and sprinkle on top.
Serve cold or hot, sometimes raisins are added.

recipes.title: Flan with Condensed Milk (Flan con Dulce de Leche)

instructions.text: Heat about 100 grams of sugar. When the sugar starts to melt, stir with a wooden spoon. Add a little more sugar and continue stirring until all the sugar is melted and turns brown.

Immediately pour the caramel into a pan (about 22 cm in diameter) and gently swirl the pan while the caramel cools. Make sure the entire surface is covered; you can spread it with a spoon. Set aside and let it cool.
Add the remaining sugar and vanilla to the center of a large bowl. Heat the milk, then pour it over the sugar. Stir well.
Add the eggs and gently mix with a whisk; the eggs do not need to be fully beaten.
Pour the mixture into the container with the caramel and cover with foil. Place in a pot and fill with hot water until half of the mold is covered with water.
Place the water bath in the oven and bake at 160°C (325°F) for 1 hour. Check to see if it is ready.
Let it cool and chill in the refrigerator for at least 3 hours.
Invert onto a plate. Drizzle with condensed milk or whipped cream and serve.
Soak the corn overnight. The next day, change the water and cook over medium heat until soft.
Strain and let cool.
Heat the milk with sugar and vanilla until boiling, then add the corn. Cook for about 10 minutes over low heat.
Add the cream and cook for another 5 minutes. Remove from heat and add vanilla essence. Mix.
Serve warm or cold, and you can garnish with cinnamon or add liquid caramel or fresh berries.
Soak the dried white corn for 12 hours - preferably overnight.
Place the onion, garlic, leek, beef, chorizo, pork knuckle, and tripe in a large pot and sauté in oil until the onion becomes translucent.
Add cumin, paprika, a little salt, and black pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Add the corn kernels and then add enough hot water to cover the ingredients by about 5 cm.
Add the vegetables and beans. Bring everything to a boil, reduce the heat, cover, and simmer for about 2 hours. Check every 20 minutes or so and stir.
Remove the lid and continue to cook on low heat. Remove the bones. Stir the vegetables slowly. Continue cooking until a thick consistency is achieved. Add a little salt to taste.
Serve hot in deep bowls, garnished with green onion.
Remove excess fat and nerves from the beef pieces. Slightly tenderize the beef slices with a mallet.
Mix garlic and parsley with the beaten eggs, salt, and pepper.
Dip the beef pieces into the beaten eggs, mix well, and place in a cool place for 45 minutes.
Heat the oil over medium heat to 170°C (350°F). Generously coat each beef piece in breadcrumbs.
Fry the milanese for a few minutes on each side. Place on a plate lined with paper towels.
Serve with French fries, mashed potatoes, green salad, potato salad, fried peppers, or tomatoes seasoned with oregano.

recipes.title: Veal in Cream Sauce with Anchovies and Tuna Vitel Toné (Vitel Toné)

ingredients.name: Canned tuna
ingredients.notes: natural or oil-packed, drained and flaked

instructions.text: Place the meat, onion, carrot, garlic, celery, parsley, and bay leaf in water. Add salt to taste. Cook until tender for about 1.5 hours on low heat, skimming off the foam.
Allow the meat to cool in the broth. Remove the meat and slice it very thinly using an electric knife or a sharp knife. Arrange on a platter or dish.
In a blender, add the yolks of 8 hard-boiled eggs and well-drained tuna. Gradually add olive oil while blending and mix until a smooth sauce is obtained.
Add about 150 ml of the prepared broth and continue blending. Add mustard, anchovies, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and black pepper. If the sauce is not liquid enough, add more broth.
Place the sliced meat on a large plate and pour the sauce over it. Sprinkle capers on top. Grate the remaining egg whites and sprinkle over the meat and edges of the plate. Garnish with parsley.
Leave in the refrigerator for a few hours. Serve cold or at room temperature with white wine, such as Chardonnay, Sauvignon Blanc, or Pinot Grigio.
Wash the zucchini well. Cook in plenty of salted water for 8-10 minutes.
Cut off the top end, slice in half. Place the zucchini halves upside down to drain the liquid on a flat surface. Once cooled, scoop out the flesh with a spoon, trying not to damage the skin.
Peel and finely chop the onion. Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk. Squeeze the zucchini flesh by hand to remove as much liquid as possible.

Heat the butter along with the vegetable oil and sauté the onion until it becomes translucent. Add the red bell pepper, diced into small cubes, along with the zucchini flesh and ground meat. Cook for a couple of minutes, adding salt and pepper to taste.
Transfer the mixture to a bowl and add the breadcrumbs, eggs, and grated cheese. Mix very well.
Place the zucchini halves in a baking dish and fill with the stuffing. Sprinkle the zucchini with breadcrumbs, drizzle with a few drops of oil or place pieces of butter, and sprinkle cheese on top.
Bake on the middle rack in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) until golden brown, about 10-15 minutes.
Serve with tomato sauce, garnished with chopped parsley.

ingredients.name: Dried Oregano
ingredients.notes: or Marjoram, you can also add Thyme

instructions.text: If cooking in the oven, preheat to 170°C (350°F). Or take a large cast iron skillet and heat it over medium heat.
Rub the cheese slices with olive oil on both sides. Sprinkle with dried oregano and chili flakes. Place on the skillet or in the oven.
Cook for about 2-3 minutes, until each side is browned and starts to melt. Then flip and cook until the second side is brown and the cheese is melted.
Season to taste, drizzle with 1 teaspoon of olive oil, and serve immediately with fresh bread and chimichurri sauce or fresh herbs. Also, serve with sausages or meat as a side.
Mix all the ingredients for the dough and knead until a homogeneous mass is obtained (add water if necessary).
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, then roll out the dough to a thickness of 1-2 mm.
Mix all finely chopped ingredients for the filling. You can add more nuts.
Place the dough in a flour-dusted sorrentino mold. Fill with the filling and brush with egg to seal with another layer of dough.
Cut and drop into a pot of boiling salted water. Cook until they rise to the surface, about 5 minutes.
If there is no sorrentino mold, place the filling on strips of dough, about 3 cm apart, top with another strip of dough, and press with fingers to join the two strips of dough.
Cook for about 15 minutes on low heat the chopped ingredients for the sauce until thick (except for the cream, basil, and parmesan). Season and serve.
Serve the sorrentinos with plenty of sauce, cream, and grated parmesan, garnished with chopped basil.

recipes.title: Corn Casserole Polenta with Tuco Sauce (Polenta)

instructions.text: Bring the broth to a boil, add 50 g of butter and milk, eggs.
Carefully and gradually pour in the flour. Season, stir, and cook over low heat. It is very important to continuously stir the polenta until it is ready (from 15 to 20 minutes).
Pour into a mold and let cool.
Sauté the onion and garlic with the spices. Add the ground beef, previously seasoned and simmer until cooked. Add the tomato and cook for 2 or 3 minutes.
Add one cup of broth and mix. Add oregano, salt, pepper, and cook over low heat for 20 minutes, stirring constantly. Then add 25 grams of butter and grated parmesan.
Once the polenta cools, it can be cut into thin slices or large pieces, add a generous portion of tuco, and sprinkle with parmesan cheese.
Clean the crab well, then place it in a large amount of water and salt to taste.
Boil for 20 to 30 minutes, depending on size and weight (if it weighs more than 2 kg, boil for 30 minutes).
Chop the onion, add butter, add the chopped onion and season. Add the crab and cook for 1 minute.
Then add the cream, cook for another 2 minutes. Before removing from heat, add ketchup, stir until you get a pink sauce.
Separate, boil the rice. Place it on a plate and add the sauce with crab.
Serve with lemon wedges and sauce.

ingredients.name: Beef flank steak
ingredients.notes: large, thin piece of flank steak from the lower abdomen of the bull

instructions.text: Cut the steak in a butterfly shape by carefully slicing it in half along one of the long sides to unfold the steak like a sheet of paper folded in half. Remove the fat.
Boil the eggs for 10 minutes. Roast the red pepper to make it easier to remove the skin, cut into wide strips. Chop the parsley and grate the carrot finely.
Grease with oil, season, and sprinkle the matambre with oregano, ground chili, chopped parsley, garlic, carrot, and grated cheese.
Spread the strips of red pepper and place whole eggs on the wide end of the matambre.
Fold in the two ends to prevent the eggs from falling out, then tightly roll it up and tie it with cotton thread.

Place in a large amount of water in a large pot with a handful of salt and broth. Once the broth boils, reduce to medium heat and cook the matambre for about 1 hour. The water level should always cover the entire roll during cooking. Add more hot water as needed.

Turn off the heat and let it cool in the broth. Remove, tightly wrap in cling film (place a weight on it) so that all ingredients are pressed tightly together, and put in the refrigerator for at least an hour before serving, but preferably overnight.
Slice and serve hot or cold with chimichurri sauce, greens, and fresh salad, Olivier salad, or with bread as sandwiches.
Boil a large pot of water. When it boils, add the osso buco and sausages and boil well for 15 minutes.
Add a bundle of parsley and celery (tied with a string for easy removal), carrots and corn, chopped into large pieces, and onion. Cook for 30 minutes.
Add the remaining vegetables: pumpkin, sweet potato, potatoes, chopped into large pieces. Season. Cook until the potatoes are done.
Remove the bundle of parsley and celery. Season to taste and add a little olive oil.
Serve hot in deep plates with mustard, hot sauce, and mayonnaise to taste. Sometimes the broth and meat are served separately.

recipes.title: Grilled Churrasco with Creole Sauce (Churrasco Argentino en Salsa Criolla)

ingredients.name: Beef
ingredients.notes: wide part of the rib, 600 grams each piece

instructions.text: Remove the meat from the refrigerator at least 30 minutes before cooking. Season with salt.

Place the meat on the heated grill. It is best to cook over medium heat (on the grate higher above the coals), until golden brown on both sides (about 6 minutes on average). Let it rest for 5 minutes.
Chop the onion, tomato, and pepper, mix the oil and vinegar, and add the remaining ingredients, stirring a little, without a blender.
Serve immediately with sauce and a side of fresh vegetables. Churrasco is also great with chimichurri sauce or any other favorite sauce.
Separate the squid's body from the head. Clean the squid by removing the cartilage, tentacles, ink (the darkest area), and brown skin.
Cut the squid into slices about 1 cm thick. Soak the squid in warm water with baking soda for ten minutes.
Beat the eggs with salt and pepper. Coat the squid slices in egg, then in flour. If necessary, remove excess flour by placing the raw slices in a sieve and shaking.
Fry in a large amount of hot oil at 180°C (350°F) for 5 minutes. Place on paper towels.
Salt to taste and serve with lemon or lime wedges and sauce.
Wash the beef testicles thoroughly and soak them for 1 hour in water with lemon juice. Remove and peel off the outer membrane.
Cut each into 4 pieces. Place in a pot with boiling salted water.
Cover with a lid and leave on low heat for 10 minutes.
Mix the breadcrumbs with garlic, thyme, cayenne pepper, salt, and black pepper and stir well.
Remove the criadillas from the water and let them drain for about 5 minutes.
Heat enough oil in a pan.
Beat the eggs and dip the criadillas in them, then into the breadcrumb mixture. Once they are all coated, place them in the pan for 3 minutes.
Remove and serve with salsa and lemon slices.

recipes.title: Meat Stew with Beans Cassoulet Castelnaudary (Le Cassoulet de Castelnaudary)

instructions.text: Soak the beans in cold water the night before and change the water two or three times.
Drain the water, place the beans in a pot with 3 liters of cold water, and bring to a boil for 5 minutes. Turn off the heat, drain the water.

In another pot, pour in 3 liters of water, add the pork skin cut into large strips, poultry stew if available, or several pork bones, some onion and carrot, bouquet garni, salt, and pepper. Cook the broth for 1 hour, then strain.
Add the beans to the broth and return the pork skin, simmer for about 1 hour.
In a large skillet, fry the duck over low heat and set aside. In the remaining fat, fry the Toulouse sausages and set aside as well.
Fry the pieces of pork until browned and set aside with the other meats.
Remove the beans and keep the broth warm. Add several cloves of garlic to the beans and salted bacon, mix.

A clay pot called 'cassolo' is needed. Line the bottom with pork skin, add about a third of the beans, layer the meat and the remaining beans, then the sausages, fill with hot broth to completely cover the ingredients, season with freshly ground pepper, and add the duck fat left from frying.
Place in the oven at 150°C (300°F) / 160°C (325°F) and cook for 2-3 hours. When the top of the beans starts to dry, add a few spoons of broth.
If preparing in advance, it should be warmed in the oven at 150°C (300°F) one and a half hours before serving. Add some broth or water, do not stir.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.notes: such as sirtema, elodie, europa or monalisa

ingredients.name: Reblochon cheese
ingredients.notes: semi-soft, washed and smeared mountain cheese

instructions.text: Peel the potatoes, cut into cubes, rinse well, and dry with a clean cloth.
Chop the onion and sauté gently in olive oil. When the onion becomes translucent, add the cubed potatoes.
Add the bacon and cream. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Scrape the rind off the reblochon until it turns orange, and cut it in half along the thickness.
Pour the cream/potato/bacon mixture into a baking dish and cover with the two halves of the reblochon. Bake for 25 minutes.
Cut a thin slice of baguette about 1 cm wide.
Spread the cream cheese evenly over the surface.
Place the arugula leaves on top, and cover with the anchovy, a slice of sun-dried tomato, and the fresh tomato.
Sprinkle finely chopped radish on top and place a basil leaf.
Preheat the oven to 210°C (400°F). Wash the cherries.
Slightly melt the butter. In a separate large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, and vanilla sugar.
Beat the eggs and add them to the flour and sugar mixture. Add the milk,
add the melted butter. Whisk well.
Grease the baking dish, cut the cherries in half, and place them at the bottom, distributing them evenly. (In the traditional recipe, cherries are left whole with pits for flavor)
Pour the batter over the cherries. Place the clafoutis in the oven for about 25-40 minutes.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve, hot, warm, or cold.
Cut all ingredients into small pieces. Slice the tomatoes thinly or cut into quarters.
Finely chop the artichokes and leave them in lemon water.
Rinse the anchovy fillets, separate the fillets, cut them in half, and finely chop the tuna.
Add the tuna, basil, and green beans, and season with olive oil, vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Serve in each plate, garnished with boiled eggs cut into quarters, anchovy fillets, tuna crumbles, and olives.
Make the crepe batter and let it sit for 1 hour.
Heat the sugar in a frying pan until it turns into caramel.
When the caramel turns amber and before it catches fire, pour in the orange juice and cognac.
Whip the butter and sugar until smooth cream is obtained. Grate the zest of the second orange very finely and add it. Then squeeze the juice from ½ orange. Mix well.
Whisk the crepe batter and cook. Serve the crepes hot. Garnish with orange zest, orange butter, and syrup.
Wash the sorrel leaves and remove the stems. Clean and wash the potatoes, cut them into pieces.
Peel, chop, and sauté the onion in a pan with butter.
Pour water over the chopped sorrel leaves, chopped potatoes, and onion. You can add a chicken broth cube or season to taste. Cook for 30 minutes over low heat.
Use a food processor or hand blender to mash the potatoes.
Remove the pot from the heat. In a bowl, mix the yolk and cream and add to the soup. Stir and serve immediately, you can add croutons and garnish with herbs.
Prepare the broth. Clean, wash, and chop the leek.
Clean the cauliflower and divide it into small florets. Select the most attractive ones for garnishing the soup.
In a pot or a sufficiently deep skillet, sauté the leek in butter. Add the flour and cook for a few minutes, stirring.
Pour in the broth and stir until boiling. Add the cauliflower, salt, cover, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Boil the remaining cauliflower florets for 5 minutes. Immerse the boiled florets in ice water to preserve their shape and firmness.
Slightly cool the prepared soup base and strain it through a sieve using a food processor or blend it with an immersion blender.
Gently whisk the yolks with the cream. Pour into the boiling pureed cauliflower mixture with leeks, stirring vigorously.
Fill deep individual plates with the puree soup. Place small florets of cauliflower and a piece of butter on the surface. Garnish with fresh parsley.
Place bacon and a slice of cheese on each piece of meat and fold in half. Season with salt and pepper.
Arrange flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs in 3 plates.
First dip each cutlet in flour, then in egg, and then in breadcrumbs.
Cook for about 5 minutes on each side over moderate heat in enough sizzling oil to lightly float on the surface.
Serve garnished with parsley and lemon slices.

ingredients.name: Veal shoulder
ingredients.notes: or neck, tendon, breast, cut into large cubes

instructions.text: Place the meat in a large pot and cover with cold water. Bring to a boil and salt. Regularly skim the foam to keep the broth clear.
After 20 minutes, add onion, cloves, and bouquet garni. Cook for another 20 minutes and add wine, carrots, and celery. Continue to simmer for 45 minutes or until the meat is tender.
If necessary, add a little water. Remove the onion and bouquet garni.
Meanwhile, sauté the mushrooms in a pan for 2 minutes with oil. Season with salt and pepper, add broth, and continue to cook for 5 minutes.
Melt the butter, add flour, whisking over low heat for 5 minutes until a thick sauce consistency is achieved.
Add the thick cream and lemon juice and continue to cook for 2 minutes.
Add the egg yolks and whisk. Pour this sauce into the pot with the meat and vegetables. Add the mushrooms and stir gently.
Serve hot, garnished with finely chopped parsley with a side of rice or potatoes.

recipes.title: Fish Provencal (Poisson au Four à la Provençale)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 210°C (400°F). Chop the onion, slice the garlic, then slice the tomatoes and lemon.
Decorate the bottom of the baking dish with onion, tomatoes, lemon, and then place the fish.
Mix olive oil, white wine, and chopped garlic.
Brush the fish with this mixture, season with salt, thyme, rosemary, and pepper, and add the bouquet garni.
Place in the oven and cook for about 25 minutes.
Serve with a side of rice or potatoes.
Mix the coriander seeds with the pepper and grind them.
Heat the honey over high heat for 2-3 minutes until it slightly caramelizes. Pour in the vinegar and mix well to dissolve the honey.
Add the ground cinnamon, cumin, pepper, and coriander. Cook for 5 minutes over low heat until a neat consistency.
Preheat the oven for 10 minutes at 230°C (450°F). Score the skin of the duck.
Sprinkle with salt and rub well to infuse the meat.
Place the duck breast skin side down in a cast iron pot. Pour the honey syrup with spices on top. Cook for 8 minutes.
Flip to the other side and cook for 2-3 minutes. Keep warm for 5 minutes.
Slice into 4-5 mm pieces and arrange on warm plates, drizzling with sauce. Serve with a side of mashed potatoes and red wine, such as Buzet.

recipes.title: Chicken Fricassée with Wine (Fricassée de Poulet au Vin)

instructions.text: Cut the chicken into eight pieces and season with salt and pepper. Wash the champignon mushrooms.
Heat the olive oil. Sauté the chicken until golden brown.
Add coarsely chopped shallots, diced onion, and mushrooms. Add the bouquet garni and stew everything together.
Pour in the wine and stir. Bring to a boil, and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, covered. Add water or broth if necessary.
At the end of cooking, remove the chicken. Add butter and cream. Mix the arrowroot with a small amount of cold water and pour it into the sauce, whisking to the desired consistency.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Return the chicken and cook for a couple more minutes.
Serve hot with a side of potatoes or rice.

recipes.title: Chestnuts with Brussels Sprouts (Châtaignes aux Choux de Bruxelles)

instructions.text: Clean the Brussels sprouts: cut off the stems, remove damaged leaves, and rinse them. Bring salted water to a boil. Immerse the Brussels sprouts in the water as soon as it boils again, and cook for 20 minutes.
Make a cut around each chestnut with the tip of a knife, then place them in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil, cook for 5 minutes. Drain the water, let cool, and carefully peel them.
Place the chestnuts in a pot, add the broth, and simmer for 20 minutes over low heat. Drain the sprouts and chestnuts.
Remove the skin from the bacon. Peel the apple, remove the core and seeds, and cut into small cubes.
In a heavy-bottomed skillet, place the bacon and lightly brown it over medium heat. Add the onion, cook for about 3 minutes, then add the Brussels sprouts and stir.
Add the apple cubes. Season with salt and pepper, pour in a little broth, and simmer for about 15 minutes.
Add the chestnuts and continue cooking for about 20 minutes without a lid to reduce the broth. Serve hot.

Cut the meat into 5 cm cubes (remove fat). Cut the peeled onion into quarters. Peel and slice 2 carrots. Clean and mince the garlic. Place everything together with the wine and bouquet garni. Add olive oil and marinate for 24 hours in the refrigerator.

Separate the meat from the marinade. Sauté the meat in oil. Remove it and replace it with the marinade ingredients. Stir for 5 minutes. Put the meat back, sprinkle with flour, and sauté for another 5 minutes.
Pour in the beef broth and bring to a boil. Add the wine from the marinade, bouquet garni, salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 2 hours and 30 minutes.
Peel the pearl onions, sauté for 5 minutes, then add the butter. Simmer on low heat. Fry the bacon.
Sauté the mushrooms in a pan. Peel the remaining carrot, slice it, and add it. Continue cooking for 40 minutes until the carrot is soft.
Serve with pasta (tagliatelle, for example) or mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Rice Pudding with Strawberries Conde (Riz Condé à la Fraises)

ingredients.name: Egg yolk (beaten (whites can be whipped and added, if desired))

instructions.text: Cook the rice in milk with added sugar and the vanilla pod. Remove the vanilla pod.
Mix the cooked rice with the egg yolk, place in a mold, and cook in a water bath in a preheated oven at 200 ℃ for 30 minutes. Remove and cool.

Alternatively, boil the mixture while stirring constantly. Reduce the heat to the lowest and cover the pot with a lid. Cook on low heat for about 40 minutes, stirring frequently, until the mixture thickens and becomes oily. Remove the vanilla pod and add powdered sugar, yolk, and butter to the cooked rice. Mix well and place in a mold.
Sprinkle half of the strawberries with sugar and pour in the brandy. Mix well and let it infuse for 1 hour.
Blend the second half of the strawberries and strain the puree through a sieve.
Mix the puree with a small amount of lemon juice and powdered sugar, trying to achieve a balance between acidity and sweetness.
Place whole strawberries on the cooled rice and pour strawberry puree over the rice.
Put in the freezer for 30 minutes before serving, then remove and let it thaw slightly.

recipes.title: Eggs in Meurette Sauce or Burgundy Style (Oeufs en Meurette à la Bourguignonne)

instructions.text: Peel and chop the garlic, onion, and shallots. Sauté with the bacon in butter, add the flour, sugar, stirring and cook for another 2 minutes.
If using champignon mushrooms, sauté them separately in a small amount of oil until cooked.
Pour in the wine (if possible, Burgundy), whisking, season with salt and pepper, add the bouquet garni, and continue to cook on low heat for 30-45 minutes. The sauce should become creamy.
Place the eggs in boiling water with vinegar. Toast the bread in butter with a crushed clove of garlic.
Place a slice of bread, put a poached egg on it, and drizzle with the sauce.

ingredients.name: Raw tiger shrimp (peeled, with or without tails, fresh or deep-frozen (and in this case, thawed))
Vegetable broth (or chicken broth (or diluted with water and a small amount of powdered broth))

instructions.text: Wash or wipe the mushrooms, cut them into pieces. Peel and finely chop the shallot and garlic. Grate the parmesan, chop the herbs if you are using fresh herbs.
In a large skillet or pot, heat the butter or olive oil. Add the shallot and garlic and cook without browning.
Add the shrimp and quickly fry for 1 minute on each side. Sprinkle with spices and herbs. Mix.
Remove the shrimp and set aside on a plate. Place the mushrooms in the skillet and fry, stirring occasionally, until they are lightly browned.
Put the shrimp back in the skillet, pour in the broth, cream, and parmesan cheese. Season with pepper and salt to taste.
Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and let it simmer for a few minutes over medium to low heat to achieve a thick sauce.
Serve immediately with pasta, potatoes (steamed or mashed), rice, or simply with bread or garlic croutons.

recipes.title: Warm Salad with Poached Egg (Salade Tiède à L’oeuf Poché)

ingredients.name: Salad leaves
ingredients.notes: or a mix of salad leaves

instructions.text: Chop the shallot in a blender with mustard, vinegar, truffle oil, and olive oil.
Blanch the beans until they are tender but still 'al dente', then plunge into cold water.
Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water, drain and slice them about 0.5 cm thick. Fry in a pan for a few minutes with a little oil.
Thinly slice the ham into strips. Boil the eggs for 2-4 minutes in boiling water.
Place the potatoes on plates, add the ham, beans, and poached egg. Drizzle with sauce and serve with green salad.
Heat the butter in a saucepan, add the flour and quickly stir for 1 minute.
Add warm milk, whisk for a few minutes over low heat. Remove the saucepan from the heat and let it cool.
Separate the egg whites from the yolks. Whip them vigorously with a pinch of salt.
Add the egg yolks one by one, then the grated cheese, a pinch of nutmeg, pepper, and a little salt. Gently mix.
Pour into a greased form, about 3-4 cm from the edge.
Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F), bake for 35 minutes.

recipes.title: Chicken Liver Salad (Salade de Foies de Volaille)

ingredients.name: Pine nuts
ingredients.notes: sometimes peanuts or walnuts are used

instructions.text: Carefully clean the chicken liver, remove any white or fibrous parts, then cut into halves or thirds.
Place in a heated pan with oil, add chopped shallot and cook for 5 minutes. Deglaze with vinegar. The liver should remain pink.
In a hot pan, melt butter, add 4 tablespoons of olive oil. When the mixture becomes frothy, add cubed bread and toast, stirring regularly. Lay on paper towels and season with salt.
Peel the apple and cut it into strips.
Wash and dry the salad, place it in a salad bowl, add pine nuts and the apple. Add the still warm liver and gently mix.
Season with salt and pepper, drizzle with oil, sprinkle with parsley, add raspberries and top with croutons. Serve immediately.

ingredients.name: Goat cheese
ingredients.notes: fresh, any other soft cream cheese can be used

instructions.text: Wash the tomatoes, remove the stems. Cut off the top of each tomato, scoop out the flesh with a small spoon.
Place the emptied tomatoes upside down on the countertop to drain the juice.
Mix the cheese with olive oil and herbs. Season to taste. You can add ham or strips of smoked salmon to the filling.
Stuff the tomatoes and close them with the tops, securing with toothpicks. Chill before serving.

recipes.title: Stuffed White Mushrooms with Crab (Champignons Farcis au Crabe)

ingredients.name: Crab
ingredients.notes: canned, can be replaced with crab sticks

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Cut off the mushroom stems and finely chop them. Arrange the caps on a baking sheet.
Mix the softened butter, chopped onion, crab meat, lemon juice, chili pepper, and pepper. Add the chopped mushrooms, cream, parmesan, and mix.
Stuff the mushrooms, sprinkle with gruyère mixed with paprika. Bake the stuffed mushrooms for 5 or 6 minutes until the cheese melts. Remove them from the oven and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Meat Terrine with Prunes (Terrine de viande aux pruneaux)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 180-220°C (425°F). Chop the garlic, shallot, and parsley. Mix all ingredients except for the prunes and parsley.
Grease a baking dish with oil and layer half of the mixture in it. Add all the prunes to form a line, then top with the remaining filling. Cover the dish with foil.
Bake for 1 hour. Then remove the dish from the oven and let it rest for 5-10 minutes.
Remove the terrine from the dish and sprinkle with parsley on top. Serve chilled with salad, sauces, and croutons.

recipes.title: Camembert with Garlic and Tomatoes (Camembert au Four Avec ail et Tomates)

instructions.text: Remove the seeds from the tomato and cut it into small cubes. Add minced garlic, olive oil, and herbs de Provence, and mix well.
Take the camembert and cut a cross on top. Place the garlic and tomato mixture into the cavity formed.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cover with a piece of baking paper and wrap in heavy aluminum foil. Or bake at 150°C (300°F) until golden brown.
Place in the oven on a baking sheet and bake for 15-20 minutes. You can sprinkle with pine nuts and fresh herbs.
Serve hot with wine, dipping small pieces of bread into the cheese.
Peel the garlic and onion, finely chop the garlic into small cubes.
Cut the pork belly into cubes about 3-4 cm apart.

In a heavy-bottomed skillet, melt the fat, add the onion, herbs, and spices, and cook for 3-4 minutes over low heat. Then add the belly and 1/2 cup of water (and wine if using), and bring to a quick boil.
Reduce the heat to the minimum, season to taste, cover with a lid, and cook for 2 hours. Check regularly.
Place the meat in a mortar to mash. Transfer to a glass or ceramic container, leaving space at the top. Let the meat cool for a few minutes, then pour off the fat.
Allow to cool completely before covering with cling film.
Let sit for at least 12 hours before serving. Store in a cool, dry place.
Serve with toast or fresh homemade bread and wine.

Pour the flour into a bowl and make a well in the center. Mix in the diced butter, egg yolk, salt, and about 3 cups of water, pour into the flour, and knead until smooth. Form the dough into a ball and let it rest for 1 hour.
Peel and slice the onion. Heat the butter in a pan and gently sauté the onion for about 15 minutes, stirring regularly. Add bacon if using.
Preheat the oven to 180-200°C (400°F). Spread the dough in a baking dish. Brush with mustard. Place the onion on the dough.
In a bowl, whisk the egg with the milk and cream, season with salt and pepper, add nutmeg, and pour over the onion. Sprinkle with cheese if using. Bake for about 30-40 minutes.
Serve the pie hot accompanied by a green salad.

recipes.title: Eggs Cocotte with Mushrooms (Oeufs Cocotte aux Champignons)

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Peel and chop the onion. Clean the mushrooms and chop finely.
In a pan, sauté the onion and mushrooms in olive oil, season with salt, and add herbs and nutmeg. Pour in the red wine and stir.
Add the cream and thicken over low heat until creamy.
Place the sautéed mushrooms in a mini pot, then crack 2 eggs on top without breaking the yolks. Optionally, sprinkle grated Emmental on top. Bake in a water bath for 10 minutes.
Serve immediately with freshly ground pepper added.

ingredients.name: Shallot
ingredients.notes: or green onion, a few stalks

instructions.text: In a bowl, mix the yolks, mustard, salt, and pepper, then gradually add the oil while continuing to whisk, like mayonnaise. Once a good consistency is achieved, add the vinegar. Add the cream.
Finely chop the cornichons, capers, shallot, and parsley (anchovy fillet, if using). Add them to the sauce. Adjust seasoning if necessary.
Serve with fish and meat dishes or fresh vegetables.

ingredients.name: Vanilla pod
ingredients.notes: or 2 packets of vanilla sugar or cookie crumbs

instructions.text: Peel the apples, cut them into four parts, remove the core and seeds, and cut each quarter in half.
Melt 150 grams of butter in a pan. Sprinkle the apples with cinnamon, half of the powdered sugar, and vanilla sugar. Cook over medium heat for 20 minutes, stirring often.
Remove the crust from the slices of bread. Cut the bread into thin slices, but not too many. Dip them quickly in milk.
Beat the egg, cream, sugar, and a bit of milk if it is too thick.
In a greased pan, layer the bread, layer the apples, layer the bread, and so on. Pour the egg mixture over it. You can sprinkle with sugar. Cover the pan.
Bake for 20-25 minutes at 180°C (350°F). Let it cool a bit. Optionally sprinkle with powdered sugar and cinnamon.
Serve warm or cold with custard or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.
Place the sheet of shortcrust pastry in a pre-greased pie dish.
Brush the pastry with egg yolk and prick small holes in the pastry with a fork. Place in the oven preheated to 200°C (400°F) for 5-10 minutes.
Separate the flesh and skin of the pork belly. Immerse the belly in boiling water for 3 minutes. Drain the water.
Place the skin in a frying pan over very high heat. Melt some fat and add the belly, cooking for 2-3 minutes.
Beat the eggs and cream. Add grated nutmeg. Mix until a homogeneous consistency is achieved. Season to taste.
In the pre-prepared pastry base, lay out the belly, pour the egg mixture, and bake for 20-30 minutes at a temperature of 180-200°C (400°F).
Serve warm with a fresh salad.
Pour 2 tablespoons of warm water into a bowl. Add the yeast and stir.

Pour the flour, 3 pinches of salt, olive oil, and yeast into the bowl. Add 15 ml of water and knead the dough by hand until an elastic ball forms. Cover with a cloth and let it rise for 1 hour at room temperature.
Preheat the oven to 210°C (400°F). Sprinkle flour on the work surface and place the dough on it. Roll out into a large rectangle. Add oregano, thyme, and olives in the center and knead.
Place the dough in a baking dish and sprinkle with flour. Brush with olive oil and make decorative cuts with a knife. Bake for 20 minutes.
Cut the chicken into 2 cm cubes. Cut the onion in half and slice it into 1 cm wide pieces.

Rinse the rice thoroughly in several waters. Drain in a colander and let sit for 1 hour. Transfer to a pot, add 3 cups of water, bring to a boil over high heat, then cover tightly with a lid, reduce the heat and cook for 15 minutes.
Combine broth, soy sauce, sake, mirin, and sugar, along with the already chopped chicken and onion in a skillet. Heat and cook for 5-8 minutes after boiling.
Beat the eggs. Increase the heat and pour in the eggs. Now reduce the heat and cover the dish with a lid. Once the eggs set, turn off the heat and let sit for about 15 seconds.
Serve the chicken over the cooked rice and sprinkle with green onions.
Peel and crush the garlic using a garlic press
Cut the peppers. You can either keep or remove the seeds, according to your preference
Grate the tomatoes, discarding the skin
Place all ingredients in a blender and blend until smooth

recipes.title: Japanese Curry (Karei Raisu カレーライス)

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.notes: or any other meat or seafood

instructions.text: Peel and chop all the vegetables. Cut the potato in half vertically and then into pieces, slice the carrot into half rings, and the onion into half rings as well.
Cut the meat into 3-4 cm pieces. Season to taste and lightly sprinkle with flour.
Heat the oil in a pan and fry the meat until golden brown on all sides, about 5 minutes.
Reduce the heat to medium and transfer the chicken to a bowl using tongs, ensuring as much oil as possible remains in the pot.
Add the grated garlic and ginger and fry in the oil until it evaporates and reaches a rich caramel-brown color.
Add the onion and stir. Cover with a lid and simmer until it becomes transparent and soft (about 10-15 minutes).

Remove the lid, switch the heat to medium, and continue frying the onion, stirring constantly, until it reduces to about 1/8 of its original volume and reaches a caramel-brown paste consistency (about 20-30 minutes).
Once the onion is fully caramelized, add the curry powder and toast it slightly until it becomes very fragrant.

Return the meat, add the broth, carrot, grated apple (optional), chuno sauce, tomato paste, cocoa powder, salt, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat. Cover with a lid and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the potato, cover with a lid, and simmer until the carrot and potato are very tender (another 15-20 minutes). Add the peas.
Add the curry and dissolve it while stirring. Optionally, you can add a little honey. Bring to a boil.
Serve with hot rice.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear. Drain the water and let the wet rice sit for half an hour.

Place the rice in a pot and add 2 cups of water, bring to a boil over high heat without a lid. Once the rice boils, cover the pot with a lid and reduce to low heat, cooking for 15-20 minutes. Remove the pot from heat, cover with a towel and let it sit for another 15 minutes.
Transfer the rice to a bowl and gently mix with a wooden spatula using cutting motions. Allow the rice to cool a bit. Mix in the sesame oil.

Moisten your hands with salted water (to prevent the rice from sticking). Divide the rice into equal portions, place it in your palm, gently squeezing, and use two fingers to make a dent in the middle to place the filling (if using).

Take a bit more rice and 'seal' the dent. Shape the onigiri into a triangle by turning the ball several times, then wrap it in nori (with the rough side inside). Sprinkle with sesame seeds, if desired.

recipes.title: Stewed Meat in a Nabemono Pot (鍋を囲む )

instructions.text: Place water and seaweed in a pot and let it sit for 30 minutes.
Cut the napa cabbage and leek into 5 cm pieces. Thinly slice the carrot. Cut the mushrooms into bite-sized pieces. Cut the tofu into cubes.
Remove the seaweed and bring the water to medium heat. Add sake, mirin, soy sauce, salt, and prepare the dashi broth.
