Add the meat. Once it is almost cooked, add the vegetables. Cover with a lid and cook until the cabbage is soft, then remove the lid.
In the end, add a little buckwheat noodles.
Serve in bowls, seasoned with yuzu and sprinkled with black pepper.
Slice the green onion thinly and diagonally. Beat the eggs. Heat the dashi until boiling. Add salt, soy sauce, mirin, sake, then the chicken.
Add the udon to the soup and cook for 1-2 minutes. Pour in the egg and stir. Add most of the green onion, then immediately turn off the heat.
Divide the noodles and soup into bowls and sprinkle with the remaining green onion and shichimi.
Carefully mix the flour, egg yolk, and cold water. The ingredients should be at the same temperature for the batter to achieve a uniform consistency.
Cut the vegetables or seafood into small pieces that can fit in your mouth.

For vegetable tempura, heat the oil to 170°C (350°F), and for seafood tempura, heat it to 180°C (350°F). Then dip the vegetable or seafood in the batter and place it in a pan with plenty of heated oil.
Place the cooked tempura on paper towels to absorb excess oil. Let the dish cool for a couple of minutes and serve immediately.
Umami sauce pairs perfectly with vegetable tempura.
Peel and chop the garlic, you can use a garlic press. Peel the ginger and grate it on a fine grater.
Combine garlic, ginger, sugar, fish sauce or water. Mix until smooth until it reaches a paste-like consistency. Stir in the chili pepper, adjusting the spiciness to taste.
Cut each cabbage head lengthwise, making incisions in each part from the base, but not all the way through.
Under running water, gently spread apart the leaves. In a large basin, salt each leaf. Stack them, cover with water, and leave for 2 hours or longer, turning every 30 minutes.
Pour water over the rice flour and bring to a boil, add sugar and boil for another minute. Remove from heat and let cool.
Rinse thoroughly to remove salt. Separate into individual leaves, cutting off the bottom part. Let drain in a colander for 20-30 minutes.
Wash the radish, peel it, and slice it thinly. Grate the carrot on a Korean carrot grater. Finely chop the green onion.
Gently squeeze the water from the cabbage and place it together with the radish, carrot, and green onion, kimchi sauce, and rice paste.
Mix thoroughly with your hands. Layer into a jar with brine and leave for 2-3 days. For best results, then leave in the refrigerator for another 2-3 days and store there.

recipes.title: Rice with Beef and Egg Bibimbap (Bibimbap 비빔밥)

instructions.text: Rinse the rice. Soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain the water through a colander.
Cook the rice, using slightly less water than required by the instructions. Then add 2-3 tablespoons of sesame oil and salt, and mix well.

Slice the zucchini. Salt them for 10 minutes. Pat dry with a paper towel. Cut the bellflower roots into pieces 5-6 cm long and 0.3 cm wide. Add salt and let stand for 10 minutes. Rinse and pat dry with a paper towel.

Wash the fern sprouts. Cut them into 5 cm strips. Place in a clean bowl, add 2 tablespoons of soy sauce, 1 tablespoon of sesame oil, 1 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds, and a pinch of pepper. Mix and let sit for 10 minutes. Sauté in a shallow pan with 1 tablespoon of sesame oil for about 5 minutes over medium heat.

Cut the beef into thin long strips (about 5 cm). Place in a bowl, add 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, 2 teaspoons of sugar, 1 tablespoon of sesame oil, 2 teaspoons of rice vinegar, 1 tablespoon of minced green onion, 1 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds, and a pinch of pepper. Mix. Marinate for 20 minutes. Stir-fry the marinated beef in a shallow pan for 2-3 minutes over high heat.

Cut the zucchini in half lengthwise, and then slice into thin slices. Place in a clean bowl, generously sprinkle with salt, and let marinate for 10-15 minutes. Drain the liquid that forms. Add 1 tablespoon of minced green onion, 1/2 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, and 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds. Sauté in a lightly oiled shallow pan for 1-2 minutes over medium heat. Then remove from heat and let cool.

Boil the soybean sprouts for 3 minutes in boiling water (1 cup of water + 1 teaspoon of salt). Quickly drain the water and place the sprouts in cold water. Drain, and place in a separate bowl. Add 1 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1 tablespoon of sesame oil, 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds, salt, and pepper to taste.

Blanch the spinach in salted boiling water for 30-40 seconds. Quickly drain and rinse with cold water. Drain. Cut into thin strips 8 cm long. Place in a clean bowl, add 1 tablespoon of minced green onion, 1 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds, salt, and pepper to taste.

Cut the cucumbers in half lengthwise, and then slice into thin slices. Place in a separate bowl and generously sprinkle with salt. Let marinate for 10-15 minutes. After that, drain the liquid that forms. Add 1 tablespoon of minced green onion, 1/2 teaspoon of minced garlic, 1 teaspoon of sesame oil, and 1/2 teaspoon of sesame seeds.
Heat oil in a pan. Sauté the bellflower roots over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Cut the carrot into thin long strips. Sauté in a lightly oiled shallow pan for 1-2 minutes over medium heat, seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Heat oil in a pan. Rinse the shiitake mushrooms and slice thinly. Sauté in the pan with added salt, just like the carrots. Cook until the mushrooms are fully done.
Combine all the ingredients for the sauce in a small bowl and mix well.

In a large bowl, place a portion of rice. On top of the rice, arrange a small portion of each garnish, distributing them beautifully by color (same colors opposite each other). Drizzle a small amount of sesame oil.
Quickly fry the eggs so that the yolk remains runny. Place one fried egg yolk side up on each dish. Serve with the prepared sauce.

ingredients.name: Freshly squeezed orange juice
ingredients.notes: or water or lemon juice, if desired

instructions.text: Mix soy sauce and sesame oil. Add water, sugar, and chopped garlic, ginger root to the mixture.
Place the Kalbi ribs in the marinade and let them marinate for 2–4 hours.
Place the ribs on a preheated grill rack. Grill the ribs on all sides for 10 minutes.
Place the cooked meat on a dish, then sprinkle with sesame seeds and chopped green onion. Serve with rice or kimchi.
Peel the carrot and cut it into large strips. Peel the garlic and place it in a small container. Rinse the chili pepper and cut it into large pieces.
Slice the green onion into thin strips for the marinade.
Mix the soy sauce, chili flakes, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and sugar to taste. Then add the green onion.
Thoroughly rinse the lettuce leaves in cold water and dry with a paper towel.
It is better to use a grill pan, add a few drops of sesame oil. But you can also cook in a regular frying pan.
Cut the pork belly into thin slices. To make slicing easier, you can freeze it slightly beforehand.
Place the slices of pork on the heated pan and fry until golden brown. Then transfer the pieces of pork to a warm plate.
In the same pan, add the chopped vegetables and chili pepper. Sauté until soft.
Serve the cooked vegetables on a plate with the pork and lettuce leaves, accompanied by the sauce.
Soak shiitake mushrooms in water. Cut the meat into thin strips (if not using minced meat).
Prepare the marinade and mix half well with the meat.
Blanch spinach for a couple of minutes in boiling salted water.
Thinly slice the carrot and onion, as well as the mushrooms. Season shiitake and spinach separately with the remaining marinade.
Fry the meat, carrot, and mushrooms separately. Fry the onion with the meat.
Boil the starch noodles for 2 minutes, and add sesame oil and soy sauce.
Mix the vegetables, meat, and mushrooms with the noodles, sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve with the sauce.
Soak the dried brown seaweed in water for 30 minutes. Drain and cut into 4-centimeter strips.
Remove blood from the beef using a cotton cloth or paper towels. Cut into 2.5 cm square pieces, about 0.2 cm thick. Season with sauce.
Heat sesame oil in a pot. Add the beef and sauté for 2 minutes over medium heat, stirring. Add the soaked brown seaweed. Cook for another 3 minutes.
Add water to the pot. Season to taste and add soy sauce. Boil for 5 minutes over high heat.
When the broth boils, reduce the heat to medium. Continue to simmer for 20-25 minutes.
You can also prepare it with shrimp, scallops, and other seafood.
Bring water to a boil in a pot for the fettuccine. While the water is heating, warm a skillet over low heat so that it is nicely warm and not hot, and turn off the heat.
When the water boils, add salt at the ratio of 10 g per 1 liter of water, cook the fettuccine,
according to the time indicated on the pasta package.
One minute before the pasta is done cooking, place the butter in the warm skillet so it begins to slightly "melt" from the heat of the skillet,

Using tongs or a special pasta ladle, transfer the fettuccine to the skillet, and gently stir the pasta with the butter using a wooden spatula until it is completely dissolved. Save half a cup of the pasta cooking water.
Add 2/3 of the cheese and a bit of the pasta cooking water, if necessary, and mix everything. The cheese should melt into a smooth creamy sauce.
Add the remaining cheese, ground white pepper, oregano if using, and mix.
Serve immediately!

Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a large frying pan over low heat and fry the 2 sausages. After 10 minutes, turn the heat up to medium and cook the sausages for another 5 minutes. Once they are ready, you can push them to the edge of the pan to keep warm.
Add 2-3 slices of bacon to the same pan. Cook them for 2 minutes on each side or until they become crispy.
Add the beans to the pot and cook them for 2-3 minutes, or until they are hot. Use canned beans to save time.
Cut the tomato into thick wedges, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and fry for 2 minutes on each side.
Toast the slices of bread in butter or in the bacon fat for 2-3 minutes or until the bread is brown and toasted. When finished, set the toasted bread aside.
Fry the eggs. Once ready, gather all the ingredients together on a serving plate.
Mix salt with rice flour, gradually add water and stir the rice with the water until it becomes lumpy.
Steam the rice mixture for 20 minutes in a steamer.
Knead the steamed rice mixture thoroughly until it becomes homogeneous.

Pour water into a bowl, add a spoonful of oil, dip your hands into this mixture and roll the dough into thin sausages: take a piece of dough, roll it into a sausage the thickness of a pinky finger and cut into pieces 3-5 cm long using scissors.
Then freeze for later or prepare traditional Korean dishes.
Bring the meat, onion, green onion, and garlic to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium and skim off the foam. Simmer until the meat is tender enough to shred, about 1-2 hours.
Remove the meat and let it cool. Add soy sauce, salt, and pepper to the broth to taste.
Slice the cooled beef into strips about 2-3 cm wide and mix well with garlic, sesame oil, salt, and pepper to taste.
To prepare the jidan (egg garnish), separate the egg white and yolk. Lightly whip the egg white. Mix the yolk with a spoon until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick skillet over medium heat. Pour each part of the egg into a thin layer, spreading it with a spoon. Cook each side quickly (do not overcook).
Cut the egg pancakes into short thin strips. Slice the green onion diagonally into thin strips. Sauté in a hot pan.
Bring the broth to a boil. Add the pieces of rice cakes tteok and cook until soft, usually about 5-8 minutes.
Pour the prepared soup into individual bowls and garnish with shredded beef, eggs, green onions, and seaweed.
Wash the cucumbers, cut them lengthwise crosswise, not reaching the end. Sprinkle with salt inside and out, place in a bowl and leave to brine for 30 minutes.
Boil water, pour the rice flour with a cup of boiling water. The consistency should be a thick paste. Cool to room temperature.
Soak the gochugaru pepper in 5–6 tablespoons of water, stir and let it swell. Chop the ginger and garlic.
Grate the carrot on a Korean carrot grater. Thinly slice the green onion. Cut the onion into very thin half rings.
Combine the chili pepper, ginger with garlic, rice paste, fish sauce, add everything to the carrot with onion, mix well and let sit for 30 minutes.
Rinse the cucumbers from the salt. Stuff each cucumber with the marinade, place them all in a tray.
Leave the kimchi at room temperature for 6 hours, then store in the refrigerator.

recipes.title: Ragout with Spicy Rice Cakes Tteokbokki (Gungjung Tteok-bokki 떡볶이)

instructions.text: Bring water to a boil, add the rice cakes. Cook until all pieces float to the top. Drain through a sieve. Mix with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and 1 teaspoon of sesame oil.
Mix the sauce ingredients well and set aside. Cut the stems from the mushrooms and slice thinly.
Combine the mushrooms and beef, if using, with 1 tablespoon of the sauce. Let marinate.

Cut the zucchini in half lengthwise, then slice thinly crosswise and slightly diagonally to make the cuts longer. Generously sprinkle salt on the zucchini slices and set aside for 10-15 minutes. Squeeze out excess moisture by hand.
In a lightly heated and oiled pan, sauté the onion, carrot, and zucchini over medium heat for about 2 minutes. Add the green onion and transfer to a bowl.
In the same pan, cook the beef and mushrooms over medium heat until the meat is cooked, 1-2 minutes. Reduce the heat to medium or low. Add the rice cakes and fry for another 1-2 minutes.
Add the tteok to the bowl with the vegetables along with the pine nuts and remaining sauce. Adjust seasoning with extra soy sauce, pepper, or sugar as needed. Serve warm.
Add 4 cups of water to the gosari. Cook over medium heat with the lid on until done, about 30 minutes.
Turn off the heat and let it cool in the cooking water. Once done, rinse in cold water and drain. Cut into stems about 10 cm long, removing any tough ends if present.

In a large pot, bring the meat, onion, radish, and garlic to a boil in 14 cups of water. Reduce heat to medium and skim off the foam. Cook covered until the meat is tender enough to shred, about 1-1.5 hours.
Remove the vegetables and meat from the broth. Once the meat cools enough, slice into strips about 7-10 cm long.
Rinse with cold water and drain. Cut the green onion into 10 cm strips. Thinly slice the soaked mushrooms.

In a pan, heat the sesame oil over low heat and add the chili powder. Turn off the heat as soon as the oil starts to redden and the chili flakes become slightly paste-like. This will only take a few seconds. Do not burn.
Add the meat, gosari, mushrooms, 1 tablespoon of soy sauce, and garlic. Mix well.
Add the meat and gosari mixture along with 1 tablespoon of soup soy sauce to the broth. Stir in gochujang and doenjang and simmer over medium heat covered for 20 minutes.
Add salt and pepper to taste. Slowly pour in the beaten eggs, stir, and turn off the heat. Add the bean sprouts and green onion. Serve with rice.
Clean and soak mussels in salted water (1 tablespoon of salt per 2-3 cups of water) for 30 minutes or longer.
Remove the top shell from the crab and discard the gills. Thoroughly clean the body using a kitchen brush or toothbrush under running water. Break (or cut) the body in half (or quarters).
Clean the squid and fish and cut into pieces. Peel the shrimp.
Slice the cabbage, radish, and carrot into thin pieces. Thinly slice the onion and mushrooms. Cut the shallot into equal lengths.
Mix the seasonings with 2-3 tablespoons of broth or water.
Using a wide, shallow pot or pan, carefully arrange the vegetables in groups, except for the watercress.
Place the seafood pieces on top of the vegetables, putting the mussels closer to the bottom. Add 3 cups of broth and the seasonings, reserving 1 tablespoon for taste.
Top with watercress and cook over medium heat until the mussels open, the fish is cooked through, and the vegetables are tender.
Drizzle with lemon juice. Stir occasionally.
You can add more broth and remaining ingredients while eating.

recipes.title: Spicy Zucchini Stew (Hobak Gochujang Jjigae 호박 고추장 찌개)

instructions.text: Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms in cold water for 30 minutes or more, until the stems are completely soft.
Add about 120 grams of dried anchovies to a pot and add 6 cups of cold water. Do not cover the pot while making the broth. Bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes.
Increase the heat to medium and add the chopped onion and mushrooms. Cover with a lid and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Chop the vegetables. Zucchini cooks quickly and becomes very soft, so cut it into large pieces.
Remove the mushrooms from the water, gently squeeze them, cut off the stem and trim part of the cap. Chop the onion.
Add the gochujang and doenjang pastes to the boiling broth with anchovies, and mix well. Add 1 cup of mushroom water.
Add the zucchini, tofu, minced garlic, garlic powder, gochugaru, and pepper with salt.
Increase the heat to medium, cover with a lid, and cook for another 10 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low and let it simmer for another 5-10 minutes. The stew is more flavorful the next day when it sits.

ingredients.name: Salted shrimp Saeu-jeot
ingredients.notes: or fish sauce, can substitute with 3/4 teaspoon of salt

instructions.text: Beat the eggs. Strain the mixture through a sieve for a smooth liquid consistency. Or beat very well.
Beat the eggs with the anchovy broth or water with salted shrimp (saeu jeot) or salt.
Take a greased clay pot or ceramic pot.
Add the egg mixture to the pot. Cover with a lid and simmer on medium heat on the stove for about 5-7 minutes.
Reduce the heat to minimum. When the omelet rises, add the chopped onion.

recipes.title: Red Bean Stuffed Cookies Panoppan (Bungeoppang 붕어빵 )

instructions.text: Mix all dry ingredients together. Whisk the egg and milk in a separate bowl. Then mix everything together.
Heat the baking tray over medium heat on both sides. (about 1 min on each side)
Take a fish-shaped baking mold. Open and coat each fish mold (a total of 4 molds) with butter. It's better to use a pastry brush.
Reduce the heat to a minimum and pour the liquid dough into one side of the mold (2 fish) only for 1/3.
Quickly place red bean in the center of the fish. About 2 full teaspoons.
Pour dough on top to completely cover half of the fish.
Close and flip.
Bake at slightly above medium temperature for 2-3 minutes on each side.
When a golden crust forms on both sides, transfer to a plate and let cool for a few minutes.
You can also use other fillings such as jam, fruit preserves, custard, and chocolate.

recipes.title: Spicy Pollock Roe Soup Al Tang, Al Jjigae (알탕)

instructions.text: Thaw the roe and milt if using frozen.
Add dried anchovies (or dried dashi) and seaweed to a pot of water. *** Simmer (do not boil) for 20 minutes. Remove the seaweed and anchovies. Set aside.
Chop the radish, zucchini, onion, green onion, tofu, red chili pepper (if desired), garlic (2-3 cloves). Also mince the garlic and ginger.
In a small bowl, add all the seasoning ingredients: gochujang, red chili powder, guk ganjang (soup soy sauce), sake, ginger, garlic, garlic powder, and salt.
Bring the broth to a boil over medium heat (with the anchovies and seaweed). Add the seasoning to the broth and stir.
Add the onion and radish to the pot. Wait for it to boil, about 3-4 minutes.
Then add the milt and pollock roe, as well as fish and seafood if using. Cook for 5-6 minutes.
Reduce the heat, then take each pouch of roe and cut into 2-3 pieces with scissors. You can skip this step and just leave the roe whole.
Increase the heat. Add all the vegetables and tofu. Add the garlic and chili pepper. Cook for another 4-5 minutes until the zucchini is cooked.
Add the bean sprouts and fresh green onion just before serving.
Serve with rice.

recipes.title: Pancake with Green Onion and Seafood Pajeon (Dongnae Pajeon 동래 파전)

ingredients.name: Vinegar
ingredients.notes: rice wine or white or 1 tablespoon of lemon juice

instructions.text: Make the Choganjang sauce by mixing gochujang, vinegar, sugar, and sesame seeds.
Make the Gochujang sauce by mixing soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and water.
Wash the green onion and minari. Cut the green onion into pieces 15 cm long or 1/2 of the full length of the green onion. The green onion should be young and tender.
Cut the minari into pieces 7 cm long. About 1/2 the length of the cut green onion pieces.
Cut the scallops and shrimp into large pieces. Beat the egg in a small bowl.
Season the ground beef with soy sauce, mirin, syrup or sugar, minced garlic, and sesame oil.
Prepare the batter by mixing flour, rice flour, sweet rice flour, anchovy broth, and salt. Mix well.
Heat a thick-bottomed frying pan (preferably cast iron) over low heat. Pour about 2 tablespoons of oil.
Layer the green onion, then the minari on top. Pour the liquid batter over the green onion and minari.
Quickly (reduce the heat if it seems to burn) sprinkle the pancake with ground beef, scallops, and shrimp.
Pour the beaten eggs on top. Flip the pancake to cook the other side. Cook for about 2 minutes until the pancake is nicely browned.
Serve with sauces and rice wine.
Wash the potatoes and dice them. Cook the potatoes in a pot with enough water.
Once it boils, reduce the heat to medium and cook for about 10 minutes. Drain the water.
Add the potatoes back to the pot, add 2 cups of water, 3 tablespoons of soy sauce, sugar, vegetable oil, and shiitake mushrooms.
Bring to a boil and cook, covered, for 30 minutes, until the liquid reduces to 1/3.
Uncover, add maple syrup. Continue cooking until almost all the liquid evaporates. Add more soy sauce (up to 1 tsp) to taste.
Mix well. Add a little sesame oil and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
If desired, add onion or nuts and a bit more seaweed (dashima) for extra flavor.
Add 1 teaspoon of sugar and 1 teaspoon of dry yeast to 3/4 cup of warm water.
Mix all the dry ingredients for the dough. Combine the yeast-sugar water with the flour. The dough should be completely wet and sticky.
Let the dough rest for 3 hours at room temperature. The dough should double in size when it is ready.
Mix the sugar, cinnamon, and chopped walnuts.
When the dough is ready, heat about 3 tablespoons of oil in a pan over medium heat.
Pour about 1 teaspoon of oil into your hand and rub both hands together to make them slippery. Take a piece of dough the size of a golf ball and roll it into a pancake larger than your palm.
Add 1-2 teaspoons of filling in the center of the dough and close it by forming a ball. Place it in the pan, pressing it down with your palm.
Brush with oil, slowly flattening it until the diameter is about 10 cm wide.
Fry in oil over low heat for 3-4 minutes, until the edges turn brown.
If using neck bones, soak in cold water for 1 hour to remove excess blood and odor. If using pork ribs, soaking is not necessary.
Boil the pork bones in a pot. Add a little mirin, 1 tablespoon of pepper, 1 piece of ginger, and 1/2 tablespoon of ground coffee.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then simmer for 10 minutes. Drain. Add the pork (just not the liquid) back into the pot.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into large cubes about 4 cm.
Rinse the green onions, perilla leaves, chili peppers, shishito peppers, and green cabbage.
Cut the chili peppers into 3 cm pieces. Cut the green onions into 5 cm pieces. Slice the perilla leaves into thick strips.
Mix all the sauce ingredients well.
In the pot with the pre-cooked pork, add water and sauce. Cook over medium heat for 10 minutes.
Add potatoes, chili peppers, cabbage, and 1/2 of the green onions to the pork and stew for 35 minutes or until the meat separates from the bones.
Add perilla leaves and more green onions. Cook for another 2-3 minutes.
Serve with rice and bananas without spices or pancakes.
Soak the beans for 12 hours before cooking.
Wash the vegetables well and cut them into cubes. Cut the sun-dried tomatoes into strips and then into small pieces, finely chop the shallot onion.
Put 4 tablespoons of oil into a large pot and heat it, add the chopped vegetables, tomatoes, peas, borlotti, add water to cover all the vegetables, salt, and cook for at least 1 hour.
Optionally, you can add rice or pasta. Add basil, cover with a lid, and cook for about 10 minutes.
Season with marjoram and adjust salt to taste if desired.
Serve with croutons and grated parmesan.

recipes.title: Neapolitan Mussel Soup (Zuppa di Cozze alla Napoletana)

instructions.text: Clean the shrimp: remove the head and tail, peel the shell, cut the back, and extract the intestinal tract (black thread) by gently pulling it with the tip of a small knife.

Rinse the mussels under running water. Then use the back of the knife blade to remove all growths and shells (parasites that form on the shell). Always under running fresh water and using a stiff brush, vigorously scrub the mussels to remove all dirt.

Take the cuttlefish and carefully remove the head and tentacles from the mantle; wash thoroughly under running water, remove the cartilaginous handle and ink sac. Cut the cuttlefish in half along the longest side, then slice into strips.
Clean the octopus: rinse it under running water, transfer it to a clean dry towel, and dry it with kitchen paper.

Place the octopus on a cutting board and cut at eye level with a knife, also remove the beak of the octopus, then hang it and beat it with a hammer. Rinse under cold running water and remove the insides from the bag, washing it thoroughly inside. Wash and scrub the head and tentacles with your hands.
Cook in a pot with water for 40 minutes. Drain and let cool. Then cut the tentacles into small pieces.
Sauté the garlic clove in a little oil. When the garlic is nicely browned, remove it with kitchen tongs and add the mussels.
Add white wine and cook covered for about 5 minutes. After this time, check all the mussels: discard those that do not open.
Turn off the heat, drain, reserving the cooking liquid. Separate the empty shells from the full ones, placing the latter in a container.
Put the garlic and a splash of oil in the pot. Sauté the garlic, and when it turns golden brown, remove it.
Add the cuttlefish, add salt and pepper to taste, shrimp, and cook on low heat for 2 minutes, stirring.
Add the cleaned octopus and mussels, shrimp, pouring all the reserved cooking liquid after their braising.
Add the peeled tomatoes and cook for another 10-15 minutes, until the sauce reduces.
Slice the baguette into 3-4 cm thick slices, place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and drizzle each crouton with olive oil.
Place in the oven or grill for 4-5 minutes until crispy and golden brown.
A few minutes before the soup is done, add the chopped parsley. Optionally, you can add 1 chili pepper.
Serve with crispy and delicious croutons.

ingredients.name: Dry Marsala wine
ingredients.notes: or Vin Santo or any other dessert wine

instructions.text: Whisk the egg yolks with sugar. Add Marsala and stir.
Transfer to a saucepan over a very hot, but not boiling, water bath.
Continue whisking until the cream becomes soft and airy.
Remove from heat and pour into dessert cups for serving.
Sprinkle with cocoa and serve immediately with shortbread cookies. Optionally add fruits.

Pour the flour onto a working surface, forming a well in the center, and add the eggs. Break the eggs with a fork and gather the flour from the sides, then knead by hand until a soft and smooth dough is formed.
Cover with plastic wrap and let rest for 30 minutes in a cool place.
Chop the meat, prosciutto, and mortadella.
Melt the butter in a pan and add the meat, frying for about 10 minutes. Let cool.
Chop the meat together with the prosciutto and mortadella and mix. Add the Parmesan cheese, nutmeg, pepper to taste, and the egg. Mix until a homogeneous mixture is obtained.
Roll out the dough into a thin sheet about 0.6 mm, trying to keep it as moist as possible, using a little flour.

Cut into small squares. Place filling in each square. Take a square and fold it into a triangle, tip to tip, pressing the edges well to stick (if the dough has dried slightly, lightly moisten the edges with a small amount of water). Join the ends of the triangle at the base.
Place on a floured surface. Then boil in meat broth.
Serve in broth, with cheese and herbs or with toppings to taste.

recipes.title: Hot Appetizer Roman Style Saltimbocca (Salt' im bocca alla Romana)

instructions.text: Cut the veal, then place each piece on a cutting board, remove all nerves and fat, and then pound to make it thin.
Place the ham and a leaf of sage on top and secure with a toothpick.
Heat 40 g of butter and 20 g of olive oil in a pan over medium heat.
Dredge each slice on one side in flour and place in the pan, increase the temperature to sear well.
When the meat is golden brown, add the white wine and let it evaporate.
Cover and cook for another minute. Transfer the saltimbocca to a plate and keep warm.
In the same pan, add 10 g of butter and water. Make a slightly thick creamy sauce. Season with pepper.
Pour the creamy sauce onto the bottom of the serving dish and place the pieces of meat on top.
Wash and dry the tomatoes. Cut them into slices about 6-7 mm thick using a thin, sharp knife.
Place the tomatoes on a wooden cutting board and sprinkle with salt (in Caprese, salt should be added only to the tomatoes).
Slice the mozzarella into 6-7 mm thick pieces. Place the cutting board in the refrigerator for a few minutes.
If the mozzarella loses moisture, pat the slices dry with a cotton cloth.
Add a few basil leaves to the bottom of the plate. Alternate in the dish: a slice of tomato, a slice of mozzarella, every 2-3 pieces, a few basil leaves.
Sprinkle with a pinch of dried oregano and pepper. Add a few more basil leaves. Drizzle with a little olive oil.
Prepare a good meat broth.
Mix the ingredients for the passatelli, adding grated lemon zest, plenty of nutmeg, and salt.
Let the dough rest for about 1 hour, then shape the passatelli by cutting the dough into strips 6-10 centimeters long.
Bring the meat broth to a boil, season with salt, and add the passatelli, gently stirring and cooking for about 2-4 minutes (they will be ready when they float to the surface).
Pour into bowls. Serve hot with grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

ingredients.name: Sea fish
ingredients.notes: mackerel, monkfish, cod, red mullet, flounder, capon, eel

ingredients.name: Seafood
ingredients.notes: squid, crab, sea scallops, baby squid, young octopuses, shrimp, mussels, sea snails

instructions.text: Thoroughly clean all the fish. Sauté the onion and two minced garlic cloves in oil with a large sprig of parsley. Let it cook on high heat with white wine vinegar.
Peel the tomatoes, remove the seeds, and chop (if using fresh). Place in the pan and season with salt and pepper.

Rinse the mussels and snails, previously placed in cold water, sprinkle them with salt, and throw them into boiling water. Cook for about an hour. Drain and rinse them again under running water at least 5/6 times!
Add the fish, starting with the squid, cut into strips, which should be cooked alone for at least 15-20 minutes.
Then add the baby octopuses and continue cooking for another 10 minutes. Continue adding crabs, shrimp with garlic sauce, cook for another 10 minutes, and add the pre-cooked mussels and snails.

Wait another 5 minutes, trying to cook on very low heat and with a lid. Then add the monkfish, toothfish, pieces of mullet, cod, and only at the end add the mullet and sea scallops, which are the most delicate and require very few minutes of cooking.
Cook for a maximum of another 15 minutes, trying not to mix the fish, but gently moving the pan to avoid breaking it. Turn off the heat and let it sit for 10 minutes.
Serve with slices of bread.

recipes.title: Eggplant Casserole Melanzana Alla Parmigiana (Melanzane Alla Parmigiana)

instructions.text: Wash the eggplants, dry them and peel them. Cut them into pieces lengthwise to a thickness of 2-3 mm.
Place in a bowl, sprinkling a little coarse salt layer by layer. Cover with a plate and place a weight on top. Leave for at least 30 minutes.
Put a little oil and peeled tomatoes in a pot. Cook on low heat and cover with a lid for about 30 minutes.
Rinse the eggplants to remove the salt, and thoroughly dry them with absorbent paper.
Dip the slices in flour one by one and fry for 2-3 minutes in boiling peanut oil (about 170°C (350°F)) in a pan. Drain the oil and dry on absorbent paper.
Pour a small layer of sauce into the baking dish. Lay a layer of fried eggplants on top, then drizzle with sauce, sprinkle with parmesan and mozzarella.
Distribute another layer of eggplants and sprinkle again with parmesan, mozzarella, sauce, and so on, until all ingredients are used. Finish with a layer of sauce and parmesan.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 30 minutes, browning the surface during the last 5 minutes of cooking by setting the oven to grill mode.
Remove from the oven and let cool before distributing basil leaves over the surface.
Wash the vegetables. Cut the celery thinly horizontally. Also, slice the tomato and onion.
Pour oil into a pot and add the onion. Fry until golden. Then add the celery and tomatoes.
Season with salt, basil leaves, and stir. Cook for about 5-7 minutes with the lid on.
Add the broth and eggs one by one, being careful not to break the yolk. Cook with the lid on until the eggs are well done. Sprinkle with pecorino.
Toast the bread. Place it in a bowl, top with an egg and pour the Acquacotta over it.
Serve hot with olive oil, garnished with fresh basil leaves and grated cheese.
In a non-stick pot, add oil and sauté the garlic, then remove it.
Then sauté the onion until golden brown.
Add the ground meat and simmer for a couple of minutes, then add the tomato puree and cook for about 20 minutes.
In a large bowl, add grated mozzarella, ricotta, and hard-boiled egg.
When the sauce is ready, transfer 80% of the meat with the tomato sauce to the bowl and mix everything.
Boil the conchiglioni in lightly salted water to al dente, using a proportion of 10 g of salt per 100 g of pasta and 1 liter of water.
Using a teaspoon, take and stuff each individual conchiglioni shell, then place it in a previously greased baking dish.
Pour the remaining sauce into the baking tray. Sprinkle with grated parmesan and basil leaves on top.
Drizzle with olive oil and bake in a preheated oven at 230°C (450°F) for about 20 minutes.
Take a heavy skillet with a thick bottom. Place cumin, coriander, cardamom, black pepper, cinnamon, cloves, and bay leaves in it and put it on low or medium heat.
Toast the spices for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until they change to a darker shade and start to release their aroma.*
When everything is ready, remove from heat, let it cool, and grind everything in a coffee grinder.
Add ground nutmeg. Mix and place in a container with a tight lid. It should yield approximately 0.5 cups.
Store in a dark, cool place. The average shelf life is 3 months. After that, the spices begin to lose their aroma.
Wash and cut the peppers into cubes. Peel and chop the onion.
In a large skillet, heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil and the peeled, whole garlic cloves.
Add the onion. Sauté over medium heat for about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the bell peppers and season with salt and black pepper, stir and cover. Cook for another 15 minutes over medium heat.
Remove the garlic cloves, pour in the tomato puree, add whole olives (optional), stir and cook for another 15 minutes covered.
Garnish the finished peperonata with fresh basil (optional).
It can be served warm or cold, with bruschetta, as a side dish for meat or fish, and also as a sauce for pasta.
Cut the bread into cubes, fry in a non-stick pan with a few tablespoons of olive oil and minced garlic. Fry on low heat, stirring frequently.
Clean the lettuce, rinse it with cold water, select the inner leaves (they are sweeter and crunchier) and then tear them apart by hand.

Place the yolks in a blender cup and beat them, adding vegetable oil. Then add lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, mustard (if desired), and beat until smooth. Add the anchovy fillets, salt, ground pepper, and blend everything until smooth again. Place the finished sauce in the refrigerator.
If desired, you can add chicken breast to the salad, cut into fairly thick slices or strips, fried in a pan with two tablespoons of olive oil and a small amount of coarse salt.
Place the salad leaves at the bottom of the salad bowl, then add the croutons, Parmesan flakes, pieces of chicken, and finally dress with the sauce.
Optionally, you can add halved cherry tomatoes on top.
Serve and mix all the ingredients.
Cut the bread and let it dry in a paper bag for two to three days, then place it in a bowl and moisten with enough water and vinegar, squeeze the bread, and crumble it with your hands.
Peel the onion and slice it thinly, peel the cucumbers, cut off the ends, remove the seeds, and slice them thinly, wash the tomatoes thoroughly and chop them very finely.
Put everything in the bowl with the bread, then wash and add the basil.
Season with oil, salt, and mix, refrigerate for at least an hour.
Optionally, you can add some cheese and oregano or other ingredients to taste.
Serve cold accompanied by a good chilled white wine, such as Bianco di Pitigliano or Ortrugo.
Heat the oil in a skillet, add the clove of garlic.
Wash the peppers and remove the stem. Place them whole in the oil (if they are small) or cut them into pieces.
Sauté everything well so that the chili pepper flavors the oil. This will be the base for the sauce.
When the garlic turns golden and before it becomes too dark, remove it.
Add the tomato and reduce the heat, season with salt and cook for 15-20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta al dente in a large pot of boiling salted water.
Rinse, gently dry, and chop the parsley, grate the pecorino cheese.
Season the pasta with the sauce, adding a good handful of parsley and pecorino to each serving. Serve immediately!
Cut the eggplants into small cubes, sprinkle with coarse salt, and leave in a colander for at least 1 hour to let the water and bitterness drain out.
Cut the celery into small cubes, place it in a pot of boiling water with a little salt, and leave for 5 minutes. Drain the water and transfer to a cotton cloth.
Chop the onion and sauté it over low heat in a pan with a little oil.
Add capers, olives, and pine nuts and cook for 10 minutes over high heat, stirring constantly (add a little water if necessary).
Cut the tomatoes into small cubes and cook them in the pan with the onion for at least 20 minutes, stirring well.
Sauté the celery in the pan with some olive oil.
Dry the eggplants and fry them in vegetable oil, drain the water and add them to the mixture with the onion.
Add the celery, mix, and cook over medium heat for 3-4 minutes, then add the vinegar and sugar.
Allow the vinegar to evaporate, then turn off the heat and serve the caponata with a little basil.

recipes.title: Lamb Burger with Cheese and Asparagus

instructions.text: Form a patty from the chopped meat and refrigerate it for 30 minutes.
Place the yolks in an immersion bowl.
Melt the butter over medium heat.
Insert the immersion blender into the bowl, and while keeping the blender at the bottom, slowly pour in the hot melted butter.
As soon as the mixture begins to thicken, you can gently raise and lower the blender.
Add lemon juice, salt, and peppers, and continue whisking until the desired creamy consistency is achieved.
Cut the brioche in half and toast the inner sides on a grill or skillet for 1 minute.
Grill or fry the patty, bacon, and asparagus, brushed with olive oil for 3 minutes on each side (the asparagus can be briefly blanched in boiling water beforehand). Season with salt and pepper.
After flipping the patty, place the brie cheese on top and cover with a lid to melt.
On the bottom half of the brioche, place the asparagus, drizzle with hollandaise sauce, add the bacon, then the patty with cheese, and drizzle with the remaining sauce on top.

instructions.text: In a saucepan, sauté the chopped leek, onion, garlic, and fennel in olive oil until soft.
Add the wine and let it evaporate completely.
Soak the saffron in boiling water – 0.5 cup. Peel the tomatoes and puree them or use blanched tomatoes. Add them to the vegetables along with the saffron and paprika. Cook for 5 minutes.
Place all fins, heads, and tails of the large fish along with cleaned and gutted small fish into the sautéed vegetables. Add water to completely cover the scraps.
Bring to a boil, add the bouquet garni, and reduce the heat to medium.
Cook for at least 40 minutes.
Remove the bones from the broth, and puree it with a blender, then strain through a sieve. During cooking, all the small fish should dissolve completely in the broth.
Slice the potatoes into circles about 2 cm thick.

Divide the cleaned fish into firm (scorpionfish, monkfish, rooster, eel, and sea bream) and more delicate (sunfish and whiting). First, cook the pieces of firm fish in the prepared broth over high heat for six minutes, then cook the soft fish for another six minutes.
Arrange on a plate. Strain the broth and pour it into serving bowls. Serve the bouillabaisse with toasted slices of baguette and rouille sauce.
Separate the yolks, blend them with a blender, then slowly pour in the olive oil. Add garlic, mustard, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and saffron water. Mix until smooth.
Crack the egg into a bowl.
Add the sifted flour to the mixture and stir.
Add salt, sugar, and baking powder to the egg and mix.
Pour in the milk and knead the batter. It should be sticky but not too thick.
Skewer half of the cheese stick and a sausage on a skewer.
Using a spoon, wrap the batter around the corn dog.
Coat the corn dog in bread crumbs and fry until golden in hot oil at 175°C (350°F).
Boil the mashed potatoes
Add salt, pepper, five spice seasoning, and finely chopped chorizo. Mix well.
Using a measuring spoon, take some mashed potatoes, place a piece of cheese inside, and roll into a ball.
Repeat the procedure until the mashed potatoes are finished.
Dip the ball into the batter and immediately coat it in panko breadcrumbs.
Fry in oil heated to 180 degrees for 3 minutes.
Cut the piece of meat across the grain butterfly-style (divide a 2 cm thick piece of meat in half without cutting all the way through, opening it like a book)
Pound the meat thoroughly through plastic wrap until the schnitzel is 4-5 mm thick.
Salt and pepper.
Prepare 3 plates:

Put flour on one, lightly beat the egg on the second, keeping some egg whites and yolks separate, and put bread crumbs on the third, adding paprika and dried herbs (thyme, basil or oregano) if desired.
Dredge the schnitzel in flour until fully coated, then dip it in the egg, and finally place it in the bread crumbs, coating it completely.

If you want the coating to be beautifully wavy and slightly separated from the meat, you should lightly spray it with water or "gently pat it" with wet hands before breading. The water will evaporate during frying and lift the coating.
In a preheated oil at 170°C (350°F) in a large skillet, place the schnitzel and fry until golden brown for 2 minutes on each side. The oil should completely cover the schnitzel.
Place the schnitzel on a paper towel to absorb excess fat, and serve immediately with lemon and potatoes. The garnish is usually served separately.
Remove the skin from the chicken thighs. Remove the bone. If using chicken fillet, butterfly it (along the whole fillet, thus dividing it into 2 wide halves).
Cut into strips 1 cm wide across.
Mix all the marinade ingredients and marinate the chicken pieces for at least 15 minutes.
While the chicken is marinating, cut the white part of the green onion into 1 cm lengths. Break the dried chili peppers and remove the seeds.
Mix all the sauce ingredients in a separate bowl. To better dissolve the sugar and salt, they can be first dissolved in a small amount of water. If cooking in a wok, water can be omitted entirely.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok (frying pan) and sauté finely chopped ginger, garlic, Sichuan pepper, and chili pepper.
Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry quickly until cooked.
Add the white parts of the green onion, pour in the sauce, mix well, and add peanuts.
Serve with rice.
Soak the clams in cold water with 1 tsp. of salt for 2 hours to expel the sand.
Then rinse them and place them in a heated pan, add the wine, and cover with a lid for a few minutes until the shells open.
Remove them from the pan, discarding any unopened clams.
Strain the liquid through cheesecloth into a bowl. It will be useful a little later.
Heat the olive oil in the pan, and sauté the garlic.
If using guanciale or bacon, first render some fat from it and sauté the garlic in that. No oil is used in this case.
Meanwhile, bring water for the pasta to a boil.
Add the fennel seeds and literally after 20 seconds, add the blanched tomatoes. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the reserved liquid, stir, and literally after a minute, add the capers, sliced olives, oregano, and pesto sauce. Stir and cook for 1 minute.
Add the cooked clams, season with salt and pepper to taste, and add the cream. Stir and turn off the heat.
Drain the pasta and add it to the sauce. Add the chopped parsley, stir, and serve immediately.
Clean and gut the fish. Cut off the fins of each fish with kitchen scissors or a knife. Remove the gills from the fish by cutting them out with kitchen scissors.
Make vertical cuts along each side of the fish, evenly spaced along its length, about 2 cm apart - this is very important, as carp are quite bony. This will help cook the fish faster.
Rinse the fish under cold water and dry it.

Mix the marinade ingredients, pour the mixture into a glass or plastic container. Add Sichuan pepper if using. Place the fish in the container and ensure the marinade completely covers the fish. Marinate for 30 minutes to 3 hours.
Slice the ginger and garlic into the thinnest possible slices.
Cut the onion into half-moons.
Heat oil in a wok over medium heat. If you don't have a wok, use the largest, deepest frying pan you have. A wok is really needed here as its shape prevents the tail fin from burning.
Meanwhile, prepare the sauce. Mix the tomato sauce, sugar, soy sauce, Chinese cooking wine, water, and corn starch and stir vigorously to combine. Set aside.
Check the oil temperature. You want it to be around 200°C (400°F). If you don't have a thermometer, the oil is ready when a drop of flour thrown into the oil sizzles immediately.
Remove the carp from the marinade and coat it in flour. Shake off the excess, and fry the fish in the oil for 8 minutes on each side.
Remove the fish from the wok, leaving about 1/4 cup of oil in it.

Throw the minced ginger, onion, chili, and minced garlic into the wok and stir-fry over high heat for 2 minutes. Add the sweet and sour sauce and mix well. Bring to a quick boil and mix well. Cook for 2 minutes.
To serve, pour some sauce onto a plate, place the fish on top, and garnish with finely chopped green onion and cilantro. This dish is best served with simple steamed white rice.

recipes.title: Squid Salad with Fennel and Avocado

instructions.text: Cut the fennel in half, then into thin slices, including the green parts. Slice the onion into half-moons. Cut the red pepper into small strips, halve the tomatoes, and roughly chop the parsley leaves. Peel and dice the avocado.
Put all the chopped vegetables in a bowl.
Prepare the dressing. To do this, combine all the ingredients for it in a separate bowl.
Clean the squid and dry them. Cut part of the tentacle in half or into quarters lengthwise (and cut any longer pieces into shorter segments) and slice the squid body into rings about 1 cm thick.
Heat 1 tbsp of olive oil in a pan, and fry the black mustard seeds in it.
When the mustard starts to pop, add the squid and sauté for 40 seconds, stirring.
Add the squid to the bowl with the vegetables and pour the dressing over the salad.
Mix everything thoroughly and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Serve with baguette. You can sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.title: Masala Omelette (like in the movie "Spices and Passion")

instructions.text: Whisk the eggs in a medium bowl until the whites and yolks are combined and the mixture is homogeneous.
Add chopped cilantro, salt, garam masala or curry powder, turmeric, and cayenne pepper flakes.
Whisk again to achieve a uniform consistency.
Meanwhile, place the tomato halves and green onion in a hot skillet to slightly wilt. (medium heat - about 3 minutes)
Heat ghee in a non-stick skillet over medium heat. Spread the melted ghee across the entire surface of the skillet.
If using mustard seeds, toss them in and wait for them to 'pop'.
Add the egg mixture. There should be a slight sizzling sound. Control the temperature for the omelette by moving the skillet off the heat.
Once the eggs are added, use a bamboo fork or a simple plastic fork to stir the eggs. I personally use a small silicone spatula.
Working quickly, break up the curds that form at the bottom. Keep the skillet moving back and forth with the other hand, and if it gets too hot, remove the skillet from the heat.

Stir the mixture with a wooden spatula until it becomes creamy. If cooked too much, it will turn into scrambled eggs, as the mixture will no longer hold together. Keep in mind that the eggs will continue to cook off the heat.
Once the eggs are set, smooth the top of the omelette with a fork or spatula and level it out.
Tilt the skillet while holding the handle with one hand, and using a fork or spatula, start rolling the omelette towards yourself. When you reach the other end, move that end to the rolled omelette.
Flip it onto a plate and serve with sun-dried tomatoes and sliced green chili pepper, if using.
Soak the dried white mushrooms in water for at least 2-3 hours.
Rinse the pearl barley well under running water and soak it for 2 hours.
Then boil it in a ratio of 1/3 to water until semi-cooked for 30-40 minutes, then drain the water.
Take the mushrooms, chop them finely into strips, and return them to the pot.
In the same water, make a strong mushroom broth.
Add the pearl barley and the freshly chopped mushrooms to the boiling broth.
Cook until ready for about 30 minutes.
In a skillet, melt the fat, add the finely chopped onion, then the finely chopped carrot and parsley root, and sauté for 10 minutes.
Next, you can either make a 'thickener' by mixing the flour with the broth to a liquid sour cream consistency, or just add the flour to the sauté and a ladle of hot broth.

15 minutes before the end of cooking, add diced potatoes to the broth, season with the sautéed onion and carrot. Add salt, pepper, caraway seeds, dill seeds, and bay leaf. If you prepared the 'thickener' separately, pour it in, stir, and cook for the remaining 15 minutes.
Serve in bread, sprinkle with dill on top. Serve sour cream separately.

ingredients.name: Yellow curry paste (or 5-6 tbsp store-bought paste)

instructions.text: Cut the dried chili peppers into pieces with scissors and remove most of the seeds.
Grind them into powder in a coffee grinder, mortar, or blender.
In a stone mortar, add cumin seeds, coriander seeds, white pepper, and grind them into powder. Set aside in a bowl; add curry powder.
Add lemongrass, galangal, ginger, turmeric, salt to the mortar and grind into a paste. When the mixture becomes too wet, add dry spices to help absorb the liquid.
Add ground chili pepper, shallots, and garlic; grind into a smooth paste. Add shrimp paste and mix.

Reduce ¾ cup of coconut milk over medium heat until thickened and the coconut oil separates (or use coconut oil). If the oil doesn't separate after reducing the coconut milk to very thick, just continue with the recipe.
Add the curry paste and fry for 2-3 minutes over medium heat until the oil starts to separate from the paste.
Add the chicken and stir in the curry paste, then add 1 cup of coconut milk and 1 cup of water and stir.
Add 1 tablespoon of fish sauce and 1 tablespoon of palm sugar and bring to a boil. Simmer the chicken for 30 minutes.
After 15-20 minutes, add the potato, onion, and add more water if necessary to ensure the liquid fully covers the potato. Simmer for another 15-20 minutes or until the potato is fully cooked.
While the curry is simmering, prick the cherry tomatoes with the tip of a knife, making a half-inch cut.
When the curry is simmering, taste and adjust the seasoning with fish sauce, sugar, and tamarind juice.
Turn off the heat and add the cherry tomatoes. The heat of the curry will be enough to cook them while you serve the curry.
If desired, sprinkle with fried shallots. Serve with jasmine rice or quinoa.
Slice the shallots thinly.
Dry them slightly with paper towels or drying.
Fry in hot oil over medium heat until browned.
Remove with a slotted spoon from the oil, and dry with a towel.
Peel the potatoes and slice them thinly.
Chop the mushrooms and sauté them in butter until the liquid evaporates completely and the mushrooms are golden brown.
Clear a space in the center of the pan, add the butter and melt it.
Pour the flour into the butter and stir to ensure the butter completely absorbs the flour.
Add water and immediately add the cream. Stir and bring to a boil.
Once everything reaches a boil, reduce the heat to low and cook until a thick creamy mixture forms (like béchamel with mushrooms). Season with salt, pepper, and herbs to taste.
Grease the bottom of the dish with garlic and generously coat it with butter.
Layer the potatoes, then add salt, pepper, herbs, and a pinch of nutmeg.
Evenly cover with the creamy mushroom mixture. Sprinkle with Parmesan.
Repeat the layer of potatoes, mushrooms, and top with a layer of grated Cheddar.
Add the final layer of potatoes, sprinkle with Parmesan, and pour cream on top to lightly cover the potatoes.
Cover with foil and place in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 1 hour.
After that, remove the foil and cook for another 30 minutes.
Then, take it out of the oven and let it cool for at least 20 minutes.
Serve by cutting into portioned pieces.
The meat must be thoroughly chilled. Then cut into large pieces and pass through a meat grinder with fine holes.
Peel and finely chop the onion and garlic, and add them to the meat mixture.
Crush all the seasoning ingredients in a mortar until powdered.
Place the meat and fat in a mixer and, gradually adding the seasoning and then water (in the form of ice), mix into a homogeneous mass.
The temperature of the mixture should not exceed 12.5°C.
For baking, take a rectangular mold, grease it with oil, and fill it with the prepared mixture. Smooth the surface and make diamond-shaped cuts on it (about 5 mm deep) with a knife.

Then place the mold with the mixture in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F), and bake for about 1 hour. You can measure the temperature inside the meat mixture. The finished meatloaf should be 70 degrees Celsius.

recipes.title: Vietnamese Fried Spring Rolls (Chả giò, Nem rán)

instructions.text: Soak the glass noodles and dried wood ear mushrooms in warm water beforehand.
Dry them well by squeezing out the water and patting with a paper towel.
Grate the carrot using a medium grater.
Finely chop the noodles and mushrooms with scissors.
Peel and chop the shrimp.
In a bowl, mix all the filling ingredients, add the egg, and knead well with your hands.
Let it marinate for 15 minutes.
Spread a clean kitchen towel, prepare a container with water for dipping the rice sheets.
Dip the sheet in water a couple of times. Allow excess water to drain by holding it vertically for a few seconds.
Place it on the towel, put 1 tablespoon of filling on the sheet, and roll it up tightly like an envelope.
The tighter the roll, the fewer problems you will have while frying.
Roll as tightly as possible to avoid air pockets that create bubbles while frying.
Set aside the rolled spring roll and continue rolling them until the filling is finished.
Heat the oil to a temperature of 190-200°C (400°F). You can check its readiness by dipping a wooden spoon or spatula into it. If it reaches the desired temperature, bubbles will form around the wood.
Fry the spring rolls for 5-6 minutes until golden brown, avoiding them touching each other for the first 3 minutes, otherwise they will stick.
Place the finished spring rolls on a paper towel to drain the oil.
Serve immediately with nuoc cham sauce or sweet chili sauce.
Dissolve the sugar in hot water, add the fish sauce, lemon juice, vinegar, crushed chili pepper, and garlic. Mix well.
First, thaw the dough.
Grate all the cheese on a coarse grater, add the egg to the cheese and mix.
Unroll the dough and cut it into equal squares.
Add the filling to each square, placing a small piece of butter on top.
Fold the opposite edges of the square together in the middle, then press the resulting "ribs" tightly together several times, forming small "crests" that should look like a cross on top.
Be sure to poke the dough in several places with a fork, so that the khachapuri does not "burst" in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Place the khachapuri on a baking sheet with parchment or a silicone mat.
Brush the top of the khachapuri with egg yolk and bake in the oven for 25-30 minutes.
Sear the shank on all sides in butter until a brown crust forms.
Remove from the pan.
In a large pot, lightly sauté the chopped onion and carrot in butter. Add a crushed clove of garlic.
Place the seared shank on top of the vegetables. Pour in the light beef broth or water.
Bring to a boil, add the bouquet garni, peppercorns, and cook for 2 hours in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
At the very end, add the tomato paste and stir. Cook for another 10 minutes.
When the broth is ready, strain it, let it cool, and remove the fat from the surface.
It can also be frozen for later use.
The meat can be served as a separate dish called ossobuco.
Chop the bacon and render its fat over low heat. Add a bit of butter to it and melt.
Sauté the onion, carrot, and celery until soft.
Add the flour and make a brown 'roux' by stirring and cooking the flour until brown.
Add the tomato paste, stir, and pour in the brown broth. Add the bouquet garni, bring to a boil, reduce to low heat, and cook for 2 hours.
During this time, the sauce should reduce to almost half its original volume.
At the very end, add salt and pepper, strain, and use to prepare sauces such as: Bourgignon, Marché de Vin, Charcuterie, Bercy, Robert, Lyonnaise, Chasseur, Mushroom, Madeira, and Port.
For this dish, you can use either chicken fillet or thighs. The chicken should be cut as thinly and small as possible so that it cooks in just a minute.
Next, we use a traditional Chinese marinade consisting of light soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, and adding baking soda, which makes the chicken incredibly tender.
Mix well and set aside, while we prepare the noodles.

The noodles need to be soaked in freshly boiled water with the heat turned off for 3-4 minutes. This method of cooking prevents the noodles from sticking together and prevents them from becoming mushy during further cooking.
The noodles should be freed from moisture, and in this state, they can actually be stored in the refrigerator for several days, adding a little vegetable oil, and cooked as needed.
Next, prepare all the vegetables, cutting them into strips, while chopping the onion and garlic.
Instead of Napa cabbage, bok choy is used in China, but unfortunately, it is extremely rare in our supermarkets. You will not notice much difference in taste.
Next, prepare the sauce by mixing all the sauce ingredients together.
Heat a pan and blanch the harder vegetables first, then add the softer vegetables and green onion.
Add a little salt and pepper, and temporarily remove them from the pan.
Then fry the marinated chicken in vegetable oil for a minute, add the noodles, and pour in the sauce.
Stir to absorb the sauce maximally into the noodles, and add the reserved vegetables. Add some bean sprouts and green onion, and it's all ready!
Peel the shrimp, remove the intestinal vein, and set aside the shells and heads.
Finely chop the leek, shallot, and carrot, and sauté in butter in a pot.
Add the shrimp shells and heads and sauté them with the vegetables for 5 minutes. You can also add 200 grams of shrimp meat if desired.
Add garlic, orange zest (if using), and tomato paste, mix, and pour in the brandy. Immediately ignite it in the pot (flambé) until the alcohol burns off.
Add the sherry and let it evaporate.
Add shrimp or fish broth (or water), and cook over medium heat for about 25 minutes.
In a saucepan, melt the butter, add the flour, and mix. Sauté a bit until the "roux" turns brown. About 6 minutes.
Add 3-4 ladles of the cooking broth from the pot and whisk until smooth.*
Using an immersion blender, puree the entire mass in the soup until smooth.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing the mixture with a wooden spatula.
Return the pot with the strained soup to the heat.
Add thick cream (or sour cream) to the soup and thicken it with the velouté sauce.
Add cayenne pepper with salt and pepper to taste. **
Sauté the shrimp in a pan with butter.
Pour the bisque into bowls and garnish with the cooked shrimp.
Serve with a baguette.

recipes.title: Fish-Squirrel in Sweet and Sour Sauce

ingredients.name: Carp
ingredients.notes: common carp or another medium-sized fish

instructions.text: Clean the fish from scales and gut it.
Cut off the head at an angle, slicing behind the front fin.
Remove the gills.
Now you need to make fillets without cutting them off the tail. Make a cut along the spine.
Cut off the rib bones. Make a cut on the other side of the spine, cut off the rib bones from the other side.
Cut off the spine at the level of the tail. You should get 2 fillets connected by the tail.
Cut off the thin rib section that has almost no meat along with the fins.
Make deep cuts (to the skin, but not damaging it) along each fillet, and then across.
Salt and pepper the fish, you can also marinate it for just 5 minutes by sprinkling with Shaoxing wine, and coat it in starch. The starch should completely cover all the cuts as well.
Lay the fish out so that the 'backs' of the fillets touch each other, moisten the edges along their length and press them together to stick the fillets at the edges.

In preheated oil at 160°C (325°F), lower the fillet skin side down, holding it by the tail and the opposite edge, preventing it from coming apart. The pan or wok should be spacious enough for the fish to fit completely.
When the top slightly hardens, lower the fish fully into the boiling oil and let it fry for 5 minutes.

Sprinkle the fish head with starch, turn the fins forward, and you can fix the mouth open either with a toothpick or a piece of carrot inserted inside. Turn the fins forward to resemble the 'squirrel's' paws.
Place it in the pan with the fish.
If the oil does not completely cover the fish, continuously ladle oil over the exposed parts of the fish.
The best option is not to flip the 'squirrel' until the entire flesh has a golden, crispy crust.
Lay the finished fish on a paper towel to let the oil drain.
Place the 'squirrel' on a large plate, add the head, and optionally insert green peas into the eye sockets.
Prepare the sauce. For this, mix all the ingredients for it and bring to a boil in a saucepan or wok over high heat.
Pour the sauce over the fish and serve.
Melt the butter over medium heat and stir in the wheat flour.
Add the milk, and stirring, bring to a boil, then immediately reduce the heat and thicken the sauce to the desired consistency.
You can also add a little nutmeg, and let the sauce absorb the aroma from the onion, bay leaf, and a couple of cloves.
Melt the fat in a pan until it becomes cracklings. Remove them from the pan. Set aside.
Fry the onion in the rendered fat until golden. Add the garlic.
Add the chopped mushrooms and fry on high heat for about 15 minutes until they release most of their moisture.
Add the cream, Dijon mustard, curry seasoning, black pepper, and salt to taste. Also, if using herbs de Provence, add them too.
Mix everything and cook for another 15-20 minutes, lowering the heat to the minimum.
Before serving, add the reserved cracklings, sprinkle with chopped parsley, and mix.
Serve with mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Turkey Thigh Baked in a Tagine

instructions.text: Mix all the marinade ingredients in the tagine.* Cumin and coriander seeds can be left whole.

Completely cover the turkey with the marinade on all sides, evenly sprinkle barberry, raisins, and lingonberry on top of the meat, and let marinate for at least 30 minutes. Optionally, add a whole dried spicy pepper. The turkey should be skin-side down.
Cover with a lid and place in a preheated oven at 225°C (425°F) for 90 minutes.
If you are using a different dish or sleeve instead of a tagine, then bake for no more than 60 minutes.
After 30 minutes, turn the turkey to be skin-side up.
After 1 hour, reduce the temperature to 195°C (375°F), remove the lid, and bake until crispy for 15 minutes on each side, basting generously with the boiling marinade.
Serve by slicing the meat into portions with rice or couscous, drizzled with the sauce in which the bird was cooked.
Wash the octopus, remove the beak located on the inside of the body.

Bring the water with wine (or water) in a large pot to a near boil, and immerse the thawed octopus 3 times for 30 seconds with a break of 30 seconds between immersions. This is done so that the skin of the octopus does not peel off during cooking.
Add the octopus to the boiling liquid, add the onion, thyme, star anise, cloves, bay leaf, and peppercorns.
Reduce the heat to the minimum so that the liquid simmers slightly.
Add salt and cook the octopus for an hour.
After an hour, remove it from the pot and let it cool for about 20-30 minutes.
Do not pour out the broth. It will be used later for cooking potatoes, and you can also make risotto or sauce with it.
Take a plastic bottle (1.5 L) with a flat bottom.
Cut it in half, and we will use the part with the bottom to prepare the carpaccio.*
Prepare the octopus by cutting off the tentacles at the joint. Cut the head into several pieces.
Place the tentacles in the bottom of the plastic bottle, packing them tightly each time with a regular glass wine bottle, for example.
Then add the remaining pieces and pack them well.
Make longitudinal cuts in the bottle at the top, like petals, so that the cut is slightly deeper (literally 3 mm) than the level of the packed meat.
Fold the petals towards the center to compress the octopus as tightly as possible, and wrap it well in plastic wrap.
Leave it in the refrigerator overnight. During this time, the gelatin will bind the parts of the octopus together.
The next day, you can cut the bottle (or pull on the petals to 'unfold') to remove the octopus roll.

Now, it can be sliced on a slicer or with a very sharp knife into pieces and served with potatoes, capers, drizzled with olive oil with garlic and sprinkled with smoked paprika. Optionally, you can also drizzle with the green sauce 'salsa verde.'
Peel the potatoes, wash them, and cut them into slices 7 mm thick.
Throw them into the boiling broth from the octopus and cook for 10 minutes.
Then, remove them with a slotted spoon and place them on a paper towel to drain all the liquid, while heating olive oil over medium heat in a pan.
Place all the potato slices in the pan so that each slice is on the surface of the pan. There should be no slices on top of each other. It is better to do this in several batches.
Fry on both sides until golden brown.
Prepare a container with ice water, adding ice.
Dip the greens in boiling water for 30 seconds, and immediately transfer them to the container with ice water. This shock procedure will preserve the bright green color.
Blend in a blender with olive oil, garlic, salt, and sherry vinegar or lemon juice.

recipes.title: Valencian Paella with Rabbit and Chicken

instructions.text: Cut the meat into small pieces. Then roughly chop the green beans and shell the Lima beans.
Clean the artichokes by removing inedible parts and cut them in half. **
In a wide pan, heat the olive oil with a pinch of salt. It is ideal to cook in a special pan called "paella"***
Fry the meat until crispy. It is important to cook over medium heat to prevent the meat from drying out.
Push the meat to the sides and add each type of vegetable to the center of the paella, distributing them around the perimeter as they cook. Finally, lightly fry the tomato puree.
Add water at a ratio of 4 parts to each part of rice, and as soon as the water boils, add saffron, salt, and pepper. Continue simmering for another 10 minutes.
Add the rice and distribute it evenly across the pan. Top with sprigs of rosemary. It is very important not to stir the paella after this.
Simmer for 5-8 minutes on high heat, then reduce to medium, and when the rice rises to the surface, lower to low (the cooking time after adding the rice is 18-20 minutes).
Soccorrat - the crispy crust that is an essential feature of proper paella. To achieve it, increase the heat in the last minutes, and you should hear a light crackling. This is the crust forming.
Valencian paella should be slightly dry (like pilaf), golden-orange in color.
Cover the paella with a clean towel, remove from heat, and let it rest for 10 minutes before serving.
Serve with lemon wedges. Lemon juice greatly enhances the incredible flavor of this Valencian dish.

recipes.title: Viennese Pork Ribs in the Oven

instructions.text: Clean the ribs from membranes. Cut off all the fat. There should be none, or it should be minimal.
Mix all the marinade ingredients in a bowl. Rub the ribs well with the marinade and leave to marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F) in the top and bottom heating mode.
Place the ribs on a rack in a baking dish.
Cook for 45 minutes.
Turn the ribs over and cook for another 15 minutes. Meanwhile, you can prepare the BBQ sauce.
You can cook further in two ways:
METHOD 1. Pour wine and water into the dish so that the water does not reach the rack with the ribs by a few mm.
METHOD 2. Remove the rack, place the ribs in the dish, and pour in the wine with water to about 5 mm high.
Mix all the ingredients for the sauce in a saucepan and place over medium heat.
Bring to a boil, reduce the heat to minimum, and cook for 15 minutes until the sauce thickens.
You can add 1 teaspoon of starch dissolved in cold water for a thicker consistency.
Completely coat the ribs with BBQ sauce and cook for 30 minutes at 180°C (350°F).
After 30 minutes, flip the ribs, coat with sauce, and cook for another 30 minutes.
15 minutes before the end of cooking, fry the potato wedges in vegetable oil.
Separate 2 yolks. Melt the butter over low heat and remove all the foam that forms.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl with an immersion blender (the attachment should not be a whisk) and slowly pour in the hot butter, keeping the blender on the bottom until the mixture starts to thicken.
Continue pouring in the butter, raising and lowering the blender to achieve an even thick consistency.
Add the vinegar and lemon juice, then the remaining ingredients in any order.
Serve the ribs with French fries and dip sauce.
Cut the chicken into small pieces and set aside.
Prepare the masala. For this, place quartered onions, coconut flakes, ginger, garlic-ginger paste, and spices in a food processor and blend to a smooth paste, adding a little water if necessary.

Heat the oil in a deep pot over medium heat. Add the paste to the hot oil and fry until the oil starts to separate from the masala (spicy onion paste). Stir frequently to prevent the masala from burning. Now add the chicken and fry until the pieces turn opaque, about 8 minutes.
Add the coconut milk, green chili pepper (if using), and potatoes. Season with salt to taste and mix.

Cook until the chicken and potatoes are done, about 15 minutes. This dish should have a medium-thick sauce; if it is too thick, add a little warm water and cook for a few minutes. If the sauce is too thin, cook until it thickens.
Add the blanched tomatoes and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn off the heat and serve the curry on plates.
Garnish with chopped fresh coriander leaves and serve with rice and a green salad or a simple vegetable side dish.
Separate 2 yolks. Melt the butter over low heat and remove all the formed foam.
Whisk the yolks in a bowl with an immersion blender (attachment not whisk), and slowly pour in the hot oil, keeping the blender on the bottom until the mixture starts to thicken.
While continuing to pour in the oil, lift and lower the blender to achieve an even thick consistency.
Add the vinegar and lemon juice, then the remaining ingredients in any order.
Defrost the tentacles and dry them with a paper towel.
Peel, wash, and cut the potatoes into sticks.
Peel the onion and slice it into thin half-rings.
Chop the garlic finely.
In two frying pans, heat enough vegetable oil over medium heat to fry the potatoes, while caramelizing the onions in the other.
Sprinkle the potatoes with coriander, curry spice, black pepper, and paprika. Add salt to taste. Mix well.
After 5 minutes, add the chopped garlic. Continue cooking, covering the potatoes with a lid, and stirring every 2 minutes.
Fry until cooked through.
In the pan, fry the squid tentacles for 1 minute.
Arrange on plates and serve immediately!
Serve with a dipping sauce. You can find the recipe here: https://foodies.academy/recipe/samyj-vkusnyj-dip-sous

recipes.title: Caprese Salad with Anchovies and Capers

instructions.text: Wash the tomatoes and slice them 6-7 mm thick with a sharp knife on a cutting board, and sprinkle with salt (in caprese, salt is added only to the tomatoes).
Slice the mozzarella 6-7 mm thick.
Place a few basil leaves on the bottom of a plate.
Alternately place a slice of tomato, a slice of mozzarella,
Sprinkle with a pinch of dried oregano and pepper.
Add a little olive oil.
Top with anchovy fillets and capers.*
Optionally, garnish with basil leaves.
Let the dish rest for 25 minutes, and serve.
Crush all the spices in a mortar. Finely chop the onion, garlic, and ginger.
Add breadcrumbs, egg, and crushed spices to a large bowl.
Add the minced meat and mix it well with the spices.
Roll into balls with a diameter of 3-4 cm, place them on a cutting board or flat plate so that they do not touch each other, and put them in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
In a large deep skillet, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
Place the balls in the skillet one by one, leaving space between them, usually cooked in several batches.
Fry the meatballs, turning them occasionally, until they are cooked and all sides are browned. They don't need to be fully cooked, just browned on all sides.
Remove the balls to a plate when they are browned.
Add the green curry paste, let it fry a little.
Add coconut milk to the skillet, stir, and add
palm sugar and fish sauce.
Add the balls back to the skillet. Add the chopped vegetables and asparagus.
Simmer them in the sauce until cooked, about 7-10 minutes.
Serve with rice, generously drizzled with sauce and lime juice. Garnish with basil leaves.
Make a crosswise incision in the fillet, 2 mm deep, on the skin side.
Salt and pepper on all sides.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place a pan over the heat and immediately lay the fillet skin-side down in it.
This technique will allow the duck fat to render.
Once enough fat has rendered, add the crushed garlic and the sprig of rosemary.
Add the pear (or apple) slices cut into 5 mm thick wedges, and sauté them on both sides.
Arrange the apples in a fireproof dish, and place the fillet on top, skin-side up.
Bake for 8-10 minutes.
When the duck is done, remove the dish from the oven and slice the breast into 1 cm thick pieces.
Serve on a plate, alternating duck and pear (apple).
Serve with risotto, mashed potatoes, or couscous with vegetables.
Optionally, drizzle honey over the duck.
Mix all the spices. The best seasoning is made from freshly ground spices.
Store in an airtight jar.

ingredients.name: Bread
ingredients.notes: white or black cut into cubes

instructions.text: Bring water to a boil.
Pierce the eggs with a blunt side of a needle to prevent excessive pressure from breaking the shell during boiling.
Boil for exactly 3-4 minutes, depending on how runny you want the eggs.
Place the eggs in ice water for 2 minutes to make the shell easy to peel.
Peel them and mix with the bread, crushing the eggs with a fork.
Add pepper, salt, and sprinkle with cilantro on top.

recipes.title: Spaghetti with Garlic, Olive Oil, and Chili Pepper

instructions.text: Place the spaghetti in boiling salted water (the ratio is 10 g of salt and 1 liter of water for 100 g of pasta) and cook for the time indicated on the package until al dente.
In a pan, pour in the olive oil, add sliced garlic, hot pepper, and a bit of water from the spaghetti to prevent burning.
If desired, add salt.
Heat on low to allow the garlic to infuse its flavor into the oil.
Add parsley and the cooked spaghetti. Mix everything and sauté for 1 minute over high heat.
Serve the cooked spaghetti in a deep plate. Sprinkle with spicy croutons and garnish with a sprig of parsley.
Cut the neck into "steaks" of 2-2.5 cm each.
Rub with olive oil, and generously sprinkle with salt, ground cumin, and pepper.
Let marinate for at least 30 minutes.
Place them on a hot grill and cook the meat for 5 minutes on each side until crispy, then continue cooking until the meat is fully cooked.
The main thing is not to overcook it so it doesn’t become dry.
When the meat is ready, transfer it to a large pot with a lid, add the cut-up butter, crushed garlic cloves, oregano, and generously drizzle with freshly squeezed lemon juice.
Add lemon zest if using.
Close the pot with a lid and shake it well so that the butter, juice, and oregano evenly coat the pork.
Let it "rest" for 5 minutes.
Serve with vegetables and BBQ sauce.

recipes.title: Salmon Steak with Creamy Cheese Sauce

instructions.text: Heat the oil in a pan. If you use parchment paper and pour oil on top, the fish will never stick to the pan.
Add crushed garlic cloves.
Place the steaks and fry for literally 1.5-2 minutes on each side.
Transfer to plates.
Pour the cream into a saucepan, bring to a boil, and immediately reduce the heat to medium.
Dissolve the cheese in the cream, stirring the contents with a spoon.
Add pesto, pepper, and salt.
The sauce should thicken literally in a minute.
Drizzle the fish with the sauce on top, and add leaves of greens or microgreens.
Generously drizzle with freshly squeezed lemon juice.

Be sure to choose potatoes with a high starch content. To determine if the potato variety is suitable for draniki, cut the washed potato in half, rub the halves against each other, and if enough starch is released, the halves will stick together.

The first thing to prepare is the mushrooms. Cut the fresh mushrooms into pieces and fry them in a dry skillet for 5 minutes, until the moisture starts to evaporate. Add vegetable oil, finely chopped onion, and cook until golden brown.
Grate the potatoes on the finest grater. Grate the onion on the same grater and add it to the grated potatoes. You can speed up the process with a blender with the appropriate attachment.
Salt and pepper to taste, add minced garlic, and mix well.
