Optionally, you can add half of the fried mushrooms to the potato mixture.
Drain excess liquid through a sieve, trying not to press the potato mixture too hard.
Pour vegetable oil 3-4 mm deep, heat it in a skillet, and place the potato mixture in small pancakes.
Cook over medium heat, so that a crust forms quickly, and the oil does not absorb into the pancakes.
Add sour cream to the fried mushrooms. Bring to a light boil, reduce the heat, and add pepper and salt to taste.
Serve the draniki generously drizzled with mushroom sauce and sprinkled with green onions or dill on top.
Crack the eggs into a deep bowl. Add salt, pepper, curry if using, and mix.
Grate the zucchini (or courgette) on a coarse grater into the same bowl. If the zucchini is young, there is no need to peel it.
Mix, add flour and chopped herbs, minced garlic, and mix again.
Pour vegetable oil into a frying pan in a layer of 3-4 mm. Heat over medium heat.
Add the zucchini mixture with a spoon, and fry until lightly browned on each side.
Meanwhile, fry the sliced shiitake (or other mushrooms) in a dry frying pan over high heat for 5 minutes.
Add finely chopped onion, and pour in vegetable oil.
Fry until done.
Reduce the heat to minimum, add sour cream, salt, pepper, and chopped parsley. Mix.
Serve the deruny with mushroom sauce.
Melt the butter over medium heat and evaporate all the moisture from it. Skim the foam from the surface.
Place 2 yolks in a immersion blender cup and blend them without lifting the blender from the bottom.
Gradually pour in a thin stream of melted butter, about the thickness of a "mouse's tail."
Start lifting the blender from the bottom, making back-and-forth movements while continuing to pour in the butter.
Add a little ice-cold water, which will help emulsify the yolks.
The sauce should thicken due to the emulsion and the volume should double.
Add lemon juice, salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
First, it is necessary to render the fat, for this place pieces of pork belly in a cold heavy-bottomed saucepan, turn on medium heat, and render for 5 minutes.

When fat appears in the saucepan, add the butter, carrot, onion (you can also add celery root, grated on a medium grater), sugar, and cook over medium heat for 5-10 minutes until soft and caramelized.
Then sprinkle the vegetables with flour and continue to cook for a couple more minutes. We do this to make a white roux.
Add the blanched tomatoes to the saucepan, and sauté them for 10 minutes.
After that, add the broth, wine, and garlic. Optionally, cloves can be added.
Cover with a lid and send to the oven for 1.5-2 hours.
Strain.
Once ready, pass the tomato sauce through a sieve, and for a smoother texture, you can first blend it and then strain the sauce through a sieve.
Adjust the sauce for salt and pepper.
Cook a rich broth. You can add vegetables to the water while cooking – onion, carrot, root vegetables, desired spices, and at the end — herbs.
After cooling, the broth should be strained.
In a stirred homogeneous velouté, simmer over heat for 10 minutes, constantly stirring.
At the end of cooking with
Melt the butter in a pan and sauté the flour in it for 2-3 minutes.
Gradually pour the broth into the pan with the flour, constantly mixing the mixture with a spatula until it comes to a boil.
Stir until a homogeneous consistency is achieved and simmer over heat for 10 minutes, constantly stirring.
Add salt.

First of all, you need to decide on the cookware in which the pilaf will be prepared. If cooking over an open fire, a kazan is the ideal option. However, if cooking on a stove, a kazan is not very suitable as its bottom area is much smaller than that of a regular thick-walled pot. The ideal option for the stove is a low wide pot with a thick bottom.
These proportions are calculated for a minimum of a 5-liter kazan/pot.
Rinse the raisins, barberry, and dried apricots well, then soak the raisins and dried apricots in water and leave them in it while preparing the zirvak.
Peel the garlic heads, but do not separate them into cloves. Peel the onions and carrots, slice the onion into half rings, and julienne the carrot to a thickness of 1 cm.

Heat the kazan over medium heat and melt the lamb fat/oil cut into small cubes in it. When the fat is fully melted, remove the cracklings with a slotted spoon. In this oil, fry half a sliced onion until it darkens. ***

Remove the onion. Increase the heat to maximum and heat the oil. Add the lamb cut into large pieces and lightly fry without stirring until a crust forms on one side. Then stir and fry for literally a minute on the other side. The amount of meat should be such that it fits in the pot/kazan in a single layer, otherwise, it will not 'sear' properly and will be dry later. It is also not advisable to over-fry the meat, as it may darken, not be crumbly, and will be dry.
Remove the meat from the kazan with a slotted spoon. If you do not plan to fry the onion to a dark color, you can leave the meat in.
At this stage, you can add a couple of pinches of salt and cumin.
Add the chopped onion and fry it until golden brown. Some recipes recommend frying until a dark golden color. This will take just under 10 minutes.

Add half of the carrot, fry without stirring for 3 minutes, then mix everything well and cook for another 10 minutes over high heat, stirring occasionally. The carrot needs to be fried initially rather than stewed, as this will help prevent it from becoming fragile during cooking.
Return the lamb, mix, and pour in hot water (not boiling) so that it covers everything in the kazan by 1 cm (about 500 g).
Immediately add the pre-soaked chickpeas (if using).
Bring to a gentle boil, add the dried hot pepper, soaked barberry, reduce the heat, and simmer (this is called zirvak) for 40 minutes without covering.

Now let's deal with the rice. If you are using Devzira rice, soak it first in warm 60-degree Celsius water for at least 1 hour, and rinse well until the water runs 'clear' before adding the rice to the zirvak. If using regular (non-parboiled) Basmati or Jasmine, rinse it until the water runs 'clear' and soak it for 10-20 minutes before the zirvak is ready.
If using parboiled Basmati rice, just rinse it well right before adding it to the zirvak. Otherwise, you are guaranteed to overcook it in the pilaf.****
And now, after 40 minutes, add salt, ground hot pepper, black ground pepper, cumin, rubbing it between your palms, ground coriander, paprika, turmeric, and marigold.
The zirvak should be slightly oversalted, as the rice will absorb a lot of salt.
Also, add the second half of the carrot, lightly pressing it down with a slotted spoon.

After another 20 minutes, place the garlic directly into the zirvak, then add the soaked raisins and dried apricots, increase the heat to maximum, and layer the rinsed rice evenly on top. Do not mix it yet; everything should remain layered. Now pour boiling water to cover the layer of rice by 2-3 cm (the remaining 1.5 l). Distribute it evenly over the surface, turn the heat up high, and leave the lid off to let the water evaporate.

When all the water evaporates (in about 5 minutes), carefully mix the rice (without mixing it with the meat below) from the edges towards the center, then use the handle of a slotted spoon to make several holes to the bottom of the pot and check for excess moisture. This will manifest as a brown fatty murky suspension appearing in the hole made. If there is still a lot of moisture, the excess will go down through the holes and will evaporate soon, making the liquid clearer. Now the rice is ready for what's called 'steaming'.

Reduce the heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly with a lid, and let it steam for 25-35 minutes. This depends on the type of rice, covering the lid with either a paper towel or cloth. Ideally, cover the top of the rice with a plate that fits the diameter ****
This way, all the excess moisture will be absorbed by the cloth/paper.
To prevent it from turning into porridge, you can open it after about 15 minutes and taste the rice; it should be al dente and crumbly.
When the rice is ready, turn off the heat and mix everything thoroughly. Cover with a lid and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Then serve it on a plate in a mound, topped with the delicious stewed garlic from the kazan.
Serve with ayran and Achik Chuchuk salad, which consists of tomatoes, onions, and chili peppers, dressed with oil and salt.
Uyghurs also add cucumber to the salad.

ingredients.name: Arborio, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano rice

instructions.text: Sauté the chopped mushrooms in butter until cooked. Set aside. You can skip the salt, as salt and pepper will be added in the risotto itself.
In a pot, melt 20 g of butter, add the shallot and chopped rosemary, and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft, but do not overcook.
Add the rice and sauté for 2 minutes, until the grains become shiny.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely.
Add half of the mushrooms. Add 2 ladles of broth, bring to a boil, and stir until the rice fully absorbs it.
Gradually add broth as it evaporates, stirring the rice, until the rice is cooked to al dente. This will take about 16-18 minutes.
5 minutes before it's done, add the remaining mushrooms.
Season with salt and pepper to your taste.
Remove the pot from the heat, add butter and grated Parmesan, and stir well for 30 seconds until creamy.
Serve immediately.
Cut the tomatoes into thin half-rings with a sharp knife.
Also, cut the onion into very thin half-rings.
In a salad bowl, mix the tomatoes and onions, add salt to taste.
Sprinkle finely chopped herbs on top to your liking (green onion, mint, cilantro).
Before serving, let it sit for at least 15 minutes so the vegetables release their juice.
Traditionally served with pilaf.
In Tajikistan, cucumbers cut lengthwise are added to the salad.
Whip the sour cream and cottage cheese with a mixer. If necessary, you can add a little water or milk for a more liquid consistency.

In a dish, first place the berry jam, then the mixture of cottage cheese and sour cream, followed by dried kiwi, then layer the cottage cheese mixture, then jam, again the mixture, grainy cottage cheese, and top with pine nuts.

recipes.title: Tori Paitan Ramen (鶏ガラパイタン)

instructions.text: Cut the chicken into pieces. Separate the chicken breast and set it aside to use later in the soup.
Carefully remove all the meat from the drumsticks, trying not to damage the integrity of the entire piece of meat from the leg and thigh.
Soak everything (except the separated meat) in water for at least 30 minutes to get rid of any remaining blood clots.
Rinse under running water.
Bring to a boil and remove all the foam and protein residues from the surface with a skimmer.
Add sake and cook on high heat with a very tightly closed lid for 5 hours.
After 3 hours, start breaking the bones with a potato masher.

30 minutes before the end, all bones should dissolve, and you can blend the entire mixture with an immersion blender. Add another cup of water, bring to a boil, strain through a fine sieve, ensuring that all small solid particles are removed. The broth should be a milky creamy color.
Place all the ingredients in a pot. Add water and bring to a boil over high heat. Allow to boil for 10 minutes, then reduce the heat to medium, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Remove from heat and let cool slightly. This is called shio (salty) tare.
If you want a spicy tare, add sambal chili paste to taste.
Season the chicken thigh with skin, as well as the meat removed from the drumsticks with salt and pepper, and place in the oven skin side up to bake for 20-30 minutes until fully cooked.

In a bowl, pour shio or spicy tare. Add a squeezed clove of garlic. Add the broth, place the previously prepared noodles. Top with sliced chicken chashu, finely chopped green onions, and add the marinated egg cut in half.
Optionally, add any remaining toppings.
Pat the duck breast dry and make diamond-shaped cuts on the skin.
Season with salt and rub in the ground Sichuan pepper.
Place the breasts in a cold skillet and turn on the heat.
This technique will help to render the fat from the breast effectively.
When enough fat has rendered, add crushed garlic and rosemary.
Sear the breast for 6 minutes on each side.
In a baking dish, layer the sliced pear and peach. Sprinkle with sugar (optional).
Place the seared breast skin side up on top, and bake for 10 minutes in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F).
Remove from the oven, slice the breast, place it on a bed of peach and pear, and drizzle with pistachio sauce.
Melt the butter in a skillet, add the chopped shallot, sauté, and then add the shelled pistachios.
After a minute, pour in the cognac, and continue cooking for another minute.
Pour all the contents into a bowl for an immersion blender.
Add all the duck fat from the skillet, straining through a sieve, add the juice, and blend everything with an immersion blender until a smooth sauce consistency is achieved.
Boil the veal for 1.5 hours in salted water. You can also use tongue. Allow to cool and cut into small cubes.
Mix the sourdough, sour cream, and heavily carbonated mineral water with kefir.
Add the juice of one lemon and salt.
Let the sourdough steep for 30 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in their skins. You can also boil the eggs hard in the same pot, after washing them well.
Cool in cold water.
Peel and cut into small cubes.
Slice the radishes and cucumbers into thin strips.
Wash the radishes and cucumbers, and cut them into thin rings.
Finely chop the dill and green onion.
Add mustard and, if desired, Tabadjan bean paste to the sourdough. This paste will incredibly enrich the okroshka, adding sharp notes.
Mix all the ingredients, season with salt, and add a pinch of sugar.
Pour over the sourdough and mix again.
Thoroughly rinse the caviar under running water, removing all sediment, and soak it in cold boiled water for 3 hours.
Select a sieve with holes small enough for the caviar to pass through but large enough for peat, soil, and any debris to wash away freely under running water.
Boil water and completely dissolve the salt in it. No tiny grains should be present. If any appear, strain through several layers of cheesecloth.
Pour the caviar with the brine solution, which should be at 70 degrees at the time.
Leave in brine for 12-24 hours.
After the time has passed, drain the caviar into a sieve (be careful, they are very 'bouncy') to completely drain the brine, transfer the caviar to a bowl, add oil, and whisk with a fork.
Transfer the caviar to sterilized containers. Store for no more than 3 months.
For serving, fry the black bread, spread cooled croutons with green garlic butter, place a spoonful of caviar on top, and eat immediately!
Blend the butter, garlic, and parsley. Refrigerate for 30 minutes.
Separate the yolks from the whites. Whisk them in a bowl large enough for the entire volume of sauce.
Add lemon juice, mustard, a pinch of salt, and whisk the mixture well. It should become homogeneous.
Start to pour in the olive oil in a thin stream while constantly whisking. Add a little, whisk, add a little more, and whisk again.
Add the minced garlic and saffron.
Continue to pour in the oil and whisk until the mixture reaches the desired consistency.
Add the ground white pepper and, if using, the chili.
Slice the onion into half rings.
Sauté the onion in butter in a saucepan over medium heat. The onion will significantly reduce in volume during cooking.
Add salt, which will draw out moisture. As the onion cooks, it will first become soft and then juicy.
The onion will start to brown or caramelize, becoming sweet and delicious due to the sugar it contains in large quantities.
This will take about 10 to 15 minutes.
You can help it a bit by adding a spoonful of sugar.
Stir occasionally to ensure even cooking of the onion.
Add a little water to collect all the concentrated juices from the bottom of the pan. Continue until the onion is soft and dark golden in color. This will take 25-35 minutes.
Optionally, add a little wine or liqueur for extra flavor. Madeira or brandy pairs well with onion.
Caramelized onion is perfect for burgers and steaks, as well as for salads and soups.

recipes.title: Baked Pasta with Four Cheeses (Pasta Ai Quattro Formaggi)

ingredients.name: Penne
ingredients.notes: fusilli, farfalle, rigatoni, rotini or shells

ingredients.name: Taleggio cheese
ingredients.notes: or another semi-soft cheese with a strong flavor

instructions.text: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil, and cook the pasta for 80% of the recommended cooking time indicated on the package, then drain and return to the pot.
While the water is heating, melt the butter in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Once the butter is melted, add the flour and mix until smooth.
Cook the flour mixture for a minute or two, then slowly pour in the milk, and bring to a smooth consistency.
Season with salt and pepper and continue to cook over medium heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce thickens, about 10 minutes.
Add the cheese and continue to cook over low heat until the cheese melts and the sauce becomes smooth.
In a skillet, sauté the guanciale or pancetta over medium heat until cooked and slightly browned, about 7-8 minutes.
Set aside.
In the rendered fat from the guanciale, blanch the chopped Brussels (cauliflower) sprouts.
Pour the cheese sauce into the pot with the pasta, add the finely chopped parsley, and mix well.
Pour the entire pasta mixture into a baking dish.
Evenly distribute the blanched cabbage on top, sprinkle with breadcrumbs and grated Parmesan.
Bake for about 20 minutes or until the cheese is melted and golden brown.

Place the diced mushroom, onion, and sweet pepper in a lightly oiled skillet and cook for about 15 minutes over low heat, stirring regularly, to remove almost all the water from the ingredients, otherwise the mushroom patty may fall apart while frying.
After 15 minutes, add the minced garlic and cook for another 5 minutes until no water remains in the skillet and the mixture is slightly browned.

Transfer the mushroom mixture to a bowl, add the lightly beaten egg, all other ingredients for forming the patty, and mix. Then combine the mixture with your hands for a few minutes to compact the filling.
Form a patty and place it in the refrigerator for 10 minutes.
If the patty falls apart, add more breadcrumbs and another beaten egg.
In a skillet, heat vegetable oil over medium heat and fry the patty until golden brown for 6 minutes on each side. In the same skillet, toast the brioche halves.
When the patty is flipped, place a slice of cheese on top and cover with a lid to melt.
Spread aioli on the bottom half of the bun, place the tomato, then the patty with cheese on top.
Top with sliced cornichons, then add chuka, generously spread the upper half of the bun with sweet chili sauce, and cover the composition with it.
Wash the wings, dry them, and cut them into 3 parts at the joints.
The wing tips can be used for broth, but we won't need them here.
Traditionally, "Buffalo" wings are deep-fried.
They can be found either breaded or unbreaded.
Wings are fried until cooked in oil until golden brown at 180°C (350°F), or baked in the oven.

Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and place a rack on a baking sheet. In a large bowl, mix the chicken wings with the butter and season with garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Transfer to the prepared baking sheet.
Coat the wings in breading (it's convenient to do this in a bag) and fry until cooked in oil. Drain the cooked wings on a sieve or place them on paper towels.
While the wings are baking, prepare the cheese sauce. For this, blend all the ingredients in a blender. The sauce does not have to be completely smooth; it's fine if it remains slightly lumpy.
The sauce is prepared just before serving the wings. For this, melt 60 g of butter with 2 tbsp of brown sugar in a saucepan over medium heat.
When the mixture starts to boil, add 3 tbsp of tomato sauce or tomato paste.
Then add 1 tbsp of chili sauce, taste, and if necessary, add more to reach your desired level of spiciness.
After that, add the clove of garlic, salt, and black pepper to taste, bring to a boil, and immediately remove from heat. The sauce should not be boiled, as it may separate.
Coat the cooked wings with the "Buffalo" sauce and mix. Place the wings on a serving dish.
Serve carrot and celery sticks cut into strips with the "Blue Cheese" sauce.
Mix all the ingredients for the patty well, shape the minced meat into a patty for the burger, and refrigerate for 15 minutes.
While it is in the refrigerator, prepare the sauce.*
For this, sauté the onion in oil until soft, add the cream, stir, add the curry, tomato paste, and cheese, and mix until the cheese is completely dissolved in the cream.
First, toast the halves of the brioche, then place the patties on the grill (pan), and cook for 3 minutes on each side, brushing the sides with mustard.
When you flip the patty, place the cheese on top and cover with a lid to let it melt.
Assemble the burger in the following order:
Brioche (bottom part) - cheese sauce - radish - cilantro - patty with cheese - ginger and cucumber - cheese sauce - top part of brioche.

recipes.title: Pasta with Cauliflower, Seafood and Laoganma Sauce

instructions.text: Bring water to a boil, adding 1/2 tablespoon of salt. When the water is boiling, cook the pasta according to the time indicated on the package.
In a frying pan (preferably in a wok), heat the oil, and first sauté the sliced onion, then add garlic, ginger, broccoli or cauliflower, cut into slices for 2 minutes.
Add carrot, the white part of the green onion, oyster sauce, mix, sauté for another 2 minutes, and add Laoganma sauce, seafood, and mix. Add salt to taste, and add the chopped leaves of bok choy.
After a minute, toss in the cooked pasta, mix everything together and serve.
Cut the vegetables into large pieces.
Slice the onion into half rings.
Place the cucumbers, tomatoes, onion, and olives in a salad bowl, drizzle with olive oil and vinegar, add dried oregano, pepper, and salt. Mix well.
Top with a whole piece of feta cheese.
Serve immediately.
Sauté garlic in olive oil and butter until fragrant. Remove from the pan.
Add the washed chanterelles, cutting larger mushrooms into several pieces.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate. Lower the heat to medium and simmer covered for 20 minutes until the mushrooms are cooked.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Cook the pasta according to the time indicated on the package.
Add cream to the pan, cooking for 5 minutes until it thickens.
Add the chopped parsley, mix, and place the cooked pasta in the pan. Stir.
Serve immediately.

Boil the eggs hard for 8-10 minutes and cool them. If desired, you can separate the yolk from the white. Finely chop the white. To the two yolks, add 2 teaspoons of sugar and 30 ml of butter. Mash with a fork until smooth.
Filet the herring and remove all small bones. If desired, it can be finely chopped, set some aside, and add the chopped herring at the very end.
Bring the butter to room temperature and whisk it.
Soak the bread crumb in cream for 10-15 minutes, then squeeze out all the moisture from the crumb.
Peel the apple and cut it into small pieces.
Finely chopped onion can be pre-fried until golden, then squeeze out all the moisture.
Pass all the ingredients through a meat grinder or blender, and chop coarsely to maintain texture.
If using cream cheese, add it along with walnuts and garlic, mix, and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Serve on toasted bread, garnished with finely chopped green onion.
Ideally, hashla should be cooked over a fire in a cauldron, but if that is not possible, it can be just as tasty in a heavy-bottomed pot.
Rinse the meat well, cut it into portion-sized pieces without separating the meat from the bones.
Peel the onion and cut it into large rings.
Remove the seeds from the peppers and cut them into strips. Cut the tomatoes into large slices.
The ingredients are layered in a container:
first the onion, covered with a layer of tomatoes, then the peppers. On top, add a layer of meat.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
The garlic can be cut in half without separating and placed between the layers.
Next, another vegetable layer and then a layer of meat. The last layer of lamb is covered with vegetables.
Add the chili pepper if desired.
If using beer, pour it into the container, cover with a lid, and place on the lowest heat for 3-4 hours.
Towards the end of cooking, add salt and spices. Before serving, garnish with fresh herbs.
First of all, you can boil broth from the bones.
Chop the onion, slightly fry it, and simmer with tomato paste and oil, adding a little broth.
Finely chop the pickled cucumbers.
Cut the carrot and potato into cubes.

Cut the meat products into thin slices, place them in a pot with the prepared onion, add finely chopped cucumbers, sliced olives, potato, carrot, salt, pepper, bay leaf, pour in the broth and cook for 20 minutes.
When serving, add sour cream, olives, slices of lemon peeled from the skin, and finely chopped parsley or dill to the solyanka.

ingredients.name: Bouquet garni
ingredients.notes: a sprig of parsley, thyme, bay leaf

ingredients.name: Arborio rice, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano

instructions.text: Wash the octopus, clean it, and remove the beak.

First, bring the water to a boil, and dip the octopus in for 1 minute, remove it, and repeat this procedure 2 more times after a couple of minutes. This will prevent the skin from peeling off in shreds during boiling.
Add half a white onion, crushed garlic cloves, the bouquet garni, black peppercorns, and 1 tsp of salt to the water.
Boil for 1 hour over medium heat.
Afterward, remove the octopus, let it cool, then cut it into pieces (you can leave the tentacles whole). Do not drain the broth after boiling; it can be used for various dishes, including risotto.
In a skillet, heat the olive oil, lightly sauté the finely chopped half of the onion, and add the pieces of octopus.
Sauté for 1 minute, gradually adding Worcestershire sauce while mixing it with the octopus. Add more sauce as it evaporates.
Sauté for 10 minutes.
In 50 grams of butter, sauté the finely chopped shallot onion, add the rice, and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in 1 ladle of the octopus broth, and continue stirring the rice, adding broth as needed.
Cook over low heat, allowing the liquid to simmer lightly.
Add cuttlefish ink, salt, pepper, and continue cooking.
Taste the rice. It should be al dente.
When the risotto is ready, add the remaining 50 g of butter, Parmesan, and stir until the last ingredients are fully dissolved.
Plate the risotto, place the octopus on top, and serve immediately.

recipes.title: Risotto with Clams and Blue Cheese

ingredients.name: Arborio rice, Carnaroli or Vialone Nano

instructions.text: In a saucepan, melt 50 grams of butter and sauté the rice, stirring, for 1 minute.
Then pour in 2 ladles of broth, reduce the heat to medium, and cook the rice for 17-20 minutes, stirring and adding broth as it evaporates.
If using saffron, crush it with your fingers into the rice.
Meanwhile, in a skillet with 20 grams of butter, sauté the onion and garlic until soft, add the clams, and sauté for 5 minutes.
You can also add and sauté the finely chopped bacon.
Add the finely chopped parsley and mix.
Five minutes before the rice is ready, add all the clams with the liquid from the skillet to the rice, and mix.
When the rice is al dente, add the crumbled cheese and the remaining butter, stirring until the butter and cheese are fully melted.
Serve on plates, garnished with clams in shells and parsley. Optionally drizzle with lemon juice.
Cut the goose neck from the breast, grabbing it near the wings, and carefully remove the skin, trying not to damage it. Sew up the hole at the thin end of the neck with culinary thread.
Boil the stomachs in water first, after 15 minutes add the cleaned hearts and liver, and cook for another 15 minutes.

Prepare the filling – finely chop the fat and skin of the bird, dice 1 onion into small cubes. Sauté the onion in the fat until light golden, add the chopped skin, minced meat, crushed garlic, and lightly fry. Then add the butter, melt it, and add the flour with semolina. Salt and pepper to taste.
Chop the cooked offal and add it to the minced meat, add the eggs and mix well.
If desired, add toasted pistachios to the mixture.
Stuff the neck with the mixture, filling it 80%. Do not pack tightly.

After filling the neck with the filling, sew up the other end of the neck. Place the stuffed neck in water (or broth), salt, add the carrot and onion cut into 4 pieces. Boil until cooked for 45 minutes. You can add a bit more salt.
After the neck is cooked, remove it from the broth, remove the threads, and fry it whole in a pan until golden brown.
Alternatively, you can bake it in the oven for 20 minutes at 180°C (350°F), greasing the baking sheet and necks with oil beforehand.
Peel the potatoes, wash them, cut into 3-4 pieces, and boil in salted water until cooked.
Chop the onion into small cubes and fry in vegetable oil in a pan until golden brown.
Mix the onion with the ground meat, add salt and pepper to taste. Fry the meat mixture with the onion until cooked.
Mash the potatoes into a puree and let it cool slightly.
Add the eggs and 3-4 tablespoons of flour to the potatoes. Mix well.
Adjust the salt to taste.
Sprinkle flour on the cutting board or other surface where the potato zrazy will be made.

Form balls from the dough, then roll the balls into flat cakes. Place the meat filling in the center of each cake and wrap the edges of the dough, forming patties. Slightly press the prepared blanks on top, giving the zrazy a flat shape.
To prevent the dough from sticking to your hands, you can moisten your fingers with cold water before shaping each blank.
Coat them lightly in flour.
Heat a pan with vegetable oil. Place the zrazy seam side down. Fry on medium heat on each side until golden brown.
Serve with sour cream.

recipes.title: Sous Vide Pork Loin with Garlic

instructions.text: Rinse the loin, trim the fat from the sides (if any).
For the marinade, add spices, mustard, and 1 clove of minced garlic to the oil, and mix well.

Season the loin with salt and pepper, and rub the marinade all over it. Actually, these are basic herbs and spices; you can add turmeric, coriander seeds, cilantro, and stuff it with pieces of carrot. Even honey can be added.
Make incisions in the meat with a knife and stuff it with garlic cloves. You can cut the garlic in half lengthwise to reduce the chances of it falling out of the meat.
Place the meat in a vacuum bag, add rosemary sprigs from both sides, and vacuum seal. Refrigerate to marinate for at least 2 hours, preferably overnight.
Pour enough water into the sous vide container and submerge the marinated loin in the vacuum bag.
Cook for 5 hours at a temperature of 60°C.

If desired, after this time, the loin can be seared either in a pan or in the oven (220°C (425°F)) until golden brown, or if you have an air pressure cooker, pour out the water from the bowl, place the meat on the rack, and select "fry-meat" for 20 minutes.
Serve on the table, sliced, and garnished with herbs.
Clean the shrimp (fresh or frozen). Remove the intestinal vein from the shrimp.
Place a frying pan or heatproof dish on the heat, pour in the olive oil. Wait for it to heat up well. Then reduce the heat to medium.
Add finely chopped garlic, pepper, paprika, and parsley. Stir.
Add the shrimp, fry on each side until they turn white-orange.
Serve immediately with a baguette.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Mix the room temperature butter with thyme, rosemary, parsley, garlic powder, cayenne pepper, salt, and pepper. Set aside.
Pat the turkey thighs dry with a paper towel; season with salt and pepper.

Arrange the potatoes, onion, and garlic on a baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and season with salt and pepper. Add the turkey thighs and rub the meat and skin under the skin with the herb butter. Top with lemon zest and juice.

Bake in the preheated oven for 90 minutes. After 30 minutes, start basting the turkey with its own juices every 15 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted near the bone should read 74 degrees Celsius.
Serve, garnished with herbs.
Clean the fish fillet from the dark meat that gives a too sharp taste.
Cut the fish into 1 cm cubes.
Pour the freshly squeezed lime juice over the fish meat, season with salt and mix well.
Cover with film and place in the refrigerator for 20 minutes.
Dice the tomato, onion, and mango. Remove seeds from the chili pepper and chop.
Peel the cucumber, and also remove the seeds using a teaspoon. Cut into cubes.
Chop the cilantro.
Put all ingredients in a bowl, pour orange juice over, season with salt, add ground pepper, oregano, and mix well.
Add tomato juice (Clamato) and ketchup. Season with salt, and mix everything together again.
Drain the liquid from the fish (which is called tiger's milk), and add it to everything else. Mix everything. Adjust salt and pepper if necessary.
Garnish with a 'flower' made from avocado, as shown in the video.

recipes.title: Delicious Turkey Thigh in Air Fryer

instructions.text: Marinate the turkey in the marinade by mixing all the ingredients together.
Place it on the rack in the air fryer and cook for 45 minutes at 200°C (400°F), selecting the Air Fryer - Poultry program.
Serve with a sweet sauce like Narsarab
Fillet the fresh fish. Remove all bones and dark meat. It gives too strong a flavor in carpaccio.
Slice it thinly.
Mix all the ingredients for the sauce. If you couldn't buy citrus Ponzu sauce, you can make it yourself.
Slice the red onion into half rings and soak it in freshly squeezed lime juice. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Arrange the sliced pieces of fish on a plate, sprinkle with salt and pepper. Drizzle with sauce, and top with the marinated onion in lime juice.
Garnish with cucumber slices arranged around the edge.
You can also optionally garnish with slices of avocado or orange.
Soak the kombu leaves in rice vinegar beforehand, then crush them in a mortar. Add the bonito flakes and crush them together with the kombu.
Mix all the ingredients for Ponzu and let it steep for at least a day. Strain through a sieve. It can be stored in the refrigerator for several weeks.

Wash the mushrooms very well under running water. It's even better to soak them in cold water for about 30 minutes, and then rinse. They usually grow in sandy soil, and you need to do everything possible to get rid of the sand.
Chop them coarsely and boil for 15 minutes.
Sauté finely chopped shallot onion in butter for 3 minutes, and add garlic.
Add the boiled morels and sauté them until golden brown.
Sprinkle with dried oregano and ground black pepper.
Meanwhile, cook the fettuccine in salted water according to the time indicated on the package.
Add cream and a ladle of pasta cooking liquid to the mushrooms.
Season with salt, add chopped parsley and basil. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Transfer the pasta to the mushrooms, and mix them well together.
Serve on a plate and generously sprinkle with Parmesan.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat. Add the onion and pepper and sauté for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are soft.
Add diced tomatoes (about 1 cm), stir, add spices, and cover with a lid.
Simmer for 5 minutes over medium heat.
Crack the eggs on top of the tomato mixture. Let the eggs cook for about 1 minute. Then, using a spoon, break the yolks and mix the eggs into the tomato mixture.
Continue cooking until the eggs reach the desired doneness.
Watch to ensure the eggs do not overcook. They should be 'moist'. Traditionally, the eggs are cooked until set but remain soft.
Sprinkle the chopped parsley on top of the omelette and serve immediately with bread.
For a good broth, the first essential step to success is choosing good homemade chicken and its parts. Store-bought chickens are not suitable for this.
Wash the chicken wings and thighs well, place them in a pot and cover with 5 liters of cold water.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes. Periodically skim off the foam that appears on the surface.
Peel the onion and carrot, and cut them in half.
After all the foam has been removed, add the onion, carrot, and all the spices except for the kaffir lime to the pot.
After 39 minutes, remove the bay leaf and add the kaffir lime leaves, tearing them by hand.
Cook the broth without covering the lid for at least 1.5 hours. It must not boil. The water should just 'simmer'. Then it will be clear.
When the broth is ready, remove all contents, separate the chicken meat from the bones, set aside for the soup, and discard all spices and vegetables.
Strain the broth.
Boil the eggs in boiling water for exactly 6 minutes. To prevent them from cracking, poke the shell in one spot (from the blunt end) with a needle.
Immediately cool them in ice water, then they will peel easily.
Add salt, fish sauce to the broth and adjust the soup to your desired taste.
Dice the carrot and potato, and add them to the broth.
Cook until the potatoes are done. This will take about 15-20 minutes depending on the variety.
Meanwhile, bring water to a boil for the noodles, adding salt at the ratio of 10 g per 1 liter of water.
When the soup is ready, place pieces of the reserved chicken at the bottom of the bowl, top with noodles, pour over the broth, and place a halved egg on top of the noodles.
Garnish with herbs, and add ground black pepper to taste.
Boil the crab in salted water for 12-18 minutes (depending on the size of the crab), and let it cool.
Turn the crab on its back, bend the tail, and detach it from the body.
Then detach the legs and claws by pulling them sideways at the joints.
Next, from the tail side, use both thumbs to push up the shell. It should open easily under pressure.
Remove all ten sponge-like 'dead man's fingers' and discard them. This is the inedible part of the crab. They resemble feathers.
Using a spoon, scoop out all the brown meat from the shell (often with crab roe) and set it aside.
Now the most labor-intensive task is to extract all the precious crab meat from the claws and legs.
This can be done using a hammer, tongs, and a wooden stick.
After all the meat is separated, use your hands to check for any hard pieces. (remnants of the shell).
Boil the egg hard, peel it, and mash it with a fork.
Cook the orzo (risoni) (a type of pasta resembling rice) according to the time indicated on the package.
Mix all the ingredients for the filling with the white crab meat, and tightly stuff the remaining upper shell.
Add the brown meat on top, and 'seal' the hole in the shell with a layer of mayonnaise and grated cheese.
If there is too much filling, it can be served with bread and mayonnaise as a toast.
Place the crab in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 5-7 minutes to melt the cheese in the filling and on top of the crab.
Serve immediately with a wedge of lemon.
Place the tripe in a pot and cover it with water. Add a little lemon juice and bring to a boil.
Drain the water, rinse the tripe, and repeat this process at least 5 times.
This is necessary to remove the characteristic smell associated with the stomach.
Then simmer it over medium heat for at least 3 hours, adding the celery root, bay leaves, carrot, and a whole onion, after which it will become perfectly tender.
When the tripe is ready, remove it and cut it into strips 1 cm wide.
Sauté diced onion, carrot, celery, and garlic over medium heat until soft. If using pancetta, sauté it along with the vegetables.
Then add the sliced tripe and sauté for 5 minutes.
Season with chili flakes to taste, add cloves, and a handful of finely chopped mint.
Now, pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely, and after
Add also 100 grams of Pecorino Romano cheese.
There are two ways to prepare tripe, where cheese is added during cooking and also to the finished dish, and there is a method where it is just sprinkled on the finished dish.
Now pour in the wine and let it evaporate completely, and then add the tomato paste passata di pomodoro. You can also use canned tomatoes in their own juice, previously mashed with a fork.
Generously sprinkle with salt, add a couple of ladles of broth or water, stir, and cook with the lid on for 1 hour on low heat.
If the sauce has not thickened, at the end increase the heat and cook for another 10 minutes without the lid.
Serve on plates, add mint leaves, and sprinkle with Pecorino Romano on top.

recipes.title: Fake Caviar from Herring and Carrots

instructions.text: Unlike recipes where the washed carrots need to be boiled for 15-20 minutes,
I personally prefer a different consistency of carrots, so to speak, al dente. This gives the characteristic "crunch" as if the caviar grains are bursting.
To do this, you need to cut the carrots into thin strips (like Korean style) and blanch them in boiling water for 2 minutes.
Let it cool.
Pass all the ingredients through a meat grinder.
First the butter, then the cheese, then the herring, and finally the carrots. The butter should not be too soft, so you can use it straight from the refrigerator or freezer.
Mix everything well, and the delicious snack is ready.
Store in the refrigerator in an airtight container for several days, but it is unlikely to last that long.
Usually, it is eaten instantly.
Serve on white bread or baguette. It can also be used as a filling for pancakes or potato pancakes.

ingredients.name: Tomato puree
ingredients.notes: or canned tomatoes in their own juice

instructions.text: Boil a large pot of water for the pasta. Add salt, about 1 tsp per liter of water.
Cut the kaffir lime leaves with scissors, removing the stem.
In a mortar and pestle, crush the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves, and Thai chili until there are no large pieces left. To a fine crumb.
In a wok or large skillet, cook the shrimp until done. Remove and set aside; do not clean the wok.

Drop the spaghetti into the boiling water, cooking for 1 minute LESS than the time indicated on the package. Immediately start making the sauce as soon as you put the pasta to cook. (At this time your sauce should be ready before the pasta is done. But if not, no problem, just drain the pasta and set it aside until ready to use.)
In the same wok, sauté the onion over medium heat for a couple of minutes until it becomes translucent.
Add the mushrooms and a bit of fish sauce, then cook for a minute.
Add the Tom Yum paste and quickly mix it with the oil, then add the tomatoes. Use a spatula to break the tomatoes into small pieces.
Add the chili paste and fish sauce and cook for a few minutes until the sauce thickens.
Once the spaghetti is ready, add it to the sauce. You can also add a bit of pasta water. If you plan to drain the pasta, be sure to save a cup of pasta water in case you need it.
Add the shrimp back in and toss everything in the sauce for another minute, adding more pasta water if you need more liquid.
Turn off the heat, then add the lime juice and cilantro. Taste and add more lime juice/fish sauce if necessary.
Serve with grated parmesan if desired.
If you have frozen shells, thaw them in warm water.
Use the tip of a knife to detach the meat of the mollusks from the shell, cutting at the attachment point.

There are many debates about whether or not to remove the black pouch located inside the mollusk. Personally, my choice is definitely no, as the mollusk will lose a lot of flavor. In extreme cases, you can poke the pouch and release the liquid from it, but it should not be completely removed.
Sprinkle each shell lightly with salt, return the mollusk inside, place a piece of butter (1x1 cm) and sprinkle with a mixture of parsley and garlic.
Place on a baking sheet, and put in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 3-5 minutes, until the butter melts.
The main thing is not to overdo it!
Transfer to plates and drizzle with lemon juice.
Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Chilean Conger Eel Soup (Caldillo de congrio)

ingredients.name: Conger eel, head and tail
ingredients.notes: or heads of any sea fish

instructions.text: Rinse the fish head well, place it in a pot with 3 liters of water, and put it on the heat.
Bring to a boil, remove the foam from the surface, reduce the heat to minimum, so that the water simmers slightly.
Add the onion, celery stalk, and carrot, cut in half, then add the bay leaves and black peppercorns. Crush the garlic with a knife and add it to the pot as well.
Cook for at least 45 minutes.
Wash all the vegetables very well. Then cut the potatoes with skin into wedges, the bell pepper into thick strips, and the chili pepper into thin strips.
Peel the carrot and slice it into rounds, and cut the onion into thin strips.
In a medium pot, sauté the vegetables with salt and ground black pepper in vegetable oil over medium heat for about 6-10 minutes or until the onion becomes soft.
Add the tomatoes or tomato paste, oregano, garlic, and paprika, and stir.

Add the potato wedges, and let them simmer for about 5 minutes. In some cases, the fish is added along with the potatoes, provided that the chosen variety of potato cooks completely within 15 minutes.
Place the slices of conger eel in the pot and pour in the white wine all at once, wait for it to boil, and cover for just a few seconds without stirring.
Pour in the fish broth, so that it completely covers the fish, and cook covered over medium heat for 15 minutes without stirring.
When the soup is almost ready, you can optionally add the heavy cream and gently stir the surface, trying not to disturb the fish.
Serve the conger eel soup very hot, garnished on top with cilantro or parsley, and optionally seasoned with lemon.

recipes.title: Thai Steamed Fish (Pla kapong neung manao)

ingredients.name: White Barramundi sea bass
ingredients.notes: or any other white sea fish. Sea bass, dorado, red snapper

instructions.text: Make 3 diagonal cuts on each side of the fish.
Stuff the fish's belly with sliced lemongrass.
Steam the fish for 10 minutes per 1 kg of fish. If the fish is less than 1 kg, steam it for 10 minutes.

Meanwhile, heat the broth over medium heat, add sugar and dissolve it completely. Pour into a bowl. In the hot broth, add garlic, chili pepper, fish sauce, lime juice, and chopped cilantro. Mix well. Taste and adjust to your liking.
When the fish is ready, transfer it to a serving dish. Place the celery with leaves on the sides of the fish. Pour the sauce over the fish.
Garnish with additional celery leaves and serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.title: Cabbage Rolls in Thai Red Curry

instructions.text: If you dared to make cabbage rolls yourself, then this is the ultimate skill. I used a ready-made semi-finished product to save time on the rolls themselves.
Sauté the red Thai curry paste in coconut or vegetable oil. In principle, you can also use green or yellow paste. I use curry paste from the manufacturer Aroy-D.

When the paste starts to separate (oil appears), it's time to place the cabbage rolls in the pan, lightly frying them on both sides. If you have frozen semi-finished products, there is no need to defrost them beforehand.
Place them tightly enough so that they do not open up during cooking.
Add coconut milk, sugar, fish sauce, and lime juice if using.
The liquid should completely cover the cabbage rolls. If it's not enough, add water or broth.
Cover with a lid and cook on low heat for 40 minutes.
Place the finished cabbage rolls in a deep plate, generously pour with sauce, and sprinkle with cilantro.
Thoroughly rinse the chanterelles, clean them of sand by placing the mushrooms in salted water for 30 minutes.
Slice the chanterelles very thinly. If you have a slicer, use it.
Arrange the sliced mushrooms on plates.

Basically, you can just salt them, sprinkle with ground black pepper, oregano, generously drizzle with freshly squeezed lemon juice, and let marinate for about 15 minutes. But you can also 'upgrade' the dish by adding the ingredients listed as optional.
To do this, slightly heat the olive oil, dissolve the sugar in the warm oil, then sauté the sliced garlic over low heat. Remove the garlic from the oil afterward.
Pour the oil onto the plate first, then place the mushrooms on top, drizzle with lemon juice, and splash with balsamic vinegar. Then add the capers to the plate.
Add salt, pepper, oregano, and garnish with arugula and slices of Parmesan if desired.

recipes.title: Pasta with Salmon, Brussels Sprouts, and Pesto Sauce

instructions.text: Cut the salmon into 2 cm cubes. Slice the garlic thinly. Cut the Brussels sprouts in half.
Heat the olive oil in a pan over low heat. Do not let it boil.
Fry the garlic slices until golden brown. This will take about 7-10 minutes. Do not rush, otherwise, you might burn the garlic.
Put a pot of water with a pinch of salt on the heat.
The correct ratio for cooking any pasta is 1:10:100. For 100 grams of pasta, you need 1 liter of water and 10 grams of salt.
Add the tagliatelle and Brussels sprouts to the boiling water. Cook according to the time indicated on the pasta package. They will cook at the same time.
Fry the salmon pieces in the same pan for just 2 minutes, then add the pesto sauce. Ideally, it should be homemade, not store-bought.
Then add pepper and salt to taste.
When the pasta is ready, transfer it and the Brussels sprouts to the pan with the sauce.
Thoroughly mix everything with a wooden spatula so that the pasta absorbs the sauce.
Immediately place on a plate and serve.
Optionally, you can sprinkle grated cheese and pine nuts on top, but this is already a deviation from tradition, although tasty.
You can also drizzle the dish with lemon juice. Of course, if you wish.

recipes.title: Classic Genoese Pesto Sauce (Pesto di basilico alla genovese)

instructions.text: Separate the basil leaves from the stem (do not use the stem as it may taste bitter), wash thoroughly and dry. To do this, lay them out on a sheet of absorbent kitchen paper, place another sheet on top, and gently press with your palm, trying not to break the leaves.

Removing all the water is an important step, so do not rush. Basil is a very delicate plant that easily darkens. Any drop of water or any tear of the leaves will cause a change in the color of our pesto, turning it dark instead of bright light green.

While the basil leaves are drying, peel the garlic cloves and cut them in half lengthwise. Toast the pine nuts in a pan without oil. By the way, you can experiment with different nuts, such as almonds, walnuts, or cashews.

Place all the ingredients in a bowl of a food processor along with half of the oil and a pinch of salt and blend. Traditionally, a mortar is used for grinding, so you can use either that or a blender.

When we have a paste and no pieces of pine nuts or basil are visible, stop blending to add the remaining oil. If using lemon juice, add it now. Turn on the blender for a few seconds again, just to mix everything, and the pesto is ready to use.

recipes.title: Perfect Sauce for Meat and Steaks

instructions.text: Pour the cream into a saucepan and place it on the heat.
Bring to a simmer and reduce the heat to the minimum.
Add the remaining sauces and stir. The sauce is ready!
Cut the bacon (or pancetta) into small pieces and fry in a pan until golden brown. Set aside.
Peel the shrimp and remove the intestinal vein.
Dice the potatoes into small cubes of 10 mm, finely chop the onion, garlic, and celery. Sauté in butter over medium heat for about 2 minutes.
Then add the broth and bring to a boil. Cook for about 10 minutes or until the potatoes are cooked.

Meanwhile, place the fish, cut into pieces, in a pot and add the milk. Bring to a boil and simmer for 10 minutes until the fish is cooked. Then strain the milk into a separate container and set the fish aside.
Add the strained milk to the potatoes and bring to a boil. Then add the cream and mix well.
Mix 1 tablespoon of butter with 1 tablespoon of flour and add to the boiling mixture. Stir until it starts to thicken.
Then add the fish, shrimp, and crab meat to the soup. Taste the sauce and season with salt and pepper to taste.
Finally, add half of the bacon to the soup, some chopped parsley, and mix well.
When serving, add the remaining bacon and parsley. Serve with bread and salted butter.

ingredients.name: Grana Padano cheese (optional) or any good melting cheese like cheddar

instructions.text: A recipe for wonderful Polish pancakes with an author's "deviation" from the traditional recipe. The fact is that in Poland, boiled or stewed meat is usually used, which remains from broth cooking or leftovers from the table. And usually, nothing is added to it apart from onions and mushrooms. Sometimes cheese. This recipe is a "modification" of the recipe; you can remove all optional ingredients, and then you will have a dish that is as close as possible to the original Polish croquettes.
In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil, add the chopped onion, then the carrot, celery, and garlic. Sauté over medium heat until softened.

Add the ground meat, salt, and freshly ground black pepper. Mix well. Continue cooking until the moisture has completely evaporated. Add the tomato paste, mix, and pour in the wine. Evaporate it. Optionally add garam masala, curry, and cinnamon.
Pour in the milk, reduce the heat to low, and simmer covered for 30 minutes. The preparation is very similar to making a ragù Alla Bolognese.
Remove from heat and let cool, while we prepare the pancakes.
Mix all the pancake ingredients in a bowl with a blender. All lumps should be broken down.
In a heated pancake skillet, fry the pancakes, pouring the pancake mixture in such a way that the pancakes are as thin as possible.
Once all the pancakes are made, let them cool a bit and proceed to assembly.
Place a pancake on a clean plate and spread a thin layer of the meat filling.
Sprinkle with grated Parmesan or another good melting cheese if desired.
Fold the edges on both sides and tightly roll the pancake into a roll. Repeat with all pancakes.
Pour the breadcrumbs into a deep bowl. In a large bowl, beat the egg with water and a pinch of salt (optional).
Dip each meat-filled pancake into the egg mixture, then thoroughly coat in breadcrumbs.
In a large skillet, heat the vegetable oil well, in such a quantity that the oil completely covers the bottom of the pan. In batches, place the rolled croquettes in the hot oil.
Fry over medium heat for a few minutes on each side until the pancakes are evenly browned.

Transfer the meat pancakes to a plate lined with paper towels and fry all pancakes in batches. If necessary, you can add more oil between batches, but before the next batch of pancakes, make sure to heat it well.
Serve hot as a standalone dish or with broth or Polish borscht.
Chop the onion and garlic. Cut the other vegetables into cubes. Halve the cherry tomatoes. You can leave some okra whole by trimming the ends.

Sauté the onion in vegetable oil until soft, then add the garlic, carrot, and celery. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring the mixture. Then add the ground meat to the pan. Fry it, breaking up any clumps with a wooden spatula.

When the moisture has completely evaporated from the meat and it starts to caramelize (turn brown), add the okra and eggplant. Sauté lightly and add the tomato paste, cherry tomatoes, and spices, garam masala, and curry.
Add salt and ground pepper to taste.
Cover with a lid and simmer on low heat for 25-30 minutes.
Meanwhile, you can bring water to a boil for the pasta. Cook it according to the time indicated on the package. You can make any garnish to your liking. The stew pairs perfectly with everything.
Optionally, when serving, you can sprinkle the stew with grated Parmesan.
Mix all marinade ingredients in a large bowl.
Add the liver, stir in the marinade, and let it marinate for at least 20 minutes, preferably 1 hour.
Fry the liver over medium heat in vegetable oil until all pieces are evenly browned on all sides.
Add the tomato paste, salt, and simmer covered for 20 minutes, reducing the heat to minimum.
Serve with rice, garnished with cilantro on top.

recipes.title: Turkey Thigh Baked in the Oven

instructions.text: Marinate the turkey thigh in the above spices and herbs for at least overnight, preferably for 24 hours.
Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).
Place the turkey in a cooking bag or wrap it in foil in at least 2 layers. Put it in the oven skin side up.

Bake for 1 hour, then unwrap the foil (cut the bag) and bake in the upper grill for the remaining 30 minutes until golden brown, periodically basting the meat with the liquid that has accumulated at the bottom.
When the turkey is ready, cut it into serving pieces and serve with mashed potatoes or couscous, sprinkling with fried dried onions if desired.

ingredients.name: Pork Ribs
ingredients.notes: Lower part of the ribs, in strips

instructions.text: Rinse the ribs, remove the membrane. In a large wide pot, pour in the beer and soy sauce, place the ribs so that the liquid completely covers them.
Turn on the maximum heat and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to minimum, skim off the foam, and add cardamom, cinnamon stick, chili pepper, cloves, and black peppercorns.
Cook covered for 45-60 minutes.
20 minutes before the end, start boiling the potatoes in their skin until half cooked.

Meanwhile, you can prepare the sauce. For this, mix all the sauce ingredients in a saucepan, add a ladle of beer from the pot where the ribs are boiling, stir, bring to a light boil, and immediately turn off. The sauce is ready!
Line a large baking tray with foil, making sure it completely covers the bottom and sides. Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

When the ribs are cooked, place them on the baking tray bone side down and generously brush with sauce. You can pour 3-4 ladles of liquid from the pot where the ribs were boiled into the bottom of the tray.
Place the halved potatoes in the remaining space on the tray, salt them, sprinkle with oregano and ground pepper.
Cover everything with foil and bake without opening for 40 minutes.
After that, remove the foil and bake for another 30 minutes without foil.
Enjoy your meal!
Preheat the oven to 180 degrees. Place the bone marrows in a baking dish. Bake for 20 minutes.
Heat the olive oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Fry the bread until golden in the garlic oil.
Chop the green onion and cornichons.
Once the bone marrows are baked, scoop out the marrow with a teaspoon and spread it on the croutons.
Add salt and sprinkle with chopped green onion and cornichons.
